sourceDefinition: Time, syn. dahorN , (S, M, Msb, K,) in an absolute sense: (TA:) or a long time, syn. dahorN TawiylN : (A, and Mgh: [and this may be meant in the S &c. by the syn. dahorN alone, q. v.:]) or, properly, a long time ( dhr Twyl ) that is unlimited: (Msb, TA:) or an extended space of time that is indivisible; for you say zamaAnu ka*aA : “ the time of such a thing,” but not A^abadu ka*aA : (Er-Rághib:) [and generally, time, or duration, or continuance, or existence, without end; endless time, &c.; prospective eternity; opposed to A^azalN , which signifies “ time, or duration, &c., without beginning: ” (see the latter word for further explanations, &c.:) each of these significations may be meant by the explanation in the S and M and K, which is also given in the Msb: each correctly applies in particular instances:] pl. [of pauc.] A=baAdN (S, M, Msb, K) and [of mult.] A^ubuwdN (S, M, K) [and A^abaduwna , of which an ex. will be found below]: but the use of these pls. is restricted to particular cases, to signify portions of time, or to serve as corroboratives to the sing.: (MF:) as signifying an extended indivisible space of time, [or the like,] A^abadN should have neither dual nor pl.; but A=baAdN is sometimes said, when the sing. is restricted to denote a particular part, or portion, of the whole of that to which it applies, in like manner as a generic noun is restricted to a special and partial signification: some, however, have mentioned A=baAdN as being post-classical; not of the language of the Arabs called AlEarabu AlEarobaA='u . (Er-Rághib.) TaAla AlA^abado EalaY lubado [ The time became long to Lubad, the last, and the longest of life, of Luk- mán's seven vultures, to the term of the life of which his own term of life was decreed to extend,] is a proverb applied to any thing that has been of long duration. (M.) And you say, razaqaka A@ll~`hu EumurFA Tawiyla AlA=baAdi baEiyda AlA=maAdi [ May God grant thee a life long in duration (lit. durations, the pl. form being used not in its proper sense, but to give intensiveness of signification), and remote in limit (lit. limits )]. (A.) And kaAna h`*aA fiY A=baAdi Ald~ahori This was a long time ago. (Mgh.) And ↓ A^abadN A=bidN (TA) and ↓ A^abadN A^abiydN , (S, M, TA,) meaning daAy^imN [in an intensive sense]; (TA;) [ A long, or an endless, period of time; ] like as you say, dahorN daAhirN (S) or dahorN dahiyrN . (M.) [In each of these phrases, the latter word is added as a corroborative, or to give intensiveness to the signification.] liloA^abida and liA^abidK and [in an intensive sense, as will be seen below,] liA^abida A^abadK and liA^abadi AlA^abadi , accord. to different recitals of a trad., signify To the end of time; for ever; and for ever and ever. (TA.) A^abadFA is an adv. n., of which the signification includes all future time; [meaning Ever; like qaT~u in relation to past time;] (El-Khafájee, El-Bedr Ed-Demámeenee, MF;) and EalaY AlA^abadi signifies the same. (TA.) [So, too, does AlA^abada , unless used in a limited sense known to the hearer.] When you say, laA A^ukal~imuhu A^abadFA , you mean, [ I will not speak to him as long as I live, or henceforth, or ever; or I will never speak to him; i. e.,] from the time of your speaking to the end of your life. (Msb.) [In this case, A^abadFA may also be considered as a mere corroborative. It is used in both these ways ( llt~aA^osiysi and lilt~awokiydi ) in affirmative as well as negative sentences. For exs. of its use in affirmative sentences, see the Kur xviii. 2 and iv. 60, &c.] One also says, laA A^afoEaluhu , (S, M, A,) and laA A=tiyhi , (T, K,) A^abada AlA=baAdi , (T, M, A, K,) which, though of classical authority, is said to be no evidence of the use of A=bAd as a pl. of A^abadN in a general way by the Arabs of the classical ages, as it is here added merely as a corroborative, as A=zAl is in the phrase A^azala AlA=zaAli ; (MF;) and A^abada AlA^abadiyna , (M, A, K,) in which the latter word is not a rel. n., for if so it would be AlA^abadiy~iyna , but app. a pl., (M,) like A^araDuwna ; (M, K;) and ↓ A^abada AlA=bidiyna , (S, K,) like as you say, dahora AlA=bidiyna ; (S;) and ↓ A^abada AlA^abadiy~api ; (M, K;) and ↓ A^abada AlA^abiydi ; (T, S, M, A, K;) and A^abiyda ↓ AlA^abiydi ; (M, K;) and A^abada AlA^abadi ; (K;) and A^abada Ald~ahori ; (M, K; [in the T yada Ald~ahori ;]) all of which phrases are the same in meaning; (K;) [i. e. I will not do it, and I will not come to him, (or lA A=tyh may here mean the same as lA AfElh ,) during the endless space of all future times, or time; or the like; or for ever and ever; εἰς αἰῶνα τῶν αἰώνων ; in seculum seculorum; in omne ævum; ] the last word in every case being a corroborative. (MF.) ― -b2- Also, [for *uw A^abadK , and (applied to a fem. n.) *aAtu A^abadK ,] Lasting: or everlasting. (S, A, K.) So in the saying, Ald~unyaA' A^amadN waAlA=xirapu A^abadN [ The present state of existence is limited in duration, but the final state of existence is everlasting ]. ('Obeyd Ibn-'Omeyr and L.) And AlA^abadu signifies [ The Everlasting; i. e. God; because He alone is ↓ AlbaAqiY AlA^abadiy~ The Enduring without end or cessation; for the Muslims hold that all living creatures (even the angels) must die, and be raised again to life: or] The Ancient without beginning. (K.) -A2- Also Offspring that is a year old. (K.)

sourceDefinition: : see A^abidN . -A2- This word, (Lth, ISh, S, K,) said by Lth and ISh to be the only word of its measure heard from the Arabs except A_ibilN and nikiHN and xiTibN , but Az says that he had not heard the last two from any person worthy of reliance, and that they are pronounced nikoHN and xiTobN , (L,) [see A_ibilN ,] and ↓ A^abidN and ↓ A_ibodN , (K,) which are thought by Az to be dial. vars. of the first, (L,) applied to a female slave, and to a she-ass, signify Prolific; that breeds, or brings forth, plentifully; (S, K;) and ↓ A^abidN and ↓ A^abidapN (Aboo-Málik, TA) and ↓ A_ibidapN , (Aboo-Málik, K,) applied to a she-camel, signify the same: (Aboo-Málik, K, TA:) and A_ibidN (Lth, ISh, L) and ↓ A^abidN , (M, L,) applied to a female slave, (M, L,) and to a she-ass, (Lth, ISh, M, L,) and to a mare, (M, L,) that brings forth every year; (Lth, ISh, L;) or applied as a pl. to the female slave and the mare and the she-ass, that breed, or bring forth: (M, L:) and AlA_ibidaAni the female slave and the mare. (K, TA.) In the following saying, Al~aAbijad~i *iY AlA_ibido lano yuqoliEa Aljad~u Aln~akido fiY kul~i maA EaAmK talido [ Hard fortune will not depart save with the fortune which is the necessary attendant of the possessor of the female slave, as long as he possesses her, (or, if we take *Y in the sense of h`*ihi , save with the fortune of this female slave, ) who every year ( mA being redundant) brings forth, ] AlAbd means the female slave because her being prolific is an obstacle to prosperity, and is not good fortune; i. e., she only increases evil [and brings reproach upon her master by bearing him children; for the Arab in ancient times was considered as dishonoured by his having a child by a slave]. (S.) The Arabs also said, lano yaboluga Aljad~a Aln~akido ↓ AlA~a AlA^abido , meaning Nothing will attain to the object of removing hard fortune save female slaves and beasts or cattle which breed, or bring forth. (M, L: [in the latter of which is added, fiY kul~i EaAmK talido in every year bringing forth. ])

definition: Remaining, staying, abiding, or dwelling, constantly, continually, or permanently, in a place;
sourceDefinition: Remaining, staying, abiding, or dwelling, constantly, continually, or permanently, in a place; applied to a man [and to a bird]. (L.) And A^awaAbidu [pl. of A=bidapN ] Birds that remain in a country constantly, winter and summer; (T, L;) contr. of qawaATiEu . (A, L.) ― -b2- For the phrases A^abadN A=bidN and A^abada AlA=bidiyna , see A^abadN . ― -b3- A wild animal; (M, L, Msb;) that shuns, and takes fright at, mankind, amp;c.: (L, Msb:) fem. with p : pl. [properly fem.] A^awaAbidu , (M, Mgh, L,) and [masc. and fem.] A^ub~adN : (M, L:) and ↓ A^abuwdN is syn. with A=bidN ; (M;) as also ↓ mutaA^ab~idN . (A.) Wild animals are called A^awaAbidu (S, M, L, K) and A^ub~adN (M, L, K) because they endure for a long, or [naturally] unlimited, time; (M, L;) because they do not die a natural death, (As, M, L, K,) but from some evil accident; and the same is asserted of the serpent. (As, M, L.) [See also A^abidN .] [Hence,] qayodu AlA^awaAbidi (assumed tropical:) The light, or active, horse, which overtakes the wild animals, and which they can hardly, or never, escape: so called because he prevents their escaping the pursuer like a shackle. (Msb.) [See also art. qyd .] [Hence also the saying,] Aln~iEamu A^awaAbidu faqay~iduwhaA biAl$~ukori (tropical:) [ Benefits are fugitive, or fleeting; therefore detain ye them by gratitude ]. (A trad.)

definition: a word denoting past time: (Lth, T, S, M, L, Mughnee, K:) it is a noun, (S, L, Mughnee, K,) indecl.
sourceDefinition: a word denoting past time: (Lth, T, S, M, L, Mughnee, K:) it is a noun, (S, L, Mughnee, K,) indecl., with its last letter quiescent; and properly is prefixed to a proposition; (S, L, K;) as in jiy^otuka A_i*o qaAma zaydN [ I came to thee when Zeyd stood ], and A_i*o zayodN qaAy^imN and A_i*o zayodN yquwmu [ When Zeyd was standing ]. (S, L.) The proposition to which it is prefixed is either nominal, as in [the words of the Kur viii. 26,] waA@*okuruwA A_i*o A^anotumo qaliylN [ And remember ye when ye were few ]; or verbal, having the verb in the pret. as to the letter and as to the meaning, as in [the Kur ii. 28, &c.,] waA_i*o qaAla rab~uka lilomalaAy^ikapi [ And when thy Lord said unto the angels ]; or verbal with the verb in the pret. as to the meaning but not as to the letter, as in [the Kur ii. 121,] wa A_i*o yarofaEu A_ibor`hiymu AlqawaAEida [ And when Abraham was rearing the foundations ]; all three of which kinds are comprised in the Kur where it is said, [ix. 40,] A_il~aA tanoSuruwhu faqado naSarahu A@ll~`hu A_i*o A^axorajahu A@l~a*iyna kafaruwA vaAniYa A@vonayoni A_i*o humaA fiY AlgaAri A_i*o yaquwlu liSaAHibihi laA taHzano A_in~a A@ll~`ha maEanaA [ If ye will not aid him, verily God aided him, when those who disbelieved expelled him, being the second of two, when they two were in the cave, when he was saying to his companion, Grieve not thou, for God is with us ]. (Mughnee.) But sometimes one half of the proposition is suppressed, as in A_i*o *aAka , [also written A_i*~aAka ,] meaning A_i*o *aAka ka*`lika [ When that was so ], or A_i*o *aAka kaAy^inN [ When that was, i. e. then, at that time ]. (Mughnee.) And sometimes the whole of the proposition is suppressed, (M, Mughnee,) as being known, (Mughnee,) and tenween is substituted for it; the * receiving kesreh because of the occurrence of two quiescent letters together, (M, Mughnee,) namely the * and the tenween, (M,) and thus one says, yawomay^i*K ; the kesreh of the * not being, as Akh holds it to be, the kesreh of declension, although A* here occupies the place of a noun governed in the gen. case by another prefixed to it, (M, Mughnee,) for it still requires a proposition to be understood after it, (Mughnee,) and is held to be indecl. (M, Mughnee) by general consent, like kamo and mano , (M,) as being composed of two letters. (Mughnee.) [J says,] when A_i*o is not prefixed to a proposition, it has tenween: (S:) and hence Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, (S, M,) nahayotuka Eano TilaAbika A^um~a EamorKw biEaAfiyapK waA^anota A_i*K SaHiyHu [ I forbade thy suing Umm-'Amr in health, thou being then sound ]; (S, M, L, Mughnee, TA; [but in two copies of the S, for biEaAfiyapK , I find biEaAqibapK ; and in the L it is without any point;]) in which [J says] the poet means Hiynay^i*K , like as one says yawomay^*K and layolatay^i*K : (S:) and Fr says that some of the Arabs say, kaAna ka*aA w ka*aA wahuwa A_i*K SabiY~N , meaning huwa A_i*o *aAka SabiY~N [ Such and such things were, he being then a boy ]. (T.) A_i*iY also occurs for A* [app. A_i*K , but whether this or A_i*o is not clear in the MS. from which I take this]. (M.) When A_i*K is adjoined to nouns signifying times, the Arabs join it therewith in writing, in certain instances: namely Hiynay^i*K [ At that time, or then ], and yawomay^i*K [ In, or on, or at, that day ], and layolatay^i*K [ In, or on, or at, that night ], and gadaAtay^i*K [ In, or on, that morning ], and Ea$iy~atay^i*K [ In, or on, that evening ], and saAEatay^i*K [ In that hour: or at that time; then ], and EaAmay^i*K [ In that year ], [and waqotay^i*K At that time; then ]; but they did not say AlA=nay^i*K , because AlA=na denotes the nearest present time, except in the dial. of Hudheyl, in which it has been found to occur. (T.) When it is followed by a verb, or by a noun not having the article Al prefixed to it, or [rather] by any movent letter, the * of A_i*o is quieseent; but when it is followed by a noun with Al , [or by any A@ ,] the * is mejroorah, as in the saying, A_i*i Alqawomu kaAnuwA naAziliyna bikaAZimaho [ When the people, or company of men, were alighting, or taking up their abode, at Kádhimeh ]. (T.) ― -b2- In general, (Mughnee, K,) it is an adverbial noun denoting past time, (M, Mughnee, K,) when it is a noun denoting such time, (Mughnee, K,) as in wa A_i*o qaAla rab~uka lilomalaAy^ikapi [explained above], (M,) and in faqado naSarahu A@ll~`hu A_i*o A^axorajahu A@l~a*iyna kafaruwA [also explained above, and in other instances already mentioned]: (Mughnee, K:) in the former of which instances, AO says that it is redundant; (M, Mughnee;) but Aboo-Is-hák says that this is a bold assertion of his; (M;) [and IHsh says,] this assertion is of no account, and so is that of him who says that it here denotes certainty, like qado : (Mughnee:) [J holds the opinion of AO on this point; for he says,] A_i*o is sometimes redundant, like A_i*aA , as in the saying in the Kur [ii. 48], waA_i*o waAEadonaA muwsaY , meaning wawaAEadonaA muwsaY [ And We appointed a time with Moses; but instances of this kind are most probably elliptical: see the next sentence]. (S.) As a noun denoting past time, it is [said to be] also an objective complement of a verb, as in [the Kur vii. 84,] waA@*okuruwA A_i*o kunotumo qaliylAF [ And remember ye when ye were few ]: (Mughnee, K:) and generally in the commencements of narratives in the Kur, it may be an objective complement of A^u*okuro understood, as in wa A_i*o qaAla rab~uka lilomalaAy^ikapi [before cited], and the like. (Mughnee: but see the third of the sentences here following.) As such, it is [said to be] also a substitute for the objective complement of a verb, as in [the Kur xix. 16,] wa A@*okuro fiY A@lokitaAbi maroyama A_i*i A@notaba*ato [ And mention thou, or remember thou, in the Scripture, Mary, the time when she withdrew aside ], where A* is a substitute of implication for mrym . (Mughnee, K: but see the second of the sentences here following.) As such, it also has prefixed to it a noun of time, of such a kind that it is without need thereof, as in yawomay^i*K , or not of such a kind that it is without need thereof, as in [the Kur iii. 6,] baEoda A_i*o hadayotanaA [ After the time when Thou hast directed us aright ]. (Mughnee, K.) And it is generally asserted, that it never occurs otherwise than as an adverbial noun, or as having a noun prefixed to it; that in the like of waA@*okuruwA A_i*o kunotumo qaliylAF , it is an adverbial noun relating to an objective complement suppressed, i. e. wa A@*okuruwA niEomapa A@ll~`hi Ealayokumo A_i*o kunotumo qaliylAF [ And remember ye the grace of God towards you when ye were few ]; and in the like of A_i*i A@notaba*ato , that it is an adverbial noun relating to a suppressed prefixed noun to [that which becomes by the suppression] the objective complement of a verb, i. e. [in this instance] wa A@*okuro qiS~apa maroyama [ And mention thou, or remember thou, the case of Mary ]: and this assertion is strengthened by the express mention of the [proper] objective complement in [the Kur iii. 98,] wa A@*okurwA niEomapa A@ll~`hi Ealayokumo A_i*o kunotumo A^aEodaA='F [ And remember ye the grace of God towards you when ye were enemies ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- Also, (Mughnee, K,) accord. to some, (T, Mughnee,) it is used (T, Mughnee, K) as a noun (Mughnee, K) to indicate future time, (T, Mughnee, K,) and A_i*aA is said to denote past time, (T,) [i. e.] each of these occurs in the place of the other; (TA;) the former being used to indicate future time in the Kur [xxxiv. 50], where it is said, walawo taraY A_i*o faziEuwA [ And couldst thou see the time when they shall be terrified ], meaning the day of resurrection; this usage being allowable, says Fr, only because the proposition is like one expressing a positive fact, since there is no doubt of the coming of that day; (T;) and in [the Kur xcix. 4,] yawomay^i*K tuHad~ivu A^axobaArahaA [ On that day, she (the earth) shall tell her tidings ]; (Mughnee, K;) this being generally regarded as similar to the expression of a future event which must necessarily happen as though it had already happened; but it may be urged in favour of those who hold a different opinion that it is said in the Kur [xl. 72 and 73], fasawofa yaEolamuwna A_i*i AlA^aglaAlu fiY A^aEonaAqihimo [ They shall hereafter know, when the collars shall be on their necks ]; for yElmwn is a future as to the letter and the meaning because of its having swf conjoined with it, and it governs A* , which is therefore in the place of A_i*aA . (Mughnee.) ― -b4- It also indicates a cause, as in [the Kur xliii. 38,] lano yanofaEakumu A@loyawoma A_i*o Zalamotumo [ It will not profit you this day, since, or because, ye have acted wrongfully ], (Mughnee, K,) i. e. because of your having acted wrongfully in the sublunary state of existence; (Bd, Mughnee;) but it is disputed whether it be in this instance a particle in the place of the causative l , or an adverbial noun: (Mughnee:) Aboo-'Alee seems to hold that A* Zlmtm [as meaning when ye have acted wrongfully ] is a substitute for, or a kind of repetition of, Alywm ; an event happening in the present world being spoken of as though it happened in the world to come because the latter immediately follows the former. (IJ, M, L, Mughnee.) You say also, AlHamodu lil~`hi A_i*o jiy^ota [ Praise be to God because, or that, thou camest, or hast come ]. But sometimes one half of the proposition is suppressed, as in A_i*o *aAka , [also written A_i*~aAka ,] meaning A_i*o *aAka ka*`lika [ When that was so ], or A_i*o *aAka kaAy^inN [ When that was, i. e. then, at that time ]. (Mughnee.) And sometimes the whole of the proposition is suppressed, (M, Mughnee,) as being known, (Mughnee,) and tenween is substituted for it; the * receiving kesreh because of the occurrence of two quiescent letters together, (M, Mughnee,) namely the * and the tenween, (M,) and thus one says, yawomay^i*K ; the kesreh of the * not being, as Akh holds it to be, the kesreh of declension, although A* here occupies the place of a noun governed in the gen. case by another prefixed to it, (M, Mughnee,) for it still requires a proposition to be understood after it, (Mughnee,) and is held to be indecl. (M, Mughnee) by general consent, like kamo and mano , (M,) as being composed of two letters. (Mughnee.) [J says,] when A_i*o is not prefixed to a proposition, it has tenween: (S:) and hence Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, (S, M,) nahayotuka Eano TilaAbika A^um~a EamorKw biEaAfiyapK waA^anota A_i*K SaHiyHu [ I forbade thy suing Umm-'Amr in health, thou being then sound ]; (S, M, L, Mughnee, TA; [but in two copies of the S, for biEaAfiyapK , I find biEaAqibapK ; and in the L it is without any point;]) in which [J says] the poet means Hiynay^i*K , like as one says yawomay^*K and layolatay^i*K : (S:) and Fr says that some of the Arabs say, kaAna ka*aA w ka*aA wahuwa A_i*K SabiY~N , meaning huwa A_i*o *aAka SabiY~N [ Such and such things were, he being then a boy ]. definition: i. q. qidamN [i. e. Eternity, with respect to past time, or considered retrospectively; existence from eternity; or ancientness ] (S, K, TA) that is without beginning; (TA;) or the continuance of...
sourceDefinition: i. q. qidamN [i. e. Eternity, with respect to past time, or considered retrospectively; existence from eternity; or ancientness ] (S, K, TA) that is without beginning; (TA;) or the continuance of existence in decreed times interminable in respect of the past; like as A^abadN is the continuance of existence in decreed times interminable in respect of the future; (KT;) or that [ existence, or time, ] which has no extremity in its beginning; like qidamN ; and A^abadN is that which has no extremity in its latter part; like baqaA='N : the former is existence without any beginning: (Kull p. 31:) said to be from the phrase lamo yazalo [“he, or it, has not ceased” to be &c.; i. e. “has ever” been &c. (see A^azaliY~N )]: or, accord. to some, from A^azolN signifying “narrowness;” because the intellect is prevented by its narrowness from perceiving its beginning: (MF:) Azl is a name for that of which the mind is prevented by its narrowness from determining the limit of the beginning; from A^azolN meaning “narrowness;”; and Abd is a name for that of which the mind shrinks from, or shuns, the determining the limit of the end; from A^ubuwdN meaning the act of “shrinking” from a thing, or “shunning” it. (Kull pp. 30 and 31.) Hence the saying, kaAna fiY AlA^azali qaAdirFA EaAlimFA [ He was, or has been, ever, powerful, knowing ]. (A, TA.) The phrase A^azala AlA=zaAli [ During the space, without beginning, of all past times; or ever, in all past times; ] is like the phrase A^abada AlA=baAdi ; said to be no evidence of the use of A=zaAlN as a pl. of A^azalN in a general way by the Arabs of the classical ages, as it is here added merely as a corroborative. (MF in art. Abd .) [See also A^azaliY~N .]

The phrase A^azala AlA=zaAli [ During the space, without beginning, of all past times; or ever, in all past times; ] is like the phrase A^abada AlA=baAdi ; said to be no evidence of the use of A=zaAlN as a pl. of A^azalN in a general way by the Arabs of the classical ages, as it is here added merely as a corroborative. (MF in art. Abd .) [See also A^azaliY~N .]

definition: [ Eternal, with respect to past time;
sourceDefinition: [ Eternal, with respect to past time; existing from eternity; or ancient without beginning; as is implied in the S and K &c.;] a thing, or being, which has not been preceded by non-existence: it is applied to God: and to [his] knowledge: that which exists must be one of three kinds only: A^azaliY~N A^abadiY~N [ existing from eternity, and consequently existing to eternity ]; and this is God [who is also called Alqadiymu AlA^azaliY~u the Ancient without beginning ]: and laA A^azaliY~N wa laA A^abadiY~N [ not existing from eternity nor existing to eternity ]; and such is the present world: and A^abadiY~N gayoru A^azaliY~ [ existing to eternity without existing from eternity ]; and such is the world to come; the reverse of which [last] is impossible: (TA:) it is a rel. n. from A^azalN : or, accord. to some, it is not [genuine] Arabic: (TA:) or it is originally yazaliY~N , a rel. n. from lamo yazalo , (S, K,) a phrase applied to that which is qadiym ; and is formed by contraction; (S;) then, the Y is changed into A , as being easier of pronunciation; as in A^azaniY~N , applied to a spear, in relation to *uw yazan ; (S, K,* Sgh, TA;) and as in A^avorabiY~N , applied to a blade, (S, Sgh, TA,) in relation to yavorib : (TA:) so say some of the learned. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. A^afokN , (with fet-h, S, TA, its only form, TA, [in the CK Aifok ,]) He changed his, or its, manner of being, or state; (S, K;) and he turned him, or it, (i. e., anything, Msb,) away, or back; (S, Msb, K;) Eani Al$~aYo'i [ from the thing ]; (S;) or Eano wajohihi [ from his, or its, mode, or manner, of being, &c.]: (Msb:) so in the Kur xlvi. 21, A^ajiy^otanaA litaA^ofikanaA Eano A=lihatinaA Hast thou come to us to turn us away, or back, from our gods? (Bd:) or he turned him away, or back, by lying: (TA:) or he changed, or perverted, his judgment, or opinion: (K:) or he deceived him, or beguiled him, and so turned him away, or back: and simply he deceived him, or beguiled him: and A^ufika signifies he was turned from his judgment, or opinion, by deceit, or guile. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [li. 9], yuw^ofaku Eanohu mano A^ufika , i. e., He will be turned away from it (namely, the truth,) who is turned away in the foreknowledge of God: (TA:) or, accord. to Mujáhid, yuw^ofanu Eanohu mano A^ufina [ he will be weak in intellect and judgment so as to be thereby turned away from it who is weak in intellect and judgment ]. (S, TA.) You say also, A^ufika Alr~ajulu Eani Alxayori The man was turned away, or back, from good, or prosperity. (Sh.) And A^afakahu , (K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He forbade him what he wished, (K, TA,) and turned him away, or back, from it. (TA.) ― -b2- A^afaka , aor. ; (Msb, K;) and A^afika , aor. ; (IAar, K;) inf. n. A_ifokN (Msb, K) and A^afokN and A^afakN and A^ufuwkN ; (K;) He lied; uttered a falsehood; said what was untrue; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ A^f~k , (K,) inf. n. taA^ofiykN : (TA:) because a lie is a saying that is turned from its proper way, or mode. (Bd in xxiv. 11.) ― -b3- A^afaka Aln~aAsa , aor. , inf. n. A^afokN , He told the people what was false; A^afaka and A^afakotuhu being like ka*aba and ka*abotuhu . (Az, TA.) ― -b4- A^afaka fulaAnFA , (K,) inf. n. A^afokN ; (TA;) or the verb is ↓ A=faka ; (so in the printed edition of Bd, xlvi. 27;) He, or it, made such a one to lie, or say what was untrue. (K.) ― -b5- A^ufika He was weak [ as though perverted ] in his intellect and judgment or opinion. (K,* TA.) But A^afakahu A@ll~`hu as meaning God rendered weak his intellect is not used. (L, TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) It (a place) was not rained upon, and had no vegetation, or herbage. (K, TA.)

definition: Female; feminine; of the female, or feminine, sex, or gender; contr. of *akarN : (T, S, M:) an epithet applied to anything of that sex or gender: (T:) IAar asserts, that a woman is termed Anvy from...
sourceDefinition: Female; feminine; of the female, or feminine, sex, or gender; contr. of *akarN : (T, S, M:) an epithet applied to anything of that sex or gender: (T:) IAar asserts, that a woman is termed Anvy from the phrase baladN A^aniyvN , q. v, because of her softness; she being more soft than a man: (M, L:) [but see the observation at the end of the first paragraph of this art.:] the pl. is A_inaAvN ; (T, S, M, A, Msb, K;) and sometimes one says A^unuvN , as though it were pl. of A_inaAvN ; (S;) or it is [truly] pl. of A_inaAvN , like as numurN is of nimaArN ; (T;) and A^anaAvaY , (T, A, Msb, K,) which last occurs in poetry. (T.) You say, h`*aA TaAy^irN wa A^unovaAhu [ This is a ( male ) bird and his female ]: not A^unovaAtuhu . (ISk, T.) In the Kur iv. 117, I'Ab reads A^uvunFA [in the place of A^unuvFA or A_inaAvFA ]; and Fr says that it is pl. of wavanN , the w in wuvunN being changed into A^ as in A^uq~itatN [for wuq~itatN ]. (T, L.) ― -b2- AimoraA^apN A^anovaY (tropical:) [ A feminine woman, ] means a perfect woman; (T, A, K;) a woman being thus termed in praise; like as a man is termed rajulN *akarN . (T, A.) ― -b3- [The pl.]

definition: a vocative particle, (S, M, Mughnee, K,) addressed to the near, (S, K,) not to the distant: (S:) or to the near, or the distant, or the intermediate;
sourceDefinition: a vocative particle, (S, M, Mughnee, K,) addressed to the near, (S, K,) not to the distant: (S:) or to the near, or the distant, or the intermediate; accord. to different authorities. (Mughnee.) You say, A^aYo zayodu A^aqobilo [ O Zeyd, advance: or, if it may be used in addressing one who is distant, ho there, soho, or holla: and if used in addressing one who is between near and distant, ho, or what ho ]: (S:) and A^aYo rab~i [ O my Lord ]; occurring in a trad.: and sometimes it is pronounced ↓ A=Yo . (Mughnee.) -A2- Also an explicative particle. (S, M, Mughnee, K.) You say, A^aYo ka*aA in the sense of yuriydu ka*aA [ He means such a thing, or yaEoniY ka*aA , which has the same signification; or A^uriydu , or A^aEoniY , I mean; or the like; for all of which, we may say, meaning; or that is ]; (S;) as in EinodiY EasojidN A^aYo *ahabN [ I have Easojad , that is, (I have) *ahaba , or gold ]. (Mughnee.) What follows it is an adjunct explicative of what precedes it, or a substitute. (Mughnee.) AA says that he asked Mbr respecting what follows it, and he answered that it may be a substitute for what precedes, and may be a word independent of what precedes it, and may be a noun in the accus. case: and that he asked Th, and he answered that it may be an explicative, or a word independent of what precedes it, or a noun governed in the accus. case by a verb suppressed: you say, jaA='aniY A^axuwka A^aYo zayodN [ Thy brother came to me; that is, Zeyd ]; and you may say, A^aYo zayodFA [ I mean Zeyd ]: and raA^ayotu A^axaAka A^aYo zayodFA [ I saw thy brother; I mean, or that is, Zeyd ]; and you may say, A^aYo zayodN [ that is, Zeyd ]: and mararotu biA^axiyka A^aYo zayodK [ I passed by thy brother; that is, by Zeyd ]; and you may say, A^aYo zaydFA [ I mean, Zeyd ]; and A^aYo zayodN [ that is, Zeyd ]. (T, TA.) When it occurs after taquwlu , in a case like the following, [i. e., when a verb following it explains a verb preceding it,] one says, taquwlu Aisotakotamotuhu AlHadiyva A^aYo saA^alotuhu kitomaAnahu [ Thou sayest, Astktmth AlHdyv , meaning sA^lth ktmAnh I asked of him the concealment of it, namely, the discourse, or story; and so when taquwlu is understood, as is often, or generally, the case in lexicons]; with damm to the t : but if you put A_i*aA in the place of A^aYo , you say, A_i*aA saA^alotahu , with fet-h, because A^a*A is an adverbial noun relating to taquwlu . (Mughnee.) -A3- See also A^aY~N , near the beginning of the paragraph, in three places.

definition: is a particle denoting a reply, meaning naEamo [ Yes, or yea ];
sourceDefinition: is a particle denoting a reply, meaning naEamo [ Yes, or yea ]; importing acknowledgment of the truth of an enunciation; and the making a thing known, to him who asks information; and a promise, to him who seeks or demands; therefore it occurs after such sayings as “Zeyd stood” and “Did Zeyd stand.?” and “Beat thou Zeyd,” and the like; as does naEamo : Ibn-El-Hájib asserts that it occurs only after an interrogation; as in the saying [in the Kur x. 54], wayasotanobiw^unaka A^aHaq~N huwa qulN A_i Yo warabiY~ [ And they will ask thee to inform them, saying, Is it true? Say, Yea, by my Lord! ]: but accord. to all, it does not occur otherwise than before an oath: and when one says, A_i Yo waA@ll~`hi [ Yea, by God! ], and then drops the w the Y may be quiescent, and with fet-h, and elided; [so that you say, A_i Yo A@ll~`hi , and A_i Ya A@ll~`hi , and A_i A@ll~`hi ;] in the first of which cases, two quiescent letters occur together, irregularly. (Mughnee.) Lth says, A_i Yo is an oath, as in A_ iYo warab~iY meaning, says Zj, naEamo warab~iY : IAar is also related to have said the like; and this is the correct explanation. (T.) [J says,] It is a word preceding an oath, meaning balaY [q. v.]; as in A_i Yo warab~iY and A_i Yo waA@ll~`h . (S.) [ISd and F say,] It is syn. with naEamo , and is conjoined with an oath: and one says also hiYo . (M, K.)

definition: is a noun, used in five different manners.
sourceDefinition: is a noun, used in five different manners. (Mughnee.) One of its meanings is that of an interrogative, (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) relating to intellectual beings and to non-intellectual things; [meaning Who? which? and what? ] (S, M, K;) and as such, it is a decl. noun: (S:) it is said in the K to be a particle; (MF;) and so in the M; (TA;) but this is wrong: (MF:) and it is added in the K that it is indecl.; (MF;) and it is said to be so in the M, accord. to Sb, in an instance to be explained below; (TA;) but this is only when it is a conjunct noun [like Al~a*iY ], or denotes the object of a vocative: (MF:) or, accord. to some, it is decl. as a conjunct noun also. (Mughnee.) You say, A^ay~uhumo A^axuwka [ Who, or which, of them, is thy brother? ]. (S.) Another ex. is the saying [in the Kur vii. 184, and last verse of lxxvii.], fabiA^aY~i HadiyvK baEodahu yuw^ominuwna [ And in what announcement, after it, will they believe? ]. (Mughnee.) Sometimes it is without teshdeed; as in the saying (of El-Farezdak, M), ↓ tanaZ~arotu naSorFA waAls~imaAkayoni A^ayohumaA EalaY~a mina Algayovi A@sotahal~ato mawaATiruho [ I looked for rain, or aid from the clouds, and the two Simáks (stars so called). Of which of them two did the rains pour vehemently upon me from the clouds? ]: (M, Mughnee, K: * [in the last of which, only the former hemistich is given, with nasorFA (meaning the star or asterism so called) instead of naSorFA :]) so by poetic licence: (M:) IJ says that for this reason the poet has elided the second Y , but should have restored the first Y to w , because it is originally w . (TA. [But this assertion, respecting the first Y , I regard as improbable.]) ↓ A^ayoma , also, is a contraction of A^aY~u maA , meaning A^aY~u $aYo'K : so in the saying, A^ayoma huwa yaA fulaAnu [ What thing is it, O such a one? ]: and A^ayoma taquwlu [ What thing sayest thou? ]. (TA in art. Aym .) In like manner, also, ↓ A^ayo$a is used as a contraction of A^aY~u $aYo'K . (Ks, TA in art. jrm .) A poet speaks of his companions as being biA^aYa waA^ayonamaA ; making A^aY~ the name of the quarter ( jihap ); so that, being determinate and of the feminine gender, it is imperfectly declinable. (M. [See A^aynN ; under which head two other readings are given; and where it is said that the verse in which this occurs is by Homeyd Ibn-Thowr.]) A^aY~ is never without a noun or pronoun to which it is prefixed, except in a vocative expression and when it is made to conform with a word to which it refers, as in cases to be exemplified hereafter. (Mughnee.) Being so prefixed, it is determinate; but sometimes, [as in the latter of the cases just mentioned,] it is not so prefixed, yet has the meaning of a prefixed noun. (S.) When used as an interrogative, it is not governed, as to the letter, though it is as to the meaning, by the verb that precedes it, but by what follows it; as in the saying in the Kur [xviii. 11], linaEolama A^aY~u AlHizobayoni A^aHoSaY [ That we might know which of the two parties was able to compute ]; and in the same [xxvi. last verse], wasayaEolamu A@l~a*ayna ZalamuwA A^aYa munoqalabK yanoqalibuwna [ And they who have acted wrongly shall know with what a translating they shall be translated ]: (Fr, * Th, Mbr, T, S: *) when it is governed by the verb before it, it has not the interrogative meaning, as will be shown hereafter. (Fr, T.) In the saying of the poet, taSiyHu binaA Haniyfapu A_*o raA^atonaA waA^aY~a AlA^aroDi ta*ohabu lilS~iyaAHi [ Haneefeh (the tribe so named) shout to us when they see us. And to what place of the earth, or land, will they go for the shouting? ], A^aY~ is in the accus. case because the prep. A_ilaY is suppressed before it. (S.) When they separate it [from what follows it, not prefixing it to another noun], the Arabs say A^aYN , and in the dual A^ay~aAni , and in the pl. A^ay~uwna ; and they make it fem., saying A^ay~apN , and [in the dual] A^ay~ataAni , and [in the pl.] A^ay~aAtN : but when they prefix it to a noun, properly so called, not a pronoun, they make it sing. and masc., saying A^aYu Alr~ajulayoni [ Who, or which, of the two men? ], and A^aYu AlmaroA^atayoni [ Who, or which, of the two women? ], and A^aY~u Al~rijaAli [ Who, or which, of the men? ], and A^aY~u Aln~isaA='i [ Who, or which, of the women? ]: and when they prefix it to a fem. pronoun, they make it masc. [as when they prefix it to a masc. pronoun] and fem., saying A^ay~uhumaA and A^ay~atuhumaA [ Who, or which, of them two? ], meaning women; (Fr, T;) [the latter of which seems to be the more common; for ISd says,] sometimes they said A^ay~uhun~a [ Who, or which, of them? referring to women], meaning A^ay~atuhun~a . (M.) It is said in the Kur [xxxi. last verse], wamaA tadoriY nafosN biA^aY~i A^arDK tamuwtu [ And a person knoweth not in what land he will die ]: (S:) but some read biA^ay~api A^aroDK ; and Sb compares this fem. form to kul~atuhun~a . (Bd.) When it is used as an interrogative relating to an indeterminate noun in a preceding phrase, A^aY~ is made to conform with that indeterminate noun in case-ending and in gender and in number; and this is done [alike, accord. to some,] in the case of its connexion with a following word and in the case of a pause; so that, [in the case of a pause,] to him who says, jaA='aniY rajulN [A man came to me], you say, [accord. to the authorities alluded to above,] A^aY~N [ Who? ]; and to him who says, raA^ayotu rajulFA [I saw a man], A^ay~aA [ Whom? ]; and to him who says, mararotu birajlK [I passed by a man], A^aY~K [ Whom? ]: and in like manner, [accord. to all authorities,] in the case of its connexion with a following word; as A^aY~u yaA fataY [ Who, O young man? ], and A^ay~aA yaA fataY [ Whom, O young man? ], and A^aYK yaA fataY [ Whom, O young man? ]: and in the case of the fem. you say, A^ay~apN and A^ay~apF and A^ay~apK [in the nom. and accus. and gen. respectively]; and in the dual, A^ay~aAni and A^ay~ataAni in the nom. case [masc. and fem. respectively], and A^ay~ayoni and A^ay~atayoni in the accus. and gen. cases [masc. and fem. respectively]; and in the pl., [with the like distinction of genders,] A^ay~uwna and A^ay~aAtN in the nom. case, and A^ay~iyna and A^ay~aAtK in the accus. and gen. cases. (I' Ak p. 319.) [Exs. in cases of pause, agreeing with the foregoing rules, are given in the T; and exs. in cases of connexion with following words, agreeing with the foregoing, are given in the Mughnee: but J gives rules differing from the foregoing in some respects; and IB gives rules differing in some points both from the foregoing and from those of J.] It is said in the S, A^aY~ is made to conform with indeterminate nouns significant of intellectual beings and of nonintellectual things, and is used as an interrogative; and when it is thus used in reference to an indeterminate noun, you make it to have a caseending like that of the noun respecting which it demands positive information; so that when it is said to you, mar~abiY rajulN [A man passed by me], you say, A^aY~N yaA fataY [ Who, O young man? ], thus giving it a case-ending [like that of rajulN ] when it is in connexion with a following word; and you indicate the case-ending [by the pronunciation termed Alr~awomu , saying A^aY~u , with a somewhat obscure utterance of the final vowel,] in pausing; and if one says, raA^ayotu rajulFA [I saw a man], you say, A^ay~aA yaAfataY [ Whom, O young man? ], giving it a case-ending [like that of rajulFA ], with tenween, when it is [thus] in connexion with a following word; and you pause upon the A , saying A^ay~aA ; and when one says, mararotu birajulK [I passed by a man], you say, A^aY~K yaAfataY [ Whom, O young man? in a case of connexion with a following word; and A^aY~i in a case of pausing]: you conform with what the other has said, in the nom. and accus. and gen. cases, in the case of connexion with a following word and in that of pausing: but IB says that this is correct only in the case of connexion with a following word; for in the case of a pause, you say only A^aY~o , in the nom. and gen., with sukoon; and you imitate in both of these cases only when you use the dual form or the pl.: it is added in the S, you say in the cases of the dual and pl. and fem. like as we have said respecting mano : when one says, jaA='aniY rijaAlN [Men came to me], you say, A^ay~uwno [ Who? ], with the n quiescent; and A^ayiyno in the accus. and gen.: but IB says, the correct mode is to say, A^ay~uwna and A^ay~ina , with fet-h to the n in both; [meaning that this is the only allowable mode in the case of connexion with a following word, and app. that it is the preferable mode in the case of a pause;] the quiescent n being allowable only in the case of a pause, and with respect to mano , for you say manuwno and maniyno with the quiescent n only: it is then added in the S, you say, also, A^ay~aho [ Who? and whom? ] in using the fem. [in a case of pause]; but in a case of connexion with a following word, [when referring to a noun in the accus.,] you say, A^ay~apF yaA h`*aA [ Whom, O thou? in the sing.], and A^ay~aAtK [in the pl.; and in like manner, A^ay~apN in the nom. sing., and A^ay~apK in the gen. sing.; and A^ay~aAtN in the nom. pl., and A^ay~aAtK in the gen. pl.]: but when the interrogation refers to a determinate noun, A^aY~ is in the nom. case (with refa) only. (TA.) [See also A^ay~aAna , below.] ― -b2- [In other cases, now to be mentioned, it is used alike as sing., dual, and pl.] ― -b3- It also denotes a condition; (T, S, M, Mughnee;) in which case, also, it is a decl. noun, applied to an intellectual being and to a non-intellectual thing. (S.) So in the saying, A^ay~uhumo yukorimoniY A^ukorimohu [ Whichever of them treats me with honour, I will treat him with honour ]. (S.) So, too, in the saying [in the Kur xvii. 110], A^ay~FA maA tadoEuwA falahu AlA^asomaA='u AlHusonaY [ Whichever ye call Him, He hath the best names ]. (T, * Mughnee.) And in the saying [in the same, xxviii. 28], A^ay~amaA A@loA^ajalayoni qaDayotu falaA EudowaAna EalaY~a [ Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there shall be no wrongdoing to me ]. (Mughnee.) One says also, SaHibahu A@ll~`hu A^ay~aA maA tawaj~aha , meaning A^ayonamaAtawaj~aha [ May God accompany him wherever he goeth ]. (AZ, T.) And Zuheyr uses the expression A^ay~apF salakuwA for A^ay~apa wijohapK salakuwA [ Whatever tract they travelled, or travel ]. (T.) The saying, A^ay~iY waA^ay~uka kaAna $ar~aA faA^axozaAhu A@ll~`hu [ Whichever of me and thee be evil, may God abase him ! ] was explained by Kh to Sb as meaning A^ay~unaA kaAna $ar~FA [ whichever of us two be evil ]; and as being like the saying, A^axozaY A@ll~`hu AlkaA*iba miniY~ waminoka , meaning min~aA . (M. [And in a similar manner, the former clause of that saying, occurring in a verse, with maA after A^ay~iY , is said in the T to have been explained by Kh to Sb.]) ― -b4- It is also a conjunct noun; (Mughnee;) [i. e.] it is sometimes used in the manner of Al~a*iY , and therefore requires a complement; as in the saying, A^ay~uhumo fiY Ald~aAri A^axuwka [ He, of them, who is in the house is thy brother ]: (S:) [i. e.] it is syn. with Al~a*iY . (M, Mughnee.) So in the saying [in the Kur xix. 70], vum~a lananoziEan~a mino kul~i $iyEapK A^ay~uhumo A^a$ad~u EalaY Alr~aHom`ni Eutiy~aA [ Then we will assuredly draw forth, from every sect, him, of them, who is most exorbitantly rebellious against the Compassionate ]: so says Sb: but the Koofees and a number of the Basrees disagree with him, holding that the conjunct noun A^aY~ is always decl., like the conditional and the interrogative: Zj says, “It has not appeared to me that Sb has erred except in two instances, whereof this is one; for he has conceded that it is decl. when separate, and how can he say that it is indecl. when it is a prefixed noun?” and El-Jarmee says, “I have gone forth from El-Basrah, and have not heard, from my leaving the Khandak to Mekkeh, any one say, laA^aDoriban~a A^ay~uhumo qaAy^imN [as meaning I will assuredly beat him, of them, who is standing ], with damm:” these assert, that it is, in the verse above, an interrogative, and that it is an inchoative, and A$d is an enunciative: but they differ as to the objective complement of the verb: Kh says that this is suppressed, and that the implied meaning is, we will assuredly draw forth those of whom it will be said, Which of them is most &c.? and Yoo says that it is the proposition [ Ayh~m &c.], and that the verb is suspended from governing, as in the instance in the Kur xviii. 11, cited above: and Ks and Akh say that it is kl~ $yEp , that mn is redundant, and that the interrogative proposition is independent of what precedes it; this being grounded on their saying that the redundance of mino is allowable in an affirmative proposition: but these [following] facts refute their sayings; viz. that the suspension of government is peculiar to verbs significant of operations of the mind; and that it is not allowable to say, laA^aDoriban~a AlfaAsiqu , with refa, as meaning by implication “I will assuredly beat him of whom it is said, He is the transgressor;” and that the redundance of mino in an affirmative proposition is not correct. (Mughnee. [Some further remarks on the same subject, in that work, mentioning other opinions as erroneous, I omit. Another reading of the passage in the Kur cited above (xix. 70) will be found in what here follows.]) [ISd states that] they said, laA^aDorban~a A^ay~uhumo A^afoDalu [ I will assuredly beat him, of them, who is most excellent ], and A^aY~N A^afoDalu [ him who is most excel-lent ]; AY~ being indecl., accord. to Sb, and therefore the verb does not govern it [save as to the meaning]. (M.) And [that] you say, AiDoribo A^ay~uhumo A^afoDalu [ Beat thou him, of them, who is most excellent ], and A^ay~ahumo A^afoDalu [meaning the same, or whichever of them, &c.]; suppressing the relative huwa after Ay~hm . (M in a later part of the same art.) Fr says that when A^aY~ is governed by the verb before it, it has not the interrogative meaning; and you may say, laA^aDoriban~a A^ay~ahumo yaquwlu *`lika [ I will assuredly beat him, of them, or whichever of them, says that ]: and he says that he who reads A^ay~ahumo , in the accus. case, in the passage of the Kur cited above (xix. 70) makes it to be governed by lananoriEan~a . (T.) Ks says, you say, laA^aDoriban~a A^ay~ahumo fiY Ald~aAri [ I will assuredly beat him, of them, or whichever of them, is in the house ]; but you may not say, Darabotu A^ay~ahumo fiY Ald~aAri : thus he distinguishes between the actual occurrence and that which is expected. (S.) Akh says, also, that it may be indeterminate and qualified by an epithet; as when one says, mararotu biA^aY~K muEojibK laka , like as one says, bimano muEojibK laka [ I passed by one pleasing to thee ]: but this has not been heard [from the Arabs]. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- It also denotes perfection, or consummateness: and in this case it is an epithet applying to an indeterminate noun; as in zayodN rajulN A^aY~u rajulK (tropical:) [ Zeyd is a man; what a man! ], meaning that he is complete, or consummate, in the qualities of men: and it is a denotative of state relating to a determinate noun; as in mararotu biEabodi A@ll~`hi A^aY~a rajulK (tropical:) [ I passed by 'Abd-Allah; what a man was he! ]: (Mughnee:) and used in this sense, it is tropical. (Har p. 534.) [J says,] it is sometimes an epithet applying to an indeterminate noun: you say, mararotu birajulK A^aY~i rajulK and A^ay~imaArajulK (assumed tropical:) [ I passed by a man; what a man! ]; and mararotu biA@moraA^apK A^ay~api A@moraA^apK (assumed tropical:) [ I passed by a woman; what a woman! ], and biA@moraA^atayoni A^ay~atimaA A@moraA^atayoni [ by two women; what two women! ]; and h`*ihi A@moraA^apN A^ay~apu A@moraA^apK (assumed tropical:) [ This is a woman; what a woman! ]: and A^ay~atumaA A@moraA^a A^ay~apu A@moraA^apK (assumed tropical:) [ What two women! ]; mA being redundant: and in the case of a determinate noun, you say, h`*aA zayodN A^ay~amaA rajulK (assumed tropical:) [ This is Zeyd; what a man is he! ]; putting it in the accus. case as a denotative of state; and h`*ihi A^amapu A@ll~`hi A^ay~atamaA jaAriy~pK (assumed tropical:) [ This is the handmaid of God; what a girl, or young woman, is she! ]: you say, also, [in using an indeterminate noun,] A^aY~u A@moraA^apK jaA='atoka and jaA='aka , and A^ay~apu A@moraA^apK jaA='atoka (assumed tropical:) [ What a woman came to thee! ]; and mararotu bijaAriyapK A^aY~i jaAriyapK (assumed tropical:) [ I passed by a girl, or young woman; what a girl, or young woman! ]; and jiy^otuka bimulaA='apK A^aY~i mulaA='apK and A^ay~api mulaA='ipK (assumed tropical:) [ I brought thee a body-wrapper; what a body-wrapper! ]: all are allowable. (S.) [In all these it evidently denotes admiration, or wonder, at some good or extraordinary quality in the person or thing to which it relates; notwithstanding that J says afterwards,] and sometimes it is used to denote wonder; as in the saying of Jemeel, buvayona A@lozamiY laA A_an~a laA A_ino lazimotihi EalaY kavorapi AlwaA$iyna A^aY~u maEuwni (assumed tropical:) [ O Butheyneh, ( buvayona being a curtailed form of buvayonap , a woman's name,) adhere thou to “No:” verily “No,” if thou adhere to it, notwithstanding the numbers of the slanderers, what a help will it be!]: (S:) i. e., an excellent help will be thy saying “No” in repelling, or rebutting, the slanderers, though they be many. (TA in art. Ewn .) Fr gives as exs. of its use to denote wonder the sayings, A^aY~u rajulK zayodN [ What a man is Zeyd! ], and A^aY~u jaAriyahK zayonabu [ What a girl, or young woman, is Zeyneb! ]. (T.) It denotes wonder at the sufficiency, and great degree of competence, of the person [or thing] to whom [or to which] it relates. (M.) El-Kattál El-Kilábee says, walam~aA raA^ayotu A^an~aniY qado qatalotuhu nadimotu Ealayohi A^aY~a saAEapi manodami [ And when I saw that I had slain him, I repented of it; in what an hour, or time, of repentance! ]: i. e., when I slew him, I repented of it, in a time when repentance did not profit: AY~ being here in the accus. case as an adv. n.; for, as it denotes the part of a whole, its predicament is made to be the same as that of the affixed noun, of whatever kind this may be. (Ham p. 95.) ― -b6- It also has k prefixed to it; and thus it becomes changed in signification so as to denote numerousness, being syn. with the enunciative kamo [ How many! ]; (S, K;) or syn. with rub~a [as meaning many ]: (Sb, M:) [and sometimes it is syn. with the interrogative kamo , meaning how many? or how much? as will be shown below:] thus it is written kaA^aY~K , (M,) or kaA^ay~ino , (S, M, K,) its tenween being written n ; (S, K;) and kaA='K , (M,) or [more commonly] kaAy^ino , (S, M, K, [in some copies of the S and K kaAyino ,]) like kaAEino , (S,) said by IJ, on the authority of Aboo-'Alee, to be formed from kaA^ay~ino , by putting the double Y before the ' , after the manner of the transposition in qisiY~N and a number of other words, so that it becomes kay~aA^K [or kay~ay^ino ], then suppressing the second Y , as is done in may~itN and hay~inN and lay~inN , so that it becomes kaYo'K [or kaYo'ino ], and then changing the [remaining] Y into A , as in [ Tayoy^iY~N , which becomes] TaAdiY~N , and in [ HiyriY~N , which becomes] HaAriY~N , so that it becomes kaA='K [or kaAy^ino ]; (M;) and it has other dial. vars.; namely kayoy^inN [one of the intermediate forms between kaA^ay~ino and kaAy^ino mentioned above]; (K; [in one copy of the K written kayay~ino , and so accord. to the TK;]) and kaA^oYK , (M, K,) of the measure of ramoYK , and most probably formed by transposition from kaYo'K , mentioned above; (M;) and kaA^ , of the measure of EamK , (M, TA,) incorrectly written in the copies of the K kaA'K , i. e. like kaAEK , (TA,) formed by the suppression of Y in kaYo'K ; a change not greater than that from A^ayomunu A@ll~`hi to mu A@ll~`hi and mi A@ll~`hi . (M.) You say, kaA^ay~ino rajulFA laqiytu [ How many a man have I met! or many a man &c.], (S, K, *) putting the noun following kA^y~n in the accus. case as a specificative; (S;) and kaA^ay~ino mino rajulK laqiytu ; (S, K; *) and the introduction of mino after kaA^y~n is more common, and better. (S. [And Sb, as cited in the M, says the like.]) You say also, kaA^ay~ino qado A^ataAniY rajulFA [ How many a man has come to me! or many a man &c.]. (Sb, M.) And bikaA^ay~ino tabiyEu h`*aA Alv~awoba , i. e. bikamo tbyE [ For how much wilt thou sell this garment, or piece of cloth? ]. (S.) Kh says that if any one of the Arabs made it to govern the gen. case, perhaps he did so by making mino to be implied, as is allowable with kamo : (M:) [so that you may say, bikaA^ay~ino dirohamK A@$otarayota h`*aA For how many a dirhem didst thou buy this? for] it is allowable to make the noun that follows kamo to be governed in the gen. case by mno implied, when km immediately follows a preposition; as in bikDmo dirohamK A@$otarayota h`*aA ; but when it is not thus preceded by a preposition, the noun after it must be in the accus. case. (I 'Ak p. 317.) It always holds the first place in a proposition, like kamo . (Idem, next p.) ― -b7- It is also a connective of the vocative yaA with the noun signifying the person or persons or thing called, when this noun has the article Al prefixed to it; (S, M, Mughnee, K;) and with a noun of indication, as *aA ; and with a conjunct noun having Al prefixed to it, as Al*~iY : (I 'Ak p. 268:) it is a noun formed for serving as such a connective; (M, K;) and has haA affixed to it. (S, M, &c.) You say, yaA A^ay~uhaA Alr~ajulu [which seems to be best rendered O thou man; more agreeably with the original, O thou, the man; or, accord. to Akh, O thou who art the man; lit., O he who is the man; often written yaA^ay~uhaA ]; (T, S, M, Mughnee, K;) and yaAA^ay~uhaA Alr~ajulaAni [ O ye two men ]; and yaAA^ay~uhaA Alr~ijaAlu [ O ye men ]; (M;) and yaAA^ay~atuhaAAlmaroA^apu [ O thou woman ]; (S, M;) and yaA A^ay~atuhaA AlmaroA^ataAni [ O ye two women ]; and A^ay~atuhaA Aln~sowapu [ O ye women ]; and yaAA^ay~uhaA AlmaroA^apu , and AlmaroA^ataAni , and Aln~isowapu ; (M;) and yaAA^ay~uhaA *aA [ O thou, this person or thing]; and yaA A^ay~uhaA Al~a*iY faEala ka*aA [ O thou who didst, or hast done, thus ]. (I 'Ak p. 267.) In the first of the exs. here given, A^aY~ is a noun of vague signification, (Zj, T, S,) denoting the person called, (Zj, T,) of the sing. number, (Zj, T, S,) rendered determinate by the vocative [ yA ], (S,) indecl., with damm for its termination; (Zj, T, S;) and haA is a particle employed to rouse attention, or to give notice, a substitute for the noun to which A^aY~ is in other cases prefixed; and Alr~ajulu is a qualificative to A^aY~ , (Zj, T, S,) wherefore it is in the nom. case. (S.) Akh asserts, [as we have indicated above,] that A^aY~ is here the conjunct noun, and that the first member of its complement, namely the relative huwa , is suppressed; the meaning being, yaA mano huwa Alr~ajulu : but this assertion is refuted by the fact that there is no relative pronoun that must be suppressed, nor any conjunct noun that necessarily requires that its complement should be a nominal proposition: though he might reply to these two objections by arguing that mA in the saying laA siy~amaA zayodN is in like manner [virtually] in the nom. case [as a conjunct noun syn. with Al~a*iY , and that the first member of its complement, namely huwa , an inchoative of which zayodN is the enunciative, is suppressed]. (Mughnee.) The putting of the qualificative of A^aY~ in the accus. case, as in the saying yaA A^ay~uhaA Alr~ajula A^aqobilo [ O thou man, advance ], is allowed (M, K) by El-Mázinee; but it is not known [as heard from the Arabs]. (M.) A^ay~uhaA and A^ay~atuhaA are also used for the purpose of particularizing; [in which case they are not preceded by yA ;] as when one says, A^am~aA A^anaA faA^afoEalu ka*aA A^ay~uhaA Alr~ajulu [ As for me, I will do thus, or such a thing, thou man ], meaning himself; and as in the saying of Kaab Ibn-Málik, related in a trad., fataxal~afonaA A^ay~atuhaA Alv~alaAvahu [ And we remained behind, or held back, ye three ], meaning, by the three, those particularized as remaining behind [with him], or holding back. (TA.)

senses.text: is a noun, used in five different manners. (Mughnee.) One of its meanings is that of an interrogative, (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) relating to intellectual beings and to non-intellectual things; [meaning Who? which? and what? ] (S, M, K;) and as such, it is a decl. noun: (S:) it is said in the K to be a particle; (MF;) and so in the M; (TA;) but this is wrong: (MF:) and it is added in the K that it is indecl.; (MF;) and it is said to be so in the M, accord. to Sb, in an instance to be explained below...

So in the saying [in the Kur xix. 70], vum~a lananoziEan~a mino kul~i $iyEapK A^ay~uhumo A^a$ad~u EalaY Alr~aHom`ni Eutiy~aA [ Then we will assuredly draw forth, from every sect, him, of them, who is most exorbi...

definition: A sign, token, or mark, by which a person or thing is known;
sourceDefinition: A sign, token, or mark, by which a person or thing is known; syn. EalaAmapN (IAar, T, S, M, Msb, K) and A^amaArapN : (M, K:) it properly signifies any apparent thing inseparable from a thing not equally apparent, so that when one perceives the former, he knows that he perceives the other, which he cannot perceive by itself, when the two things are of one predicament; and this is apparent in the object of sense and in that of the intellect: (Er-Rághib, TA:) it is of the measure faEolapN , (M, K,) originally A^ay~apN ; the [former] Y being changed to A because the letter before it is with fet-h, though this is an extraordinary change: (M:) this is related as on the authority of Sb: (TA:) or it is of the measure faEalapN , (M, K,) accord. to Kh; (M;) originally A^awayapN ; (S;) [for, accord. to J and Fei,] Sb said that its medial radical letter is w , and that the final is Y , because words of this class are more common than those of which the medial and final radical letters are both Y ; (S, Msb;) and the rel. n. is A^awawiY~u : (S:) but IB says, Sb did not state that the medial radical letter of A=yapN is w , as J states; but he said that it is originally A^ayapN , and that the quiescent w is changed into A ; and he relates of Kh, that he allowed the rel. n. of A=yapN to be ↓ A=y^iY~N and ↓ A=yiY~N and A=wiY~N ; but as to A^awawiY~N , he says, I know not any one who has said it except J: (TA:) or it is of the measure faAEilapN , (S, Msb, K,) originally A=yayapN , contracted by the suppression of its final radical letter [with the preceding kesreh]: so accord. to Fr: [but see what follows (after the pls.), where this is said to be the opinion of Ks, and disallowed by Fr:] (S, Msb:) the pl. is A=yaAtN and ↓ A=YN , (S, M, Msb, K,) [or the latter is rather a coll. gen. n.,] and pl. pl. A=yaA='N : (M, K:) J says that one of its pls. is A=yaAYN ; [and we find the same also in some copies of the K;] but this is a mistake for A=yaA='N , which is pl. of A=YN , not of A=yapN : (IB, TA:) and this pl., being of the measure A^afoEaAlN , has been adduced as evidence that the medial radical letter is Y , not w : (TA:) the dim. is ↓ A_iyay~apN , [of the measure fuEaylapN changed to fEayolapN because of the medial radical Y ,] which, accord. to Fr, shows the opinion of Ks, that A=yapN is of the measure faAEilapN rendered defective by the suppression of its final radical letter, to be incorrect, because [Fr holds, in opposition to some others, that] a noun of this measure has not its dim. formed on the measure fuEayolapN unless it is a proper name. (T.) They said, AifoEalohu biA=yapi ka*aA [ Do thou it at the sign of such a thing ]; like as you say, biEalaAmapi ka*aA and biA^amaArapi . (M.) And [in this sense, as is indicated by the context in the M,] it is one of the nouns that are prefixed to verbs [as virtually governing the gen. case], (M, K, *) because of the nearness of its meaning to the meaning of time: (K:) as in the saying [of a poet], biA=yapi tuqodimuwna Alxayola $uEovFA [ At the sign of your urging forward the horses, unsmoothed in their coats, or not curried; which means nearly the same as “at the time of your urging” &c.]. (M.) ― -b2- A sign as meaning an indication, an evidence, or a proof. (TA.) ― -b3- A sign as meaning a miracle; [and a wonder; for] A=yaAtu A@ll~`hi means the wonders of God. (TA.) ― -b4- An example, or a warning; (Fr, T, M, Msb, K;) as, for instance, the case of Joseph and his brethren, related in the Kur: (Fr, T:) pl. ↓ A=YN (M, K) and A=yaAtN . (Fr, T.) ― -b5- A message, or communication sent from one person or party to another; syn. risaAlapN . (TA.) ― -b6- The body, or corporeal form or figure or substance, (S, M, K,) of a man, (S,) which one sees from a distance; [as being a kind of sign;] or a person, or an individual; syn. $axoSN . (S, M, K.) ― -b7- A whole company of people: as in the saying, xaraja Alqawomu biA=yatihimo The people, or party, went forth with their whole company, not leaving behind them anything. (AA, S, M.) ― -b8- [Hence, accord. to some, A verse of the Kur-án; as being] a collection of words of the Book of God: (S:) or a connected form of words of the Kur-án continued to its breaking off; (K, TA;) accord. to Aboo-Bekr, so called because it is a sign of the breaking off: (TA:) or a portion of the Kur-án after which a suspension of speech is approvable: (Msb:) or a portion of the Kur-án denoting any statute, or ordinance, of God, whether it be [ what is generally termed ] an A=yap , [i. e. a verse, ] or a chapter ( suwrap ), or an aggregate [ and distinct ] portion of the latter. (Er-Rághib, Kull, TA. *) [ AlA=yapa , written after a quotation of a part of a verse of the Kur-án, means AiqoraA^i AlA=yapD Read thou the verse. ]

sourceDefinition: is syn. with zaAla [in two senses; i. e. as an attributive verb, and also as a non-attributive verb; as will be shown by what follows]. (S, A, Mgh.) [Using it as an attributive verb,] you say, laA A^aboraHu Hat~aY taqoDiYa HaAjatiY I will not go away, or depart, or withdraw, ( laA A^azuwlN , and laA A^atanaH~aYi ,) until thou accomplish my want: from bariHa AlmakaAnu , inf. n. baraAHN , he went away, or departed, from the place; syn. zaAla minohu : and to be distinguished from the phrase in the Kur [xviii. 59, similar as to words,] mentioned below. (Mgh.) You say, bariHa makaAnahu , (S, A, L, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. baraAHN (S, L, K) and buruwHN (L, TA, and Ham p. 250) and baraHN , (L,) or baroHN , (as in a copy of the TA,) He went away, or departed, from his place; (S, L, K, and Ham ubi suprà;) and he became in the baraAH [or wide, uncultivated, or uninhabited, tract ]. (S, L, K.) And maA bariHa makaAnahu He did not quit his place. (Msb.) And bariHa [alone], aor. , inf. n. baraAHN , It (a thing) went away, or departed, ( zaAla ,) from its place; (Msb;) as also ↓ tbr~H . (L.) In the phrase laA baraAHa [ There is, or shall be, no quitting of place, or going away, or departing ], the noun is in the accus. case, as in laA rayoba : but it is allowable to put it in the nom. case, so that lA is used in the manner of layosa ; (S, K;) as in the following saying of Saad Ibn-Málik, [in the TA, in one place, Ibn-Náshib,] in a poem of which the rhyme is with refa, (S, IAth,) alluding to El-Hárith Ibn-'Abbád, who had withdrawn himself from the war of Teghlib and Bekr the sons of Wáïl: (IAth, TA:) faA^anaA A@bonu qayosK laA baraAHu mano far~aEano niyraAnihaA [ Whoso fleeth from its fires, (i. e. niyraAni AlHarobi the fires of the war, ) let him do so: but as for me, I am the son of Keys: to me there is not, or shall not be, any quitting of place ]. (S, IAth. [See also Ham p. 250, where, for man far~a , we find mano Sad~a whoso turneth away. ]) [Hence,] bariHati Alr~iyHu biAlt~uraAbi The wind carried up, raised, or swept up and scattered, [lit. went away with, ] the dust. (Msb.) [Hence also, accord. to some,] bariHa AlxafaA='u , (T, S, K, &c.,) and baraHa , (Ibn-ElLihyánee, Z, and TA, [thus written in a copy of the A,]) (tropical:) The state of concealment departed, or ceased: or (tropical:) what was in a state of concealment became apparent; from baraAHN meaning “what is open and apparent” of land: or (tropical:) what I was concealing became apparent: (T, TA:) or (tropical:) the affair, or case, became manifest, (S, A, K,) and its concealment ceased, (A,) [or] as though the secret departed, and ceased: (S:) or, as some say, (assumed tropical:) the secret became apparent: (TA in art. xfY :) or, lit., the low ground became high and apparent; meaning (assumed tropical:) what was concealed became revealed: (Har pp. 133—4:) the first who said it was Shikk the Diviner. (IDrd, TA.) ― -b2- [Using it as a non-attributive verb,] you say, laA A^aboraHu A^afoEalu *`lika I will not cease, or I will continue, ( laA A^azaAlu ,) to do that: (S, A: *) and maA bariHa yafoEalu ka*aA [ he ceased not to do thus; or] he persevered in, or kept to, doing thus: (Msb:) and maA bariHa zayodN qaAy^imFA [ Zeyd ceased not to be, or he kept, or continued, standing ]: in this case, the verb is of the category of kaAna ; (Mgh;) relates to time; and requires a predicate: and its inf. n. is baraAHN . (Ham p. 250.) Hence the saying in the Kur [xviii. 59], laA A^aboraAHu Hat~aY A^aboluga majomaEa AlbaHorayoni , but the predicate is suppressed: it may be maA naHonu fiyhi ka*`lika [i. e. I will not cease in that wherein we are thus engaged until I reach the place of meeting of the two seas ]: (Mgh:) or it means laA A^azaAlu A^asiyru [ I will not cease journeying ]: (Bd, Jel:) or lA AbrH here may mean I will not depart ( laA A^azuwlu ) from that upon which I am intent, namely journeying and seeking; and I will not relinquish it; so that it does not require the predicate. (Bd. definition: Difficulty, distress, affliction, or adversity;
sourceDefinition: Difficulty, distress, affliction, or adversity; evil, or mischief; (K, TA;) annoyance, molestation, or hurt; severe punishment; trouble, inconvenience, or fatigue; (TA;) a difficult, a distressing, an afflictive, or adverse, and a wonderful, thing or event: (Ham p. 135:) and annoyance, or molestation, by distressing importunity or pressing; a subst. from 2: (T, TA:) and binotu baroHK , [and app. Aibonu baroHK also,] a calamity, misfortune, or disaster; or a great, or terrible, thing, affair, or case; (TA;) as also ↓ binotu baAriHK , and ↓ Aibonu bariyHK ; (K;) pl. banaAtu baroHK and banuw baroHK . (TA.) [See also taboriyHN .] You say, laqiytu minohu baroHFA ↓ baAriHFA I experienced from him, or it, [ great ] difficulty, distress, affliction, or adversity; [ great ] annoyance, molestation, or hurt; (S, A, * K; *) a phrase having an intensive signification, (K, TA,) like layolN A^aloyalu [and layolN laAy^ilN ]; and so baroHFA ↓ mubar~iHFA . (TA.) When used as an imprecation, the more approved way is to put the two words in the accus. case: but sometimes they are put in the nom. case; as in the saying of a poet, ↓ baroHN laEyonaka baAriHN [ May great difficulty, &c., befall thy two eyes! ]. (TA.) You say also, laqiytu minohu banaAti baroHK , (S, A,) and baniy baroHK , (S,) I experienced from him, or it, difficulties, distresses, afflictions, or adverse events; and calamities, misfortunes, or disasters: (S:) and, in the same sense, ↓ lqyt mnh AlbiraHiyna , and ↓ AlburaHiyna , (S, K,) and ↓ AlbaraHiyna ; (K;) or, accord. to some copies of the K, ↓ AlbiroHayni , and ↓ AlburoHayoni , and ↓ AlbaroHayoni , as duals; but the former reading is the more correct: (TA:) [MF disapproves of the form baraHiyna , and it is not mentioned in the L; but the dual form baroHayoni is there mentioned:] it seems as though the sing. of bariHiyna [or buraHiyna ] were biraHapN [or buraHapN ], and that the pl. is formed by the termination wn to compensate for the rejection of the p , as is virtually the case in A^araDuwna ; [or because the signification is regarded as that of a personification;] and that the pl. only is used. (L.) It is said in a prov., binotu baroHK $arakN EalaY raA^osika [ Calamity is, or be, a snare upon thy head ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of bariHa , q. v.; whence the phrase laA baraAHa , explained above. (S, L, K.) -A2- A wide, or spacious, tract of land, (S, A, K,) kaving in it no seed-produce nor trees: (S, K:) or land having in it no building nor habitation: (Ham p. 237:) and applied as an epithet to land, signifying wide, or spacious, open, or conspicuous, and having in it no herbage nor habitation: and what is open, uncovered, and wholly apparent, of land: (TA:) or a place having no trees nor other things to cover or conceal it; as though such things had departed; (Mgh;) a place free from trees &c.: (Msb:) or an elevated and open tract of land. (Har p. 134.) ― -b2- Habiylu baraAHK is an appellation given to (tropical:) A lion: and (assumed tropical:) a courageous man: as though each of them were bound with ropes, (K, TA,) and did not quit his place. (TA.) -A3- An affair, a thing, or a case, that is plain, evident, or manifest; (K, TA;) or open, or public. (TA.) You say, jaA='anaA biAlA^amori baraAHFA [ He told us, or did to us, the thing ] plainly [or openly ]. (S.) And jaA='a biAlkufori baraAHFA wa biAl$~ar~i SuraAHFA [ He uttered, or committed an act of, infidelity plainly, or openly, and evil, or mischief, unmixedly ]. (A, TA.) ― -b2- Counsel, or an opinion, that is disapproved, or deemed evil. definition: , (S, K, &c.,) as also ↓ baruwHN and ↓ bariyHN , (K,) applied to a gazelle, (S,) or what is hunted or shot, (K, TA,) of gazelles and birds and wild animals [in general], (TA,) Turning his left side...
sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) as also ↓ baruwHN and ↓ bariyHN , (K,) applied to a gazelle, (S,) or what is hunted or shot, (K, TA,) of gazelles and birds and wild animals [in general], (TA,) Turning his left side towards the spectator, (S,) passing from the direction of the right hand of the latter towards the direction of his left hand: (S, K:) or turning his right side towards the spectator, passing from the direction of the latter's left hand towards that of his right: (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, IF, A, * L, Msb, * in art. snH :) contr. of saAniHN : (S, * TA:) pl. bawaAriHu . (L in art. snH .) The Arabs [who apply the epithet in the latter sense] regard the bArH as an evil omen, and the sAnH as a good omen; because one cannot shoot at the former without turning himself: (S:) but some of them hold the reverse: (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee and L in art. snH :) the people of Nejd hold the sAnH to be a good omen; but sometimes a Nejdee adopts the opinion of the Hijázee [which is the contrary]. (IB in that art.) The first of these epithets is also applied to a bird as meaning Inauspicious; ill-omened. (A.) It is said in a prov., mano liY biA ls~aAniHi baEoda AlbaAriHi (TA) i. e. [ Who will be responsible to me ] for a fortunate, or lucky, event, after an unfortunate, or unlucky? (K in art. snH :) applied in the case of a man's doing evil, and its being said, “He will at a future time do good to thee:” originally said by a man on the occasion of gazelles' passing before him in the manner of such as are termed baAriHap , and its being said to him, “They will present themselves to thee in the manner of such as are termed saAnHap .” (TA.) And in another prov. it is said, A_in~amaA huwa kabaAriHi AlA^arowaY [ It, or he, is only like the mountain-goat passing in the manner of such as is termed bArH ]: for it dwells on the tops of the mountains, and men scarcely ever see it passing with the right or left side towards them save once in the course of ages: (S, K:) applied in the case of an extraordinary occurrence: (K:) [or in the case of a benefit conferred by a man who very rarely confers benefits on others: (Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 35:)] or when a man has delayed, or been tardy in, visiting [but has come at last]. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, fitolapN baAriHapN i. q. $azorapN [i. e. (tropical:) A manner of twisting contrary to that which is usual: see $azara ]. (A.) ― -b3- And h`*ihi faEolpN baAriHapN (tropical:) This is an action that has not happened rightly. (A.) ― -b4- [Hence,] binotu baAriHN : and [perhaps] laqiytu minohu baroHFA baAriHFA : and baroHN liEayonaka baAriHN : see baroHN . ― -b5- [And hence, perhaps, because of its evil effect; or because it comes, accord. to some, from the left, i. e. northerly direction, or, accord. to others, from the right, i. e. southerly direction; or] from baroHN as signifying “a difficult, a distressing, an afflictive, or adverse, and a wonderful, thing, or event;” (Ham p. 135;) baAriHN signifies also A hot wind: (S:) or a hot wind in the SayofN [i. e. summer or spring ]: (K:) or a hot wind coming from the direction of El-Yemen: (Ham p. 135:) or a wind that carries up, raises, or sweeps up and scatters, the dust: (Msb:) pl. bawAriHu : (S, K, &c.:) or the bwArH are hot north, or northerly, winds in the Sayof : (AZ, Az, S:) this Az found to be the sense in which the term was used by the Arabs in his time: (TA:) or violent winds that carry with them the dust by reason of their violence: (TA:) or this name (the pl.) was given by the Arabs to all winds in the time of the stars of the qayoZ [or summer ]: they mostly blow in the time of the stars of Libra; [app. meaning when Libra is on, or near, the meridian at nightfall, agreeably with a statement in modern Arabic almanacs, that the periods of the beginning and end of the winds thus called are the 30th of May and the 9th of July;] and these winds are what are termed the samaAy^im [pl. of samuwmN ]. (Ibn-Kunáseh, TA.) ― -b6- AlbawaAriHu is also said by some to signify AlA^anowaA='u [pl. of nawo'N , q. v.]; as mentioned by AHn; but he repels their assertion. (TA.)

definition: The next, or nearest, past, or preceding, night;
sourceDefinition: The next, or nearest, past, or preceding, night; yesternight: (S, A, Mgh, * Msb, * K:) from bariHa signifying zaAla [“he, or it, went away” &c.]. (S, A.) [In modern Arabic, Yesterday; as also AlbaAriH .] It has no dim. formed from it. (Sb, in S, in art. A^ms ; and TA.) You say, laqiytuhu AlbaAriHap [ I met, or met with, him, or it, last night, or yesternight ]: and laqiytuhu AlbaAriHapa AlA^uwlay [ I met, or met with, him, or it, the night before last; this being the sense in which the phrase is now used by the learned: but the vulgar expression is A^aw~al AlbaAriHap , generally pronounced A^aw~al AamobaAriHaho or A^aw~al AamobaAriHo , agreeably with a peculiarity of the dial. of the people of El-Yemen, or of Teiyi and Himyer, by the substitution of Aamo for Aalo : see art. Am ]. (S) From daybreak to the time when the sun declines from the meridian, one says, raA^ayotu All~ayolapa fiY manaAmiY [I saw to-night in my sleep (such a thing)]; but when the sun has declined, one says, raA^ayotu AlbaAriHapa [ I saw last night, or yesternight ]: (AZ, Th: [and the like is said in the Mgh and Msb:]) or one says, kaAna ka*aA wa ka*aA All~ayolapa [ Such and such things happened to-night ] until the sun is somewhat high and the day has become bright; but after this, one says, kaAna AlbaAriHapa [ It happened last night, or yesternight ]. (Yoo, Seer.) The Arabs say, maA A^a$obaha All~ayolapa biA lbaAriHapi How like is this night wherein we are to the former night that has departed! (TA:) [or, this night to yesternight! ]: originally occurring in a poem of Tarafeh: used as meaning “how like is the child to the father!” and applied to [any] two things resembling each other. (Har p. 667.)

sourceDefinition: , first pers. ba$i$otu , aor. yaba$~u , (S, K,) and, accord. to a relation of a verse of Ru-beh, yabi$~u , so that perhaps ba$a$otu was also said, (TA.) inf. n. ba$aA$apN (S, A, K) and ba$~N (A, K) and ba$iy$N , (TA,) He was, or became, cheerful in countenance. (S, A, K.) You say, ba$i$otu bihi I was, or became, cheerful in countenance [ by reason of meeting ] with him: (S:) or ba$~a bihi (TK,) inf. n. ba$~N (Lth, K) and ba$aA$apN , (K,) signifies he rejoiced in him, or was pleased with him, namely, a friend, (Lth, K,) at meeting: (Lth:) or he showed joy, or pleasure, at meeting him. (TK.) You say also, biY ↓ laqiytuhu fataba$oba$a [app. meaning I met him and he became cheerful in countenance by reason of meeting with me ]; originally ↓ taba$~a$a ; the middle $ being changed into b : (Yaakoob, S:) or bihi ↓ taba$oba$a signifies he was, or became, sociable, or companionable, or cheerful, with him; and held loving communion with him: syn. A=nasahu , and waASalahu : (K:) but when said of God, it means (tropical:) He regarded him with favour, and honoured him, (IAmb, K,) and received him graciously, and drew him near to Him. (IAmb.) ― -b2- Also ba$~a lahu , (TK,) inf. n. ba$~N (IDrd, K) and ba$aA$apN , (K,) He presented a favourable aspect to him; or met him kindly, namely, his brother; syn. A^aqobala Ealayohi : (K:) he behaved laughingly towards him; without shyness, or aversion; or boldly; or in a free and easy manner; or cheerfully; syn. DaHika A_ilayohi , (IDrd, K,) and AinobasaTa . (IDrd.) ― -b3- And ba$~a lahu fiY AlmasoA^alapi , (TK,) inf. n. ba$~N (IAar, A, K) and ba$aA$apN , (A, K,) He was courteous, or gracious, to him in asking. (IAar, A, K.) ― -b4- And ba$~a liY bixayori (tropical:) He gave me [ something good ]. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (JK, S, A, Mgh, Msb,) or , (K,) [but this seems to be a mistake,] inf. n. baqorN , (S, Msb,) He slit; ripped; split; cut, or divided, lengthwise. (S, Msb, K, &c.) He slit, or ripped open, an animal's belly. (A, Mgh.) One says, AuboqurohaA Eano janiynihaA Rip thou open her [a camel's] belly so as to disclose her fœtus. (S.) [See baqiyrN .] ― -b2- He opened, or laid open. (S, A, Msb.) ― -b3- He widened; made wide, or ample. (S, K.) ― -b4- He opened, and widened, or made wide, a house, or tent. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b5- He opened and revealed to a person a story. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b6- baqara AlA^aroDa said of a hudohud [or hoopoe], It looked for the place of water and saw it: (K:) [or it clave the ground and discovered water: ] occurring in a trad. respecting the hdhd of Solomon [mentioned in the Kur ch. xxvii.] (T.) ― -b7- baqara fiY baniY fulaAnK He knew the state, condition, case, or affair, of the sons of such a one, and examined, or inspected, them. (K.) ― -b8- baqara Eani AlEuluwmi He inquired, and searched to the utmost, after sciences. (A.) ― -b9- baqara AlEiloma : see 5. -A2- baqira , aor. , He (a dog) became confounded, (S, K,) and stupified, (TA,) with joy, (K,) at seeing baqar , (S, K,) i. e., baqar AlwaHo$ [ wild oxen, or wild bulls or cows ]; (TA;) like as one says gazila meaning “ he sported, ” or “ played, ” “ at seeing a gazelle, ” or “ a young gazelle; ” as also ↓ bayoqara : or the former, he feared, so that he was astonished, amazed, or stupified, at seeing many baqar : (TA voce baHiza :) and ↓ the latter signifies also [simply] he became confounded, or perplexed: (IAar, TA:) and he doubted respecting a thing. (K.) ― -b2- Also, aor. as above, inf. n. baqarN (S, K) and baqorN ; (K;) but Az says, El-Mundhiree has informed me that A Heyth disallowed baqorN , saying that it is accord. to analogy baqarN , as the verb is intrans.; (TA;) He (a man) became tired, or fatigued, (S, K,) so that he could hardly see; (K;) and he became weary, or jaded; (S, K;) as also ↓ bayoqara . (S, K. *)
