definition: a gen. n., (S, Msb,) a word of well-known meaning, (S, Msb, K,) [The bovine genus; the ox, or bull, and cow; and oxen, or bulls, and cows; neat; black cattle; ] applied to the domestic and the wild:...
sourceDefinition: a gen. n., (S, Msb,) a word of well-known meaning, (S, Msb, K,) [The bovine genus; the ox, or bull, and cow; and oxen, or bulls, and cows; neat; black cattle; ] applied to the domestic and the wild: (TA:) [but the wild have also distinctive appellations, as will be seen below:] n. un. baqarapN , (S, Msb, K, [but in the K it is said that baqarN is pl. of baqarapN ,]) which is applied to the male and the female; (S, Msb, K;) the p being added only to restrict it to unity: (S, Msb:) the pl. of baqarN is A^aboqurN [a pl. of pauc.]; (M,) and A^aboqaArN , meaning herds of oxen, or bulls, or cows: (Msb and TA in art. Abl :) and the pl. of baqarapN is baqaraAtN (S, Msb, K) and buqurN and buq~aArN (K) and bawaAqiru (As, T, K) and ↓ A^uboquwrN ; (K;) [or rather this last is a quasi-pl. n.;] and the following [also] are quasi-pl. ns., namely, ↓ bayoquwrN , (K,) which is syn. with baqarN , (S,) and ↓ baqiyrN , (K,) or this signifies a collection, or herd, of baqar , (S,) and ↓ baAqirN , (K,) or this signifies a collection, or herd, of baqar with their pastors, (Lth, S,) and ↓ baAquwrN , and ↓ baAquwrapN , (K,) or this last is syn. with baqarapN in the dial. of the people of El-Yemen: (S:) or ↓ baAquwrN and ↓ yaboquwrN and ↓ A^uboquwrN are all syn. with baqarN ; and so, accord. to Ktr, is ↓ baAquwrapN . (Mgh.) ― -b2- baqaru AlwaHo$i [and Albaqaru AlwaHo$iY~u signify The wild ox, or bull, and cow; and wild oxen, or bulls, and cows, collectively: n. un. baqarapu AlwaHo$i and Albaqarapu AlwaHo$iy~apu ; masc. and fem.: in Egypt, these appellations are applied to the antilope defassa of modern zoologists: so says Sir Gardner Wilkinson; and to this, I believe, they generally apply in the poems &c. of the early Arabs: it is a species of bovine antelope: in Barbary, it seems that the animal thus called is another species of bovine antelope, or perhaps a variety of the former; it is said to be what is termed by Pallas antilope bubalis; by others, alcephalus bubalis, or acronotus bubalis; and this is said to come occasionally to the Nile: but the Arabic appellations given above are employed with much laxity: thus we find baqaru AlwaHo$i explained as meaning] a kind of animal of which there are four different species: the first called mihiA [i. e. mahFA , a coll. gen. n. of which the n. un. is mahaApN ]; the second, Ayl [i. e. A_iy~alN ]; the third yHmwr [i. e. yaHomuwrN ], or yAmwr [i. e. yaA^omuwrN ]; the fourth, vyvl [or vayotalN ], and also wEl [i. e. waEolN ]: (Ed-Demeeree, cited by De Sacy, erroneously written by him “ Domaïri, ” in his Chrest. Ar. sec. ed. ii. 435 et seq.:) or what is called in Persian kwzn [or Gawazono (see also A_iy~alN in art. Awl )]; it has a great horn, with branches; an additional branch growing upon its horn every year; and its horn is solid, thus differing from the horns of other animals, for their horns are hollow: when it hears singing, and the sounds of musical instruments, it listens thereto, and then it takes no care to guard itself from the arrows, by reason of its intense delight therein: when it raises its ear, it hears sounds; and when it relaxes it, it hears not anything. (Kzw: also cited by De Sacy, ubi suprà.) The Arabs regard baqar [meaning bqr AlwH$ ] as ominous of evil, because of the sharpness of their horns. (Ham p. 285.) ― -b3- milo'u masoki Albaqarapi [ The quantity that fills the hide of the bull, or cow, ] means (tropical:) a large quantity. (A.) ― -b4- AlZ~ibaA='a EalaY Albaqari [or AlZ~ibaA='u ] and AlkiraAba EalaY Albaqari [or AlkiraAbu , and AlkilaAba or AlkilaAbu ,] are provs. of the Arabs. (TA.) [See arts. Zby and krb and klb .] ― -b5- Eayonu Albaqari (assumed tropical:) [ The buphthalmum, or ox-eye; ] i. q. bahaArN , q. v. (S in art. bhr .) ― -b6- Euyuwnu Albaqari (tropical:) A species of grape, black, large, round, and not very sweet. (K, TA.) In Palestine, applied to (tropical:) A species of A_ij~aAS [or plum ]. (K, TA.) ― -b7- baqarN is also applied to (tropical:) A family, or household; those who dwell with a man, and whose maintenance is incumbent on him. (TA.) You say, jaA'a fulaAnN yajur~u baqarahu (tropical:) Such a one came dragging along his family, or household. (A, * TA.) And EalaY fulaAnK baqarapN mino EiyaAlK wamaAlK (tropical:) Upon such a one is dependent a troop, or large number, of his family, and of camels or the like; (A, * TA;) and in like manner you say, kari$N mino EiyaAlK . (A.) And fulaAnN fiY baqarK mina Aln~aAsi (tropical:) Such a one is among a large company of men. (A.)

sourceDefinition: [The mild species of leprosy termed “alphus,” or “vitiligo alba;” in Hebrew בֹּהַק ;] a whiteness, less than what is termed baraSN , that comes upon the external skin of a man; (JK;) a whiteness that affects the skin, (S,) or body, (Mgh, Msb,) differing from the colour of the latter; (S, Msb;) not from what is termed baraS , (S, Mgh,) or not baraS : (Msb:) and, accord. to IF, a blackness that affects the skin; [i. e. the species of leprosy termed “melas,” or “lepra maculosa nigra;” ] or a colour differing from that of the skin: (Msb:) a thin whiteness that affects the exterior of the cuticle, by reason of a bad state of the temperament of the part, inclining to coldness, and the predominance of the phlegm over the blood: the black [ species ] thereof alters ( yugay~iru , in the CK yaEotariY ,) the skin to blackness, by reason of the mixing of the black bile with the blood. (K, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] bahaqu AlHajari (assumed tropical:) [ Lichen, or liverwort; ] a certain plant; (K;) i. e. Haz~aAzu AlHajari [more commonly called Haz~aAzu AlS~axori ]: (TA:) or i. q. Aljawozu Aljanoduma , (K, TA,) or Aljawoza janoduma , (CK,) [evidently from the Persian jawozi Ganoduma explained in Johnson's Pers. Ar. and Engl. Dict. as “sandix-gum, juniper:” but SM says that] this is a certain plant, the body [or substance ] of which is muHab~ab [app. meaning composed of globules or the like; probably a particular species of lichen, with spherical cells ]. (TA.)

definition: , (M, Mgh, * Msb, * K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (M, Mgh, * Msb, * K,) aor. yabuwo'u , (M, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. bawo'N , (M, Mgh,) He returned, went back, or came back, (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) to it, (M, K, *) namely, a thing: (M:) or he withdrew [from a person or persons, or a place,] to it, or him; or, perhaps, he made himself solely and peculiarly a companion, or an associate, to him, or it; syn. AinoqaTaEa [q. v.]: (K:) but in some copies of the K, the latter explanation is connected with the former by wa [and] instead of A^aw . (TA.) wabaAw^uwA bigaDabK mina A@ll~`hi [in the Kur ii. 58 and iii. 108] means And they returned with anger from God; (Akh, S, Bd in ii. 58, and Jel in the same and in iii. 108;) i. e. the anger of God came upon them: (Akh, S:) or they returned deserving anger from God: (Bd in iii. 108:) or they became deserving of anger from God: from baA='a fulaAnN bifulaAnK such a one was deserving of being, or fit to be, slain in retaliation for such a one, (Ksh and Bd in ii. 58,) because his equal: (Ksh ibid.:) the primary signification of bawo'N being [said to be] that of equalling, or being equal with. (Bd in ii. 58.) [See a similar phrase, also from the Kur, below.] ― -b2- buw^otu bihi A_ilayohi [ I returned with it to him: and hence,] I returned it, took it back, or brought it back, to him; (M, K;) as also ↓ A^abaA^otuhu , (Th, M, K,) and buw^otuhu , (Ks, M, K,) but this last is rare. (M.) ― -b3- baA='a biA_ivomihi , aor. and inf. n. as above, (T, S,) signifies, accord. to Akh, He returned [laden] with his sin: (S:) or, accord. to As, he acknowledged it, or confessed it: (T:) or, accord. to others, (TA,) baA='a bi*anobihi , (T, * M, Msb, K,) aor. as above, inf. n. bawo'N and bawaA='N , (M, K,) he bore, or took upon himself, the burden of his sin, or crime, or offence; syn. AiHotamalahu ; (Aboo-Is-hák, T, M, K, TA;) and became [ as though he were ] the abiding-place thereof: (TA:) or he became burdened, or laden, with it: (Msb:) or he became, or made himself, answerable, responsible, or accountable, for it, by an inseparable obligation; syn. Ailotazama bihi ; for the primary signification of bawaA='N is [asserted to be] luzuwmN [i. e. adhesion, &c.]; and it is afterwards used in every case [so as to imply a meaning of this kind] according to the exigency of that case; as is said in the Nh, and expressly stated by Z and Er-Rághib: (TA:) or he acknowledged it, or confessed it. (M, K.) A_in~iY A^uriydu A^ano tabuwo'a biA_ivomiY wa A_ivomika , in the Kur v. 35, means Verily I desire that thou return [laden] with the sin committed against me in slaying me, and thy sin which thou hast committed previously: (Jel:) or I desire that thou shouldst bear ( taHomila ) my sin if I were to extend my hand towards thee, and thy sin in extending thy hand towards me: or the sin committed against me in slaying me, and thy sin for which thine offering was not accepted: and each noun is in the place of a denotative of state; i. e., [it means] that thou return involved in the two sins; bearing them: and perhaps the speaker may have meant, if that must inevitably take place, I desire that it may be thine act, not mine; so that the real meaning is, that it should not be his, not that it should be his brother's: or by the A_ivomN may be meant the punishment thereof; for the desire of the punishment of the disobedient is allowable: (Bd:) accord. to Th, the meaning is, if thou have determined upon slaying me, the sin will be in thee, not in me. (M.) fabaAw^uwA bigaDabK EalaY gaDabK [in the Kur ii. 84] is explained by Aboo-Is-hák as meaning So they bore the burden of anger upon anger; syn. AiHotamaluwA ; this being said by him to be the proper signification of the verb: or, as some say, the meaning is, [ they bore the burden of ] sin for which they deserved the fire [ of Hell ] following upon sin for which they deserved the same: or they returned [laden with anger upon anger ]: (T:) or they became deserving of anger upon anger. (Ksh.) [See a similar phrase, also from the Kur, above.] It is said in a form of prayer, A^abuwo'u A_ilayoka biniEomatika , meaning I acknowledge, or confess, to Thee thy favour [towards me, as imposing an obligation upon me]. definition: He lodged him in an abode;

sourceDefinition: They two (namely, two slain men, M) became equal [ by being slain, one in retaliation for the other ]. (M, K.) (T.)

sourceDefinition: a subst. from baw~aA^ahu manozilFA . (M, K.) [See 2; and] see also mabaA='apN . ― -b2- A mode, or manner, of taking for oneself a place of abode: (M:) and [hence,] a state, or condition. (AZ, T, S, M, K.) You say, A_in~ahu laHasanu Albiyoy^api Verily he has a good mode, or manner, of taking for himself a place of abode: (M:) or verily he is of good state or condition. (S.) And baAta bibiyoy^api He passed the night in an evil state or condition (AZ, T, S, * M.) bawaA='N Equal; equivalent; like; alike; a match; (Akh, T, S, M, Mgh, K;) and particularly, if slain in retaliation for another. (M.) It is applied to one, and to two, and to more: so that you say, fulaAnN bawaA='N fulaAnN Such a one is the equal, &c., of such a one if slain in retaliation for him: (M:) and huwa bawaA='N He is an equal, &c.; and so hiYa she: and humo bawaA='N They are equals, &c.; and so hun~a they, referring to females: (Mgh:) and humo bawaA='N fiY h`*aA AlA^amori They are equals in this affair. (T.) Hence, in a trad. of 'Alee, respecting witnesses, A_a*a kaAnuwA bawaA='N When they are equals in number and rectitude. (Mgh.) And maA fulaAnN lifulaAnK bibawaA='N Such a one is not an equal, &c., to such a one. (T.) And damu fulaAnK bawaA='N lidami fulaAnK The blood of such a one is an equivalent for the blood of such a one. (S.) And AljiraAHaAtu bawaA='N Wounds are to be retaliated equally: a trad. (T, Mgh.) And Alqawomu EalaY bawaA='i The people, or company of men, are in a state of equality. (T.) And qusima AlmaAlu bayonahumo EalaY bawaA='K The property was divided among them equally. (T. [A similar ex. is given in the Mgh, and explained in the same manner; but there I find Eano bawaA='K ; perhaps a mistranscription.]) And kal~amonaAhumo faA^ajaAbuwA Eano bawaA='K waAHidK [in a copy of the M EalaY bwA=' wAHd ] We spoke to them, and they replied with one reply: (T, S, O, K: *) i. e., their reply was not discordant: Eano being here used in the sense of bi . (TA.) ― -b3- Also Retaliation. (T.) [See 1, near the end of the paragraph: as well as in other places.] It is related in a trad., that Jaafar Es-Sádik, being asked the reason of the rage of the scorpion against the sons of Adam, said, turiydu AlbawaA='a [ It desires retaliation ]; i. e., it hurts like as it is hurt. (TA.)

definition: The nightly resting-place of camels;
sourceDefinition: The nightly resting-place of camels; (T;) the resting-place of camels, where they are made to lie down, at the watering-place; (T, S, * M, * L, K; *) and of sheep or goats likewise; also termed ↓ mutabaw~aA^N : (L, TA:) or the place to which camels return; (Mgh;) as also ↓ baA='apN : (Mgh, Msb:) this is the primary signification. (T.) [Hence,] huwa raHiybN AlmabaA='api (assumed tropical:) He is largely bountiful. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The covert of the wild bull. (M.) [See also mavaAbapN ; and mavaAbN .]

definition: The limit, or boundary, (S, Msb,) of any town (S) or land: (S, Msb:) pl.
sourceDefinition: The limit, or boundary, (S, Msb,) of any town (S) or land: (S, Msb:) pl. tuxuwmN : (S, Msb:) a poet (Aboo-Keys Ibn-El-Aslat, TA) says, yaA baniY~a Alt~uxuwmu laA taZolimuwhaA (Fr, S,) or, as some relate it, ↓ Alt~axuwmu : (TA:) accord. to the former reading, Fr says, the meaning is, [ O my sons, ] the limits, or boundaries, [ misplace ye not them ], for he does not say taZolimuwhu : but ISK says, I heard AA say, it is ↓ taxuwm , and the pl. is tuxumN ; like SabuwrN and SuburN : (S:) both IAar and ISk say that the sing and pl. are like rasuwlN and rusulN : (Msb:) but the latter mentions also tuxuwmN , with damm, as a pl. form, having no sing.: (TA:) or ↓ taxuwmN signifies a sign, or mark [ of a boundary or of a way ]: and limits, or boundaries: and is sometimes with ↓ [to the t ]: (Mgh:) Lth says that txwm [written without any vowel-sign] signifies a division, or place of division, between two districts and two towns or villages; and the limit, or boundary, of the land of any district and town or village is its txwm : and AHeyth says that this word signifies limits, or boundaries: (TA:) or tuxuwmN , with damm, signifies a sign, or mark, and a limit, or boundary, that is a division between two lands; and is of the fem. gender: and the pl. is tuxuwmN also, and tuxumN : (K:) this app. means that these are pls. of tuxuwmN ; but the former is a word that is used as a sing. and as a pl.; and the latter is pl. of taxuwmN , like as SuburN is of SabuwrN , and gufurN of gafuwrN : (TA:) or (as ISk says, TA) the sing. is ↓ tuxomN and taxomN (K) and ↓ taxuwmapN : (AHn, S, * K:) accord. to A'Obeyd, the Arabic linguists say ↓ taxuwmN , like SabuwrN , making it fem. and sing.; but the people of Syria say tuxuwmN , with damm to the t , making it pl., and the sing. is taxomN : accord. to IB, one says ↓ taxuwmN and tuxuwmN , and zabuwrN and zubuwrN , and Ea*uwbN and Eu*uwbN ; and no fourth instance of the kind is known; [but see Ea*uwbN ;] and the Basrees pronounce it with damm [to the t ], and the Koofees with fet-h. (TA.) It is said in a trad., maloEuwnN mano gay~ara tuxuwma AlA^aroDi , meaning, accord. to A'Obeyd, [ Cursed is he who alters ] the limits, or boundaries, of land; and the signs, or marks, of the way: or, as some say, the limits, or boundaries, of the sacred territory. (TA.) And AjEl hm~k txwmFA , [or rather AijoEalo liham~ika ↓ taxuwmFA ,] means (tropical:) [ Set thou to thy purpose ] a limit, to which go thou, and pass not beyond it. (TA.) And huwa Tay~ibu Alt~uxuwmi (assumed tropical:) He is good in respect of ancestry, or origin: (JK:) or in respect of natural dispositions; or, as some relate the saying, ↓ Alt~axuwmi . (TA.) tuxuwmN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A state, or condition, that one desires [app. as the limit of his wish]. (IAar, Sh, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, A,) or tay~aHaAnN , (so in one copy of the S,) or both, (L, K,) like $ay~iA=nN and $ay~aA=nN applied to a horse, and hayib~aAnN and hayab~aAnN applied to a man, the only other instances of the kind, (L,) or the former is not allowable, (Ham p. 58,) so says Sb, as is stated in a marginal note in a copy of the S, (TA,) applied to a horse, meaning That goes obliquely, (S, A, K,) by reason of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, (S, K,) and bends over on each side; (S, A,) as also ↓ tay~aAHN and ↓ mitoyaHN : (S, A, K:) or that runs vehemently: and all signify, applied to a horse, fleet, swift, or excellent in running. (T, TA.) AHeyth explains the first and second as meaning Tall, or long. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also applied to a man, meaning Who addresses himself to every generous action, and difficult affair: (T, TA:) or forward, officious, meddling, or a busybody, (A, and Ham pp. 58 and 505,) who says that which does not concern him: (Ham p. 505:) or who obtrudes himself, or interferes, in affairs: (Abu-l-'Alà El-Ma'arree in a marginal note in a copy of the S, and Ham p. 58:) or, as also ↓ mitoyaHN , (S K,) and ↓ tay~aAHN , (K,) who obtrudes himself, or interferes, in that which does not concern him: (S, K:) or who falls into trials, or afflictions: (K:) or ↓ mitoyaHN , (TA,) which is also applied as an epithet to a heart, (S, A, TA,) signifies who obtrudes himself, or interferes, in everything, and falls into that which does not concern him; or who incessantly falls into trials, or afflictions; and its fem. is with p ; (TA;) or who intrudes among a people whose affair, or business, is not his: (IAar, T, TA:) and ↓ mitoyaAHN , (K,) applied to a man, (TA,) signifies much in motion; forward, officious, meddling, or a busybody. (K,* TA. [In the CK, AlEaryDu is erroneously put for AlEir~iyDu .])

sourceDefinition: [in its primary sense, He, or it, rendered it vaxiyn , i. e. thick, &c. ― -b2- And hence,] (tropical:) He, or it, (a man, JK, T, Mgh, Msb, and a wound, S, Mgh, and disease, Bd in viii. 68,) rendered him heavy: (JK, T, Bd ubi suprà, TA:) or weakened him, rendered him languid, or enervated him. (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA.) You say, Avxnhu DarobFA (assumed tropical:) He rendered him heavy by beating: (JK:) or he beat him much, or vehemently, or excessively. (TA.) And A^avoxanotuhu biAljirAHapi (assumed tropical:) I weakened him, rendered him languid, or enervated him, by the wound, or wounds. (Msb.) ― -b3- A_i*aA A^avoxanotumuwhumo , in the Kur xlvii. 4, means (assumed tropical:) When ye have made much slaughter among them: (Jel:) or when ye have made a great and vehement slaughter of them: (Bd:) or when ye have overcome them, and wounded them much, or inflicted many wounds upon them, (Abu-l-'Abbás, K, TA,) so that they give with their hands. (Abu-l-'Abbás, TA.) ― -b4- Avxn fiY AlEaduw~i (tropical:) He made a great, or vehement, slaughter, (A,) or a great, or vehement, wounding, (K,) among the enemy. (A, K.) ― -b5- Avxn fiY AlA^aroDi , (assumed tropical:) He made much slaughter in the earth, or land: (Bd in viii. 68, Mgh, TA: in the S, Avxn fiY AlA^aroDi qatolFA , which means the same: TA:) or he went against the enemy, and made a wide, or large, slaughter of them [ in the land ]: (Msb:) or he fought vehemently in the earth, or land. (Jel in viii. 68.) ― -b6- Avxn fiY AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) He exceeded the usual, or the just, bounds, or degree, in the affair; strove, or exerted himself, vigorously, or strenuously, therein; or did his utmost therein. (TA.) ― -b7- Avxnhu quwoluhu (assumed tropical:) His saying took, or had, an effect upon him; or distressed, or afflicted, him. (TA.) ― -b8- A^avoxanotu fulaAnFA maEorifapF (tropical:) I knew such a one, or was acquainted with him, thoroughly, or very well. (TA.)

definition: The earth that is taken forth from a well: (T, S, M, K:) and the mud that is taken forth from the bottom of a well: (M:) and the space upon which is cast the earth taken forth from a well, around its mouth;
sourceDefinition: The earth that is taken forth from a well: (T, S, M, K:) and the mud that is taken forth from the bottom of a well: (M:) and the space upon which is cast the earth taken forth from a well, around its mouth; which space, when the well has been dug in a place that is not the property of any one, belongs exclusively to the owner of the well: (A 'Obeyd, T:) pl. vulalN . (K.) ― -b2- ↓ val~apN mavoluwlapN A grave ( turobapN ) filled up with earth, after it has been dug. (T.) -A2- A thing that is made of clay, or mud, (M,) like a manaArap [q. v.], (K,) in the desert, for the sake of its shade. (M, K. [Erroneously written by Golius and Freytag maval~apN , and compared to maZal~apN .]) -A3- Wool, (T, S, M, K,) alone: (M, K:) or a portion of wool collected together: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and wool and goats' hair ( $aEar ) and camels' hair ( wabar ) together; (Aboo-Yoosuf, T, S, K;) but not the second of these alone, nor the third alone: (Aboo-Yoosuf, T, S:) or it signifies camels' hair ( wbr ) also: (T:) or wool and $Er and wbr together; but none of these alone. (M.) kisaA='N jiy~idu Alv~al~api is said to mean A ksA' of good wool: (S, M:) and Habolu val~apK , a rope of wool. (S.) It is said in a prov., laA taEodamu SanaAEN val~apF [ A clever woman is not without wool to spin or weave when she has nothing else to do]: applied to a skilful man. (TA.) And you say, Einoda fulaAnK val~apN kaviyrapN , meaning Such a one has much wool and goats' hair ( $Er ) and camels' hair ( wbr ). (Aboo-Yoosuf, S.) [Hence,] fulaAnN kaviyru Alv~al~api [sometimes] means (tropical:) Such a one has much hair on his body. (TA.) ― -b2- A flock of sheep or goats, (T, M, K,) whether many or few: (M:) or many thereof: (M, K:) or specially a flock of sheep: or sheep, absolutely: (M:) or a numerous flock of sheep: (ISk, T, S, K:) and numerous sheep and goats together: many goats are not thus called; but are called HayolapN : (Aboo-Yoosuf, S, M:) pl. vilalN , (S, M, K,) which is extr., (M,) and vilaAlN . (M, K.) ― -b3- Many pieces of money; or much money; (M, K;) as also ↓ vul~apN . (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) -A4- In relation to the times of camels' coming to water, ( fiY mawaAridi AlA_ibili , TA, [in the copies of the K, fY is omitted, and mawaAridu is put for mawaAridi ,]) The interval of two days, or keeping from water during two days, between two drinkings. (K, TA. [The word to which this signification is assigned is erroneously written by Golius and Freytag maval~apN ; and explained as meaning “Locus ubi aquantur cameli postquam per biduum non biberint.”])

sourceDefinition: , aor. , He restrained, or withheld, himself; refrained, forbore, or abstained; or turned back, or reverted. (K, TA.) You say, jabaA^a Eanohu , and jabiy^a , meaning He restrained, or withheld, himself, &c., from him, or it; and regarded him, or it, with reverence, veneration, dread, awe, or fear: (TA:) [or,] accord. to AZ, jabaA^otu Eani Alr~ajuli , inf. n. jabo'N and jubuwo'N , [to which Golius adds jubuw^N and jibaA='N , but, I suspect, from incorrect MSS.,] means I drew, or held, or hung, back from the man; or remained behind him; or shrank from him; or shrank from him and hid myself: and he cites (from Nuseyb Ibn-Mihjen, TA) fahalo A^ana A_il~a mivolu say~iqapi AlEidaY A_ini A@sotaqodamato naHorN waA_ino jabaA^ato EaqorN [ And am I otherwise than like the beasts driven away by the enemy? If they go before, slaughter befalls them; and if they remain behind, hocking ]. (S, TA.) You say also, maA jabaA^a Eano $atomiY He did not draw back from reviling me; did not desist, or abstain, therefrom. (TA.) ― -b2- It (a sword) recoiled, or reverted, without penetrating, or without effect: (K:) or so the former verb [only]. (TA.) ― -b3- It (the sight, or the eye,) recoiled, or reverted: (K:) or so the former verb [only]; and disliked, or disapproved, or hated, the thing [ that was before it ]. (TA.) You say, jabaA^ato EayoniY Eani Al$~aYo'i My eye recoiled, or reverted, from the thing. (S.) And of a woman of displeasing aspect you say, A_in~a AlEayoni latajobaA^u EanohaA [ Verily the eye recoils from her with dislike ]. (As, TA.) ― -b4- He disliked, disapproved, or hated: (K:) or so the former verb [only]. (TA.) You say, jabaA^a Al$~aYo'a He disliked, &c., the thing. (TA.) ― -b5- He inclined his neck: (K:) or so the former verb [only]. (TA.) ― -b6- He hid himself; (K, TA;) [app. from fear; ] as, for instance, a Dab~ [q. v.] in its hole. (TA.) ― -b7- He, or it, came, or went, forth, or out: (K:) [or so the former verb only.] You say of a serpent, jabaA^a Ealayohi It came forth upon him from its hole (S, TA) so as to frighten him; and in like manner one says of a hyena, and a Dab~ , and a jerboa. (TA.) And jabaA^a EalaY Alqawomi He came forth unexpectedly upon the people, or company of men. (TA.) And jabaA^a AljaraAdu The locusts invaded, or came suddenly upon, the country. (TA.)

[See also majoHuw$N .]

definition: A young ass; (S, Msb, K;) domestic and wild: or before it becomes big: (TA:) or from the time when it is brought forth until it becomes big from sucking: when it has completed the year, it is called...
sourceDefinition: A young ass; (S, Msb, K;) domestic and wild: or before it becomes big: (TA:) or from the time when it is brought forth until it becomes big from sucking: when it has completed the year, it is called tawolabN : (As:) [or the latter is applied to a wild ass of that age:] pl. [of pauc.] A^ajoHaA$N (so in a copy of the S) and [of mult.] jiHaA$N and jiHo$aAnN (S, Msb, K) and juHuw$N (Msb) and jiHa$apN : (As, TA:) [dim. juHayo$N :] and fem. jaHo$apN . (S, K.) It is said in a prov., AljaHo$a lam~aA ba*~aka AlA^aEoyaAru , (A, TA,) i. e., Seek thou, or pursue thou, the young ass when the full-grown asses outstrip thee: applied to him who seeks much, and it escapes him; so one says to him, Seek thou less than that. (TA.) [Meyd gives faAtaka in the place of ba*~aka .] ― -b2- Also (tropical:) A mare's colt; (A, K;) as being likened to a young ass. (TA.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A gazelle; (Ibn- 'Abbád, K;) in the dial. of Hudheyl: (TA:) or a young gazelle; (A, TA;) in that dial.; occurring in a poem of Aboo-Dhu-eyb; but accord. to one relation, the word there is x$of . (TA.)

(S, A, K.) (A.) And yajoraDu EalaY nafosihi He dies. (TA.) And jariDati Aln~aAqapu bijir~atihaA [app. meaning The she-camel was choked with her cud: or swallowed her cud with difficulty ]. (TA.) You say, A^afolata minohumo waqado jaraDuwhu He escaped from them when they had strangled him [ so as almost to kill him ]. (TA.)

definition: [A man having his throat, or fauces, choked by his spittle.
sourceDefinition: [A man having his throat, or fauces, choked by his spittle. ― -b2- And hence,] Having his soul reaching his fauces: or near to dying: (TA:) or at the point of death, his soul having reached his fauces, so that he is choked by it: (A, TA:) or dying: (TA:) or made, or suffered, to escape, after evil: (Lth:) or oppressed by grief or sorrow; (S, K;) as also ↓ jiroyaADN and ↓ jiroA=DN : (ADk, K:) or affected by intense anxiety or grief: (TA:) [see also jar~aADN :] pl. jaroDaY ; (A, K;) like as maroDaY is pl. of mariyDN . (A, TA.) You say, A^afolata fulaAnN jariyDFA , or A^ufolita , Such a one escaped, or was made to escape, being near to death; (TA;) or being at the point of death, his soul having reached his fauces, so that he was choked by it. (A, TA.) And maAta fulaAnN jariyDFA Such a one died oppressed by grief or sorrow. (S.) -A2- In the following prov., HaAla AljariyDu duwna AlqariyDi [ The jryD interposed as an obstacle in the way of the qryD ], AljryD signifies the thing choking the throat or fauces; (S, A;) and AlqryD signifies the cud: the meaning being, the thing choking the throat or fauces hindered from chewing the cud: (A:) or the former signifies the choking, or having the throat, or fauces, obstructed; and the latter, the poetry: (TA:) or the former, the swallowing of spittle in dying; and the latter, the sound, or voice, of a man in dying: (Er-Riyáshee:) or the former, spittle swallowed: (Har p. 150, q. v.:) and also, the chokings ( guSaS ) of death: [see also jaraDN :] and the moving to and fro of the two jaws at death: (TA:) the prov. relates to an affair which is hindered by some obstacle: (A, O, K:) or it is said on the occasion of any affair which was possible and which has been hindered by the intervention of some obstacle: and the first who said it was 'Obeyd Ibn-El-Abras, when El-Mundhir [on one of the days when it was his custom to slay whomsoever he met] desired him to recite some of his verses: (Zeyd Ibn-Kuthweh:) or the first who said it was Jowshan [in some copies of the K, Showshan, which, as is said in the TA, is a mistake,] El-Kilábee, when his father, having forbidden him to poetize, and seeing him sick of grief thereat, and at the point of death, gave him permission to do so: (K, TA:) whereupon, after saying these words, he recited some verses, and died. (TA.)

definition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ jizoEN , (Kr, K,) but IDrd ascribes the latter to the vulgar, (TA,) [The onyx;
sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ jizoEN , (Kr, K,) but IDrd ascribes the latter to the vulgar, (TA,) [The onyx; so called in the present day;] certain beads, or gems, ( xarazN ,) (Msb,) the beads, or gems, ( xaraz , [here rendered by Golius “ Murœna seu concha Veneris, ” though he also gives what I regard as the only correct signification, namely “ onyx, ”]) of El-Yemen (S, K) [and] of China, (K) in which are whiteness and blackness, (S, Msb, K,) and to which eyes are likened, (S, K,) and in particular, by Imra-el-Keys, the eyes of wild animals, because their eyes, while they are alive, are black, but when they die, their whiteness appears; (TA;) a kind of stone having many colours, brought from El-Yemen and China; (Kzw;) so called because interrupted by various colours; its blackness being interrupted by its whiteness and its yellowness: (IB:) 'Áïsheh's necklace [which she lost on the occasion that subjected her to the accusation of adultery] was of jazoE of Dhafári: (TA:) the wearing it in a signet induces anxiety, or disquietude of mind, and grief, and terrifying dreams, and altercation with men; and if the hair of one who experiences difficulty in bringing forth be wound upon it, she brings forth at once: (K: [and Kzw says the like, and more of a similar kind:]) n. un. jazoEapN (Msb, K, * TA) and jizoEapN . (K, * TA.) -A2- See also what next follows.

definition: A little, or small quantity, of property, or wealth;
sourceDefinition: A little, or small quantity, of property, or wealth; and of water, (S, K,) remaining in a skin, (Lh, IDrd,) and in a leathern bottle, or other vessel, (IDrd,) and in a pool left by a torrent, but not in a well, (TA,) as also ↓ juzoEapN (IDrd, K) and [the dim.] ↓ juzayoEapN , (IDrd,) and of milk, in a skin; (Lh;) or a third part, or nearly that quantity, of water, in a trough, or tank; (ISh;) or a quantity of water, and of milk, less than the half of the skin or other vessel, and of the trough; (TA;) and, as also ↓ juzoEapN , somewhat remaining; (O, K;) or the latter, particularly, of milk; (IAar;) or both, accord. to some, [ a remainder consisting of ] less than half; (TA;) and the former, a portion [ not defined ] of property, or wealth; (S;) and particularly a portion of a flock of sheep or goats; (Aboo-Leylà, K;) as also ↓ juzayoEapN ; (S;) thus in the handwriting of Aboo-Sahl El-Harawee; but in the Mj of IF, ↓ jaziyEapN , of the measure faEiylapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN : (TA:) the pl. of jizoEapN is jizaEN . (ISh.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (tropical:) A part, or portion, of the night, (S, O, K,) past or to come, (TA,) less than half, (O, K,) of the former part thereof or of the latter part. (K.) -A2- A place in which is a collection of trees (K, TA) among which the camels or other beasts are made to rest at night from the cold, and are confined when they are hungry, or returning from water, or under rain. (TA.) -A3- Also n. un. of jizoEN as syn. with jazoEN . (TA.)

definition: Interrupted by various colours [ like the jazoE or onyx ]: (IB:) or anything in which are blackness and whiteness;
sourceDefinition: Interrupted by various colours [ like the jazoE or onyx ]: (IB:) or anything in which are blackness and whiteness; as also ↓ mujaz~iEN : (K:) and flesh-meat in which are whiteness and redness. (TA.) [Hence,] nuwFY mujaz~aEN and ↓ mujaz~iEN Datestones of which some, or some parts, have been scraped, or abraded, so as to have become white, the rest being left of their [ original ] colour: (K:) likened to the jazoE . (TA.) And ↓ busorN majaz~iEN (S, K) and mujaz~aEN ; (K;) the former, says Sh, accord. to El-Ma'arree, but he adds that he himself held the latter to be the right; Az says that he heard the former from the people of Hejer, and it has the authority of A' Obeyd; (TA;) Full-grown dates that have ripened to the half; (K, TA;) from the bottom: (TA:) or to the extent of two thirds: (S:) or that have become partly ripe: (TA:) fem. with p : (S, K:) and in like manner you say ↓ tamorN mutajaz~iEN dates that have ripened to the half. (TA.)

definition: The spathe of the palm-tree;
sourceDefinition: The spathe of the palm-tree; the envelope of the TaloE ; (AA, A'Obeyd, S, K;) as also jub~N ; (AA, TA;) or [in other words] the qiyqaA=' of the TlE ; (K;) i. e., the envelope that is with the waliyE : (Lth, K:) or, as some say, the envelope of the TlE when it has become dry: (TA:) pl. jufuwfN . (A' Obeyd, TA.) [See jub~N .] ― -b2- A receptacle such as is termed wiEaA=' that is not to be tied round at its mouth. (K, TA.) ― -b3- An old, worn-out water-skin or milk-skin, of which half is cut off and made into a bucket: (S, K:) and sometimes it is made of the lower part of a palm-tree hollowed out: (Lth, S, K: *) or a thing that is hollowed out in ( fiY [probably a mistranscription for min , i. e. of ]) the trunks of palm-trees: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or a worn-out milk-skin or butter-skin: (IAar, TA:) or a water-skin, or milk-skin, of which part is cut off at the fore legs, and in which the beverage called nabiy* is prepared: (Kt, TA:) or the lower half of a water-skin or milk-skin, made into a bucket: (IDrd, TA:) or a thing of camel's skin, like a vessel, or like a bucket, in which the rainwater is taken, holding half the quantity of a water-skin or the like. (TA.) ― -b4- An old man; (K;) as being likened to an old, worn-out water-skin or milk-skin: mentioned in the L from ElHejeree, and by Sgh from Ibn-'Abbád. (TA.) ― -b5- Anything hollow, such as has something within it, like the nut, and the magodap [or fruit of the tanoDub , &c.: in the CK, the maEidap ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, K, TA.) ― -b6- The body, or substance, ( $axoS ,) of a thing. (TA.) ― -b7- An obstruction that one sees between him and the kibleh. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) -A2- huwa juf~u maAlK He is a good manager of cattle, (K,) acquainted with the art of pasturing them, and of collecting them at their proper time in the place of pasture. (TA.) -A3- See also what next follows.

definition: He broke his side: (S, K:) or he hit, or hurt, his side.
sourceDefinition: He broke his side: (S, K:) or he hit, or hurt, his side. (TA.) [The aor. of the verb in this sense is probably , and the inf. n., accord. to the TK, is janobN .] ― -b2- He led him by his side; (S, A, * Msb, K;) namely, a horse (S, A, Msb, TA) or the like, (S, A,) and a captive. (S, TA.) In this sense, its aor. is , (A, Msb, TA,) and the inf. n. janabN (S, A, Msb, K) and majonabN . (K.) Hence, TawoEu Aljanabi : see janabN .jinaAbN which is forbidden (S, A, TA) in a trad., [in which it is said, laA jalaba walaA janaba ] (A, TA) relating to horse-racing and to [the collecting of] the poor-rate, (TA,) means [in the former case] A man's leading, by the side of a horse that he rides in a race, another horse, (S, A, K,) without a rider, (TA,) and when the horse that he rides has become languid and weak, (K,) or when he fears that he will not outstrip upon it, (S,) or when he draws near to the goal, (A,) transferring himself to the other, (S, A, K,) in order that he may outstrip: (A:) and in relation to the poorrate, it means the collector's alighting in the most remote of the places whence the portion appointed for the poor-rate is to be collected, and then ordering that the camels or the like [ that constitute that portion ] shall be led to him: or the going of the owner of the property to a distance, [or aside, or out of the way, ] with his property, so that the collector is obliged to go to a distance in quest of it. (K. See more in art. jlb , first paragraph.) ― -b3- He placed, or put, at a distance, or he put, or sent, away, or far away, or far off, or he removed far away, alienated, or estranged, him, or it; (K;) as though he put him, or it, aside, or as though he walked aside; as also ↓ jAnbhu (TA.) And He pushed, thrust, or drove, him, or it, away, aside, or to a distance. (K, * TA.) And janabahu Al$~aYo'a (S, K, *) or Al$~ar~a (Fr, Zj, Msb,) aor. ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ jn~bhu , (Fr, Zj, S, A, Msb, K,) but this has an intensive signification; (Msb;) and ↓ Ajnbhu ; (Fr, Zj, A, K;) He put aside, or away, or he warded off, from him, (S,) or he removed from him, (S, Msb, K,) or removed far from him, (Msb, K,) the thing, (S, K, *) or evil. (Fr, Zj, A, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xiv. 38], waA@jonuboniY wabaniY~a A^ano naEobuda AlA^aSonaAma [ And put Thou away from me and my sons our worshipping of idols ], (S,) or, accord. to one reading, ↓ waA^ajoniboniY . (TA.) ― -b4- He yearned towards, longed for, or desired, him, or it. (K, * TA.) -A2- janaba bihi , aor. , [ He went aside, apart, out of the way, to a distance, or far away, with him, or it: or, like janabahu , in a sense explained above,] he placed, or put, at a distance, or he put, or sent, away, or far away, or far off, him, or it. (K, TA.) ― -b2- janaba fiY baniY fulaAnK , (S, K, *) aor. , inf. n. janaAbapN ; (S;) and ↓ tjn~b ; (so, app., in the TA;) He alighted, or descended and abode, or settled, as a stranger, among the sons of such a one. (S, K, * TA.) One says, niEoma Alqawomu humo lijaAri AljanaAbapi [ Excellent are the people, they, ] to the neighbour who is a stranger. (S. [See also junubN .]) And laA taHoriman~iY Eano janaAbapK Do not thou by any means refuse me because of being remote (S, A, TA) in respect of relationship. (A, TA.) [See also janaAbapN mentioned below as a subst.] ― -b3- janabati Alr~iyHu , (S, A, K,) aor. (TA,) inf. n. junuwbN ; (K;) and ↓ Ajnbt ; (TA;) The wind was, or became, such as is termed januwb [i. e. south, or southerly ]; (K;) it blew in the direction of the wind thus called: (A, TA:) or the former, (S,) or janibat , (TA,) the wind changed, or veered, so as to become januwb (S, TA.) ― -b4- [And hence, (see januwbN ,)] janaba A_ilayohi , (IAar, K,) or A_ilaY liqaAy^ihi , (TA,) aor. ; (K;) and janiba , aor. ; (Th, K;) [inf. n., app., janobN , for the verb is said in the K to be like naSara and samiEa ;] (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, disquieted by vehement desire to see him, or to meet him. (K, * TA.) -A3- janiba , aor. , (S,) inf. n. janabN , (S, K,) He (a camel) limped, or halted, by reason of [ pain in ] his side: (S:) or he had an affection resembling ZaloE [i. e. limping, or halting ], (K, TA,) but not the same as this: (TA:) and, (K,) or accord. to As, (S,) his lungs clave to his side by reason of vehement thirst: (S, K:) or, accord. to the Arabs of the desert, as ISk says, he became bent, or contorted, by reason of vehemence of thirst: (S:) and he (a camel) had a pain in his side from vehemence of thirst. (TA.) The epithet is ↓ janibN ; which is applied by Dhu-r-Rummeh to an ass. (S, TA.) ― -b2- jnbt Ald~alowu [app. janibat ] The bucket inclined to one side in consequence of the breaking of one or two of the thongs attacking it to the cross-bars. (L, TA.) -A4- janiba and januba and janaba are syn. with A^ajonaba in a sense explained below: see 4. -A5- juniba He had, or became affected by, the disease termed *aAtu Aljanobi [or pleurisy ]: (S, Mgh, Msb:) he had a complaint of his side. (K.) -A6- junibuwA They were, or became, affected by the [ south, or southerly, wind called ] junuwb . (S, A, K.) And also, [in allusion to the fertilizing effect attributed to the wind so called,] They were, or became, affected by that wind in their cattle. (L, TA.)

(K.) ― -b2- jn~b Alqawomu The milk of the people's camels became little: (S:) or the people's milk ceased; (K, TA;) or became little: or the people's camels had no milk: and jn~b said of a man, his camels had no milk, nor had his sheep or goats. (TA.) Hence, EaAmu tajoniybK [ A year of little, or no, milk ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- jn~bt AlA^ibilu The camels, with the exception of one or two, brought forth no young. (AZ, TA.) The camels did not conceive, so as to have milk. (TA.) -A3- tajoniybN [as an inf. n. of which the verb, if it have one in any of the following senses, is jun~iba ,] also signifies A bending, or curving, and tension [ of the sinews ] ( tawotiyrN ), of the hind leg of a horse; which is a quality approved: (S, K:) or, accord. to AO, a turning aside of his fore legs in raising them and putting them down: but accord. to As, it is in the kind legs, and taHoniybN is in the back-bone and in the fore legs. (TA.) [See also 2 in art Hnb ; and see also mujan~abN .]

sourceDefinition: , (A, K,) inf. n. mujaAnabapN and jinaAbN , (K,) He was, or became, at, or by, his side: (A, K:) and he walked, or went, by his side. (A.) -A2- Also i. q. baA Eadahu ; (A, K;) i. e. He was, or became, [ distant, remote, far off, or aloof, from him; or] apart from him; or in a part, quarter, or tract, different from that in which he (the other) was; (TA;) thus bearing two contr. significations. (A, K.) jAnbhu and ↓ tjAnbhu and ↓ tjn~buhu and ↓ Ajtnbhu all signify the same, (S, K,) i. e. He was, or became, distant, remote, far off, or aloof, or he went, or removed, or retired, or withdrew himself, to a distance, or far away, or far off, or he alienated, or estranged, himself, or he stood, or kept, aloof, from him, or it; he shunned, or avoided, him, or it; as also ↓ jin~bh (K) [and minohu ↓ tjn~b ]. You say, jaAnibi All~iy^aAma [ Remove thyself far from the mean, or ignoble; stand, or keep, aloof from them; shun, or avoid, them ]. (A.) And laj~a fiY jinaAbK qabiyHK He persisted in removing himself to a distance, or estranging himself, from his family. (S, A, K. [In two copies of the S, I find jnAb here written with fet-h to the j ; but it is expressly said in the TA to be with kesr.]) ― -b2- See also 1.

definition: , a word of well-known meaning;
sourceDefinition: , a word of well-known meaning; (S;) The side, or half, or lateral half, syn. $iq~N , (A, K,) of a man &c.; as also ↓ jaAnibN and ↓ janabapN : (K:) or the part of a man that is beneath the arm-pit, extending to the flank; as also ↓ jaAnibN , because it is the side of the person: (Msb:) pl. (of the first, Msb) junuwbN (Msb, K) and [of the same, a pl. of pauc.,] A^ajonaAbN (CK) and [of jaAnibN ] jawaAnibu (Lh, ISd, K, but not in the CK) and [app. of janobN (like as layaAy^ilu is a pl. of layolN ) or of janabapN (like as HawaAy^iju is pl. of HaAjapN which is originally HawajapN ) or of both these] ↓ janAy^ibu (M, K,) which is extr. (M, TA.) [Hence,] qaEadotu A_ilaY janobi fulaAnK and flAn ↓ AlY jaAnibi [ I sat by the side of such a one ]: both meaning the same. (S.) And ↓ A_in~ahu lamunotafixu AljawaAnibi [ Verily he is inflated in the side ]: jwAnb being here one of those words which are used in the sing. sense though in the pl. form. (Lh, TA.) And A^aEoTaAhu Aljanoba [lit. He gave him the side; meaning] he was, or became, submissive, manageable, easy, or tractable, to him. (A.) And jaAru Aljanobi He who cleaves to one, keeping by one's side. (K. [Differing from jaAru Aljunubi , q. v. infrà.]) And AlS~aAHibu biAljanobi [in the Kur iv. 40] The travelling-companion; the companion in a journey: (S, K:) or he who is near one; or by one's side: or the companion in every good affair: or the husband: or the wife. (TA.) And *aAtu Aljanobi , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) with which ↓ AljunaAbu is syn., (K,) [and sometimes Aljanobu , as will be seen in what follows,] A well-known disease; (Mgh;) [ the pleurisy; called by the first of these three appellations in the present day;] a severe disease, being an inflammatory tumour in the [ pleura, or] membrane within the ribs: (Msb:) or an ulcer, or a purulent pustule, that comes within a man's side: (S, TA:) it is a severe disease in the side: accord. to El-Hejeree, it is in either side; and they assert that when it is in the left side, the patient perishes: accord. to ISh, the dubayolap ; which is an ulcer that penetrates into the belly: or the ulcer ( dubayolap and dum~al ) that comes forth within the side, and discharges internally; the sufferer from which seldom recovers: he who suffers from it [and dies in consequence], or, as some say, he who is afflicted by a complaint of the side (absolutely) while warring in the cause of God, is reckoned a martyr: (TA:) [soldiers in a campaign are notoriously more subject to it than persons in most other circumstances; and it is app. for this reason that] it is termed daA='u AlS~anaAdiydi [the disease of the courageous chiefs]. (A, TA.) *uw Aljanobi , of which *aAtu Aljunobi is the fem., signifies Having a complaint of his side by reason of [ the disease above mentioned, or what is termed ] Ald~ubayolap . (TA. [See also majonuwbN .]) ― -b2- A poet says, Aln~aAsu janobN waAlA^amiyru janobu [ The people are a side and the prince is a side ]: (Akh, S, TA:) as though he reckoned the latter equal to all the people. (TA. [This is cited in the S and TA as though it were an ex. of jnb in the sense here next following: but it seems to be rather an ex. of this word in the sense first explained in the present paragraph.]) ― -b3- I. q. naAHiyapN [ A side; meaning a lateral, or an outward or adjacent, part or portion, region, quarter, or tract; or a part, region, quarter, or tract, considered with respect to its collocation or juxtaposition or direction, or considered as belonging to a whole; a vicinage, or neighbourhood ]; (S, K;) as also ↓ jaAnibN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ janaAbN and ↓ janobapN (S, K) and ↓ janabapN (S) and ↓ janaAbapN . (L, TA.) It is said that the primary signification of janobN is the part of the body mentioned in the beginning of this paragraph, and that its use in the sense of naAHyapN is metaphorical, as is the case of yamiynN and $imaAlN ; but naAHiyapN is mentioned in the Msb as the primary signification of ↓ jaAnibN ; (MF, TA;) though its primary signification accord. to the K and ISd seems to be that first mentioned. (TA.) You say, ↓ ma$awoA jaAnibayohi and ↓ janaAbayohi and ↓ janobatayohi and ↓ janaAbatayohi [ They walked, or went on foot, on either side of him ]. (A, TA. *) And ↓ mar~uwA yasiyruwna janaAbayohi (S, L) and ↓ janobatayohi and ↓ janaAbatayohi (L, TA) They went along journeying on either side of him. (S, L.) And kun~aA Eanohumo ↓ janaA bayoni and ↓ janaAbFA We were apart from them [ on two sides and on one side ]. (TA.) And nazaluwA AlwaAdiY ↓ fiY janaAbaAti [ They alighted in the sides of the valley, or in the tracts beside the valley ]. (A.) And ↓ fulaAnN laA yaTuwru bijanabatinaA Such a one will not approach our quarter: (S:) thus accord. to AO; with fet-h to the n : IJ, however, says, people are wont to say, ↓ A^anaA fiY *araAka wajanabatika [meaning I am under thy protection and in thy quarter ]; but that the correct expression is ↓ janobatika , with the n quiescent. (IB, TA.) The Arabs also said, suhayolK ↓ AlHar~u jaAnibaYo , meaning (assumed tropical:) The heat is on either side of Suheyl [or Canopus: i. e., during the period next before, and that next after, the auroral rising of Canopus; which rising began, in central Arabia, at the commencement of the era of the Flight, about the 4th of August, O. S.]: this is the greatest heat. (TA.) One also says, ↓ A^aHaATuwA bihi mino jaAnibayohi [meaning They surrounded him on all his sides; lit., on his two sides ]; dividing the surrounding parts into two, but not meaning that any of these remained vacant. (Expos. of the exs. cited as testimonies by Sb, TA in art. Hwl .) ― -b4- Also, [and ↓ jaAnibN , which is thus used in the L in art. jnH , and by many authors,] A part, or portion, of a thing; (L;) the greater, or main, or chief, part or portion thereof; most thereof; (L, K;) or a great part or portion thereof; much thereof. (L.) Hence, [or perhaps from janobN in the second of the senses assigned to it above, conveying the idea of juxtaposition, and thus of comparison,] h`*aA qaliylN janobi mawad~atika [ This is little in comparison with the magnitude of thy love; or simply, in comparison with thy love ]. (TA.) ― -b5- yaA HasorataA EalaY maA far~aTotu fiY jnobi A@ll~`hi [in the Kur xxxix. 57] means ↓ fY jaAnibih , i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ O my grief, or regret, for my negligence, or remissness, ] in respect of that which is the right, or due, of God! (A, Bd, TA,) i. e., (Bd,) in respect of obedience to God! (Bd, Jel:) or, in respect of [ the means of attaining ] nearness to God! (Fr, TA;) or, nearness to God in Paradise! (IAar, TA:) or, in respect of the way of God, to which He hath called me! i. e., the profession of his unity, and the confession of the prophetic office of Mohammad. (Zj, TA.) The saying of the Arabs, Ait~aqi A@ll~`ha fiY janobihi walaA taqodaHo fiY saAqihi [may be rendered (assumed tropical:) Fear God in respect of his (thy brother's) right, or due, and impugn not his honour, or reputation: or] means, accord. to the copies of the K, laA taqotulohu [ slay him not ], or, as in the L, and in the original draught of the author [of the K] lA tagotalohu [ slay him not clandestinely, or on an occasion of inadvertence ], from Algiylapu , and throw him not into trouble, or trial: (TA:) or, accord. to some, fY jnbh means in detracting from his reputation, or reviling him. (K, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 240.]) A poet, cited by IAar, says, xaliylaY~a kuf~aA waA@*okuraA A@ll~`ha fiY janobiY (assumed tropical:) [ O my two friends, refrain, and be mindful of God in respect of my reputation; (see also jaAnibN ;)] meaning, in detracting from my reputation, or reviling me: or, accord. to MF, in my case. (TA.) And one says, maA faEalota fiY janobi HaAjatiY (assumed tropical:) What didst thou, or what hast thou done, in the case of the thing that I want? (L, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (El-Fárábee, S, A, Msb, K,) which is sometimes used in the sing. form as pl., and has no fem. form, (TA,) and ↓ jaAnibN and ↓ A^ajonabiY~N , (El-Fárábee, S, Msb, K,) which is said by Az in art. rwH to be seldom or never used by the Arabs, but is mentioned by him in its proper art., (Msb,) and ↓ A^ajonabu , (Az, S, Msb, K,) are syn., (El-Fárábee, S, Msb, K,) signifying A stranger; (K;) as also ↓ janiybN : (S:) or a man who is distant, or remote: (Msb:) or distant, or remote, in respect of relationship: (Az and Msb in explanation of the third and fourth:) [or not a relation; as will be seen from what follows:] and ↓ jaAnibN [as an act. part. n.] signifies one alighting, or descending and abiding, or settling, as a stranger, among a tribe: (S:) pl. of the first A^ajonaAbN , (A, TA,) and of the second jun~aAbN , (S, TA,) and of the fourth A^ajaAnibu . (Msb.) AljaAru Aljunubu [occurring in the Kur iv. 40] (T, S, A, Msb, K) and jaAru Aljunubi (TA) The person who is one's neighbour, but who belongs to another people; (T, S, A, Msb, K;) who is not of one's family nor of one's lineage; (A;) who is of another lineage than he of whom he is a neighbour; (T, TA;) who is not a relation: (MF:) or one who is distant, or remote, in an absolute sense: (TA:) or the person who is not a relation to another, and who comes to him, and asks him to protect him, and abides with him: such has the title to respect that belongs to him as neighbour of the other, and to his protection, and as relying upon his safeguard and promise. (TA in art. jwr . [Differing from jaAru Aljanobi , q. v. suprà.]) It is said in a trad., humo A^ajonaAbu Aln~aAsi They are the strangers of mankind, or of the people. (TA.) And in another trad., qaAla lijaAriy~pK halo mino mugaribapi Alxabaru ↓ xabarK qaAlato EalaY jaAnibK [ He said to a girl, Is there any news from abroad? She answered, ] It is for a stranger coming from a journey [ to give such news ]. (TA.) And one says, huwa min~iY ↓ A^ajonabiY~N [ He is a person not related to me ]. (A.) ― -b2- Also, ↓ the same four words, (of which only the last is mentioned in this sense in the S,) That will not be led; intractable. (K.) ― -b3- junubN is also an epithet from AljanaAbapu ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) signifying A man under the obligation of performing a total ablution, by reason of sexual intercourse and discharge of the semen: (IAth, TA: [see 4:]) and is used alike as masc. and fem. (S, Mgh, Msb) and sing. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and dual (Msb, TA) and pl.; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) being regarded as quasi-coordinate to the class of inf. ns.; for the inf. n., when used as an epithet, must remain, in form, sing. and masc.: (MF in art. Eft :) or one may use the dual form junubaAni ; (K;) and sometimes they used the pl. A^ajonaAbN (S, Msb, K *) and junubuwna , (S, Msb,) and the fem. pl. junubaAtN ; (Msb;) but not junubapN , (K, TA,) applied to a female. (TA.) It is said in a trad., laA tadoxulu AlmalaAy^ikapu biyotFA fiyhi junubN , meaning [ The angels will not enter a house, or chamber, or tent, in which is ] one who usually neglects the total ablution when under an obligation to perform it for the cause above mentioned. (IAth, TA.)

(TA.) You say, rajulN *uw janobapK A man of retirement. (TA.) And nazala janobapF He alighted, or descended and abode, or settled, in a place aside, or apart. (S, TA.) And qaEada janobapF He [ sat apart, or] retired from others. (A, TA.) ― -b4- The state of being a stranger; as also ↓ janaAbapN . (K. (TA.) -A2- Also, janobapN , A piece of skin from the side of a camel, (S, L, K, *) of which is made a kind of milking vessel ( Eulobap ), (S, L,) larger than the miEolaq , but smaller than the jawobap . (L.) -A3- And Every kind of plant, (S,) or every kind of tree in general, (K,) that produces [ new leaves such as are termed ] rabol in the season of the Sayof [which may mean either summer or spring ]: (S, K:) or every kind of plant that produces leaves in that season without rain: (TA:) or a name given to many plants, all of them Euruwq [perhaps meaning resembling roots, i. e. straggling, or spreading like roots ]; so called because less than large trees and higher than those that have no root-stock ( A^aruwmap ) in the earth; comprising the naSiY~ and Sil~iyaAn and HamaAT and makor and H*r [so in the TA, but I do not find it elsewhere, and think it may be a mistranscription for Hazor , of which Hazorap (the name of a certain sour tree) is probably the n. un.,] and dahomaA=' ; which are smaller than $ajar and superior to buquwl : all this has been heard from the Arabs: (T, TA:) or green and fresh Sl~yAn : (TA:) or what is [ of a kind ] between baqol and $ajar ; (AHn, K, TA;) being [in the TA whmA , but this is evidently a mistake for wahiYa ,] of the kind of which the root remains in the winter while the branches perish: (AHn, TA:) or herbage of which the root is deep in the earth; such as the naSiY~ and the Sil~iyaAn . (TA voce xaDirN .)

definition: [Hence,] kun~aA Eanohumo janaAbayoni and janaAbFA We were remote, or retired, from them;
sourceDefinition: : see janobN , in five places. [Hence,] kun~aA Eanohumo janaAbayoni and janaAbFA We were remote, or retired, from them; or out of their way. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, (S, A, Msb, K,) and ↓ jaAnibN , (Msb, * TA,) A court, or yard, or an open or a wide space in front of a house or extending from its sides: (S, A, K, TA:) and a place of alighting or abode; or a settlement, or place of settling: (A:) a mansion; an abode; a habitation; or a place to which a man betakes himself, or repairs, for lodging, covert, or refuge, in a city or town or village or other place of settled habitations; syn. raHolN : (K:) and a vicinage, neighbourhood, or tract adjacent to the place of abode or settlement, of a people or company of men: pl. A^ajonibapN . (S.) You say, A^anaA fiY janaAbi zayodK I am in the court, or yard, of Zeyd; and in his place of alighting or abode, or settlement. (A, TA.) And fulaAnN raHobu AljanaAbi , (A, TA,) and xaSiybu AljanaAbi , (S, A,) the former meaning Such a one is possessed of an ample raHol [or mansion, &c., as explained above]: (TA:) [and the latter, such a one is surrounded by a plentiful, or fruitful, tract: ] or both mean (tropical:) such a one is generous or bountiful [or hospitable ]. (A.) And falaAnN jadiybu AljanaAbi (S, TA) [meaning Such a one is environed by a tract affected with drought, or barrenness; as explained in the S in art. jdb : but generally used tropically, as meaning (assumed tropical:) such a one is ungenerous, illiberal, or inhospitable ]. And A^axoSaba janaAbu Alqawomi [ The neighbourhood of the people, or the tract surrounding them, became plentiful, or fruitful ]. (S, TA.) And A^ajodaba binaA AljanaAbu [ Our neighbourhood, or the tract surrounding us, became affected with drought, or barrenness ]. (TA from a trad.) ― -b3- rajulN lay~inu AljanaAbi [perhaps a mistranscription for AljaAnibi ] (tropical:) A man easy to deal with, compliant, or obsequious. (A.) ― -b4- [ AljanaAbu is also a title often given by writers of letters and the like to any great man to whom others betake themselves, or repair, for protection; and sometimes to God; meaning (tropical:) The object of recourse; the refuge; the asylum: similar to AlHaDorapu , q. v., and used in the same manner, i. e., alone, and, without the article, prefixed to the name of the person to whom it is applied, or to a pronoun; but the latter is generally considered as implying greater respect than the former.]

definition: , aor. , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. Haj~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He repaired, or betook himself, to, or towards, syn. qaSada , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) a person (S, A, Mgh) [or place], in an absolute sense:...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. Haj~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He repaired, or betook himself, to, or towards, syn. qaSada , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) a person (S, A, Mgh) [or place], in an absolute sense: or to, or towards, an object of reverence, veneration, respect, or honour: or, accord. to Kh, he repaired, or betook himself, much, or frequently, to, or towards, an object of this kind: and also he repaired to, betook himself to, or visited, a person: (TA:) and he went to, or visited, a person repeatedly, or frequently. (ISk, T, S, Mgh, K. *) You say also, Haj~a banuw fulaAnK fulaAnFA The sons of such a one continued long going repeatedly to visit such a one. (S.) ― -b2- Hence, (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) and inf. n. Hij~N also, (Sb, L,) or this is a simple subst., (S, Msb, K,) by a conventional usage, (S,) or predominantly, (Mgh,) or by restriction of its usage in the law, (Msb,) He repaired to Mekkeh, (S, K,) or to the Kaabeh, (Mgh, Msb,) to perform the religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) or for the purpose of the Eumorap [q. v.; but this latter meaning is very rare: the usual meaning is, he performed the pilgrimage to Mekkeh and Mount' Arafát, with all the rites and ceremonies prescribed to be observed at, and between, those two places ]: (Msb:) or he repaired to the House [ of God, at Mekkeh, ] and performed the actions prescribed for that occasion by the law of the Kur-án and the Sunneh. (L.) [See Haj~N , below.] You say also, Haj~a Alayota , aor. , inf. n. Haj~N , (T, S,) and ↓ AHtj~hu , (El-Hejeree, TA,) He performed the pilgrimage to the House [ of God, at Mekkeh ]; (T, S;) because people repair to it every year. (T, TA.) And Haj~uwA mak~apa [ They performed the pilgrimage to Mekkeh ]. (A.) And maA Haj~a wal`kin~ahu daj~a He did not repair to Mekkeh to visit the House of God, (Aboo-Tálib, Az,) or for the performance of the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage, (Msb,) but he journeyed for mercantile purposes. (Aboo-Tálib, Az, Msb. [See also art. dj .]) And hence, accord. to some, laj~a faHaj~a , a prov., which see below. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, (TA,) inf. n. Haj~N , (K,) He came, or arrived. (K, TA.) You say, Haj~a EalayonaA fulaAnN Such a one came to us. (TA.) -A2- Also, [aor., accord. to rule, as above,] inf. n. Haj~N , He shaved [his head; as one does on completing the performance of the rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage: see Haj~N , below]. (TA.) -A3- Also, (IAar, A, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. Haj~N , (TA,) He probed a fracture of the head, (K,) or a wound, (A, TA,) with a miHojaAj , (A, K,) or miyl , (TA,) for the purpose of curing it: (TA:) or he probed a wound to know its depth: (IAar, TA:) or he examined a cleft in the head to know whether there were in it bone or blood: (ISh, TA:) or he dressed and cured a wound in the head reaching to the brain: or he poured boiled clarified butter upon a fracture of the head, in consequence of which the blood was mixed with the brain, until the blood appeared, which he took away with a little cotton: (TA:) or Haj~ahu , inf. n. Haj~N , signifies he probed a fracture of his head for the purpose of curing it: (S:) or he made a perforation in the bone [ of his broken head ] ( qadaHa fiyhi ) with an iron instrument, it being broken so that the brain was befouled with blood, and pulled off the skin that had dried up, and then cured it, so that it closed up with a [ new ] skin: it relates to a wound reaching to the brain. (L.) ― -b2- Also, aor. , inf. n. Haj~N , He cut out and extracted a bone from a wound. (TA.) -A4- Also, (A, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. Haj~u , (K,) He overcame another in, or by, an argument, a plea, an alle- gation, a proof, an evidence, or a testimony. (A, Msb, K.) See 3. It is said in a prov., laj~a faHaj~a (S, TA) He was pertinacious in litigation, dispute, or altercation, and overcame therein [as is implied in the S, and expressed in the TA]: or he persevered until he performed the pilgrimage [not having intended to do so when he set out: see Freytag's “ Arab. Prov. ” ii. 452]. (TA.) -A5- Also, (TA,) [aor., accord. to rule, ,] inf. n. Haj~N ; (K;) and ↓ HajoHaja , (K,) inf. n. HajoHajapN ; (TA;) He refrained, forbore, or abstained, (K, TA,) Eano $aYo'K from a thing. (TA.) [See also the latter verb below.]

definition: and ↓ Hij~N , the former an inf.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ Hij~N , the former an inf. n., and the latter a simple subst., (S, Msb, K,) or the latter also is an inf. n., (Sb, L,) [both used as substs.,] The pilgrimage to Mekkeh, (S, K,) or to the Kaabeh, (Msb,) to perform the religious rites and ceremonies prescribed to be observed on that occasion: (S, Msb, K:) Ks makes no difference between these two words: some say that the former is employed to signify the religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage because they follow the repairing to Mekkeh, or because they are completed by shaving [the head], or because people continue long going to and fro to perform them: accord. to Az, it signifies the performance of the religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage of one year; and some say ↓ Hij~N and ↓ Hij~apN : (TA:) or this last signifies a single pilgrimage, for the performance of its appointed religious rites and ceremonies; deviating from rule; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) for by rule it should be ↓ Haj~apN , (S, Mgh, K,) which, Th says, has not been heard from the Arabs: (Mgh, Msb:) Ks says that ↓ Hajajotu Hij~apF and raA^ayotu ruw^oyapF are the only deviations from the model of faEalotu faEolapF in all the language of the Arabs: but El-Athram and others are related to have said, We have not heard from the Arabs Hajajotu Hij~apF nor raA^ayotu riy^oyapF ; they saying only ↓ Hajajotu Haj~apF : (L, TA:) whence it appears that ↓ Haj~apN and ↓ Hij~apN were both used: (TA:) the pl. of the latter is HijajN : (Mgh, Msb:) so in the saying, na*ara xamosa HijajK [ He made a vow to perform five pilgrimages ]. (Mgh.) Hence, ↓ *uw AlHij~api (S, Mgh, Msb) and ↓ *w AlHaj~api , (Msb, TA,) which latter is said by Kz and 'Iyád and Ibn- Kurkool to be the more common, (TA,) [or, accord. to Fei, the contr. is the case, for he says,] some pronounce it in the latter manner, (Msb,) [ The last month of the Arabian calendar; ] the month of the pilgrimage; (S, Mgh, Msb;) so called because the pilgrimage to Mekkeh, and the religious rites and ceremonies thereof, are performed in it: (TA:) pl. *awaAtu AlHj~hi : (S, Msb:) they did not say *awuw AlHaj~pi agreeably with the singular. (S.) [Hence also,] ↓ waHaj~api A@ll~`hi laA A^afoEalu [ By the pilgrimage which is the ordinance of God, I will not do this or that thing]: a form of oath used by the Arabs. (S, K.) What is commonly termed AlHaj~u is sometimes termed AlHaj~u AlA^akobaru [ The greater pilgrimage ]: AlEumorapu [q. v.] being termed AlHaj~a AlA^aSogaru [ the minor pilgrimage ]. (Kull p. 168.) ― -b2- See also HaAj~N .

definition: A mode [ of argument or the like ] by which one overcomes in a litigation, dispute, or altercation;
sourceDefinition: A mode [ of argument or the like ] by which one overcomes in a litigation, dispute, or altercation; so called because recourse is had to it ( liA^an~ahaA tuHaj~u , i. e. tuqoSadu ): (T, TA:) that by which one rebuts, or refels, an adversary in a litigation, dispute, or altercation: an argument; a plea; an allegation: [it may be true or false: see Kur xlii. 15, and xlv. 24:] (TA:) a proof; an evidence; a testimony: (S, Msb, K:) [ a title; a voucher: often thus used in the present day:] also applied to a person; like vabatN ; (A and Mgh and TA in art. vbt ;) [as in the saying, mano HifiZa Huj~apN EalaY mano lamo yaHofaZo He who preserves in his mind a word, or an authority, &c., is an evidence against him who does not; occurring often in the larger lexicons, expressing the superior authority of hearsay, or usage, over analogy &c.; and in the saying,] A^anota Huj~apN EalaY nafosika [ Thou art an evidence against thyself ]; a phrase mentioned by Akh: (S in art. bSr :) [also, an excuse: ] pl. HujajN (A, Msb) and HijaAjN . (TA.)

definition: and ↓ HijaAjN The surrounding bone of the eye, (Msb, TA,) upon [ the upper part of ] which grows the eyebrow;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ HijaAjN The surrounding bone of the eye, (Msb, TA,) upon [ the upper part of ] which grows the eyebrow; (TA;) the bone that surrounds the cavity of the eye, upon [ the upper part of ] which grows the hair of the eyebrow: (ISk, TA:) it is said in a trad. that a female hyena and her young ones were within the HjAj of the eye of an Amalekite: (TA:) or the [ supra-orbital ] bone upon which grows the hair of the eyebrow; (S, K;) the bone that projects over the cavity of the eye: (IAmb, Msb:) or the upper bone, beneath the eyebrow: (TA:) of the mase. gender: (Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aHij~apN (S, Msb) and [of mult.] ↓ HujujN , deviating from a general rule, accord. to which a sing. of the measure to which this belongs does not assume this form of pl. because the reduplication is disapproved: also, by poetic license, HawaAjiju , contr. to rule, for HawaAj~u . (TA.) The expression fiY HajaA HaAjibK DamorK is used by poetic license for fY HajaAji HAjb Dmr . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] both words also signify (tropical:) The upper limb of the disk ( i. q. HaAjib ) of the sun, appearing when it begins to rise. (A, K, TA: but in the A, only the latter form of the word is given.) ― -b3- Also, [hence,] both words, (tropical:) A side. (A, * K.) You say, mar~uwA biHijaAjaYi Aljabali (tropical:) They passed by the two sides of the mountain. (A.)

Huj~aAjN and ↓ HajiyjN (S, A, Msb, K) and Huj~N ; (S, K;) or rather the second of these is a quasi-pl. n., a kind of noun which, as well as the coll. gen. n., is often called by the lexicographers a pl., though not so called by the grammarians: (MF:) HaAj~N is also used as a pl., syn. with Huj~aAjN , like as saAmirN is with sum~aArN : (Mgh:) it may be considered as a gen. n., and is sometimes a quasi-pl. n., like jaAmilN and baAqirN ; (TA;) as is also ↓ Hij~N ; signifying a company of pilgrims of Mekkeh; or pilgrims, collectively; (ISk, L;) and likewise ↓ Haj~N . HawaAj~u : (S, K:) you say HawaAj~u bayoti A@ll~`hi when they have performed the pilgrimage; but when they have not yet performed it, [being in the act of performing it,] you say HawaAj~u bayota A@ll~`hi , in which latter case you would say HawaAj~N were not this word imperfectly decl.; [and in like manner, HaAj~u bayoti A@ll~`hi , and HaAj~N bayota A@ll~`hi ;] like as you say DaAribu zayodK A^amosi , and DaAribN zayodFA gadFA . HawaAj~u : (S, K:) you say HawaAj~u bayoti A@ll~`hi when they have performed the pilgrimage; but when they have not yet performed it, [being in the act of performing it,] you say HawaAj~u bayota A@ll~`hi , in which latter case you would say HawaAj~N were not this word imperfectly decl.; [and in like manner, HaAj~u bayoti A@ll~`hi , and HaAj~N bayota A@ll~`hi ;] like as you say DaAribu zayodK A^amosi , and DaAribN zayodFA gadFA . (TA. [See also art. dj .]) And walaA daAj~apF ↓ lamo yatoruko He left not a company of pilgrims to Mekkeh ( jamaAEapF HaAj~apF ), nor a company of their followers, or dependents. (TA from a trad. definition: What is guarded, kept, preserved, or taken care of.
sourceDefinition: What is guarded, kept, preserved, or taken care of. (Msb.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A thing stolen: (K:) or a sheep, or goat, that is stolen by night: (S:) of the measure faEiylapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN : (TA:) hence, Hariysapu Aljabali (S) a sheep, or goat, that is overtaken by the night before its return to its nightly resting-place, and is stolen from the mountain: (Msb:) or a sheep, or goat, that is stolen, of those that are guarded, or kept, in the mountain: or, as some say, from HaArisN applied ironically to a thief: (Mgh:) pl. HaraAy^isu (S, K.) Hence the saying, (TA,) laA qaToEa fiY Hariysapi Aljabali (tropical:) [ There shall be no amputation of the hand for the sheep, or goat, that is stolen by night from the mountain ]. (A, TA.) IF says that there are two explanations of the expression Hrysp Aljbl : some make it to signify theft, or the thing stolen, ( Als~ariqapu ,) itself: others make the meaning to be, that there shall be no amputation for [stealing] what is guarded, or kept, in the mountain, because it is not a place well protected: ISk says that AlHariysapu signifies Als~ariqapu . (Msb.) ― -b3- A wall of stones, made for sheep, or goats, (K,) to guard them. (TA.)

definition: [ Prudence, or discretion, and precaution;
sourceDefinition: [ Prudence, or discretion, and precaution; ] sound management of one's affair or case, (S, K,) and taking the sure course therein, (T, S, K,) and precaution, that it may not become beyond the power of management: (TA:) said in a trad. to consist in evil opinion: and in another, in the asking counsel of people of judgment and obeying them: (TA:) or good judgment: (Mgh:) or strength, [or firmness of mind or of judgment, (see HaAzimN ,)] and sound management: (Ham p. 33:) the first part thereof said by Aktham Ibn-Seyfee to be consultation: (Ham ibid:) from the same word as signifying the act of “ binding the HizaAm , ” (Mgh,) or from this word as signifying the act of “ binding with the HzAm , ” and “ with the rope: ” (T, TA:) and ↓ HazomapN signifies the same; as in the saying, A_in~a AlwaHaA='a mino TaEaAmi AlHazomahi [ Verily quickness is of the food of prudence, &c.], a prov., mentioned by Ibn-Kethweh, alluding to people's collecting themselves together and aiding one another, when they act with quickness, or sharpness, and vigour; and said in praise of him who thus acts. (TA.) You say, A^axa*a baAlHazomi (TA) and [sometimes] fiY AlHazomi (K in art. HwT ) [ He took the course prescribed by prudence, discretion, precaution, or good judgment; he used precaution: and, like A^axa*a biAlv~iqapi , he took the sure course in his affair]. -A2- Elevated ground; as also ↓ A^aHozamu and ↓ HayozuwmN : (K:) or this last signifies rough, or rugged, ground: (Yz, IB, K:) and HazomN is [ ground ] more elevated than what is termed HazonN : (S:) or more rough, or rugged, than what is termed HzonN : (Ham p. 45:) or elevated ground, or rugged and elevated ground, that is girt (↓ AiHotazaAma ) by a torrent: or rugged ground, having many stones, which are more rugged and rough and scabrous than those of the A^akamap , but the top of which is broad and long, extending to the length of two leagues, and three, and less than that, which the camels do not ascend except by a road that it has: accord. to Yaakoob, the m is a substitute for the n of HazonN : pl. HuzuwmN . (TA.)

definition: and ↓ HaziymN The breast, or chest: (K:) or the middle thereof;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ HaziymN The breast, or chest: (K:) or the middle thereof; (S, K;) and the part which the HizaAm [i. e. girth or girdle ] embraces, (S, TA,) where the heads of the jawaAniH [or ribs of the breast ] meet, above the lower extremity of the sternum, opposite the kaAhil [or uppermost third portion of the backbone ]: (TA:) the part of the breast which is the place of the HizaAm : (Ham p. 704, in explanation of the latter word:) and the former word, the part that surrounds the back and the belly: or the ribs of [ the part where lies ] the heart: and the part of the side of the breast on the right and left of the Huloquwm [or windpipe ]; (K;) the two parts thus described being called HayozuwmaAni : (TA:) pl. of the former HayaAziymu ; (TA;) and of the latter A^aHozimapN [a pl. of pauc.] (Kr, K) and HuzumN [a pl. of mult.]. (K.) One says, Au$odudo Hayozuwmaka lih`*aA AlA^amori , and HayaAziymaka , i. e. (assumed tropical:) Dispose and subject thyself to this affair, or case; meaning prepare thyself for it: and ↓ $~d~a Haziymahu [(assumed tropical:) He disposed and subjected, or prepared, himself ]: (TA:) or $ad~u AlHayaAziymi is an expression denoting, by way of similitude, patient endurance of that which has befallen one. (Ham p. 163.) ― -b2- And the former, (assumed tropical:) The breast [or bows ] of a ship or boat. (MA.) -A2- Hayozuwmu [so in my copies of the S, imperfectly decl., app. regarded as of foreign origin, (not AlHayozuwmu as is implied in the K,)] the name of One of the horses of the angels; (S;) the horse of Gabriel: (K:) accord. to some, [ Hyzwn ,] with n in the place of the m . (TA.) -A3- See also HazNmN .

HuSuwlN (Msb, K, &c.) and maHoSuwlN , (K,) like maEoqurlN and maEosuwrN and mayosuwrN , (TA,) [ It was, or became, produced, educed, extracted, taken forth, or fetched out; as gold or silver from the stone of the mine, and the kernel from the shell, and wheat from the straw: (see 2:)] it came out, it became apparent: (KL:) it was, or existed, or came into being or existence; it became realized; syn. with the complete [i. e. attributive ] kaAna : (Msb in art. kwn :) [ it presented itself: it was, or became, prepared, or ready: it became attained, obtained, gotten, or acquired: ] it came, came to pass, happened, took place, betided, befell, or occurred; said of an event; syn. with waqaEa , (TA in art. wqE ,) which is also syn. with the complete [or attributive ] kaAna ; (Msb in art. kwn ;) likewise syn. with jaA='a : (Er-Rághib, TA in art. jyA^ :) [ it resulted; and particularly as a sum; and as a product; and as a quotient: it ensued: it arose, originated, proceeded, came, supervened, or accrued: in which senses, also, it is syn. with the attributive kaAna , and with jaA='a , followed by mino :] it remained, and continued, when the rest had gone, or passed away; (K, TA;) relating to a reckoning, and to an action, and the like: (TA:) and i. q. vabata and wajaba ; as in the saying, HaSala liY Ealayohi ka*aA [ Such a thing, or sum, was, or became, or proved to be, binding, obligatory, or incumbent, on him to render as a debt to me ]. (Msb.) -A2- HaSila , [aor. ,] inf. n. HaSalN , He (a horse) had a complaint of his belly from eating the earth of the herbage: (S:) or HaSilati Ald~aAb~apu , aor. , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) the beast ate earth, (M, K,) or pebbles, (K,) and they remained in its inside, (M, K,) fixed: (M:) or HaSalN signifies a horse's taking into the mouth earth from the herbs, some of which earth, collecting in his belly, kills him: and the horse so killed is said to be ↓ HaSilN : (T, TA:) or a camel's having pebbles [ which he has swallowed ] remaining in the omasum, so as not to come forth in the cud when he ruminates; and when this is the case, they sometimes kill: or a young camel's eating earth, and in consequence not ejecting the cud; which sometimes kills it. (TA.) ― -b2- Said of a boy, it signifies waqaEa AlHaSaY (K) or waqaEati AlHaSaApu (O) fiY A^unovayayohi (O, K) [app. meaning The stones, or the stone, fell, or descended, in his scrotum: Freytag, following the TK, in which fY Anvyyh is considered (I know not on what authority) as meaning fY mavaAnatihi , renders it “ laboravit lapidibus in vesica urinæ orientibus ”].

(Bd.) -A2- See also 4, in two places.
