sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. HukomN , (Msb, K, [in the TK HakomN ,]) in its primary acceptation, (Msb,) He prevented, restrained, or withheld, him (S, Msb, K) from acting in an evil, or a corrupt, manner; as also ↓ AHkmhu : (K:) and (K) from doing that which he desired; as also ↓ AHkmhu ; and ↓ Hk~mhu , (S, K,) inf. n. taHokiymN : (S:) and HukuwmapN [is another inf. n. of Hakamahu , and], accord. to As, primarily signifies the turning a man back from wrongdoing. (TA.) Ibrá- heem En-Nakha'ee is related to have said, ↓ Hak~imi Alyatiyma kamaA tuHak~imu waladaka , meaning Restrain thou the orphan from acting in an evil, or a corrupt, manner, and make him good, or virtuous, as thou restrainest thine offspring &c.: and of every one whom thou preventest, or restrainest, or withholdest, from doing a thing, thou sayest, [ Hakamotuhu and] ↓ Hk~mth and ↓ AHkmth : or, accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer, as related by Sh, the forementioned saying of En-Nakh'ee means let the orphan decide respecting his property, when he is good, or virtuous, as thou lettest thine offspring &c.; but this explanation is not approved. (Az, TA.) And Jereer says, sufahaA='akumo ↓ A^FbaniY Haniyfapa A^aHokimuwA A_in~iY A^axaAfu Ealayokumu A^ano A^agoDabaA [ O sons of Haneefeh, restrain your lightwitted ones: verily I fear for you that I may be angry ]: (S, TA:) i. e., restrain and prevent them from opposing me. (TA.) You say, also, Eani ↓ AHkmhu AlA^amori He made him to turn back, or revert, from the thing, or affair. (K.) ― -b2- Hakama Alfarasa , and ↓ AHkmhu , and ↓ Hk~mhu , He pulled in the horse by the bridle and bit, to stop him; he curbed, or restrained, him. (TA.) And Hakama Ald~aAb~apa , (S,) or Alfarasa , (K,) inf. n. HakomN ; (S; [so in my two copies of that work;]) and ↓ A^aHokamahaA , (S,) or AHkmhu ; (K;) He put a Hakamap [q. v.] to the bit of the beast, or horse. (S, * K.) ― -b3- And ↓ Hk~m AlHawaAdiva (assumed tropical:) [ He controlled events: see muHak~amN ]. (MF.) ― -b4- Hakamotu Ealayohi bika*aA originally signifies I prevented, restrained, or withheld, him from doing, or suffering, any other than such a thing, so that he could not escape it. (Msb.) [Hence it means I condemned him to such a thing; as, for instance, the payment of a fine or of a debt, and death.] And hence, (Msb,) Hakama , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. HukomN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and HukuwmapN , (K,) He judged, gave judgment, passed sentence, or decided judicially, bayonahumo between them, (S, Msb, K, TA,) and lahu in his favour, and Ealayohi against him. (S, TA.) And Hakama Ealayohi biAlA^amori He decided judicially the thing, or affair, or case, against him. (K, TA.) And Hakama lahu Ealayohi bika*aA [ He awarded by judicial sentence in his favour, against him (i. e. another person), such a thing ]. (Mgh.) [And Hakama Ealayohi He exercised judicial authority, jurisdiction, rule, dominion, or government, over him. And Hakama bika*aA He ordered, ordained, or decreed, such a thing. ] -A2- Hakama Eani AlA^amori He turned back, or reverted, from the thing, or affair. (IAar, Az, K.) -A3- Hakuma , (S, MA, TA,) with damm to the k , (S,) like karuma , (TA,) [not Hakama as in the Lexicons of Golius and Freytag,] inf. n. HukomN (KL, MA) and HikomapN , (MA,) He was, or became, such as is termed HakiymN [i. e. wise, &c. ]. (S, KL, MA, TA.) ― -b2- And Hkm , inf. n. Hkm , [so in the TA, without any syll. signs, app. Hakuma inf. n. HukomN ,] is said of a man, signifying He reached the utmost point, or degree, in its meaning ( fiY maEonaAhu [i. e., app., in what is the radical meaning of the verb, namely, in judging; like qaDuwa ]); in praising, not in dispraising. (TA.)

(TA.) bika HaAkamotu , occurring in a trad., is said to mean I have submitted the judgment [of my case] to Thee, and there is no judgment but thine; and by Thee [or thy means or aid] I have litigated in seeking judgment and in proving the falseness of him who has disputed with me in the matter of religion. (TA. [The past tense, here, is perhaps used as a corroborative present.])

(TA.) ― -b2- AHkmhu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iHokaAmN , (TA,) i. q. A^atoqanahu [ He made it, or rendered it, (namely, a thing, S, Mgh, Msb,) firm, stable, strong, solid, compact, sound, or free from defect or imperfection, by the exercise of skill; he made it firmly, strongly, solidly, compactly, so that it was firmly and closely joined or knit together, soundly, thoroughly, skilfully, judiciously, or well; he so constructed, constituted, established, settled, arranged, did, performed, or executed, it; he put it into a firm, solid, sound, or good, state, or on a firm, solid, sound, or good, footing: and he knew it, or learned it, soundly, thoroughly, or well; see 1, last sentence, in art. definition: [inf. n. of 1, q. v.,] originally signifies Prevention, or restraint. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, (Msb,) Judgment, or judicial decision: (S, Msb, K, TA:) or judgment respecting a thing, that it is such...
sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of 1, q. v.,] originally signifies Prevention, or restraint. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, (Msb,) Judgment, or judicial decision: (S, Msb, K, TA:) or judgment respecting a thing, that it is such a thing, or is not such a thing, whether it be necessarily connected with another thing, or not: (TA:) [whence,] in logic, [what our logicians term judgment; i. e.] the judging a thing to stand to another [ thing ] in the relation of an attribute to its subject, affirmatively or negatively; or the perception of relation or non-relation: (Kull:) or it properly signifies judgment with equity or justice: (Az, TA:) and ↓ HukuwmapN signifies the same; (K, TA;) originally, accord. to As, the restraint of a man from wrongdoing: (TA:) [each, though an inf. n., being used as a simple subst., has its pl.:] the pl. of the former is A^aHokaAmN , (K,) [properly a pl. of pauc., but] its only pl. form: and the pl. of the latter is HukuwmaAtN . (TA.) You say, wa yafoSilu ↓ huwa yatawal~aY AlHukuwmaAti AlxuSuwmaAti [ He presides over the affairs of judgment, and decides litigations ]. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., A_in~a mina Al$~iEori laHukomFA meaning Verily, of poetry, there is that which is true judgment: so says Er-Rághib: or, as others say, profitable discourse, such as restrains from, and forbids, ignorant and silly behaviour; i. e., [what contains] exhortations and proverbs profitable to men: or, the right reading is, as some relate it, ↓ laHikomapF [i. e. wisdom, &c.]: (TA:) or HikamFA [pl. of Hikomap ]. (So in a copy of the “ Jámi' es-Sagheer ” of Es-Suyootee.) ― -b3- [The exercise of judicial authority; jurisdiction; rule; dominion; or government. See also HukuwmapN . ― -b4- An ordinance; a statute; a prescript; an edict; a decree; or a particular law; like qaDaA='N . Hence the phrase Hukoma AlEaAdapi According to custom or usage; properly, according to the ordinance of custom or usage. ― -b5- A rule in grammar &c.; as when one says, Hukomu AlfaAEili Alr~afoEu or A^ano yurofaEa , i. e. The rule applying to the case of the agent is that it be put in the nom. case; and Hukomuhu Hukomu ka*aA , or kaHukomi k*A , i. e. The rule applying to it is the same as the rule applying to such a thing, or like the rule applying to such a thing. ― -b6- It may often be rendered Predicament: (thus the last of the foregoing exs. may be rendered Its predicament is the same as the predicament of such a thing, or like the predicament of such a thing: ) and HukomFA , or fiY AlHukomi , predicamentally, or in respect of predicament; and virtually; as distinguished from lafoZFA (literally), and HaqiyqapF (really), and the like.] ― -b7- Also Knowledge of the law in matters of religion. (TA.) ― -b8- See also HikomapN , in two places. It is a more general term than HikomapN ; for all Hikomap is Hukom , but the reverse is not the case. (Er-Rághib, TA.)

definition: [properly, or primarily,] signifies What prevents, or restrains, from ignorant behaviour: (Mgh:) [in its most usual sense, which is wisdom, agreeably with explanations here following,] it is derived...
sourceDefinition: [properly, or primarily,] signifies What prevents, or restrains, from ignorant behaviour: (Mgh:) [in its most usual sense, which is wisdom, agreeably with explanations here following,] it is derived from HakamapN , signifying a certain appertenance of a beast, [a kind of curb,] because it prevents its possessor from having bad dispositions: (Msb:) it means knowledge; or science; (S, K;) as also ↓ HukomN : (S, TA:) or [generally] knowledge of the true natures of things, and action according to the requirements thereof; and therefore it is divided into intellectual and practical: or a state, or quality, of the intellectual faculty: this is the theological Hikomap : in the Kur xxxi. 11, by the Hikomap given by God to Lukmán, is meant the evidence of the intellect in accordance with the statutes of the law: (TA:) in the conventional language of the learned, it means the perfecting of the human mind by the acquisition of the speculative sciences, and of the complete faculty of doing excellent deeds, according to the ability possessed: (Bd on the passage of the Kur above mentioned:) or it means the attainment of that which is true, or right, by knowledge and by deed: so that in God it is the knowledge of things, and the origination thereof in the most perfect manner: and, in man, the knowledge and doing of good things: or it means acquaintance with the most excellent of things by the most excellent kind of knowledge: (TA:) [and in the modern language, philosophy: pl. HikamN :] see HukomN . ― -b2- Also Equity, or justice, (K, TA,) in judgment or judicial decision; and so ↓ HukomN . (TA.) ― -b3- And i. q. HilomN ; (K, TA;) i. e. [ Forbearance, or clemency, or] the management of one's soul and temper on the occasion of excitement of anger: which, if correct, is nearly the same as equity or justice. (TA.) ― -b4- And Obedience of God: and knowledge in matters of religion, and the acting agreeably therewith: and understanding: and reverential fear; piety; pious fear; or abstinence from unlawful things: and the doing, or saying, that which is right: and reflection upon what God has commanded, and doing according thereto. (TA.) ― -b5- And [ Knowledge of ] the interpretation of the Kur-án, and saying that which is right in relation to it: so in the Kur ii. 272. (TA.) ― -b6- And The gift of prophecy, or the prophetic office; (K, TA;) and apostleship: so in the Kur ii. 252 and iii. 43 and xxxviii. 19: (TA:) or in the [first and] last of these instances it means ― -b7- The Book of the Psalms [of David]: or, as some say, any saying, or discourse, agreeable with the truth: (Mgh:) and it also means [in other instances] the Book of the Law of Moses: (TA:) and the Gospel: and the Kur-án: (K:) because each of these comprises what is termed AlHikomapu AlmanoTuwqu bihaA , i. e. the secrets of the sciences of the law and of the course of conduct; and AlHikomapu Almasokuwtu EanohaA , i. e. the secrets of the science of the Divine Essence. (TA.)

HikamN :] see HukomN . ― -b2- Also Equity, or justice, (K, TA,) in judgment or judicial decision; and so ↓ HukomN . (TA.) ― -b3- And i. q. HilomN ; (K, TA;) i. e. [ Forbearance, or clemency, or] the management of one's soul and temper on the occasion of excitement of anger: which, if correct, is nearly the same as equity or justice. (TA.) ― -b4- And Obedience of God: and knowledge in matters of religion, and the acting agreeably therewith: and understanding: and reverential fear; piety; pious fear; or abstinence from unlawful things: and the doing, or saying, that which is right: and reflection upon what God has commanded, and doing according thereto. (TA.) ― -b5- And [ Knowledge of ] the interpretation of the Kur-án, and saying that which is right in relation to it: so in the Kur ii. 272. (TA.) ― -b6- And The gift of prophecy, or the prophetic office; (K, TA;) and apostleship: so in the Kur ii. 252 and iii. 43 and xxxviii. 19: (TA:) or in the [first and] last of these instances it means ― -b7- The Book of the Psalms [of David]: or, as some say, any saying, or discourse, agreeable with the truth: (Mgh:) and it also means [in other instances] the Book of the Law of Moses: (TA:) and the Gospel: and the Kur-án: (K:) because each of these comprises what is termed AlHikomapu AlmanoTuwqu bihaA , i. e. the secrets of the sciences of the law and of the course of conduct; and AlHikomapu Almasokuwtu EanohaA , i. e. the secrets of the science of the Divine Essence. (TA.)

definition: [ A kind of curb for a horse;
sourceDefinition: [ A kind of curb for a horse; ] a certain appertenance of a beast; so called because it renders him manageable, or submissive, to the rider, and prevents him from being refractory and the like; (Msb;) or because it prevents him from vehement running: (TA:) it is the appertenance of the lijaAm [or bridle] that surrounds the Hanak [or part beneath the chin and lower jaw ]: the Arabs used to make it of untanned thong or of hemp; because what they aimed at was courage, not finery: (S:) or the appertenance of the ljAm that surrounds the HanakaAni [which word app. here means the two jaws ] of the horse, and in which are [ attached ] the Ei*aAraAni [or two side-pieces of the headstall, that lie against the two cheeks ]: (K:) or a ring which surrounds the marosin [or part of the nose which is the place of the halter ] and the Hanak [or part beneath the chin and lower jaw ], of silver or iron or thong: (IDrd in his Book on the Saddle and Bridle:) or a ring which is upon ( fY ) the mouth of the horse: (ISh, TA:) pl. HakamaAtN (S, TA) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ HakamN . (TA.) Zuheyr says, describing horses, HakamaAti Alqid~i wa AlA^abaqaA ↓ qado A^uHokimato meaning qado A^uHokimato biHakamaAti Alqid~i wa biHakamaAti AlA^abaqi [ That had been curbed with curbs of untanned thong, and with curbs of hemp ]: (S, TA:) or, accord. to Abu-l-Hasan, [the meaning is that had been furnished with curbs &c.; for he says that] AHkmt is here made trans. because it implies the signification of qul~idato : (TA:) some relate the hemistich thus: HakamaAti Alqid~i wa AlA^abaqaA ↓ maHokuwmapF [ furnished with curbs of untanned thong, and hemp ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) The chin of a sheep (S, K) or goat. (S.) ― -b3- And, of a man, (tropical:) The fore part of the face: (K, TA:) or, as some say, the lower part of the face: a metaphorical term from the Hakamap of the lijaAm : (TA:) or [in some copies of the K “ and ”] (tropical:) his head: [accord. to the CK, or the fore part of the head of a man:] and (tropical:) his state, or condition: and (tropical:) rank, and station. (K, TA.) You say, rafaEa A@ll~`hu Hakamatahu (tropical:) God exalted, or may God exalt, his head, or his state, or condition, and his rank, and station: because the stooping of the head is a characteristic of the low, or abject. (TA.) And lahu EinodanaA HakamapN (tropical:) He has rank in our estimation. (TA.) And fulaAnN EaAliY AlHakamapi (tropical:) [ Such a one is elevated in respect of rank, or station. ] (TA.) -A2- [See also HaAkimN , of which it is a pl.]

definition: Possessing knowledge or science;
sourceDefinition: Possessing knowledge or science; [in its most usual sense,] possessing Hikomap [as meaning wisdom ]; (S, TA; [see also A^aHokamu AlHaAkimiyna ;]) [ wise; a sage: and in the modern language, a philosopher: and particularly a physician: ] one who performs, or executes, affairs firmly, solidly, soundly, thoroughly, skilfully, judiciously, or well; (S, IAth;) so that it is, in this sense, of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mufoEilN : (IAth, TA:) one who executes well, and firmly, solidly, &c., the niceties of arts: (TA:) [pl. HukamaA='u .] AlHakiymu [as meaning The All-wise ] is one of the names of God. (TA.) ― -b2- Al*~ikoru AlHakiymu , applied to the Kur-án, means [ The admonition ] that decides judicially in your favour and against you: or that is rendered free from defect or imperfection; in which is no incongruity, nor any unsoundness. (TA.)

definition: One who judges, gives judgment, passes sentence, or decides judicially;
sourceDefinition: One who judges, gives judgment, passes sentence, or decides judicially; a judge; an arbiter, arbitrator, or umpire; (S * Msb, K, TA;) between people: (Msb, TA:) [ one who exercises judicial authority, jurisdiction, rule, dominion, or government; a ruler, or governor: ] and ↓ HakamN signifies the same: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) the HaAkim between people is so called because he restrains from wrongdoing: (As, TA:) the pl. is Huk~aAmN (Msb, K) and HakamapN , meaning judges, [&c.,] (TA,) and HaAkimuwna is allowable. (Msb.) It is said in a prov., ↓ fiY bayotihi yuw^otaY AlHakamu [ In his house the judge is to be come to ]. (S. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 204.]) AlHaAkimu [as meaning The Supreme Judge ] is one of the names of God. (TA.) See also the next paragraph. -A2- [The pl.] HakamapN also signifies Mockers, scoffers, or deriders. (TA. [The H in this case seems to be a substitute for h : see art. hkm .]) ↓ A^aHokamu AlHaAkimiyna [ The most qualified to judge of those who judge: or] the most knowing and most just [ of them ]: (Bd and Jel in xi. 47, where it is applied to God:) or it may mean the wisest of those who possess attributes of wisdom; supposing HaAkimN to be [a possessive epithet] from AlHikomapu , like daAriEN from Ald~iroEu . (Bd.)

(Bd in iii. 5.) And AlmuHokamu The portion of the Kur-án called AlmufaS~alu [q. v.]; because nought thereof has been abrogated: or, as some say, what is unequivocal, or unambiguous; because its perspicuity is made free from defect, or imperfection, and it requires nothing else [to explain it]. sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. HaniynN , He was, or became, affected with [ a yearning, longing, or desire, or] an intense emotion of grief or of joy; as also ↓ AstHn~ and ↓ tHAn~ . (K.) [See an instance of its denoting an emotion of joy voce Han~aAnN .] You say, Han~a A_ilayohi , aor. and inf. n. as above, He, or his soul, yearned towards, longed for, or desired, him, or it. (S.) And Han~a A_ilaY waTanihi He yearned towards, longed for, or desired, his home. (TA.) And taHin~a A_ilaY zawojihaA AlA^aw~ali [ She yearns towards her first, or former, husband ]. (TA.) And Han~ato , inf. n. as above, She (a woman) yearned towards, longed for, or desired, her child, or children. (Msb.) So, too, one says of a she-camel, meaning She yearned towards, longed for, or desired, her home, or her young one; and in like manner, of a pigeon: but in most instances it means she (a camel) yearned with a cry, or uttered a cry when yearning [or a yearning cry or the cry produced by yearning ], towards her young one or her companions: or she uttered a cry with emotion after her young one: in its primary sense, she reiterated her [ yearning ] cry after her young one: but when you say, Han~a qalobiY A_ilayohi , you mean My heart yearned towards, longed for, or desired, him, or it, without the uttering of a cry or sound. (TA.) They said also, laAA^afoEaluhu Hat~aY yaHin~a AlD~ab~u fiY A^avari AlA_ibili AlS~aAdirapi [ I will not do it until the lizard called Db~ yearn after the camels returning from the water; meaning I will never do it ]: this is only a prov.; for the Db~ has no Haniyn nor does it ever go to the water. (TA.) [And Hn~a AlEuwdu , aor. and inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) The lute produced plaintive sounds: or excited lively emotions of sadness, or of mirth: see Han~aAnN . And in like manner one says of a musical reed: see muvaq~ab .] And Han~ati Alqawosu , (K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) (assumed tropical:) The bow [ twanged, or] made a sound (K, TA) when its string had been pulled and then let go. (S.) And Han~ati AlT~asotu A_i*aA nuqirato (tropical:) [ The brazen basin rang when it was knocked, or pecked ]. (TA.) And Han~ati Als~aAriyapu [ The mast creaked, or made a creaking sound ]. (TA in art. Sr .) And Han~a qidoHu layosa minohaA (assumed tropical:) [ An arrow of those used in the game called Almayosir produced a sound: it was not of them ]: a prov., applied to a man who ascribes to himself a false origin, or who arrogates to himself that to which he has no relation: by the qdH is meant one of the arrows of the mysr ; for when this is not of the same substance as the others, and is made to vibrate, it produces a sound different from the sounds of the others, and is known thereby. (TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 341.]) And Han~ati Alr~iyHu and ↓ AstHn~t (assumed tropical:) [ The wind made a plaintive, or moaning, or perhaps a shrill, sound; made a sound like the Haniyn of camels: see HanuwnN ]: both signify the same. (TA.) [See also HaniynN , below.] ― -b2- Han~a Ealayohi , (S, Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (S, Msb,) inf. n. HanaAnN (S, Msb, K *) and Han~apN (Msb, TA *) and Han~N , (K, * TA,) He was merciful, compassionate, or pitiful, towards him, or it; (S, Msb, K, * TA:) as also ↓ tHn~n : (S, K:) he was, or became, favourably inclined towards him, or it; (Msb;) and so ↓ tHn~n : (TA:) he was, or became, affectionate, or pitiful, or compassionate, towards him; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ HanoHana . (IAar, Az, K.) And EalaY waladihaA ↓ taHan~anato She (a camel, and a ewe or goat,) became favourably inclined, or compassionate, towards her young one. (Lh, TA.) ― -b3- See also 2. ― -b4- Han~a Ean~iY , aor. , means Sad~a ; (S;) i. e. He turned away from me, avoided me, or shunned me: so that it is anomalous; for by rule the aor. should be ; and it is not mentioned among the exceptions [to the rule applying to a case of this kind]. (MF, TA.) [But it appears from what here follows that Sad~a may perhaps be here meant to be understood in its trans. sense.] -A2- Han~ahu , (K,) [aor. , as is shown below,] inf. n. Han~N , (TA,) signifies Sad~ahu and Sarafahu [ He turned him, or it, away, or back ]. (K, TA.) You say, Hun~a Ean~iY $ar~aka , inf. n. Han~N , Turn thou away, or back, from me thy evil, or mischief. (K.) And maA taHun~uniY $ayoy^FA mino $ar~ika Thou dost not turn away, or back, from me aught of thy evil, or mischief (S.) -A3- [ Hun~a , inf. n. Han~N , app. He was, or became, possessed by a demon, or by one of the tribe or kind or class termed AlHin~ ; and hence, he was, or became, mad, or insane: for] Han~N is syn. with junuwnN ; (TA as from the K; [but not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K;]) whence maHonuwnN applied to a man [as meaning majonuwnN ]. (TA.)

definition: Mercy, compassion, or pity: (S, K:) tenderness of heart;
sourceDefinition: Mercy, compassion, or pity: (S, K:) tenderness of heart; (K;) which is the same; (TA;) as also ↓ Hin~apN , with kesr; (Kr, TA;) for which the vulgar say ↓ Han~iy~ipN : (TA:) and ↓ Han~apN [in like manner] signifies affection, and compassion. (Az, TA.) waHanaAnFA mino ladun~aA , in the Kur [xix. 14], respecting which I 'Ab is related by 'Ikrimeh to have said, I know not what is AlHanaAnu , means And mercy from us. (S, TA.) The Arabs say, HanaAnaka yaA rab~i and HanaAnayoka [I beg thy mercy, O my Lord ]: both signify the same; i. e. raHomataka : (S:) the latter is the expression commonly used: (A 'Obeyd, in a marginal note in a copy of the S:) or [rather] the latter means have mercy on me time after time, and with mercy after mercy: (K, * TA:) it is a dualized inf. n., of which the verb is not expressed; like lab~ayoka and saEodayoka : (TA:) or it means [ let thy mercy be continuous to me; ] whenever I receive mercy and good from Thee, let it not cease, but be conjoined with other mercy from Thee: (ISd, TA:) the dual form is not to be understood as restricting the signification to duality: (Suh, TA:) the word is not used in this form otherwise than as a prefixed noun: (Sb, TA:) but sometimes they said HanFAnFA , in the sing., without prefixing it. (ISd, TA.) They said also, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi waHanaAnayohi meaning [ I extol, or celebrate, or declare, the absolute purity, or perfection, or glory, of God, ] and I beg his mercy; like as they said, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi warayoHaAnahu . (TA.) And HanaAna A@ll~`hi as meaning maEaA*a A@ll~`hi [ I seek the protection, or preservation, of God ]. (K.) ― -b2- Also i. q. rizoqN [ Means of subsistence, &c.]: and barakapN [ a blessing; any good that is bestowed by God; prosperity, or good fortune; increase; &c.]. (K.) ― -b3- A quality inspiring reverence or veneration or respect or honour: (El-Umawee, K:) gravity, staidness, or sedateness. (K.) One says, maAtaraY lahu HanaAnFA Thou seest him not to possess any quality inspiring reverence &c. (El-Umawee, TA.) -A2- Evil, or mischief, long continuing. (K.)

(Az, TA.) waHanaAnFA mino ladun~aA , in the Kur [xix. 14], respecting which I 'Ab is related by 'Ikrimeh to have said, I know not what is AlHanaAnu , means And mercy from us. (S, TA.) The Arabs say, HanaAnaka yaA rab~i and HanaAnayoka [I beg thy mercy, O my Lord ]: both signify the same; i. e. raHomataka : (S:) the latter is the expression commonly used: (A 'Obeyd, in a marginal note in a copy of the S:) or [rather] the latter means have mercy on me time after time, and with mercy after mercy: (K, * TA:) it is a dualized inf. n., of which the verb is not expressed; like lab~ayoka and saEodayoka : (TA:) or it means [ let thy mercy be continuous to me; ] whenever I receive mercy and good from Thee, let it not cease, but be conjoined with other mercy from Thee: (ISd, TA:) the dual form is not to be understood as restricting the signification to duality: (Suh, TA:) the word is not used in this form otherwise than as a prefixed noun: (Sb, TA:) but sometimes they said HanFAnFA , in the sing., without prefixing it. They said also, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi waHanaAnayohi meaning [ I extol, or celebrate, or declare, the absolute purity, or perfection, or glory, of God, ] and I beg his mercy; like as they said, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi warayoHaAnahu . definition: One who yearns towards, longs for, or desires, a thing, (K,) and inclines to it.
sourceDefinition: One who yearns towards, longs for, or desires, a thing, (K,) and inclines to it. (TA.) [Hence,] Han~aAnapN A woman who remembers a former husband with yearning ( AlHnyn ) and grieving, or moaning, (K, TA,) in tenderness for her children, when they are young, that the husband may maintain them; like A^an~aAnapN : or who yearns towards her former husband, and inclines to him: or who yearns towards her child, or children, by her husband who has separated from her: (TA:) or a woman who yearns towards her former husband, and grieves for him: or who marries, having been divorced, and yearns towards him who has divorced her. (Har p. 569.) And (assumed tropical:) A bow; (K;) [because of the sound made by the twanging of its string;] accord. to AHn, as a proper name; but ISd holds it to be, when thus applied, an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant: (TA:) or a bow that [ twangs, or] makes a sound (S, K) when its string has been pulled and then let go. (S.) And EuwdN Han~aAnN (tropical:) [ A lute that produces plaintive sounds: or] that excites lively emotions of sadness, or of mirth. (TA.) And saHaAbN Han~aAnN (assumed tropical:) Clouds that have [or produce ] a Haniyn [or moaning sound, by their thunder heard from a distance,] like the Haniyn of camels. (TA.) And sahomN Han~aAnN (assumed tropical:) An arrow that produces a sound when thou triest its sonorific quality by turning it round between thy fingers: (AHeyth, K, TA: [in the CK, naqarotuhu is erroneously put for naq~arotahu :]) or that produces a sound when it is turned round ( A^udiyra [or A^udir~a ]) with the ends of the fingers upon the thumbs, by reason of the excellence and compactness of its wood. (TA. [See dar~a Als~ahomu , in art. dr .]) And ximosN Han~aAnN (tropical:) i. q. baAy^iSN [ A hurrying, or hard, journey in which the camels are watered only on the first and fifth days: (in the CK and a MS. copy of the K, erroneously, nAbDN :)] (K, TA) i. e. (As, TA) in which there is a Haniyn [or yearning of the camels] by reason of its quickness; (As, K, TA;) or in which the camels yearn [ towards their accustomed places ] ( taHin~u ) by reason of fatigue. (A, TA.) And TariyqN Han~aAnN (tropical:) A conspicuous road, (S, K, TA,) in which the old camel becomes joyous ( yaHin~u , i. e. yanobasiTu ): or, accord. to the A, a road in which there is [ heard ] a Haniyn [or yearning cry ] of the camels; like TariyqN nah~aAmN meaning a road in which is [heard] a nahiym [or chiding] of camels. (TA.) ― -b2- One who shows favour, or presents a favourable aspect, to him who turns from him, or shuns him. (K.) ― -b3- Merciful, or having mercy. (S.) [Hence,] AlHan~aAnu a name of God; (K;) meaning The Merciful (Aboo-Is-hák, Az, IAth, K) to his servants. (IAth, TA.)

HayoDN and maHiyDN (S, Msb, K) and maHaADN , (Aboo-Is-hák, K,) said of a woman, (S, A, Msb, K,) She menstruated; i. e. her blood flowed; (A;) or [rather] blood came forth from her womb; (Mgh;) [ not in consequence of disease nor of childbirth, nor before she had attained to puberty; as explained in the law-books of the Muslims;] as also ↓ tHy~Dt : or this latter signifies she likened herself to the HaAy^iD . (TA.) ― -b2- Also She attained the age of menstruation. (TA.) [See HaAy^iDN .] ― -b3- HaADati Als~amurapu , (S, A, Msb,) aor. as above, (Msb,) inf. n. (A, TA: [but in a copy of the A, and in one instance in the TA, Al$~ajarapu is put in the place of Als~amurapu , app. by mistake.]) [I have marked this signification as tropical on the authority of the A and TA; but the author of the Msb has commenced the art. with it; and shows that he held the opinion, which some others have shared with him, that it is the primary signification.] ― -b4- HaADa Als~ayolu (assumed tropical:) The torrent overflowed; or poured out, or forth, from fulness; or ran; syn. faADa . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (TA,) [aor. ,] inf. n. xadoEN , (Bd in ii. 8,) He hid it, or concealed it; (TA;) as also ↓ AxdEh , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. A_ixodaAEN . (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, app.,] (Lh, K,) inf. n. as above, (Lh,) (tropical:) He doubled it, or folded it, one part upon another; namely, a garment, or piece of cloth. (Lh, K, TA.) ― -b3- [And hence, also, accord. to some,] xadaEahu , aor. , inf. n. xadoEN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and xidoEN , (AZ, S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb, TA,) and xadiyEapN , (TA,) or this [also] is a simple subst., (Msb, TA,) like xidaAEN , [which is also an inf. n. of 3,] and like xudNEapN , (TA,) He deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him; syn. xatalahu ; (S, Mgh, K;) and desired to do to him a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, without his knowing whence it proceeded: (S, K:) or he dissembled [or acted deceitfully ] with him; pretended to him the contrary of what he concealed: (TA:) or he made him to resign, or relinquish, the object that he had in view, by pretending to him something the contrary of what he concealed: (Er-Rághib, B:) and ↓ xAdEhu , (S, TA,) inf. n. muxaAdaEapN (S) [and xidaAEN ], signifies the same; (S, * TA;) as also ↓ AxtdEhu ; and ↓ txd~Ehu ; and ↓ xd~Ehu , inf. n. taxodiyEN : (TA:) or this last signifies he deceived him, deluded him, beguiled him, circumvented him, or outwitted him, much: (KL:) [and of another of these verbs we find the following various explanations:] ↓ xAdEhu is syn. with kaAyadahu [which has the first of the meanings assigned in this sentence to xadaEahu ; or signifies he practised with him mutual deceit, delusion, guile, or circumvention; he deceived him, &c., being deceived, &c., by him; and this latter meaning, if not each meaning, may be intended here by kAydh ; for Bd says, (in ii. 8,) that muxaAdaEap is between two]: (TA:) or it signifies he strove, endeavoured, or desired, to deceive, delude, beguile, circumvent, or outwit, him; (AAF, L;) [agreeably with what is said by Kemál Páshá Zádeh, (as I find in a marginal note in a copy of the MS, and also in the Kull p. 178,) that one says of a man xAdE when he has not attained his desire, and xadaEa when he has attained his desire;] for many a verb of the measure faAEala relates to one only; as in the instances of EaAqabotu All~iS~a and TaAraqotu Aln~aEola : (L:) or it signifies, [like xadaEahu ,] he pretended to him something different from that which was in his mind. (K.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 8], A@ll~`ha waA@l~a*iyna A=manuwA ↓ yuxaAdiEuwna , (TA,) meaning They pretend, to God and to those who have believed, something different from that which is in their minds, by concealing unbelief and pretending belief; for when they do thus to the believers, they do thus to God: (K:) and again, [in iv. 141], A@ll~`ha wahuwa xaAdiEuhumo ↓ yuxaAdiEuwna [ They strive, endeavour, or desire, to deceive God, or] they think that they deceive God, but He is [ their deceiver, i. e.,] the requiter, to them, of their xidaAE [or deceit, &c.]: (TA:) or the meaning is [ they deceive ] the friends of God: (S:) and [agreeably with this last rendering, and that given in the K,] Aboo-Hayáh reads, in the former passage, yaxodaEuwna A@ll~`ha : (TA:) [which passage continues thus:] A_il~aA A^anofusahumo ↓ wamaA yuxaAdiEuwna [ but they do not deceive any save themselves ]; i. e., the re- sult of their xidaAE [or deceit ] does not befall any save themselves: (K:) here, again, Aboo-Hayáh reads yaxodaEuwna : (TA:) Muärrik reads wamaA ↓ yaxad~iEuwna , meaning yaxotadiEuwna . (K.) Accord. to IAar, AlxadoEu signifies manoEu AlHaq~i [meaning The preventing from discovering, or accepting, the truth ]. (L.) [“ He deceived him, ” or the like, seems to be generally regarded as the primary signification of xadaEahu , for it occupies the first place in all the lexicons to which I have access: but Bd says (in ii. 8) that this meaning is from xadaEa said of the Dab~i , and that the primary signification of xadoEN is the act of “ concealing: ” the action of the Db~ , however, as will appear in what follows, implies, and originates from, a desire of deceit; and so, often, does the act of concealing.] ― -b4- [Hence, app.,] xadaEotuhu I gained the mastery over him. (TA.) ― -b5- xadaEa , (Lth, TA, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. xadoEN , (TA,) said of a [lizard of the kind called] Dab~ , [as though meaning either xadaEa AlmuHotari$a It deceived the hunter, or xadaEa nafosahu it concealed itself, ] signifies it entered into its hole; (Lth;) as also xadaEa fiY Hujorihi : (S, K:) or it scented a man, and therefore entered its hole, in order that it might not be caught; as also ↓ AnxdE : (TA:) or it entered into its hole in a tortuous manner: and in like manner, a gazelle into its covert: but mostly said of a Db~ : (Abu-l-'Omeythil:) also said of other things: (Lth:) of a fox, meaning he took to going to the right and left, deceitfully, or guilefully: and of a man, meaning he hid himself from another: and he assumed a disposition not his own. (TA.) [See also xidaAEN , below.] ― -b6- Hence, i. e. from xadaEa said of the Db~ , (A, TA,) xadaEato Eayonu Al$~amosi (tropical:) The disc of the sun set; (A, K, TA;) like xaDaEato . (TA in art. xDE .) ― -b7- [And] xadaEato Eayonuhu (tropical:) His eye sank, or became depressed, in his head. (Lh, K, TA.) [Also meaning (assumed tropical:) His eye did not sleep: for] xadaEati AlEayonu signifies (assumed tropical:) the eye did not sleep. (TA.) ― -b8- [Hence also, as indicated in the S,] maA xadaEato fiY EayoniY naEosapN (assumed tropical:) [ A slumber did not enter my eye ]: (S:) or maA xadaEato biEayonihi naEosapN , (so in the L,) or xadoEapN , i. e. naEosapN , (so in the TA,) meaning (tropical:) a slumber did not pass by his eye. (L, TA.) [And from the same source have originated several other tropical significations, of which exs. here follow.] ― -b9- xadaEati AlA^umuwri (tropical:) The affairs varied in their state; or were, or became, variable. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b10- xadaEati Als~uwqu , (S, K,) inf. n. xadoEN , (TA,) (tropical:) [ The market varied in its state; at one time being brisk, and at another time dull, in respect of traffic: (see xaAdiEN , below:) or] the market became dull in respect of traffic; (S, K;) as also ↓ AnxdEt ; (Lh, TA;) or AnxdE : (K: [but swq is generally fem.:]) and, as some say, it became brisk in respect of traffic: thus it appears to have two contr. significations: (TA:) and xadaEa Als~iEoru (tropical:) The price became high, or dear. (TA.) ― -b11- Said of a man, xadaEa also signifies (tropical:) His wealth, (K, TA,) and the like, (TA,) became small in amount, or little. (K, TA.) ― -b12- Said of a time, inf. n. xadoEN , (tropical:) Its rain became little: (TA:) and of rain, (tropical:) It became little. (K, TA.) ― -b13- Said of spittle, or saliva, (tropical:) It dried: (S, K, TA:) or it became little, and dried, in the mouth: (A, TA.) or it became deficient; and when it becomes deficient, it becomes thick; and when it becomes thick, it becomes stinking: (TA:) or it became corrupt: (IAar, TA:) and in like manner, said of a thing, it became corrupt, or bad. (TA.) [See also xaAdiEN , below.] ― -b14- Said of a generous man, (K,) (tropical:) He refrained [from giving], (S, L, K,) and refused. (L.) You say, kaAna fulaAnN yuEoTiY vum~a xadaEa (tropical:) [ Such a one used to give; then he refrained, and refused ]. (S.) -A2- xadaEahu aor. , inf. n. xadoEN , He cut, or severed, his [ vein called the ] A^axodaE . (TA.)

(S, * TA;) as also ↓ AxtdEhu ; and ↓ txd~Ehu ; and ↓ xd~Ehu , inf. n. taxodiyEN : (TA:) or this last signifies he deceived him, deluded him, beguiled him, circumvented him, or outwitted him, much: (KL:) [and of another of these verbs we find the following various explanations:] ↓ xAdEhu is syn. with kaAyadahu [which has the first of the meanings assigned in this sentence to xadaEahu ; or signifies he practised with him mutual deceit, delusion, guile, or circumvention; he deceived him, &c., being deceived, &c., by him; and this latter meaning, if not each meaning, may be intended here by kAydh ; for Bd says, (in ii. 8,) that muxaAdaEap is between two]: (TA:) or it signifies he strove, endeavoured, or desired, to deceive, delude, beguile, circumvent, or outwit, him; (AAF, L;) [agreeably with what is said by Kemál Páshá Zádeh, (as I find in a marginal note in a copy of the MS, and also in the Kull p. 178,) that one says of a man xAdE when he has not attained his desire, and xadaEa when he has attained his desire;] for many a verb of the measure faAEala relates to one only; as in the instances of EaAqabotu All~iS~a and TaAraqotu Aln~aEola : (L:) or it signifies, [like xadaEahu ,] he pretended to him something different from that which was in his mind. (K.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 8], A@ll~`ha waA@l~a*iyna A=manuwA ↓ yuxaAdiEuwna , (TA,) meaning They pretend, to God and to those who have believed, something different from that which is in their minds, by concealing unbelief and pretending belief; for when they do thus to the believers, they do thus to God: (K:) and again, [in iv. 141], A@ll~`ha wahuwa xaAdiEuhumo ↓ yuxaAdiEuwna [ They strive, endeavour, or desire, to deceive God, or] they think that they deceive God, but He is [ their deceiver, i. e.,] the requiter, to them, of their xidaAE [or deceit, &c.]: (TA:) or the meaning is [ they deceive ] the friends of God: (S:) and [agreeably with this last rendering, and that given in the K,] Aboo-Hayáh reads, in the former passage, yaxodaEuwna A@ll~`ha : (TA:) [which passage continues thus:] A_il~aA A^anofusahumo ↓ wamaA yuxaAdiEuwna [ but they do not deceive any save themselves ]; i. e., the re- sult of their xidaAE [or deceit ] does not befall any save themselves: (K:) here, again, Aboo-Hayáh reads yaxodaEuwna : (TA:) Muärrik reads wamaA ↓ yaxad~iEuwna , meaning yaxotadiEuwna . (K.) Accord. to IAar, AlxadoEu signifies manoEu AlHaq~i [meaning The preventing from discovering, or accepting, the truth ]. (L.) [“ He deceived him, ” or the like, seems to be generally regarded as the primary signification of xadaEahu , for it occupies the first place in all the lexicons to which I have access: but Bd says (in ii. 8) that this meaning is from xadaEa said of the Dab~i , and that the primary signification of xadoEN is the act of “ concealing: ” the action of the Db~ , however, as will appear in what follows, implies, and originates from, a desire of deceit; and so, often, does the act of concealing.] ― -b4- [Hence, app.,] xadaEotuhu I gained the mastery over him. (TA.) ― -b5- xadaEa , (Lth, TA, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. xadoEN , (TA,) said of a [lizard of the kind called] Dab~ , [as though meaning either xadaEa AlmuHotari$a It deceived the hunter, or xadaEa nafosahu it concealed itself, ] signifies it entered into its hole; (Lth;) as also xadaEa fiY Hujorihi : (S, K:) or it scented a man, and therefore entered its hole, in order that it might not be caught; as also ↓ AnxdE : (TA:) or it entered into its hole in a tortuous manner: and in like manner, a gazelle into its covert: but mostly said of a Db~ : (Abu-l-'Omeythil:) also said of other things: (Lth:) of a fox, meaning he took to going to the right and left, deceitfully, or guilefully: and of a man, meaning he hid himself from another: and he assumed a disposition not his own. (TA.) [See also xidaAEN , below.] ― -b6- Hence, i. e. from xadaEa said of the Db~ , (A, TA,) xadaEato Eayonu Al$~amosi (tropical:) The disc of the sun set; (A, K, TA;) like xaDaEato . (TA in art. xDE .) ― -b7- [And] xadaEato Eayonuhu (tropical:) His eye sank, or became depressed, in his head. (Lh, K, TA.) [Also meaning (assumed tropical:) His eye did not sleep: for] xadaEati AlEayonu signifies (assumed tropical:) the eye did not sleep. (TA.) ― -b8- [Hence also, as indicated in the S,] maA xadaEato fiY EayoniY naEosapN (assumed tropical:) [ A slumber did not enter my eye ]: (S:) or maA xadaEato biEayonihi naEosapN , (so in the L,) or xadoEapN , i. e. naEosapN , (so in the TA,) meaning (tropical:) a slumber did not pass by his eye. (L, TA.) [And from the same source have originated several other tropical significations, of which exs. here follow.] ― -b9- xadaEati AlA^umuwri (tropical:) The affairs varied in their state; or were, or became, variable. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b10- xadaEati Als~uwqu , (S, K,) inf. n. xadoEN , (TA,) (tropical:) [ The market varied in its state; at one time being brisk, and at another time dull, in respect of traffic: (see xaAdiEN , below:) or] the market became dull in respect of traffic; (S, K;) as also ↓ AnxdEt ; (Lh, TA;) or AnxdE : (K: [but swq is generally fem.:]) and, as some say, it became brisk in respect of traffic: thus it appears to have two contr. significations: (TA:) and xadaEa Als~iEoru (tropical:) The price became high, or dear. (TA.) ― -b11- Said of a man, xadaEa also signifies (tropical:) His wealth, (K, TA,) and the like, (TA,) became small in amount, or little. (K, TA.) ― -b12- Said of a time, inf. n. xadoEN , (tropical:) Its rain became little: (TA:) and of rain, (tropical:) It became little. (K, TA.) ― -b13- Said of spittle, or saliva, (tropical:) It dried: (S, K, TA:) or it became little, and dried, in the mouth: (A, TA.) or it became deficient; and when it becomes deficient, it becomes thick; and when it becomes thick, it becomes stinking: (TA:) or it became corrupt: (IAar, TA:) and in like manner, said of a thing, it became corrupt, or bad. (TA.) [See also xaAdiEN , below.] ― -b14- Said of a generous man, (K,) (tropical:) He refrained [from giving], (S, L, K,) and refused. (L.) You say, kaAna fulaAnN yuEoTiY vum~a xadaEa (tropical:) [ Such a one used to give; then he refrained, and refused ]. (S.) -A2- xadaEahu aor. , inf. n. xadoEN , He cut, or severed, his [ vein called the ] A^axodaE . (TA.)

definition: A single act of deceit, delusion, guile, circumvention, or outwitting.
sourceDefinition: A single act of deceit, delusion, guile, circumvention, or outwitting. (Mgh.) It is said in a trad., (Mgh, TA,) AlHarobu xadoEapN , and ↓ xudoEapN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ xidoEapN , (K,) and ↓ xudaEapN , (AZ, Ks, S, Mgh, K,) accord. to different relaters; (Th, Mgh, K;) the first being the most chaste, (S, Mgh, Msb,) said to be the form used by Mo- hammad; (Th, Mgh, Msb;) the second ascribed by El-Khattábee to the vulgar; (TA;) the last the best in point of meaning: (Mgh:) i. e., accord. to the first reading, (Mgh,) War is finished by a single act of deceit, &c.; (Mgh, O, K;) accord. to the second, war is a thing by which one is deceived; (Mgh, Msb;) or war is deceived; for when one of the two parties deceives the other, it is as though the war itself were deceived; (IAth, TA;) [accord. to the third, war is a mode, or manner, of deceiving; ] and accord. to the fourth, war is a deceiver of those engaged in it (IAth, Mgh, TA) by the frequent deceits which occur therein. (Mgh.) -A2- (tropical:) A slumber. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Deceit, delusion, guile, circumvention, or outwitting; and a desire to do to another a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, without the latter's knowing whence it proceeds; (S, K;) a subst. from xadaEahu ; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ xidoEN , (Msb, TA,) or this is an inf. n.; (AZ, S, K;) and ↓ xudoEapN ; (TA;) and ↓ xidaAEN ; (TA;) which [is also an inf. n. of xaAdaEahu , and] originally signifies concealment: (Ham p. 541:) [and hence as above: and] also signifies prevention ( manoEN ); and art, artifice, cunning, or skill, in the management of affairs; (IAar, Sgh, K;) or a making another to resign, or relinquish, the object that he has in view, by pretending to him something the contrary of what he conceals. definition: [ Deceiving, deluding, beguiling, circumventing, outwitting, or the like;
sourceDefinition: [ Deceiving, deluding, beguiling, circumventing, outwitting, or the like; ] act. part. n. of xadaEahu ; as also ↓ xaduwEN ; (Msb;) or [rather] this latter is an intensive epithet, signifying one who deceives, &c., much, or often; or very deceitful, &c.; or a great deceiver, &c.; (Mgh, K;) and ↓ xad~aAEu , (Msb, TA,) and ↓ xadiEN , and ↓ xayodaEN ; (TA;) [but these three are also intensive epithets, like xaduwEN ;] and ↓ xudaEapN signifies one who deceives, &c., other men; (S;) or [rather] this last is syn. with xaduwEN as explained above, (K,) or xad~aAEN : (Mgh:) [the pl. of xaAdiEapN , fem. of xaAdiEN , is xawaAdiEu :] and the pl. of ↓ xaduwEN is xuduEN . (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Dab~N xAdiEN A [ lizard of the kind called ] Db~ that deceives, beguiles, or circumvents; (Z, TA;) as also ↓ xadiEN . (S, K.) ― -b3- And dahorN xaAdiEN and ↓ xudaEapN (assumed tropical:) [ Deceiving, or varying, and very deceitful, or very variable, fortune, or time ]. (TA.) [Whence, or] because of its variableness, (TA,) ↓ AlxudaEapu is (tropical:) a name for Fortune, or time. (K, TA.) ― -b4- And fulaAnN xaAdiEu Alr~aA^oYi (tropical:) Such a one remains not steadily in one opinion. (TA.) ― -b5- And xuluqN xaAdiEN (tropical:) A varying, or variable, disposition. (S, K, TA.) ― -b6- And suwqN xaAdiEapN (tropical:) A market varying, or variable, in its state; (S, A, O, K;) at one time being brisk, and at another time dull, in respect of traffic: (A, TA:) or a market dull in respect of traffic: or a market in which one cannot obtain a thing because of its dearness. (TA.) xaAdiEN also signifies (tropical:) Anything unsaleable, or difficult of sale, and in little demand. (TA.) And accord. to Fr, the Benoo-Asad use the epithet ↓ muxaAdiEu [perhaps a mistake for xaAdiEN ] in the sense of (tropical:) High, or dear, applied to a price. (TA.) ― -b7- And TariyqN xaAdiEN (tropical:) A road that appears at one time and disappears at another; as also ↓ xaduwEN : (K:) a road which one does not know: (TA:) a road deviating from the right course; (TA;) as also ↓ xayodaEN ; (S, K, TA;) which one does not know. (S, TA.) And maA='N xaAdiEN (tropical:) A water to which one does not know the way. (TA.) ― -b8- [Hence also,] sinuwna xawaAdiEu (tropical:) Years in which is little good; bad years: (Sh, TA:) and sinuwna ↓ xad~aAEapN (tropical:) (tropical:) years in which is little increase: (S, K, TA:) from xadaEa said of rain, or of spittle; and therefore doubly tropical: (TA:) or, as some say, years in which is much rain, and in which the produce is little. (Sgh.) xaAdiEN also signifies (assumed tropical:) Corrupt, or bad; applied to food and other things. (TA.) And you say, diynaArN xaAdiEN (assumed tropical:) A deficient, or defective, deenár. (S.) And rajulN xaAdiEN (tropical:) A man who brings evil upon others. (TA.)

definition: [ More, and most, deceitful, deluding, guileful, outwitting, or the like ].
sourceDefinition: [ More, and most, deceitful, deluding, guileful, outwitting, or the like ]. [Hence,] A^axodaEu mino Dab~K [ More deceitful, or guileful, than a dabb ]; a prov.; (S, K;) applied to a person over whom one has not power, by reason of deceit, or guile. (IAar.) They said also, A_in~aka laA^axodiEu mino Dab~K Hara$otuhu [ Verily thou art more deceitful, or guileful, than a dabb that I have hunted ]. (AZ, AAF, O.) [See xidaAEN .] -A2- AlA^axodaEu [app. Each of the two branches of the occipital artery which are distributed upon the occiput; ] a certain vein, (S, K,) one of a pair of veins, called the A^axodaEaAni , (S, Mgh, Msb,) in the cupping-place (Mgh, Msb) of the neck, (Mgh,) or in the place [ of the application ] of the two cupping-instruments; being a branch from the wariyd [or carotid artery ]; (S, K;) sometimes the scarification [for cupping] happens to be upon one of them, and the patient consequently is exhausted by loss of blood: (S:) the AxdEAn are two concealed veins in the place of the cupping of the neck: Lh says, they are two veins in the neck: some say that they are the wadajaAni , q. v.: (TA:) the pl. is A^axaAdiEu . (K.) ― -b2- fulaAnN $adiydu AlA^axodaEi means Such a one is strong in the place of the AxdE . (As, S, O.) ― -b3- It also means (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one is ] a person who resists; unyielding; uncomplying. (TA.) And lay~inu AlA^axodaEu (assumed tropical:) One who does not resist; yielding; complying. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, lawaY fulaAnN A^axodaEahu (tropical:) Such a one turned away, or aside, and behaved proudly, or haughtily. (TA.) And saw~aY A^axodaEahu (tropical:) He relinquished pride, or haughtiness. (TA.) And to him who is proud, one says, laA^uqiyman~a A^axodaEayoka , meaning (assumed tropical:) I will assuredly dispel thy pride. (Ham p. 432.)

definition: and ↓ mixodaEN (Fr, Yaakoob, S, Msb, K) and ↓ maxodaEN ;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ mixodaEN (Fr, Yaakoob, S, Msb, K) and ↓ maxodaEN ; (Msb, TA;) the first of which is the original form, the second being adopted because the first was found to be difficult of utterance; (Fr, Yaakoob, S;) and the first is the only proper subst. of the measure mufoEalN ; other words of that measure being epithets; (Sb;) A closet, or small chamber, in which a thing is kept, or preserved; (Msb;) i. q. xizaAnapN ; (Fr, Yaakoob, S, K;) by which is meant a small chamber within a large chamber: (TA:) from A^axodaEahu meaning “he hid it,” or “concealed it:” (Msb:) and [in like manner] ↓ xaAdiEapN signifies a chamber within a chamber: (K:) Er-Rághib says, as though its builder made it a deceiver of him who might seek, or desire, to take, or reach, a thing in it. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. xu$uwEN , He was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Axt$E (S, K) and ↓ tx$~E ; (Abu-lFet-h, Ham pp. 24 and 127;) xu$uwEN being syn. with xuDuwEN : (S, Msb, K:) or x$wE is nearly the same as xDwE : (Lth, K:) or the former is mostly used as meaning in the voice; and the latter, in the necks: (Msb:) or the latter is in the body; and the former is in the voice and in the eyes: (K:) or, as we read in the 'Eyn, the former is nearly the same as the latter, except that the latter is in the body, and signifies the acknowledging of humility and submission, and the former is in the voice and in the eyes; and the like is said in the Nh [and in the Msb in art. xDE ]. (TA.) You say, xa$aEati AlA^aSowaAtu The voices were [or shall be (as in the Kur xx. 107]) still and low: (Msb:) or low: or, as some say, still. (TA.) And xa$aEa bibaSarihi He lowered his eye. (S.) And ↓ Axt$E and ↓ tx$~E He cast his eye towards the ground, and lowered his voice. (TA.) Lth says that you say, fulaAnN ↓ Axt$E , but not Axt$E bibaSarihi . (TA.) And xa$aEa baSaruhu His eye became contracted. (TA.) And xa$aEato duwnahu AlA^aboSaAru (tropical:) [meaning The eyes were cast down before him, or it ]. (TA.) xu$uwEN also signifies The being, or becoming, still: and the abasing oneself; or lowering oneself. (K, TA.) And ↓ Axt$E , He lowered, or stooped, or bent down, his breast. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, inf. n. as above, He feared; for instance, in prayer: (TA:) or xa$aEa fiY SalaAtihi and fiY duEaAy^ihi signifies He applied himself with his heart to [or in ] his prayer, and his supplication. (Msb.) ― -b3- xa$aEati AlkawaAkibu , (Aboo-'Adnán,) inf. n. as above, (K,) (tropical:) The stars approached to the place of setting; (Aboo-'Adnán;) or approached to setting: (K:) or sank, and nearly disappeared in their setting-place. (Aboo- Sálih El-Kilábee.) [The corresponding phrase in Hebrew, occurring in Gen. xxxvii. 9, probably has the same meaning.] ― -b4- xa$aEati Al$~amosu (tropical:) The sun became eclipsed. (TA.) ― -b5- xa$aEa Als~anaAmu (tropical:) The hump for the most part went away; (O, K;) i. e. the hump of the camel: (TA:) or became lean; its fat going away, and its height becoming lowered. (L.) ― -b6- fulaAnN ji*olN HikaAkN xa$aEati Eanohu AlA^ubanu is a saying of the Arabs, explained in art. Hk . (TA in that art.) ― -b7- xa$aEa Alwaraqu (tropical:) The leaves withered. (TA.) ― -b8- xa$aEati AlA^aroDu (tropical:) The earth, or land, dried up, not being rained upon. (TA.) -A2- xa$aEa fulaAnN xaraA$iY~N Sadorihi Such a one ejected the viscous saliva [or phlegm of his chest ]. (O, K.) ― -b2- And xa$aEato xaraA$iY~N Sarihi The viscous saliva [or phlegm of his chest ] became ejected. (O, K.) The verb is thus intrans., as well as trans. (O.)

definition: A low hill: (S:) or a hill cleaving to the ground: (IAar, K:) and a piece of rugged ground: (IDrd, K:) or [ elevated ground such as is termed ] quf~ that is for the most part soft, i.
sourceDefinition: A low hill: (S:) or a hill cleaving to the ground: (IAar, K:) and a piece of rugged ground: (IDrd, K:) or [ elevated ground such as is termed ] quf~ that is for the most part soft, i. e. neither stone nor clay: (Lth:) and a rock growing in the sea: (TA:) pl. xu$aEN . (K.) It is said in a trad., kaAnati AlA^aroDu xu$oEapF EalaY AlmaA='i vum~a duHiyato [ The earth was a low hill, &c., upon the water: then it was spread out ]: (S:) but this trad. is variously related. (TA.)

definition: Lowly, humble, or submissive, (K, TA,) and still: (TA:) [or so in the voice and in the eyes: (see 1:)] pl.
sourceDefinition: Lowly, humble, or submissive, (K, TA,) and still: (TA:) [or so in the voice and in the eyes: (see 1:)] pl. xaA$iEuwna and xu$~aEN ; the latter also signifying men lowering, humbling, or abasing, themselves: or constraining themselves to be, or to become, lowly, humble, or submissive; or to be so, or to become so, in voice, or in the eyes: or casting their eyes towards the ground, and lowering their voices. (TA.) Hence, in the Kur [lxviii. 43, and lxx. 44], accord. to different readings, xaA$iEapF A^aboSaAruhumo and xaA$iEFA A^aboSaAruhumo [ Having their eyes cast down ]: the accus. case being used as denotative of state. (Zj, TA.) ― -b2- Bowing; or bending down the head and body. (K.) ― -b3- Fearing. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) A camel's foot ( xuf~N ) cleaving to the ground. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A wall that has cracked, and given notice of its falling, and [ then ] become even with the ground. (TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A herb dried up, and falling down upon the ground. (TA.) ― -b7- Applied to a place, (S, K,) and, with p , to a balodap [or portion of country], (S,) (tropical:) Overspread with dust, [in the CK AlmuEanobaru is erroneously put for Almugab~aru ,] and having in it no place of alighting, or of abiding: (S, K:) and to land ( A^aroDN ), meaning of which the wind raises the surface, by reason of its softness, so as to efface its traces, or tracks: (L:) or in this case it is with p , as in the Kur xli. 39, and means altered ( mutagay~irap [probably a mistranscription for mutagab~irap overspread with dust ]), and having its herbage broken in pieces: (Zj, * TA:) or dried up, and containing no herbage: (Jel:) or containing no green herbage: or low, or depressed, and still: (TA:) and, without p , applied to a place, to which one finds not his way: (Sgh, K:) pl. xu$~aEN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) or bika*aA , (A, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. xaS~N (K) and xuSuwSN (S, Msb, K) and xaSuwSN (TA) and xaSuwSiy~apN and xuSuwSiy~apN , (S, Mgh, * Msb, K,) of which last two the former is the more chaste, (S, TA,) and is the form mentioned in the Fs and its Exposi tions, and the Y in it is said to be the relative Y , and the Y which is characteristic of an inf. n., whereas in the latter it is said to be a characteristic of intensiveness, but MF thinks that this requires consideration, because the Y is also said to be, and by some more commonly, without teshdeed, as in karaAhiyapN and EalaAniyapN , (TA,) and xiS~iySaY , (S, K,) like mik~iyvaY , which is said to be the only other instance of this measure, (TA,) [but some others might be added, as dil~iylaY and fix~iyraY and qit~iytaY ,] and xiS~iySaA='u , (IAar, Kr, K,) [like mik~iyvaA='u ,] the former of which last two [each of which has an intensive signification] is the chaste, and com monly known, form, (TA,) and xuS~iy~apN , or xiS~iy~apN , or xaSiy~apN , (accord. to different copies of the K,) written by Sgh with damm, (TA,) and taxiS~apN , (Ibn-' Abbád, K,) or, as some say, xaSuwSiy~apN and xiS~iy~apN [or xuS~iy~apN or xaS~iy~apN ] are each a quasi-inf. n., as also xaAS~apN , (TA,) He distinguished him particularly, peculiarly, or specially, i. e., above, or from, or exclusively of, others, by the thing, or by such a thing; he particularized him, or particularly or peculiarly or specially characterized him, thereby; syn. faD~alahu (A, K, TA) duwna gayorihi , and may~azahu ; (TA;) he appropriated, or assigned, [ the thing or] such a thing, or made it to belong, to him alone, or in particular, or peculiarly, or specially, exclusively of others; (Msb;) and bihi ↓ AxtS~hu signifies the same; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ AxS~hu , (A, [but for this I know not any other authority,]) and ↓ xS~Shu ; (A;) or this last has an intensive signification. (Msb.) You say, xaS~ahu biAluwd~i He distinguished him &c. by love, or affection; or favoured him in preference to another, or others, thereby. (K, TA.) As to the saying of AZ, A_ini A@moraA^N xaS~aniY EamodFA mawad~atahu EalaY Alt~anaAniY laEinodiY gayoru makofuwri [ If a man distinguish me above, or from, or exclusively of, others, purposely, by his love, or because of his love of me, notwithstanding distance of each from the other, it will not be disacknowledged with me, ] the meaning is, xaS~aniY bimawad~atihi ; or it may be xaS~aniY limawad~atihi A_iy~aAYa [in the TA bimawad~atihi , which is evidently a mistranscription]; for, says ISd, we have not heard xaS~ahu [or rather xaS~a ] doubly transitive. (TA.) And [hence] xaS~ahu bika*aA also signifies He gave him such a thing in large quantity, or abundantly. (TA.) [You say also, xaS~ahu biAl*~ikori He distinguished, &c., or singled out, him, or it, by mention: or he particularized, peculiarized, or specified, him, or it, thereby; he particularly, peculiarly, or specially, mentioned him, or it. And xaS~ahu , alone, He pointed particularly, or peculiarly, to him, or it, in what he said; or he meant particularly, or peculiarly, him, or it. And xaS~a minohu ka*aA He distinguished, particularized, peculiarized, or specified, thereof such a thing: and he distinguished therefrom such a thing; he particularly, peculiarly, or specially, excepted therefrom such a thing. ] You also say, xaS~ahu linafosihi (TA) and linafosihi ↓ AxtS~hu (T, A, TA) [ He appropriated, or took, or chose, him, or it, particularly, or specially, to, or for, himself; as also xaS~a bihi nafosahu and bihi nafosahu ↓ AxtS~ ]. And fulaAnFA ↓ huwa yasotaxiS~u and yasotaxoliSuhu (A, TA) [ He appropriates such a one purely to himself, exclusively of any partner; (see the latter verb;)] he chooses such a one for himself; he appropriates him to himself as his particular, or special, intimate; (TA in art. xlS ;) both signify the same. (S and K in art. xlS .) [And ↓ AxtS~hu He treated him, or behaved towards him, with partiality; was partial towards him: a signification implied by the first explanation in this art.: and in this sense it is often used.] -A2- xaS~a , aor. , [contr. to general rule, by which it should be , for it is intrans., and of the measure faEala , accord. to the Msb,] inf. n. xuSuwSN , [and app. xaSuwSiy~apN and xuSuwSiy~apN , accord. to modern usage,] It was, or became, particular, peculiar, or special; restricted, or confined, to one or more of persons, places, or things; distinct, or distinguished, from others; not common, or general; contr. of Eam~a ; as also ↓ AxtS~ : (Msb:) [each, also, followed by lahu , signifies He, or it, belonged, pertained, or appertained, to him, or it, particularly, peculiarly, specially, or exclusively; it so related to him, or it; it was, or became, peculiar to him, or it: see also the latter verb below.] -A3- xaS~a , sec. pers. xaSiSota , (in the CK xuSiSotu ,) [inf. n., app., xaSaASapN and xaSaASN and xaSaASaA='u ,] (tropical:) He was, or became, poor; in a state of poverty; (Fr, Sgh, K;) as also ↓ AxtS~ . (A, TA.)

definition: An interstice, interval, or intervening space or opening;
sourceDefinition: An interstice, interval, or intervening space or opening; (S, K;) as also ↓ xaSaASN [which is commonly used as a coll. gen. n.] and ↓ xaSaASaA='u : (K:) or an interstice, &c., in the vagor [app. meaning the front teeth ]; as also ↓ the second of these words: (TA:) or the first and ↓ second, (TA,) or ↓ all, (K,) any interstice, &c., or hole or perforation, in a door, and sieve, and [ veil of the kind called ] buroquE , and the like, (K, TA,) such as a cloud, and a strainer, &c.: (TA:) [ a crevice, cranny, chink, or fissure: ] or the first, (TA,) or ↓ all, (K,) a small hole or perforation: (K, TA:) or the first has this signification as well as the signification first mentioned: (S:) or the ↓ second, the like of a kaw~ap [or mural aperture ] in a [ structure of the kind called ] qub~ap , or the like, when as wide as the face; or, accord. to some, whether wide or narrow: (TA:) and the same, interstices, intervals, or intervening spaces or openings, in a xuS~ ; (TA;) or narrow interstices, &c., therein: (T, TA:) and the same, (TA,) or ↓ all, (K,) the intervening spaces between the three stones upon which a cooking-pot is placed; (K, TA;) and between the fingers: (TA:) and the first, the intervening spaces between the feathers of an arrow: (IAar, TA:) pl. [of the first,] xaSaASaAtN . (TA.) You say of the moon, badaA mino xaSaASapi Algayomi [ It appeared from the gap of the cloud, or clouds ]. (S, A.) ― -b2- Also A cloud itself; or clouds; syn. gayomN . (TA.) -A2- Also the first, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ second, (S, K,) and ↓ third, (IDrd, K,) (tropical:) Poverty; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) need; (A, Msb, TA;) straitness, or difficulty; (Mgh;) an evil state or condition: (TA:) from xaSaASaAt meaning the “ holes ” of a sieve: whence a saying cited voce tajam~ala : (Mgh:) or from the first of the senses explained in this paragraph; because a thing, when it opens so as to form an interstice, becomes weak and unsound. (TA.) You say also, ↓ sadadotu xuSaASapa fulaAnK , with damm, meaning, (tropical:) I repaired the broken fortune of such a one. (A, TA.) ― -b2- Also the first, (tropical:) Thirst; as in camels when they return from water without having satisfied themselves with drink: and hunger; as in a man when he has not satisfied himself with food. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: dim. of xaAS~apN ; (A, K;) [like duwayob~apN , q. v., dim. of daAb~apN ;] originally xuwayoSiSapN ; (TA;) the Y being quiescent because the Y of the dim. cannot be movent; (A, K;) [properly signifying A little, or young, particular, or peculiar, or special, friend, companion, associate, attendant, or servant; and used in other senses, like other diminutives; implying littleness of estimation; and also affection, and awe.] It is said in a trad., (TA,) Ealayoka bixuwayoS~api nafosika [ Keep thou to the little, or dear, particular friend of thine own self: so it seems to mean accord. to Z, being mentioned by him among the proper expressions belonging to this art.: but accord. to the TK, it appears to be tropical; for the meaning is there said to be, (assumed tropical:) thine own particular state, or condition ]. (A, TA.) In another trad., xwyS~p is used as signifying A little, young, particular, or peculiar, or special, servant. (TA.) And in another trad. it is said, baAdiruwA biAlA^aEomaAli sit~FA Ald~aj~aAli waka*aA waka*aA waxuwayoS~apa A^aHadikumo , i. e. (assumed tropical:) Strive ye to be before six things with [ good ] works; Antichrist, and such and such things, and the event of death which is specially, or peculiarly, appointed to any one of you: [or, I would rather say, the awful special awaiter of any one of you; though it is asserted that] the diminutive form is here used to denote low estimation of that which it signifies in comparison with what follows it, namely, the resurrection, &c. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, A, K) and ↓ xufaArapN (S, A, Msb, K) [both, in Ham p. 677, said to be inf. ns., but they are rather to be regarded as quasi-inf. ns.,] and ↓ xifaArapN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ xafaArapN (K) Protection, refuge, preservation, rescue, or liberation, (S, * A, Msb, K,) from one seeking or pursuing: (Msb:) a compact, a covenant, or an obligation, by which one becomes responsible for the safety, or safe-keeping, of a person or thing; or the like; or simply responsibility, or suretiship; syn. *im~apN : (S, TA:) pl. of the first, xufarN . (TA.) It is said in a trad., mano Sal~aY AlS~uboHa fahowa fiY xuforapi A@ll~`hi Whoso performeth the prayer of daybreak, he is in the protection of God. (TA.) And in another trad., Ald~umuwEu xufaru AlEuyuwni Tears are the protections of the eyes from Hell-fire when they weep from the fear of God. (TA.) And wafato , (S, A,) and ↓ xufaAratuka , (A,) May thy compact, covenant, or obligation, which hath made thee responsible for my safety, be fulfilled, (S,) is said by the object of protection to his protector when he has not as yet preserved him in safety. (A.)

definition: A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' , black, square, and having EalamaAni [i.
sourceDefinition: A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' , black, square, and having EalamaAni [i. e. two ornamental or coloured or figured borders ]: (S, A, Mgh, K:) or a black ksA' , having a border such as is above described ( muEolam ) at each end, and which is of xaz~ , [q. v.], or of wool: (Msb:) if not bordered, it is not so called: (S, Msb:) or, accord. to As, a mulaA='ap of wool, or of xaz~ , bordered ( muEolamap ); not unless bordered: so called because of its softness and thinness, and smallness of bulk when it is folded: Ahmad Ibn-Fáris says that it is the black kisaA=' : and he says that it may be thus called because a man wraps himself with it, so that it is against his A^axomaS , meaning by this his waist: (Har p. 21:) pl. xamaAy^iSu : or xmAy^S are garments of xaz~ , thick, black, and red, and having thick A^aEolaAm [or borders such as above described ]; worn by people of old. (TA.) El-Aashà says, A_i*aA jur~idato yawomFA Hasibota xamiySapF EalayohaA wa jiroyaAla Aln~aDiyri Ald~ulaAmiSaA [ When she is stripped of her clothing, any day, thou wouldst think there was upon her a khameesah, and the glistening redness of gold ]: As says, he likens her [long and spreading] hair to a xmySp , which is black. (S.) [See also xamiysN , voce ximosN , near the end of the paragraph.]

definition: A man whose foot rises from the ground, [or is hollow in the middle of the sole, ] so that it does not touch it: fem.
sourceDefinition: A man whose foot rises from the ground, [or is hollow in the middle of the sole, ] so that it does not touch it: fem. xamoSaA='u : and pl. xumoSN : (Msb:) and ↓ xumoSaAnN signifies having the middle of the sole of the foot moderately rising from the ground; which is a goodly quality; but when it is flat, or rises much, it is dispraised: so explained by IAar when he was asked by Th respecting 'Alee's saying of Mohammad, [cited, but not explained, in the K,] kaAna xumoSaAna AlA^axomaSayoni : or, accord. to Az, xumoSaAnN signifies having the part [ of the sole ] of the foot which does not cleave to the ground in treading very much retiring from the ground. (TA.) ― -b2- AlA^axomaSu [when without the article Al also written without tenween accord. to the best authorities, because the quality of an epithet is original to it, and that of a subst. is accidental,] also signifies The part [ of the sole ] of the human foot which does not cleave to the ground in treading; (Az, TA;) the part of the sole of the human foot which is hollow, so that it does not touch the ground; (S, K; *) the part of the bottom of the human foot which is thin, and retires from the ground; or, as some explain it, [meaning the same,] the xaSor of the human foot: (TA:) pl. A^axaAmiSu . (Msb.) ― -b3- See also xamiySN . ― -b4- Also The waist of a man. (Har p. 21.)

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, A, K) and ↓ daA^abN (S, M, K) [both originally inf. ns. of 1: and hence,] (tropical:) A custom, manner, habit, or wont: (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K:) an affair, a business, or a concern: (Zj, T, S, A, K:) and a case, state, or condition: (Zj, * T, * S, * M, A, * K: *) and a deed, or work. (T.)

definition: , (S, M, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K,) aor. and , (M, K,) inf. n. dabolN , (M,) He collected it together, (S, M, K,) like as one collects together a morsel, or gobbet, or mouthful, of food with his fingers: (S:) and ↓ db~lhu , inf. n. tadobiylN , [in like manner] signifies he collected it together. (TA.) And dabala All~uqomapa , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. as above; (M;) and ↓ db~lhA , (M, K,) inf. n. tadobiylN ; (TA;) He made the morsel, or gobbet, or mouthful, large, (M, K,) collecting it together with his fingers: (M:) or the latter signifies he made the morsel, or gobbet, or mouthful, large, and swallowed it. (IAar, TA.) And dabalotu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ dab~alotuhu ; (S;) I made the thing into lumps, or compact pieces or portions: (S, * TA:) and AlHayosa ↓ db~l , inf. n. tadobiylN , He made the Hys [generally explained as meaning dates mixed with clarified butter and the preparation of dried curd called A^aqiT , kneaded, or rubbed and pressed with the hand until they mingle together and their stones come forth, ] into dubal [pl. of dubolapN , q. v.]. (T, TA.) -A2- dabala AlA^aroDa , (T, M, K,) inf. n. dabolN (S, M, K) and dubuwlN , (M, K,) He put the land into a right, or proper, state, prepared it, or improved it, [or manured it, ] with dung such as is termed sirojiyn , [in the K siroqiyn ,] and the like, (T, S, M, K,) in order that it might become good: (T, M:) and so damalahaA . (T.) ― -b2- And dabalotuhu means I put it into a right, or proper, state; prepared it; or improved it; namely, anything; as also damalotuhu : for instance, a rivulet; i. e. he cleansed it, and put it into a right, or proper, state. (S.) -A3- dabalahu , (K,) inf. n. dabolN , (TA,) also signifies He struck him consecutive strokes with a staff, or stick, (K,) and with a whip. (TA.) ― -b2- dabalatohu ↓ Ald~ubuwlu Calamities, or misfortunes, befell him: or may calamities, or misfortunes, befall him. (K.) And ↓ dabalatohumu Ald~ubayolapu Calamity, or misfortune; befell them: or may calamity, &c.: (A'Obeyd, S, M:) or they perished: or may they perish. (T.) And ↓ dabalatohu Ald~abuwlu , (K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, Ald~ubuwlu ,]) and *abalatohu Al*~abuwlu , (TA,) Calamity, or misfortune, befell him: or may calamity, &c.: (TA:) or the bereft woman, i. e. his mother, became bereft of him by death: or may the bereft woman, &c. (K, TA.) ― -b3- ↓ maA lahu dabala daboluhu , or *abala *aboluhu , is a form of imprecation: see the latter in art. *bl . (TA.) -A4- dabila , aor. , inf. n. dabalN , He (a camel, or other animal,) became full of fat and flesh. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A certain malady (M, Mgh, K) in the jawof , (M, K,) [i. e.,] in the belly, (Mgh,) being a collection of corrupt matter therein; (Mgh, TA;) wherefore it is thus called; (TA;) as also ↓ adbolapN (M, K) and ↓ dubolapN : (K:) accord. to ISh, an ulcer that penetrates into the belly: [see also dubaAlN :] or an ulcer that comes forth within the side, and discharges internally; the sufferer from which seldom recovers: also called *aAtu Aljanobi : (TA in art. jnb :) a large tumour (in Pers. waram buzurG ). (KL.) [Abu-l-Kásim Ez-Zahráwee describes the modes of cauterizing the dbylp in order to hasten its coming to maturity. (See “ Albucasis de Chirurgia, ” p. 98, where the word is twice written *bylp ; once, *bEylp ; and once, correctly, dbylp .) Golius explains dabolapN and dubolapN by “ vomica, apostema, ” as on the authority of the S and KL; in neither of which do I find anything of the kind: nor do I find dabolapN even mentioned in either of those works.] ― -b2- See also dibolN . Hence the saying, dabalatohumu Ald~ubayolapu : see 1, in the latter part of the paragraph.

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. duxuwlN (S, Msb, K) and madoxalN , (S, K,) He, or it, entered; or went, came, passed, or got, in; contr. of xaraja ; (K;) as also ↓ Aid~axala , of the measure AifotaEala , and ↓ Andxl , (S, K,) this last occuring in poetry, but not chaste, (S,) and ↓ tdx~l , (K,) or this signifies it (a thing) entered by little and little. (S, O.) You say, daxalotu madoxalFA HasanFA [like duxuwlFA HasanFA I entered with a good entering ]. (S.) And daxalotu Albayota (S) or Ald~aAra , i. e. [ I entered the house, or] I became within the house, and the like, (Msb,) correctly meaning A_ilaY Albayoti [&c., or fiY Albayoti &c., i. e. I entered into the house, &c.], the prep. being suppressed, and the noun put in the accus. case after the manner of an objective complement: for nouns of place are of two kinds, vague and definite; the vague being such as the six relative locations, xalofN , and qud~aAmN , and yamiynN , and $imaAlN , and fawoqN , and taHotN , and the like, such as A^amaAmN , and waraA='N , and A^aEolaY , and A^asofalu , and Einoda , and laduno , and wasoTN in the sense of bayonN , and qubaAlapN , all which, and similar nouns of place, may become adverbs, because indefinite; for dost thou not see that what is xalof to thee may be qud~aAm to another? but that which is definite, having make, and corporeal substance, and tracts that comprehend it, as a mountain and a valley and a market and a house and a mosque, the noun signifying such a thing cannot become an adverb; for you may not say, qaEadotu Ald~aAra , nor Sal~ayotu Almasojida , nor nimotu Aljabala , nor qumotu AlwaAdiYa ; the phrases of this kind that occur being instances of the suppression of a prep.; as daxalotu Albayota , and nazalotu AlwaAdiYa , and SaEidotu Aljabala . (S, O, TA.) You say also, daxalotu EalaY zayodK Ald~aAra , meaning I entered the house after Zeyd, he being in it. (Msb.) [And simply daxala Ealayohi He came in upon him: and also he came upon him; i. e. invaded him. ] And daxala biA@moraA^atihi , (Msb, TA,) and EalayohaA , (MA,) inf. n. duxuwlN , (Mgh, Msb,) [like daxala biA^aholihi , and EalayohaA , (see A^aholN ,) i. e. (tropical:) He went in to his wife or woman, ] is a metonymical phrase, denoting AljimaAE , (Msb, TA,) i. e. AlwaTo' , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) whether it be such as is allowed by the law or such as is forbidden, (Mgh,) generally such as is lawful. (Msb, TA. [See what is said in explanation of the term xalowapN in the first paragraph of art. xlw .]) And daxala baEoDuhu fiY baEoDK i. q. tadaAxala [q. v.]. (TA in art. qSr , &c.) [For ex.,] you say, daxala baEoDu Aln~ujuwmi fiY baEoDK [ The stars became confused together ]. (Mgh and TA in art. $bk : in the former coupled with AixotalaTato .) And daxala fiyhimo [ He entered among them, so as to become a member of their community, confraternity, party, sect, or the like; ] said of a stranger. (K.) [And daxala fiY TaAEatihi : see TaAy^iEN , in art. (S, O, TA.) You say also, daxalotu EalaY zayodK Ald~aAra , meaning I entered the house after Zeyd, he being in it. (Msb.) [And simply daxala Ealayohi He came in upon him: and also he came upon him; i. e. invaded him. ] And daxala biA@moraA^atihi , (Msb, TA,) and EalayohaA , (MA,) inf. n. duxuwlN , (Mgh, Msb,) [like daxala biA^aholihi , and EalayohaA , (see A^aholN ,) i. e. (tropical:) He went in to his wife or woman, ] is a metonymical phrase, denoting AljimaAE , (Msb, TA,) i. e. AlwaTo' , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) whether it be such as is allowed by the law or such as is forbidden, (Mgh,) generally such as is lawful. (Msb, TA. [See what is said in explanation of the term xalowapN in the first paragraph of art. xlw .]) And daxala baEoDuhu fiY baEoDK i. q. tadaAxala [q. v.]. (TA in art. qSr , &c.) [For ex.,] you say, daxala baEoDu Aln~ujuwmi fiY baEoDK [ The stars became confused together ]. (Mgh and TA in art. $bk : in the former coupled with AixotalaTato .) And daxala fiyhimo [ He entered among them, so as to become a member of their community, confraternity, party, sect, or the like; ] said of a stranger. (K.) [And daxala fiY TaAEatihi : see TaAy^iEN , in art. TwE .] When daxala is said of income, or revenue, [meaning It came in, accrued, or was received, ] the aor. is as above, and the inf. n. daxolN : (Msb:) and you say, yadoxulu EalaY AlA_inosaAni [ It comes in, or accrues, to the man ]. (Msb, K. *) daxala bihi [lit. He entered with him, or it ]: see 4. ― -b2- [Hence, daxala fiyhi meaning (assumed tropical:) It became included, comprehended, or comprised, in it. And hence,] daxala fiY diyni AlA_isolaAmi (assumed tropical:) [ He entered within the pale of the religion of ElIslám; he entered the communion of that religion; he entered into, embraced, or became a proselyte to, that religion ]. (Msb in art. slm , &c. [See Kur cx. 2.]) And daxala fiY AlA^amori , inf. n. duxuwlN , (assumed tropical:) He entered upon, began, or commenced, the affair. (Msb.) [And daxala fiY A^amori gayorihi , and A^umuwri gayorihi , and ↓ tdx~l , and ↓ tdAxl (assumed tropical:) He entered into, or mixed himself in, another's affair, and another's affairs. ] ― -b3- [Hence also, daxala Ealayohi said of night, &c., It came upon him, or invaded him. And said of a word, such as a prep. &c., It was, or became, prefixed to it, preposed to it, or put before it. ] ― -b4- [ daxalaniY minohu seems (from an instance in art. bDE in the K) to mean (assumed tropical:) An evil opinion of him entered my mind; from daxolN as signifying “ a thing that induces doubt, or suspicion, or evil opinion. ”] -A2- duxila , (S, K,) like EuniYa ; (K;) and daxila , aor. ; inf. n. [of the former] daxolN and [of the latter] daxalN ; (K;) (assumed tropical:) He had an unsoundness ( daxalN , S, K, i. e. fasaAdN , K) in his intel-lect, (S, K,) or in his body, (K,) or in his grounds of pretension to respect. (TA in explanation of the former verb.) And daxila A^amoruhu , aor. , (K,) inf. n. daxalN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) His affair, or case, or state, was, or became, intrinsically bad or corrupt or unsound. (K.) ― -b2- duxila AlT~aEaAmu The corn, or food, became eaten by worms or the like.
