sourceDefinition: Income, or revenue, or profit, that comes in, or accrues, to a man from his immovable property, such as land and houses and palm-trees &c., (T, Msb, K,) and from his merchandise; (Msb;) contr. of xarojN ; (S;) as also ↓ madoxuwlN [for madoxuwlN bihi ]: (TA:) the former is originally an inf. n., of which the verb is daxala , aor. . (O, TA. [See also another reading of this verse voce raqolapN .]) -A3- See also dixaAlN : -A4- and daxilN .

definition: primarily signifies A thing that enters into another thing and is not of it.
sourceDefinition: primarily signifies A thing that enters into another thing and is not of it. (Bd in xvi. 94.) See daxolN , in three places. Also Badness, corruptness, or unsoundness; or a bad, a corrupt, or an unsound, state or quality; (S in art. dgl , and K;) in intellect or in body [&c.]. (K.) You say, fiY Eaqolihi daxalN [ In his intellect is an unsoundness ]. (S, K.) And h`*aAAlA^amoru fiyhi daxalN and dagalN [ This affair, or case, in it is an unsoundness ]: both signify the same. (S.) ― -b2- Rottenness in a palm-tree. (TA.) ― -b3- Leanness, or emaciation. (TA.) ― -b4- Perfidiousness, faithlessness, or treachery: (K and TA; but not in the CK:) deceit, guile, or circumvention. (S, K.) Hence, in the Kur [xvi. 96], walaA tat~axi*uwA A^ayomaAnakumo daxalFA bayonakumo [ And make ye not your oaths to be a means of] deceit, or guile, or circumvention, between you. (S, TA. [And in the same sense it is used in verse 94 of the same ch.]) -A2- Also People, or persons, who assert their relationship to those of whom they are not: (K:) in this sense thought by ISd to be a quasi-pl. n. [app. of daxiylN (q. v.), like as $arafN is of $ariyfN ]. (TA.) You say, humo daxalN fiY baniY fulaAnK They are, among the sons of such a one, persons who assert their relationship to them not being of them. (S, K.) [But Freytag asserts, though without naming any authority, evidently taking it from the TK, in which I find it, that one says, hm dxl lhm , and also hw ; thus applying it to a single person (which is questionable) as well as to a plurality.] ― -b2- And Tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, trees; (K;) as also dagalN . (TA.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) A companion, [ such as is ] a confidant, and special friend;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A companion, [ such as is ] a confidant, and special friend; as also ↓ daxiylN (KL) and ↓ daxiylapN [app. for SaAHibu daxiylapK ] (K * and TA voce waliyjapN ) and ↓ dixolapN [app. for SaAHibu dixolap ]: (L voce waliyjapN :) [the pl.] duxoluluwna signifies special, or particular, and choice, or select, friends: (Az, TA:) or duxolulN signifies, as also ↓ dixolalN and ↓ daxiylN and ↓ mudaAxilN , one who enters with another into the affairs of the latter: (K, TA:) [i. e.] Alr~ajuli ↓ daxiylu and duxoluluhu signify the man's particular, or special, intimate, who enters with him into his affairs. (S.) You say, bayonahumaA duxolulN and ↓ dixolalN , meaning (assumed tropical:) Between them two is a particular, or special, intimate, who enters with them into their affairs: so says Lh: but ISd says, I know not what it is: accord. to the T, on the authority of AO, the meaning is, between them is brotherhood, or fraternization, and love, or affection: and accord. to ISd and the K, AlHub~i ↓ duxolalN and duxoluluhu [the latter not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K] and ↓ daAxiluhu signify (assumed tropical:) purity of inward love. (TA.) ― -b2- duxoluluwna signifies also Persons of the lower, or lowest, sort, who enter among a people, or party, of whom they are not: thus having two contr. meanings. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- Aldxll [app. Ald~uxolulu ] and ↓ Ald~ux~aAlu [thus in the TA] and ↓ Ald~aAxilu , accord. to IAar, all signify The same as AlA^u*uni ↓ dax~aAli [an appellation now applied to the ear-wig; in the K, art. Eqrb , said to be the EuqorubaAn , but not as meaning the Eaqorab or the male Eaqorab ]: accord. to AZ, it is the hrnSAn [i. e. hironiSaAn or hirinoSaAn , a kind of worm, the species of which is doubtful]. (TA.) ― -b4- See also dix~alN . -A2- And see duxolapN .

sourceDefinition: [an inf. n. of 3, q. v.]. ― -b2- In watering, (S, K,) it is The putting in a camel, that has drunk, between two camels that have not drunk, (K,) or the bringing back a camel, that has drunk, from the resting-place by the water, to the watering-trough, and putting him in between two thirsty camels, (S,) in order that he may drink what, may-be, he has not drunk: (S, K:) in like manner it is explained in the T, on the authority of As, who adds that this is done only when the water is scanty: (TA:) or the putting in a weak or sick camel [ that has already drunk ] with those that are drinking, and then, after that, with those that are returning to the water, so that he drinks three times: (Skr:) or the driving of camels to the watering-trough a second time, in order that they may complete their drinking, after they have already been watered drove by drove: (JK, TA:) so says Lth; but the approved explanation is that of As: (TA:) or the driving of camels to the watering-trough at once, all together; as also ↓ daxolN . (JK.) -A2- The forelocks of a horse; (K;) because of their entering, one into another; (TA;) as also ↓ duxaAlN : (K:) so in the M. (TA.) -A3- See also duxolapN .

(TA.) ― -b3- A portion, or portions, of flesh, or of muscle, lying within sinews: (M, K:) or flesh whereof one portion is intermixed with another: (TA:) or dux~alu All~aHomi means flesh that cleaves to the bone; and such is the best of flesh. (T, TA.) ― -b4- Applied to a man, (TA,) Thick, and compact, or contracted, in body; (K, * TA;) lit, having one portion thereof inserted into another. (TA.) ― -b5- A certain bird, (S, K,) of small size, (S, TA,) dust-coloured, (K, TA,) that alights upon palm-trees and other trees, and enters among them; (TA;) also called ↓ duxolalN and ↓ duxolulN : (K:) n. un. dux~alapN : ISd says that it is an intrusive bird, smaller than the sparrow, found in El-Hijáz: accord. to the T, it is a kind of small bird, like the sparrow, that has its abode in caves and in dense trees: AHát says, in “the Book of Birds,” that the dux~alap is a certain bird that is found in caves, and enters houses or tents, and is caught by children: when winter comes, the birds of this kind disperse; and some of them become of a dusky colour, and of a dark and somewhat reddish colour, and gray ( zaroqaA=' ); and some, variegated with blackness and redness, and with whiteness: they are of the size of the lark, but the latter is larger than they are in the head; neither short nor long in the tail; but short in the legs, which are like the legs of the lark: (TA:) the pl. is daxaAxiylu , (S, M, K,) which is anomalous in respect of the insertion of the Y : (M:) in the T, dxAlyl [which is app. a mistranscription]. (TA.) -A2- See also duxolapN .

definition: The part of the AzAr [or waist-wrapper ] that is next the body;
sourceDefinition: The part of the AzAr [or waist-wrapper ] that is next the body; (Mgh;) the extremity of the AzAr that is next the body, (S, K,) next the right side (K, TA) of a man when he puts it on; being the inner extremity in that case: and the part of the body which is the place thereof; not of the AzAr : IAmb says that, accord. to some, it is a metonymical term for the ma*aAkiyr [meaning the penis with what is around it ]: or, accord. to some, the hip, or haunch. (TA.) ― -b2- daAxilapu AlA^aroDi The part of the ground that may serve as a place for concealment, and that is low, or depressed: pl. dawaAxilu . (T, K.) One says, maA fiY A^aroDihimo daAxilapN mino xamarK [ There is not in their land a place for concealment such as a hollow or a covert of trees ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [In the K and TA in art. jwz , the term daAxilap is applied to Bad pieces of money intermixed and concealed among good pieces; as is there indicated in the K, and plainly shown in the TA.] ― -b4- Ald~awaAxilu in the phrase Ald~awaAxilu waAlxawaAriju has been explained in art xrj . (Msb. See xaArijapN .) ― -b5- See also duxolapN , in two places.

definition: A wound in the head, reaching the dimaAg [or brain ];
sourceDefinition: A wound in the head, reaching the dimaAg [or brain ]; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) with which there is no living: (Msb:) it is the last [ in degree ] of [ the wounds termed ] $ijaAj [pl. of $aj~apN ]; these being ten, as follows: [1] qaA$irapN , also called HaAriSapN (S, K, TA) and HaroSapN , or, as some think, the HArSp or HrSp is different from the qA$rp : (TA:) [2] baADiEapN : [3] daAmiyapN : [4] mutalaAHimapN : [5] simoHaAqN : [6] muwDiHapN : [7] haA$imapN : [8] munaq~alapN : [9] A=m~apN , (S, K, TA,) also termed maA^omuwmapN : (TA:) [10] daAmigapN : (S, K, TA:) and A'Obeyd adds daAmiEapN , with the unpointed E , after daAmiyapN ; (S;) or, accord. to F, who pronounces J to have erred in saying thus, before dAmyp : but J is right in this case. (TA.) [See $aj~apN daAmiEapN , voce daAmiEN . Several other terms are mentioned in the TA; but these, which will be found in their proper arts., appear to be all syn. with some that are mentioned above. See also $aj~apN .] ― -b2- Also A spadix ( TaloEapN ) that comes forth from amid the broken portions of the qulob [or heart of the palm-tree ], long and hard, and, if left, mars the palm-tree; (S, K, * TA;) wherefore, when its existence is known, it is detached. (TA.) ― -b3- And An iron above the muw^ax~arap [or hinder part ] of the [ camel's saddle called ] raHol ; (As, K;) also called gaA$iyapN : (TA:) or an iron with which the back of the rHol is fastened: (JK:) the pl. is dawaAmigu : ISh says that the dwAmg are above the middle of the heads, or upper extremities, of the [ curved pieces of wood called ] A^aHonaA=' [pl. of HinowN ]; and sometimes they are of wood, firmly bound; and i. q. xa*aAriyfu , pl. of xu*oruwfN [q. v.]: [but] Az says that when the dAmgp is of iron, it is placed across, or athwart, above the two extremities of the HinowaAni , and nailed with two nails, the x*Aryf being fastened upon the heads of the cross-pieces, in order that it, or they, may not become disconnected. (TA.) [What it is, I am unable further to explain. It is perhaps thus called because so placed that a person is liable to have his head wounded by it.] ― -b4- And A piece of wood placed across between two poles, upon which is hung the skin for water or milk. (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, K.)

definition: a noun signifying What is false, or vain;
sourceDefinition: a noun signifying What is false, or vain; a lie; syn. baATilN and ka*ibN : as also duhodur~ayoni , (K,) its dual, (TA,) or duho dur~ayoni , or duho dur~ayono : (as in different copies of the S:) whence duhodur~ayoni and ↓ duhodur~iy~apN are epithets applied to a liar; or a great or habitual liar: and accord. to AZ, the Arabs used to say, duhodur~aAni laA yugoniyAani Eanoka $ayoy^FA [ Lies will not avail thee aught ]: and duhodun~N signifies the same as duhodur~N . (TA.) ― -b2- duhodur~ayoni is also a noun, (K,) i. e. a verbal noun, (TA,) signifying He was, or has become, unoccupied, or without work; syn. baTala ; (K;) like saroEaAna for saruEa , and hayohaAti for baEuda . (TA.) Hence the prov., (TA,) duhodur~ayoni saEodu Alqayoni , (As, K,) without the conjunction wa [after the first word], and dhdr~yn being written as one word, (TA,) meaning Saad the blacksmith became, or has become, unoccupied, or without work; not being employed because of the people's being diverted from other things by drought (As, K) and distress. (TA.) Some say saAEdu Alqayoni : and Aboo-'Obeydeh Maamar Ibn-El-Muthennà relates it thus: dhdr~yn saEoda Alqayon , with sEd in the accus. case, and says that dhdr~yn is governed in the accus. case by a verb understood; apparently meaning that it is a noun signifying AlbaATilu , dual of duhodur~N , not a verbal noun, as though the prov. meant Cast ye away what is false, or vain, and Saad the blacksmith: but what he says is not correct. (TA.) Or a certain blacksmith asserted his name to be Saad for some time, and then his lying became manifest; so this was said to him; meaning, Thou hast added falsehood to falsehood, O Saad the blacksmith. (K.) It is also related separately; (K;) and so J and others relate it; saying dh dr~yn : (TA:) [in one copy of the S, I find it written duho dur~ayono : in another, duho dur~ayoni :] duho being an imperative from Ald~ahaA='u ; its final radical letter being transposed to the place of the medial, so that it becomes duwoho , and the w being then rejected because of the two quiescent letters, (K,) so that it becomes duho , like as is done in the case of qulo : (TA:) and dur~ayoni being from dar~a , “ it was consecutive; ” (K;) by the dual form being meant repetition, as in the case of lab~ayoka &c.: (TA:) so that the meaning is Be thou very lying (K) and cunning, (TA,) O Saad (K) the blacksmith: (TA:) and this explanation, says IB, is good, except inasmuch as that the d in dr~yn thus derived should be with fet-h; or, he adds, it may be with damm to assimilate it to the d in duho [like as Alqayoni is terminated with kesr to assimilate it to dur~ayoni ]. (TA.) Or the origin of the saying was this: Saad the blacksmith was a Persian, who went about the districts of ElYemen, working for the people; and when he became without work in a district, he used to say, in Persian, diho badoruwdo : [so in a copy of the S; and this, or diho bidoruwdo , is the correct reading: in another copy of the S, daho baduwrudo : and in the copies of the K, diho badoruwdo :] (S, K:*) meaning, [ O town, or village, ] farewell: to acquaint them that he was going forth on the morrow: (K:) or meaning I am going forth to-morrow: (S:) in order that he might be employed: and they arabicized the expression, and made him the subject of a prov. with respect to lying; and said, When ye hear of the blacksmith's departure at night, he is assuredly coming in the morning. (S, K.) Some say that the prov. is elliptical, for baTala qawolu saEodK Alx [ False is the saying of Saad &c.]. (TA.) [This is mentioned in the S in art. dr .]

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, &c.,) for which some say raA [suppressing the ' and the Y ,] (M,) and some say raA='a , (T in art. bwA^ , and M and K in art. ryA^ ,) like xaAfa , (TA in the latter art.,) formed by transposition, (T in art. bwA^ ,) first pers. raA^ayotu , (M, Msb, K, &c.,) for which some say rayotu , without ' , (T, S, M,) but the former is that which is general and preferred, (T, M,) aor. yaraY (T, S, M,) for which yaroA^aY , agreeably with the root, is said by none except [the tribe of] Teym-erRibáb, (T, M,) or by such as require this form in poetry, (S,) sec. pers. fem. sing. and pl., alike, tarayona , so that you say tarayonaniY [with an affixed pronoun], and if you will you may say tarayon~iY , incorporating one n into the other by teshdeed, (S,) imperative ra and A_iro'a (AZ, T, S, M,) the people of El-Hijáz saying ra dual rayaA , pl. masc. rawoA and fem. rayona , and Teym saying Airo'a &c., (T, M,) inf. n. ruw^oyapN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and riy~apN , (T, M, K,) the former being altered to ruwoyapN and then to ruy~apN and then to riy~apN , (T, M,) and raA^oYN (T, S, K) and raA='apN , (S, M, K, [in the CK raA^ap ,]) like raAEapN [in measure], (S,) in which the p is not necessarily a restrictive to unity, (M,) and raAyapN (K [but this I do not find elsewhere]) and riy^oyaAnN , (Lh, M, TA,) for which last we find in the copies of the K ruw^oyaAn , (TA,) He saw [a person or thing] with the eye: (S:) in this sense the verb has [only] one objective complement: (S, Msb:) you say, raA^ayotuhu (T, M, Msb, K) and ↓ AistaroA^ayotuhu , (T, M, K,) for which some say Aisotarayotuhu , (T, M,) and ↓ AirotaA^ayotuhu , (T, M, K,) for which some say Airotayotuhu , (T, M,) all signifying the same, (T, M, K,) I saw him, or it, (a person and a thing, Msb) with the eye; (T, M, Msb, K, TA;) [or so,] and also, with the mind. (M and K in relation to the first, and K in relation to all.) ruw^oyapN is of several sorts: (TA:) first, it signifies The seeing with the eye: (M, K, TA:) and with what serves for the same purpose as the organ of sight; as in the saying in the Kur [ix. 106], waquli A@EomaluwA fasayaraYA@ll~`hu Eamalakumo [ And Say thou, Work ye, for God will see your work ]; because the sense of sight cannot be attributed to God: (TA:) [and similar to this is the phrase, raA^aY fiyhi ka*aA He saw in him such a thing: and raA^aY minohu ka*aA He experienced from him such a thing. ] Secondly, The seeing by supposition, or fancy; as in the saying, A^araY A^an~a zayodFA munoTaliqN [ I suppose, or fancy, that Zeyd is going away ]. (TA.) Thirdly, The seeing by reflection, or consideration; as in the saying [in the Kur viii. 50], A_in~iY A^araY maA laA tarawona [ Verily I see by reflection, or consideration, what ye see not ]. (TA.) Fourthly, The seeing with the mind, or mentally; [the opining, or judging, a thing; a sense in which the inf. n. raA^oYN is more commonly used;] (M, * K, * TA;) as in the saying in the Kur [liii. 11], maA ka*aba Alfuw^aAdu maA raA^aY [ The heart did not belie what he mentally saw ]. (TA.) [Of these meanings, other exs. here follow; with exs. of similar meanings.] ― -b2- An ex. of raA for raA^aY occurs in the saying of a poet, mano raA mivola maEodaAna boni aHoyaY [ Who has seen the like of Maadán the son of Yahyà? the measure being waAfir , with the first foot reduced to mufoEalotuno ]. (M.) AlHamodulil~`hi EalaY riy~atiki , for ruw^oyatika , altered in the manner explained above, [meaning Praise be to God for the seeing of thee, ] (M, K, *) is a saying mentioned by IAar. (M.) SuwmuwA liruw^oyatihi means [ Fast ye ] at the time of seeing it; [referring to the new moon of Ramadán;] i. e., when ye see it. (Mgh.) In the phrase raA^ayotuhu qaAy^imFA [ I saw him standing ], qAy^mA is in the accus. case as a denotative of state. (Msb.) raA^oYu EayoniY zayodFA faEala *aAka [ My eye saw (lit. my eye's seeing ) Zeyd do that ] is held by Sb to be an instance of an anomalous use of an inf. n., and is [said to be] the only instance of the kind, among inf. ns. of trans. verbs except samoEu A^u*uniY . (M, TA: but in a copy of the former written raA^oYa EynY and samoEaA*nY .) raA^ayotuhu raA^oYa AlEayoni means [ I saw him, or it, ] where the eye, or sight, fell upon him, or it. (TA.) biEayonK m~aA A^arayan~aka [lit. With some eye I will assuredly see thee ] is a saying mentioned by AZ as meaning hasten thou, ( AiEojalo thus in copies of the S and in the TA, or Eaj~ilo as in one copy of the S,) or work thou, ( AiEomalo , thus in two copies of the S,) and be as though I were looking at thee: (S, TA:) it is said to one whom you send, and require to be quick; and means pause not for anything, for it is as though I were looking at thee. (TA in art. Eyn .) raA^aY AlmakaAnu AlmakaAna (tropical:) The place faced [or (as we say) looked upon ] the place, as though seeing it, (M, TA,) is tropical: (TA:) [and in like manner you say,] daAriY taraY daArahu (tropical:) My house faces [or looks upon ] his house. (T, IAth, TA.) ― -b3- raA^aYfiY manaAmihi ruw^oyaA [ He saw, i. e. fancied that he saw, in his sleep, a vision, or dream ]. (S, Msb, K. *) ― -b4- A^alamo tara A_ilaY ka*aA [ Has thou not considered such a thing, so as to be admonished thereby?] is a phrase used on an occasion of wonder (IAth, K, TA) at a thing, and in rousing the attention of the person to whom it is addressed; as in the saying in the Kur [ii. 244], A^alamo tara A_ilaY A@l~a*iyna xarajuwA mino diyaArihimo [ Hast thou not considered those who went forth from their houses, so as to be admonished by their case?]; meaning, hast thou not wondered at their act, and has not their case come to thy knowledge? and so in other instances in the same: (IAth, TA:) Er-Rághib says that, when raA^ayot is made trans. by means of A_ilaY , it denotes consideration that leads to the becoming admonished. (TA.) In like manner also, (IAth, K,) A^araA^ayotaka and A^araA^ayotakumaA and A^araA^ayotakumo , (T, IAth, K,) and to a woman A^araA^ayotaki , and to a pl. number of women A^araA^ayotakun~a , (T,) [which may be lit. rendered Hast thou, and have ye two, &c., considered? ] are expressions used to arouse attention, (IAth, TA,) meaning tell thou me and tell ye two me &c.; (T, IAth, K;) as in the saying in the Kur [xvii. 64], qaAla A^araA^ayotaka h`*aA A@l~a*iY kar~amotu EalaY~a [ He said, Hast thou considered? meaning tell me, respecting this whom Thou hast honoured above me ]; and in the same [vi. 40 and 47], qalo A^araA^ayotakumo A_ino A^ataAkumo Ea*aAbu A@ll~`hi [ Say thou, Have ye considered? meaning tell me, if the punishment of God come upon you ]; and occurring without the k in other places thereof: (IAth, TA:) you say also, A^araA^ayota zayodFA and A^araA^ayotaka zayodFA , meaning Tell thou me [respecting Zeyd ]: (Mgh:) and for A^araA^ayota and A^araA^ayotaka [&c.] some say A^arayota and A^arayotaka : (S:) the pronunciation without ' is the more common: the t in A^araA^ayotaka &c. is always with fet-h; and accord. to the grammarians of accredited science, the k in these cases is redundant; (T;) [i. e.] it is a particle of allocution, to corroborate the pronoun [ t , which it therefore immediately follows in every case, distinguishing the genders and numbers by its own variations, which are the same as those of the pronominal affix of the second person]: (Bd in vi. 40:) [IHsh says,] the correct opinion is that of Sb; that the t is an agent, and the k is a particle of allocution: (Mughnee in art. k :) but sometimes A^araA^ayotaka &c. mean halo raA^ayota nafosaka &c.; the k being in this case an objective complement [and the verb being differently rendered according as it has not, or has, a second objective complement, as is shown here by what precedes and what follows]. (T.) In A^aturaAka , also, [from ↓ A^uriYa , not from ruy^iYa ,] meaning AtZn~ [i. e. A^ataZun~u , Thinkest thou? ], the pronoun [as some term it, but properly the final particle,] is [a particle of allocution] like that in A^araA^ayotaka in the Kur vi. 40 and 47 [cited above; and in the same sense as this latter phrase, A^aturaAka is used, as meaning tell thou me ]. (Har p. 570.) ― -b5- When raA^aY means He knew, (S, Msb,) or he thought, (Msb,) it has two objective complements: (S, Msb:) or when it has two objective complements, it necessarily means knowing [or the like]. sourceDefinition: , (IAar, T, S, M, K,) originally A^araA^ayotuhu , (S,) inf. n. A_iraA='apN (Sb, IAar, T, M, K) and A_iraAyapN (IAar, T) and A_iraA='N , (Sb, IAar, T, M, K,) [the last originally A_iroA^aA'N ,] the p in the first inf. n. being a substitute [for the suppressed A^ , and in like manner in the second], and the last inf. n. being without any substitution, (Sb, M,) [ I made him to see the thing; i. e. I showed him the thing: ] you say, A^arayotuhu Al$~aYo'a faraA=hu [ I showed him the thing, and he saw it [. (S.) See also 8. Aboo-'Amr read A^aronaA manaAsikanaA , [in the Kur ii. 122, for A^arinaA i. e. Show Thou to us our religious rites and caremonies of the pilgrimage, or our places where those rites and ceremonies are to be performed, ] which is anomalous. (M.) ― -b2- One says also, A^araY A@ll~`hu bifulaAnK , meaning God showed men by [the example of] such a one punishment and destruction: (K:) or God showed by [the example of] such a one that which would cause his enemy to rejoice at his misfortune: a saying of the Arabs: (T in art. rY :) said only in relation to evil. (Sh, TA.) ― -b3- And A^ariniY Al$~aYo'a Give thou, or hand thou, to me the thing. (M, TA.) ― -b4- A^araY in the sense of A^aEolama [as meaning He made such a one to know a thing, or person, to be, as in the saying, A^arayotu zayodFA EamorFAmunoTaliqFA I made Zeyd to know “ Amr to be going away, which may be rendered I showed Zeyd that 'Amr was going away, ] requires [as this ex. shows] three objective complements. (M, and Bd in iv. 106. [See I “ AK, p. 117.]) ― -b5- This is not the case in the saying in the Kur [iv. 106], litaHokuma bayona Aln~aAsa bimaA A^araAka A@ll~`hu ; (M, Bd;) for here it has but two objective complements, namely, the k in ArAk , and the suppressed pronoun hu in A^araAkahu : it is in this instance from Alr~aA^oYu in the sense of AlA_iEotiqaAdu : (M:) the meaning is, [ That thou mayest judge between men ] by means of that which God hath taught thee, syn. Ear~afaka , (Ksh, Bd,) or Eal~amaka , (Jel,) and revealed to thee. (Ksh, Bd.) ― -b6- See also 1, in the latter half of the paragraph, in two places, in which the pass., A^uriYa , is mentioned. -A2- A^aroA^aY [as an intrans. v., preserving the original form, inf. n. A_iroA='N , as below,] He looked in the mirror; (T, K;) and so fiY AlmiroA=pi ↓ taraA^~aY and fiyhaA ↓ taraA='aY : (T, M, K:) or ↓ taraA='aY signifies he (a man) looked at his face in the mirror or in the sword: (S:) and fiY AlmaA='i ↓ tamaroA^aY he looked at his face in the water; the doing of which is forbidden in a trad; of the measure tamafoEala [from AlmiroA=pu ]; mentioned by Sb; like tamasokana from Almisokiynu , and tamadoraEa from AlmidoraEapu , and tamanodala from Alminodiylu . (M.) ― -b2- He (a man) had many dreams. (T, K. *) ― -b3- He moved his eyelids, (K,) or made much motion with his eyes, (T,) in looking: (T, K:) you say, huwa yuroy^iYbiEayonayohi , (TA,) and yuraA^oriy^N biEayonayohi . (T, TA. *) ― -b4- He acted (T, K) well, or righteously, (T,) in order to make others see what he did, and hear of it. (T, K.) [See also 3.] ― -b5- He possessed, or became possessed of, intelligence (K, TA) and judgment and forecast: (TA:) inf. n. A_iroA='N . (K, TA. [The inf. n. is mentioned with this signification, in the K, app. because it is the first there explained, and therefore as applying to the verb in all its senses.]) ― -b6- And He had the appearance, or evidence, of foolishness, or stupidity, in his face: (T, K, TA: [the words by which Az explains this meaning are tabay~anato A=rAw^hu fY wajohihi whY AlHmAqpu , accord. to one copy of the T; in another copy of the same, Alrw^Ah : the TA follows the former reading: but the right reading is Alr~aA^owapN ; mentioned in the T, thus correctly written, in art. rA^rA^ ; in the S, in the present art; and in the M, in art. rA^w , which is its proper art., and therefore the proper art. of the verb in the sense thus explained:]) thus it bears two contr. meanings. (K. [But it is added in the TA that this requires consideration.]) ― -b7- Also He had what is termed a ray^iY~ , of the jinn, or genii; (T, K, TA;) i. e., a follower, of the jinn. (TA.) ― -b8- And He followed the opinion, or belief, of some one, or more, of the lawyers (K, TA) in the science of the law. (TA.) ― -b9- A^aroA^ato said of a she-camel and of a ewe or she-goat, (M,) and of any female in a state of pregnancy, except a solidhoofed animal and a beast of prey, Her udder showed her to be pregnant: (M, K:) and in like manner it is said of a woman: (M:) or, said of a ewe or she-goat, she was, or became, big in her udder: (S:) and accord. to IAar, said of a she-goat, she was, or became, swollen in her vulva, and her being so became apparent, or evident. (M.) And A^aroA^aY said of a man, His ewe, or she-goat, was, or became, black in her udder. (T.) -A3- See also 1, in two places, near the end of the paragraph. -A4- [It is also said in the K and TA that A^arA^aY , said of a camel, means Ainotakava xaTomuhu EalaY Haloqihi ; in the CK Anotakaba ; and in the TA this is said to be on the authority of En-Nadr: but in a copy of the T, I find it stated, on the authority of ISh, (i. e. En-Nadr,) that AlArA= (i. e. AlA_iroA='u ) signifies AntkAvu xTm AlbaEyri ElY Haloqih : in another copy of the T, on the authority of En-Nadr, that AlrA= (a mistranscription for AlA_iroA='u ) signifies AntkAv xTm AlbEyr xilqp : and it is added that the epithet applied to a camel is murA^Y (as in one copy, i. e. ↓ muroA^aY , and thus it is written in the TA, but in the other copy of the T mrAoY , an obvious mistranscription); and to camels, murA=AtN (as in one copy, for muroA^aAtN , i. e. muroA=tN , in the other copy of the T erroneously written muraA^Ap , and in the TA mrAyAt ): therefore the verb is evidently A^uroy^iYa , in the pass. form, inf. n. A_iroA='N ; and I think that the correct explanation is Ainotakava xaTomuhu xiloqapF , app. meaning His muzzle was thin, or lean, by nature: see art. nkv : and see also muroA^FY below.]

definition: They saw one another: (M, K:) dual taraA='ayaA .
sourceDefinition: They saw one another: (M, K:) dual taraA='ayaA . (TA.) And taraA='aY AljamoEaAni , (S, TA,) in the Kur [xxvi. 61], (TA,) The two bodies of people saw each other: (S:) or approached and faced each other so that each was able to see the other. (TA.) And taraA='ayonaA We met and saw each other. (A'Obeyd, T.) See also 3, first sentence. It is said in a trad, (T,) laAtaraAA=naArAhumaA , [for tataraAA= , as it is written in some copies of the K,] (T, K,) [i. e. (tropical:) Their two fires shall not be within sight of each-other; ] meaning that the Muslim may not dwell in the country of the believers in a plurality of gods, and be with them so that each of them shall see the fire of the other: (T, K *) so says A'Obeyd: or, accord. to AHeyth, it means that the Muslim may not mark himself with the mark of the believer in a plurality of gods, nor assimilate himself to him in conduct and guise, nor assume his manners, or dispositions; from the phrase maA naAru baEiyrika , meaning “ What is the brand of thy camel? ” (T:) IAth explains it similarly to A'Obeyd; and says that the verb is thus used tropically. (TA.) ― -b2- trA='Y liY He addressed, or presented, himself [ to my sight, or] in order that I might see him; as also lY ↓ trA^~Y . (M, K.) And trA='Y lahu $aYo'N mina Aljin~i [ Somewhat of the jinn, or genii, presented itself to his sight ]. (S.) ― -b3- trA='Y Aln~axolu The palm-trees showed the colours of their unripe dates. (AHn, M, K.) ― -b4- taraA='ayonaA AlhilaAla We tasked the sight by trying whether or not we could see the new moon: or, as some say, we looked [ together, at, or for, the new moon ]: (Sh, * T, TA:) or we lowered our eyes towards the new moon in order that we might see it. (Msb.) [See also 6 in art. nqD .] ― -b5- See also 4, in the former half of the paragraph, in two places. ― -b6- taraA='ayonaA fiYAlA^amori or trA='ynA AlA^amora : see 8. ― -b7- huwa yataraA='aY biraA^oYi fulaAnK He takes to, or holds, the opinion, or persuasion, or belief, of such a one; and inclines to it; and conforms to it. (T, TA.) ― -b8- See also 1, in the latter half of the paragraph.

sourceDefinition: is an inf. n. of raA^aY [q. v.]: (T, S, K:) [and is also a subst.: used as a subst.,] it means The raA^oY of the eye; (Lth, T, Msb;) i. e. the sight thereof; like ruw^oyapN , q. v.: (Msb:) and also, of the mind; (Lth, T;) [i. e.,] it signifies also mental perception: (Msb:) [ conception: idea: nation: ] belief; (M, K;) as a subst., not as inf. n.: (M:) [or judgment: or persuasion: or opinion; i. e.] a preponderating belief of one of two things that are inconsistent, each with the other: (Er-Rághib, TA:) a thing that a man has seen with his mind, looked into, examined, or considered, ( maA A@rotaA=hu ,) and believed: (Mgh:) [ a tenet: ] also intelligence: and forecast: and skill in affairs: (Msb:) [and hence it often means counsel, or advice: ] pl. A^aroA='N (T, S, K &c.) and A=raA='N , (S, M, K,) the latter formed by transposition, [being for A^aA^oraA='N ,] (S,) and A^aroY'K [originally A^arow^uYN , like as A^aZobK is originally A^aZobuYN ,] (Lh, M, K, TA, in some copies of the K A^aroYN ) and ruy^iY~N and riy^iY~N [both originally ruw^uwYN ], (Lh, M, TA,) in the K ruY~N , with damm, [in the CK raY~N ,] and riY~N , with kesr, (TA,) and [quasipl. n.] ↓ ray^iY~N , (S, K,) of the measure faEiylN , like Day^iynN . A^aSoHaAbu Alr~aA^oYi , [often meaning The speculatists, or theorists, ] as used by those who treat of the traditions, means the followers of analogy; because they pronounce according to their raA^oY [or belief, &c.,] in relation to that concerning which they have not found any [tradition such as is termed] Hadiyv or A^avar , (IAth, K, TA,) or in relation to that which is dubious to them in a tradition. (IAth, TA.) But accord. to the usage of others, one says, fulaAnN mino A^ahuli Alr~aA^oY meaning Such a one holds the belief, or opinion, &c., of the [ heretics, or schismatics, called ] xawaArij , and says according to their persuasion. (TA.) [Sometimes, also, this phrase means Such a one is of the people of intelligence; or of counsel, or advice. ] See also ray^iY~N . And rajulN *uw raA^oYK means A man having mental perception, and skill in affairs. (Msb.) ― -b2- See also the next paragraph.

definition: and ↓ riy^iY~N (Lth, T, M, K, TA) A jinnee, or genie, that presents himself to a man, and shows him, or teaches him, divination or enchantment or the like: (Lth, T, TA:) or a jinnee whom a man sees: or, accord.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ riy^iY~N (Lth, T, M, K, TA) A jinnee, or genie, that presents himself to a man, and shows him, or teaches him, divination or enchantment or the like: (Lth, T, TA:) or a jinnee whom a man sees: or, accord. to Lh, one whom a person loves, and with whom he becomes familiar: (M:) or a jinnee that is seen and loved: or the latter word means such as is loved: (K:) and the former word, some other than this: (TA:) or the former means a follower, who is of the jinn; of the measure faEiylN or faEuwlN ; [if the latter, originally raw^uwY ;] so called because he presents himself to the sight of him of whom he is the follower; or from the saying, fulaAnN ray^iY~u qawomihi , meaning, SaAHibu ↓ raA^oyihimo [i. e. Such a one is the counsellor, or adviser, of his people, or party ]: and sometimes it is pronounced riy^iY~N (IAth, TA.) You say, lahu ray^iY~N He has a jinnee &c. (Lh, M, TA.) And maEahu riy^iY~N With him is a jinnee &c. (Lth, T, TA.) And bihi ray^iY~N mina Aljin~i , meaning mas~N [i. e. In him is a touch, or stroke, from the jinn, or genii ]. (S.) ― -b2- Also, both words, A great serpent, (K, TA,) that presents itself to the sight of a man; (TA;) so called as being likened to a jinnee; (K, TA;) or because they assert that the serpent is a transformed jinnee, wherefore they call it $ayoTaAnN and jaAn~N . (IAth, TA.) ― -b3- And A garment, or piece of cloth, that is spread out for sale. (Aboo-'Alee, M, K.) -A2- For the former word, see also raA^oYN [of which it is a quasi-pl. n.].

sourceDefinition: The womb, i. e. the place of origin, (Mgh, Msb, K,) and the receptacle, (Mgh, K,) of the young, (Mgh, Msb, K,) in the belly; (Mgh;) as also ↓ riHomN , (Msb, K,) a contraction of the former, and ↓ raHomN , which is of the dial. of Benoo-Kiláb: (Msb:) in this sense, (Msb,) which is the primary signification, (Mgh,) [i. e.] as meaning the raHim of the female, (S,) it is fem.; (S, Msb;) or, as some say, masc.; (Msb;) but IB cites a verse in which riHom is fem.: (TA:) pl. A^aroHaAmN . (MA.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh, Msb,) as also ↓ riHomN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ raHomN , (Msb,) (tropical:) Relationship; i. e. nearness of kin; syn. qaraAbapN : (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) [by some restricted to relationship by the female side; as will be shown below:] and connexion by birth: (Mgh, Msb:) or relationship connecting with a father or an ancestor: or near relationship: so in the T: (TA:) or a connexion, or tie, of relationship: (A, TA:) or the ties of relationship: (M, K, TA:) accord. to the K, Alr~aHimu signifies AlqaraAbapu or A^aSoluhaA and A^asobaAbuhaA : but in the M it is said, Alr~aHimu A^asobaAbu AlqaraAbapi waA^aSoluhaA Alr~aHimu Al~atiY hiYa manobitu Alwaladi ; in which waA^aSoluhaA forms no part of the explanation of AlrHm , as the author of the K asserts it to do: (TA:) as meaning relationship, rHm is in most instances masc.: (Msb:) pl. as above. (K.) It is said in a holy tradition ( Hadiyv qudosiY~ [i. e. an inspired or a revealed tradition]) that God said, when He created Alr~aHim [meaning “ relationship, ” &c.], A^anaA Al~aHom`nu waA^anota Alr~aHimu $aqaqotu A@somaka mini A@somiY famano waSalaka waSalotuhu wamano qaTaEaka qaTaEotuhu (assumed tropical:) [ I am AlrHm`n and thou art AlrHm : I have derived thy name from my name: therefore whoso maketh thee close, I will make him close; and who severeth thee, I will sever him ]. (TA.) [ waSala raHimahu means (assumed tropical:) He made close his tie, or ties, of relationship, by kind behaviour to his kindred: and qaTaEa raHimahu , He severed his tie, or ties, of relationship, by unkind behaviour to his kindred: see art. wSl : and see also bal~a raHimahu , in the first paragraph of art. bl ; and a verse there cited.] ― -b3- *uw Alr~aHimi means (assumed tropical:) [ The possessor of relationship, &c.; i. e.] the contr. of AlA^ajonabiY~u : (Mgh, Msb:) the pl. *awuw AlA^aroHaAmi , [or, as in the Kur viii. last verse, and xxxiii. 6, A^uwluw AlA^aroHaAmi ,] in the classical language, means any relations: and in law, any relations that have no portion [ of the inheritances termed faraAy^iD ] and are not [ such heirs as are designated by the appellation ] EaSabap [q. v.]; (KT, TA in art. *w ;) [i. e.,] with respect to the faraAy^iD , it means the relations by the women's side. (IAth, TA in the present art.) *uw raHimK maHoramK and [some say] muHar~amK [and *uw raHimK maHoramN also (see art. Hrm )] mean (assumed tropical:) A relation whom it is unlawful to marry, [whether male or female, the latter being included with the former, but the female, when particularly meant, is termed *aAtu raHimK maHoramK &c.,] such as the mother and the daughter and the sister and the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt [ and the male relations of such degrees ]: and most of the learned, of the Companions and of the generation following these, and Aboo-Haneefeh and his companions, and Ahmad [Ibn-Hambal], hold that when one possesses a person that is termed *uw raHimK maHoramK , this person becomes emancipated, whether male or female; but Esh-Sháfi'ee and others of the Imáms and of the Companions and of the generation following these hold that the children and the fathers and the mothers become emancipated, and not any others than these. (IAth, TA.) ― -b4- [ HaAs~apu raHimK means (assumed tropical:) A feeling of relationship or consanguinity, or sympathy of blood; and in like manner, elliptically, raHimN alone. You say, A^aT~ato lahu min~iY HaAs~apu raHimK ; expl. in art. Hs : and A^aT~ato lahu raHimiY ; and A^aT~ato bika Alr~aHimu ; expl. in art. AT . ― -b5- raHimN is also often used for farojN or HayaA='N , meaning (assumed tropical:) The vulva: see, for exs., $uforN , and 1 in art. ZA=r , and 8 in art. HwS .] -A2- As an epithet, with p , applied to a she-camel: see raHuwmN . ― -b2- And as an epithet without p , applied to a water-skin: see 1, last sentence but one.

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ raHamapN (Sb, K) and ↓ ruHomN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ ruHumN , (S, K,) thus in a verse of Zuheyr, (S, TA,) and thus in the Kur xviii. 80 accord. to the reading of Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà, (TA,) and ↓ maroHamapN , (S, Msb, K,) of which last maraAHimu is pl., (TA,) [all inf. ns.; when used as simple substs. signifying Mercy, pity, or compassion; i. e.] tenderness (S, Msb, K, and Bd on the basomalap ) of heart; (Bd ibid.;) and inclination to favour, (S, Msb, K,) or inclination requiring the exercise of favour and beneficence: (Bd ubi suprà:) and pardon, or forgiveness: (K:) accord. to Er-Rághib, raHomapN signifies tenderness requiring the exercise of beneficence towards the object thereof: and it is used sometimes as meaning tenderness divested of any other attribute: and sometimes as meaning beneficence divested of tenderness; as when it is used as an attribute of the Creator: when used as an attribute of men, it means tenderness, and inclination to favour [ without necessarily implying beneficence ]: accord. to El-Káshánee, it is of two kinds; namely, gratuitous, and obligatory: the former is that which pours forth favours, or benefits, antecedently to works; and this is the rHmp that embraces everything: the obligatory is that which is promised to the pious and the doers of good, in the Kur vii. 155 and vii. 54: but this, he says, is included in the gratuitous, because the promise to bestow it for works is purely gratuitous: accord. to the explanation of the Imám Aboo-Is-hák Ahmad Ibn-Mohammad-Ibn-Ibráheem Eth-Thaalebee, it is God's desire to do good to the deserving thereof; so that it is an essential attribute: or the abstaining from punishing him who deserves punishment, and doing good to him who does not deserve [ this ]; so that it is an attribute of operation. (TA.) The saying in the Kur [xxi. 75] waA^adoxalonaAhu fiY raHomatinaA (tropical:) [ And we caused him to enter into our mercy ] is tropical: so says IJ. (TA.) ― -b2- waA@ll~`hu yaxotaS~u biraHomatihi mano ya$aA='u , in the Kur [ii. 99 and iii. 67], means (assumed tropical:) [ And God distinguishes ] with his gift of prophecy [ whom He will ], or his prophetic office or commission. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- raHomapN also means (assumed tropical:) Sustenance, or the means of subsistence: this is said to be its meaning as used in the Kur xli. 50. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) Rain: (TA:) so in the Kur vii. 55. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) Plenty; or abundance of herbage, and of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life: so in the Kur x. 22 and xxx. 35. (TA.)

definition: [thus generally written when it has the article Al prefixed to it, but in other cases raHomaAnu , imperfectly decl.
sourceDefinition: [thus generally written when it has the article Al prefixed to it, but in other cases raHomaAnu , imperfectly decl.,] and ↓ Alr~aHiymu are names [or epithets] applied to God: (TA:) [the former, considered as belonging to a large class of words expressive of passion or sensation, such as gaDobaAnu and EaTo$aAnu &c., but, being applied to God, as being used tropically, or anthropopathically, may be rendered The Compassionate: ↓ the latter, considered as expressive of a constant attribute with somewhat of intensiveness, agreeably with analogy, may be rendered the Merciful: but they are variously explained: it is said that] they are both names [or epithets] formed to denote intensiveness of signification, from raHima ; like AlgaDobaAnu from gaDiba , and AlEaliymu from Ealima ; and Alr~aHomapu , in the proper language, is “ tenderness of heart, ” and “ inclination requiring the exercise of favour and beneficence; ” but the names of God are only to be taken [or understood] with regard to the ultimate imports, which are actions, exclusively of the primary imports, which may be passions: and the former is more intensive in signification than the latter; the former including in its objects the believer and the unbeliever, and ↓ the latter having for its peculiar object the believer: (Bd on the basomalap :) accord. to J, (TA,) they are two names [or epithets] derived from Alr~aHomapu , and are like nadomaAnu and nadiymN , and are syn.; the repetition being allowable when the [mode of] derivation is different, for the purpose of corroboration: (S, TA:) or the repetition is because the former is Hebrew, [originally 165 ,] and ↓ the latter is Arabic: (I'Ab, TA:) but the former is applicable to God only; though Museylimeh the Liar was called raHomaAnu AlyamaAmapi ; (S, TA;) and it is said to mean the Possessor of the utmost degree of Alr~aHomap ; and accord. to Zj, is a name of God mentioned in the most ancient books: (TA:) whereas ↓ the latter is syn. with ↓ Alr~aAHimu : (S, TA:) or [rather] ↓ raAHimN is the act. part. n. [signifying having mercy, &c.], and ↓ raHiymN has an intensive signification [i. e. having much mercy, &c.]: (Msb:) the latter is applied also to a man; and so is ↓ raHuwmN , in the same sense, and likewise to a woman: (TA:) the pl. of ↓ raHiymN is ruHamaA='u ; (Msb, TA;) occurring in the trad., A_in~amaA yaroHamu A@ll~`hu mino EibaAdihi Alr~uHamaA='a , or Alr~uHamaA='u , as related by different persons; [i. e. God has mercy on the merciful only of his servants, or verily those on whom God has mercy, of his servants, are the merciful; ] AlrHmA' being in the accus. case as the objective complement of yrHm , and in the nom. case as the enunciative of mA in the sense of Al~a*iY . (Msb.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, K,) aor. yaroguw , (S,) said of a camel, (S, Mgh, K,) and of a hyena, and of an ostrich; (K;) or ragato , aor. taroguw , said of a she-camel; (JK, Msb;) inf. n. rugaA='N , (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, * K,) with which ↓ raAgiyapN is syn. [either as an inf. n. or as a simple subst.]; (JK;) He grumbled, or uttered a grumbling cry; syn. Daj~a ; (S;) or uttered a cry, (Mgh, K,) and grumbled; syn. Saw~ata faDaj~a : (K:) or she uttered a cry [&c.]: (Msb:) so camels are wont to do when the loads are lifted upon them; and youthful camels do so much: (TA:) rugaA='N signifies the cry or crying [or grumbling, which is a kind of gurgling growl, ] (S, Msb) of the camel [when he is being laden, and on some other occasions of discontent], (Msb,) or of animals having the kind of foot called xuf~ : (S:) also of the bird called rag~aA='N [&c.]. (TA.) It is said in a prov., kafaY birugaAy^ihaA munaAdiyFA [ Her grumbling cry suffices as a caller ] i. e., the rugaA=' of his camel serves instead of his calling in presenting himself for entertainment as a guest: (S:) A'Obeyd says that it is well known to the Arabs as relating to the accomplishment of an object of want before the asking for it: and it is applied also to the case of a man whose aid is wanted and who does not come to thee; excusing himself by saying that he did not know: and to the case of one who stands at a man's door, and to whom it is said, “ Send him who shall ask permission for thee [to go in]; ” whereupon he replies, “ His knowledge of my standing at his door suffices for asking permission for me: if he pleased, he would grant me permission. ” (Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 328—9.]) And in another prov., Albakori ↓ kaAnato Ealayohimo karaAgiyapi , (JK, Meyd,) or Als~aqobi , [i. e. There befell them the like of the grumbling cry of the young camel, ] meaning, the rugaA=' of the young camel of Thamood [which preceded the destruction of those who heard it]: the prov. relates to the auguring evil from a thing. (Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 327.]) ― -b2- ragaA said of a boy, or child, means (tropical:) He wept most violently. (K, TA.) ― -b3- [It is also, app., said of a man, as meaning (assumed tropical:) He shouted: and (assumed tropical:) he spoke with a loud voice. (See 6, and rag~aA='N .)] -A2- See also 2.)

definition: He made his she-camel to utter the grumbling cry termed rugaA=' : (S, K:) [and] he made his camel to do so in order that he might be entertained as a guest.
sourceDefinition: He made his she-camel to utter the grumbling cry termed rugaA=' : (S, K:) [and] he made his camel to do so in order that he might be entertained as a guest. (M, TA. [See a prov. cited in the first paragraph.]) Sebrah Ibn-'Amr El-Fak'asee says, wamaA yurogaY li$ad~aAdK faSiylu [ And a young camel belonging to the family of Sheddád is not made to utter its grumbling cry for the want of its mother]; meaning that they are niggardly; that they will not separate the young camel from its mother by slaughter nor by gift. (S.) And it is said in a prov., A^aroguwA lahaA HuwaArahaA taqir~u [ Make ye her (the camel's) young one to utter its grumbling cry, then she will be quiet ]: for the she-camel when she hears the rugaA=' of her young one becomes still: (Meyd:) the prov. means, give him that which he wants, [then] he will be quiet. (JK, Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 532.]) A^arogawoA lilr~aHiyli means They made their saddle-camels to utter the grumbling cry [ for removal, or departure, or journeying ]; camels being wont to do so when the loads are lifted upon them. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, ArgAhu (assumed tropical:) He subdued, subjected, or oppressed, him; and abased him: because the camel [generally] does not utter the cry termed rugaA=' except in consequence of abasement, or humiliation. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] hiYa maliykapu AlA_irogaA='i (assumed tropical:) She is the slave ( maliykap meaning mamoluwkap ) of noise and loquacity, so that she distresses the hearers: or it may mean [ she is subject to ] the frothing of her lips, by reason of her loquacity; from ragowapN meaning “ froth. ” (TA. [See rag~aA='N .]) ― -b4- You say also, maA A^avogaY walaA A^arogaY He gave not a sheep or goat, nor a she-camel; (S, K;) like as you say, maA A^aHo$aY walaA A^ajal~a . (S. [See 4 in art. vgw .]) -A2- See also 2, in two places. ― -b2- [Hence,] ArgY said of him who is discharging his urine, (tropical:) He had much froth to his urine. (K, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] turogiynaA suqaATa HadiyvihaA , a phrase used by a poet, means (assumed tropical:) She feeds us with [or gives us ] little discourse, [or the refuse of her discourse, ] like froth. (TA.)

definition: He drank ragowap , i.
sourceDefinition: He drank ragowap , i. e. froth: (S, Msb:) or ArtgY ragowapF he took, and sipped, or supped, froth. (K.) definition: [The pomegranate;
sourceDefinition: [The pomegranate; ] a certain fruit, (T,) the produce of a certain tree, (M,) well known: (T, S, M, K:) n. un. with p : (S, M, Msb, K:) the sweet sort thereof relaxes the state of the bowels, and cough; the sour sort has the contrary effect; and that which is between sweet and sour is good for inflammation of the stomach, and pain of the heart: the rm~An has six flavours, like the apple; and is commended for its delicacy, its quick dissolving, and its niceness, or its elegance: (K:) rum~aAnN is of the measure fuEolaAnN accord. to Sb: (M in art. rm :) Kh, being asked by Sb respecting Alr~um~aAn , (S,) or [rather] respecting rum~aAn , (M in art. rm ,) when used as a proper name, (S,) said that he declined it imperfectly (S, M) when [thus made] determinate; (S;) and that he made it to accord to the majority, because its derivation is unknown, (S, M, *) i. e., that he regarded its A and n as augmentative: (S:) but accord. to Akh, the n is radical, (S,) [i. e.] he held it to be of the measure fuE~aAlN , making it to accord to many similar names of plants, (M,) like Hum~aADN &c., (S, M,) fuE~aAlN being more common than fuEolaAn ; (S;) he meant, as applied to plants; for otherwise the contr. is the case: (TA:) [Fei says,] the measure is fuE~aAlN , the n being radical, and therefore the word is perfectly decl., unless when used as a proper name, in which case it is imperfectly decl., being made to accord to the majority [of proper names ending with A and n , as EuvomaAnu &c.]. (Msb.) [Freytag mentions several varieties of rm~An , as follows: but the names, as given by him and here transcribed, require verification or correction: “ rmAn AlqsTysY , rmAn AlmrsY , rmAn AlEdsY , rmAn AlxzAynY , rmAn AltrHyn , rmAn AlmrwnY , qui ad speciem dulcium pertinent: tum rmAn $ErY dulce et corticem tenuissimum habens: rmAn AmlysY Malum Punicum maximum, esu gratissimum et acinorum expers: rmAn AlsHY , rmAn AldlwY , rmAn AldwArY , sunt minoris magnitudinis, formæ rotundæ: rmAn AlsfryA Malum Punicum magnitudine et sapore præstantissimum, a viro Sefri dicto ita appellatum, quod a Syria Cordubam regnante Abd-Alrahmano hanc speciem transtulerat: ” and he refers to “ Casiri, Bibl. Ar. Hisp. T. i. p. 329; and Avicenn. L. ii. p. 254; ” the latter of which authors only mentions the properties of the rm~An .] ― -b2- rum~aAnu Als~aEaAliY [in the CK Als~uEAlaY ] The white xa$oxaA$ [or poppy ]: or a species thereof. (K. [The heads of the poppy are called rum~aAnu Alxa$oxaA$i because of their resemblance to pomegranates.]) ― -b3- rum~aAnu AlA^anohaAri [ Androsæmum; or hypericum majus; ] the large species of hayuwfaAriyquwn . (K.) ― -b4- [In the present day, rum~aAnN and more properly rum~aAnataAni are used as meaning (assumed tropical:) A young woman's breasts, when small and round; they being likened to pomegranates. In a saying of Umm-Zara, (mentioned in the M in art. rm ,) rum~aAnataAni seems to be used in this sense, or as meaning a woman's posteriors. ] ― -b5- The n. un., rum~aAnapN , is also used, vulgarly, as meaning (assumed tropical:) The qaTinap [or third stomach, commonly called the manyplies, and by some the millet, of a ruminant animal]: (K in art. qTn :) or it signifies (assumed tropical:) the thing [or part ] in which is the fodder, of the horse. (M and TA in art. rm and in the present art.) One says, malaA^ati Ald~aAb~apu rum~aAnatahaA (assumed tropical:) [ The beast filled its rm~Anp ]. (TA.) And A^akala Hat~aY nataA^ato rum~aAnatahu , meaning (assumed tropical:) He ate until his navel with the parts around it projected. (TA.) ― -b6- [(assumed tropical:) A knob of metal, of wood, and of silk, &c.: so called as resembling in shape a pomegranate.] ― -b7- And [for the same reason] (assumed tropical:) The weight of a steelyard, or Roman balance. (MA.) [Also applied in the present day to (assumed tropical:) The steelyard itself; and so ruwmaAnap .]

definition: (Lth, S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (Lth, S, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ rahaTN , (Lth, Msb, K,) but the former is the more chaste, (Lth, Msb,) A man's people, and tribe, (S, Msb, K,) consisting of his nearer relations: (Msb:) [i. e. his near kinsfolk: ] and a number of men less than ten, among whom is no woman; (AZ, S, Msb, K;) as also nafarN : (AZ, Msb:) or from seven to ten; (IDrd, Msb, K;) and sometimes a little more; (IDrd;) less than seven, to three, being called nafarN : (Msb:) or from three to ten: (K:) or i. q. Ea$iyrapN : (ISk, Msb:) or more than ten, to forty: (As, IF, Msb:) a pl., (S, Msb,) or a word having a pl. meaning, (Th, Az, Msb,) without any proper sing.; (Th, Az, S, Msb, K;) like nafarN and qawomN and maEo$arN and Ea$iyrapN ; all applied to men, exclusive of women: (Th, Msb:) and ↓ A^urohuwTN signifies the same: (ISh, TA:) the pl. of rhT is A^arohuTN (Lth, S, K) and A^arohiTapN (Lth) and A^arohaATN , (S, K,) [all pls. of pauc.,] the last of these being pl. either of rahaTN or of rahoTN , (TA,) and A^araAhiTu , (S, ISd, K,) as though pl. of A^arohuTN , (S, ISd,) though Sb makes it pl. of rahoTN , because of the rareness of the pl. pl., (ISd,) and A^araAhiyTu [which is app. pl. of A^arohaATN ]. (S, K.) You say, humo rahoTuhu dinoyapF They are his people, and his tribe, closely related. (S, TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xxvii. 49], wakaAna qiY Almadiynapi tisoEapu rahoTK , (S,) but this means, [ And there were in the city ] nine persons, (Bd,) or nine men. (Jel.) ― -b2- You also say rahoTN mino Eu$arK [ A collection of plants of the kind called E$r ]. (IAar, Sh, TA in art. Ayk .) -A2- An enemy; syn. Eaduw~N ; (K, TA; [in the CK Eadow ;]) mentioned by Sgh, on the authority of Ibn- 'Abbád. (TA.) -A3- A skin, (K,) or a waistwrapper ( A_izaAr ) made of leather, (Jm,) the sides of which are slit in several places in their lower parts, so that one may walk in it; (Jm, K;) or made of skin, and also of wool; (Aboo-Tálib the Grammarian;) or a skin of Et-Táïf, slit in several places; (M, TA;) or a skin of a size equal to the space between the navel and the knee; (S;) or a skin slit into a number of thongs or strips; (ISh, S, K;) or a skin cut into a number of thongs or strips, these being one above another; (AHeyth;) or a waist-wrapper ( miy^ozar ) made of skin, or leather, slit in several places, except in the place of the pudendum; (TA;) or a skin slit into strips, each strip being of the breadth of four fingers; (IAar;) worn by children, (M, K,) or by a young girl before she has arrived at puberty, (IAar,) and by a woman in menstruis: (IAar, S, M, K, &c.:) [in Nubia, the rahoT , still called by that name, is very neatly made, consisting of a great number of slender thongs: it is worn there by young girls, and is generally their only covering, completely surrounding and concealing the pelvic portion of the body, and the whole or part of the thighs:] in the Time of Ignorance, the men used to perform their circuitings [around the Kaabeh] naked, and the women wearing [only] the rhT : (S:) [see also HawofN , in two places:] the pl. is A^arohaATN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, TA) and rihaATN : (ISh, S, K:) or this last is a sing. also, (K,) signifying a piece of leather of a size equal to the space between the place of the waist-band and the knee, slit in several places like the [ thongs called ] $uruk [ of the sandal, pl. of $iraAk ]; worn by a girl of seven years: or a garment worn by the boys of the Arabs of the desert, consisting of overlapping folds or plies, one above another, like fans: (TA:) pl. A^arohiTapN [a pl. of pauc.]. (K.)

A^arohiTapN [a pl. of pauc.]. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) sec. pers. riHota , (Msb,) aor. yaraAHu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. riyHN ; (K;) and aor. yaruwHu , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. rawoHN , (Msb,) or ruw^uwHN ; (TA;) It (a day) was violently windy. (S, Msb, K.) And rAH , aor. yaruwHu , inf. n. ruw^uwHN , It (a day) was one of good, or pleasant, wind. (TA.) ― -b2- rAH , aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. rawoHN , It was, or became, cool and pleasant [ by means of the wind ]. (L.) It (a house, or tent, the door being opened,) [ was, or became, aired by the wind; or] was entered by the wind. (L.) ― -b3- rAH Al$~ajaru The trees felt the wind. (AHn, K.) [See also another meaning below.] ― -b4- [Hence, perhaps,] rAH , aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. raAHN , (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, prompt, or quick; [as though he felt the wind and was refreshed by it;] (L;) as also ↓ ArtAH : (S, A, L, K:) raAHN and ↓ AirotiyaAHN signify the same: (S, L, K: [in the CK, AlAirotiyAHi is erroneously put for AlAirotiyaAHu :]) and ↓ AisotarowaHa (assumed tropical:) he (a man) became light, or active, and quick; syn. $am~ara . (Msb.) You say, rAH lil$~aYo'i [and A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i ] and ↓ ArtAH [and ArtAH bihi ] (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, brisk, lively, &c, as above, at the thing, [or betook himself with briskness, liveliness, &c., to the thing, ] and was rejoiced by it. (Lth, TA.) A poet says, wa zaEamota A^an~aka laA taraAHu A_ilaY Aln~isaA [(assumed tropical:) And thou assertedst that thou dost not, or wilt not, betake thyself with briskness, &c., to women, nor be rejoiced by them ]. (Lth, TA.) And rAH liloA^amori i. q. ↓ ArtAH [ He betook himself with briskness, &c., to the thing, or affair; or was brisk, &c., to do it ]. (TA.) And rAH li*`lika AlA^amori , (L, K,) and A_ilayohi , (L,) aor. yaraAHN , inf. n. rawaAHN and ruw^uwHN and raAHN and riyaAHapN (L, K) and raAHapN and A^aroyaHiy~apN , (L,) (assumed tropical:) He brightened in countenance at that thing, (L, [there explained by A^a$oraqa lahu , and this I regard as the right reading, rather than that which I find in the copies of the K, which is A^a$orafa lahu , perhaps meaning the same as A^a$orafa Ealayohi , i. e. he became acquainted with that thing, or knew it, syn. AiT~alaEa Ealayohi ,]) and rejoiced in it, or at it, (L, K,) and was thereby affected with alacrity, cheerfulness, briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, disposing him to promptness in acts of kindness or beneficence: said of a generous man when he is asked to confer a gift; and sometimes, metaphorically, of dogs when called by their owner, and of other animals. (L.) [It is also said that] rawaAHN and rawaAHapN and raAHapN and rawoHapN and rawiyHapN [all app. inf. ns. of raAHa , or some of them may be simple substs.,] and muraAyaHapN [as though inf. n. of ↓ raAyaHa ] (L, K) signify (assumed tropical:) The experiencing relief from grief or sorrow, after suffering therefrom: (L:) or the experiencing the joy, or happiness, arising from certainty. (K. [See also rawoHN , below.]) You say also, A_ilaY Hadiyvihi ↓ AisotarowaHotu [app. meaning (assumed tropical:) I was affected with cheerfulness, liveliness, or the like, at his discourse, or narration; as seems to be indicated by the context in the place where it is mentioned: or perhaps, he trusted to his discourse, and became quiet, or easy, in mind; agreeably with an explanation of the verb which see below]: (A:) or AlY Hdyvh ↓ AstrAH (assumed tropical:) he inclined to his discourse. (MA.) And rAH lilomaEoruwfi , (S, A, L, K,) sec. pers. riHota , (L,) aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. raAHapN (S, L, K) and riyHN ; (L;) and lh ↓ ArtAH ; (A, L;) (tropical:) He was affected with alacrity, cheerfulness, briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, disposing him to promptness to do what was kind or beneficent: (As, S, L, K:) he inclined to, and loved, kindness or beneficence. (L.) And liln~adaY ↓ ArtAH (assumed tropical:) [ He was affected with alacrity, &c., and so disposed to bounty or liberality ]. (S, K.) And nazalato A@ll~`hu biraHomatihi faA^anoqa*ahu minohaA ↓ bihi baliy~apN faA@rotaAHa (tropical:) [ A trial, or an affliction, befell him, and God was active and prompt with his mercy, and delivered him from it ]: (T:) but ISd disapproves of thus speaking of God; and El-Fárisee says that it is an instance of the rudeness of speech characteristic of Arabs of the desert. (TA.) [Hence seems to have originated, as is app. implied in the TA, the assertion that] ↓ AlAirotiyaAHu signifies (assumed tropical:) The being merciful: and A@ll~`hu lahu biraHomatihi ↓ ArtAH , (assumed tropical:) God delivered him from trial, or affliction: (K:) or A@ll~`hu lifulaAnK ↓ ArtAH (assumed tropical:) God was merciful to such a one. (S.) One also says, rAHt yaduhu lika*aA , (K,) or bika*aA , (S L,) (tropical:) His hand was active, prompt, or quick, (S, L, K, TA,) to do such a thing, (K, TA,) or with such a thing; (S, L, TA;) as, for instance, with a sword, to strike with it. (L.) Hence the saying of the Prophet, mano raAHa A_ilaY AljumuEapi fiY Als~aAEapi AlA^uwlaY fakaA^an~amaA qad~ama badanapF (tropical:) [ Whosoever is brisk, or prompt, or quick, in repairing to the Friday-prayers in the first hour, he is as though he offered a camel, or a cow or bull, for sacrifice at Mekkeh ]: (K, * TA:) the meaning is, xaf~a A_ilayohaA , (K, TA,) and maDaY ; (TA;) not the going in the latter part of the day. (K, * TA.) [See also what follows.] ― -b5- raAHa , aor. yaruwHu , inf. n. rawaAHN ; and ↓ trw~H ; both signify the same; (S, Msb, K, &c.;) contr. of gadaA ; (S;) said of a man, (TA,) and of a company of men, (K, TA,) He, and they, went, or journeyed, or worked, or did a thing, in the evening, (K, TA,) or in the afternoon, i. e., from the declining of the sun from the meridian until night: (IF, Msb, K, TA:) this is said to be the primary meaning: (TA:) but they also mean he, or they, returned: (Msb:) and went, or journeyed, at any time: (Msb, * TA:) [for] Alr~awaAHu is not, as some imagine it to be, only [ the going, or journeying, ] in the last, or latter, part of the day; but is used by the Arabs as meaning the going, or journeying, at any time of the night or day; as also Alguduw~u : so say Az and others: (Msb:) or rAH , inf. n. rawaAHN , signifies he came, or went, after the declining of the sun from the meridian: but is sometimes used as meaning he went in an absolute sense: (Mgh:) and thus it means in the trad. commencing mano raAHa A_ilaY AljumuEapi [mentioned above, where a different explanation of the verb is given]: (Mgh, * Msb:) and [in like manner] one says to his companion or companions, ↓ taraw~aHo or taraw~aHuwA as meaning Go, or journey: (TA:) but raAHati AlA_ibilu , (S, L, K,) aor. taruwHu and taraAHu , inf. n. rawaAHN (L) and raAy^iHapN , (AZ, L, K,) signifies only The camels returned in the evening, or afternoon, (S, * Msb,) when their pastors drove or brought them back to their owners: so says Az. (Msb.) You say, ruHotu A_ilayohimo and Einodahumo , inf. n. rawoHN and rawaAHN , I went, (K, TA,) and I came, (TA,) to them in the evening, or afternoon; [or at any time, as appears from what has been said above;] and so ruHotuhumo , (K, TA,) inf. n. rawoHN ; (TA;) and ↓ raw~aHotuhumo , (K, TA,) inf. n. tarowiyHN ; (TA;) and ↓ taraw~aHotuhumo : (K, TA:) and ↓ A^anaA A^ugaAdiyhi wa A^uraAwiHuhu [ I go, or come, to him early in the morning, in the first part of the day, or between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise, and I go, or come, to him in the evening, or afternoon, app. he doing the like to me ]. (A. [See also 6.]) And raAHato Ealayohi A_ibiluhu , and ganamuhu , and maAluhu , His camels, and his sheep or goats, and his cattle, returned to him after the declining of the sun from the meridian; only at that time: and ↓ ArAHt may perhaps be a dial. var. thereof: (L, TA:) or rAHt biAlEa$iY~i EalaY A^aholihaA they (i. e. camels) returned from the place of pasture in the evening, or afternoon, to their owners. (S, * Msb.) ― -b6- rAH Al$~ajaru , (S, A, K,) aor. yazaAHu ; (S, A;) and ↓ trw~H ; (S, A;) [said in the TA to be tropical, but not so in the A;] The trees broke forth with leaves: (S, A, K:) or the former, the trees broke forth with leaves before the winter, when the night became cold, without rain; (As, TA;) and so the latter: (L:) or the latter, the trees broke forth with leaves after the close of the Sayof [or summer ]: (S, TA:) and AlguSonu ↓ trw~H The branch put forth leaves after other leaves had fallen from it. (R, TA.) [See another meaning of rAH Al$jr near the beginning of this art.] ― -b7- rAH , (S, K,) aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. raAHapN , (S,) said of a horse, [perhaps from the same verb as signifying “ he was, or became, brisk, lively, ” &c.,] He became a stallion, or fit to cover. (S, K.) -A2- raAHatohu Alr~iyHu , aor. taraAHu , The wind smote it; namely, a thing; (L, K;) as, for instance, a tree, and said of a tempestuous wind. (L.) And riyHa , said of a pool of water left by a torrent, It was smitten [or blown upon ] by the wind. (S, A, K.) In like manner also it is said of other things. (TA.) One says, riyHati Al$~ajarapu The tree was blown upon by the wind: or was blown about, or shaken, by the wind, so that its leaves were made to fall: or had the dust scattered upon it by the wind. (L.) And riyHuwA They (a people, or party,) were smitten and destroyed by the wind: (K, TA:) or they entered upon [ a time of ] wind; (K;) as also, in this latter sense, ↓ A^araAHuwA , (S, K,) or ↓ A^arowaHuwA . (A.) ― -b2- rAH Al$~aYo'a , (A 'Obeyd, S, K,) first pers. riHotu , (A 'Obeyd, S,) aor. yaraAHu (A 'Obeyd, S, K,) and yariyHu , (AA, S, K,) [inf. n., app., of the former rawoHN and of the latter riyHN as in the phrase of similar meaning following;] and ↓ A^araAHahu , (Ks, S, K,) and ↓ A^arowaHahu ; (AZ, K;) He smelt the thing; perceived its smell, or odour; (S, K, &c.;) as also ↓ AstrAHhu and ↓ AisotarowaHahu : (Ham p. 228:) and rAH Alr~iyHa , aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. rawoHN ; and aor. yariyHu , inf. n. riyHN ; and ↓ A^araAHahaA ; He smelt the odour. (Msb.) You say of an object of the chase, ↓ A^araAHaniY , (S,) and ↓ A^arowaHaniY , (AZ, S, A,) inf. n. of the latter A_irowaAHN , (AZ, TA,) He smelt me; perceived my smell, or odour: (AZ, S, A, TA:) and of the same, ↓ ArAH , (K,) and ↓ A^arowaHa , (T, S, K,) and ↓ AisotarowaHa , and ↓ AstrAH , (T, S,) He smelt a human being; perceived his smell, or odour: (T, S, K:) and the second of these four, (K, TA,) and the third and fourth, (TA,) he smelt gently, that he might perceive the odour of a thing: (K, TA:) or the third and fourth of the same, he smelt, or perceived, odour: (A:) and these two, said of a stallion, he perceived the smell of the female: and of a beast of prey you say, Alr~iyHa ↓ A^arowaHa , and ↓ A^araAHahaA , and ↓ AstrAHhA , and ↓ AisotarowaHahaA , meaning he smelt, or perceived, the odour; and accord. to Lh, some say, raAHahaA ; but this is seldom used. (TA) [It is asserted (in Har p. 324) that ↓ AstrAH is only from Alr~aAHapu ; but this assertion is of no weight against the authorities cited above.] It is said in a trad., mano qatala nafosFA muEaAhidapF lamo yaraHN raAy^iHapa Aljan~api , (A 'Obeyd, S, Mgh, * Msb, *) or lm yariHo , (AA, S, Msb,) or ↓ lm yuriHo , (Ks, S, Mgh, Msb,) i. e. [ He who slays a person with whom he is on terms of peace, (or, as in' the TA, muw^ominFA , i. e. a believer, )] he will not perceive the odour of Paradise: (S, Mgh, Msb:) As says, I know not whether it be from riHotu or from A^araHotu . (S.) You say also, minohu TiybFA ↓ A^arowaHotu I perceived from him (a man, S) a sweet odour. (S, A.) ― -b3- [And hence, app.,] rAH minoka maEoruwfFA , and ↓ ArAHhu , (assumed tropical:) He obtained from thee a favour, or benefit. (K.) -A3- rawiHa , aor. yarowaHu , inf. n. rawaHN , He (a man) had the quality termed rawaHN , [explained below, i. e. width in the space between the thighs or legs; &c.; or] a spreading in the fore part of each foot. (Lth, TA.) And rawiHato qadamuhu His foot had the quality so termed. (TA.)

[Hence seems to have originated, as is app. implied in the TA, the assertion that] ↓ AlAirotiyaAHu signifies (assumed tropical:) The being merciful: and A@ll~`hu lahu biraHomatihi ↓ ArtAH , (assumed tropical:) God delivered him from trial, or affliction: (K:) or A@ll~`hu lifulaAnK ↓ ArtAH (assumed tropical:) God was merciful to such a one. (S.) One also says, rAHt yaduhu lika*aA , (K,) or bika*aA , (S L,) (tropical:) His hand was active, prompt, or quick, (S, L, K, TA,) to do such a thing, (K, TA,) or with such a thing; (S, L, TA;) as, for instance, with a sword, to strike with it. (L.) Hence the saying of the Prophet, mano raAHa A_ilaY AljumuEapi fiY Als~aAEapi AlA^uwlaY fakaA^an~amaA qad~ama badanapF (tropical:) [ Whosoever is brisk, or prompt, or quick, in repairing to the Friday-prayers in the first hour, he is as though he offered a camel, or a cow or bull, for sacrifice at Mekkeh ]: (K, * TA:) the meaning is, xaf~a A_ilayohaA , (K, TA,) and maDaY ; (TA;) not the going in the latter part of the day. (K, * TA.) [See also what follows.] ― -b5- raAHa , aor. yaruwHu , inf. n. rawaAHN ; and ↓ trw~H ; both signify the same; (S, Msb, K, &c.;) contr. of gadaA ; (S;) said of a man, (TA,) and of a company of men, (K, TA,) He, and they, went, or journeyed, or worked, or did a thing, in the evening, (K, TA,) or in the afternoon, i. e., from the declining of the sun from the meridian until night: (IF, Msb, K, TA:) this is said to be the primary meaning: (TA:) but they also mean he, or they, returned: (Msb:) and went, or journeyed, at any time: (Msb, * TA:) [for] Alr~awaAHu is not, as some imagine it to be, only [ the going, or journeying, ] in the last, or latter, part of the day; but is used by the Arabs as meaning the going, or journeying, at any time of the night or day; as also Alguduw~u : so say Az and others: (Msb:) or rAH , inf. n. rawaAHN , signifies he came, or went, after the declining of the sun from the meridian: but is sometimes used as meaning he went in an absolute sense: (Mgh:) and thus it means in the trad. commencing mano raAHa A_ilaY AljumuEapi [mentioned above, where a different explanation of the verb is given]: (Mgh, * Msb:) and [in like manner] one says to his companion or companions, ↓ taraw~aHo or taraw~aHuwA as meaning Go, or journey: (TA:) but raAHati AlA_ibilu , (S, L, K,) aor. taruwHu and taraAHu , inf. n. rawaAHN (L) and raAy^iHapN , (AZ, L, K,) signifies only The camels returned in the evening, or afternoon, (S, * Msb,) when their pastors drove or brought them back to their owners: so says Az. (Msb.) You say, ruHotu A_ilayohimo and Einodahumo , inf. n. rawoHN and rawaAHN , I went, (K, TA,) and I came, (TA,) to them in the evening, or afternoon; [or at any time, as appears from what has been said above;] and so ruHotuhumo , (K, TA,) inf. n. rawoHN ; (TA;) and ↓ raw~aHotuhumo , (K, TA,) inf. n. tarowiyHN ; (TA;) and ↓ taraw~aHotuhumo : (K, TA:) and ↓ A^anaA A^ugaAdiyhi wa A^uraAwiHuhu [ I go, or come, to him early in the morning, in the first part of the day, or between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise, and I go, or come, to him in the evening, or afternoon, app. he doing the like to me ]. (A. [See also 6.]) And raAHato Ealayohi A_ibiluhu , and ganamuhu , and maAluhu , His camels, and his sheep or goats, and his cattle, returned to him after the declining of the sun from the meridian; only at that time: and ↓ ArAHt may perhaps be a dial. var. thereof: (L, TA:) or rAHt biAlEa$iY~i EalaY A^aholihaA they (i. e. camels) returned from the place of pasture in the evening, or afternoon, to their owners. (S, * Msb.) ― -b6- rAH Al$~ajaru , (S, A, K,) aor. yazaAHu ; (S, A;) and ↓ trw~H ; (S, A;) [said in the TA to be tropical, but not so in the A;] The trees broke forth with leaves: (S, A, K:) or the former, the trees broke forth with leaves before the winter, when the night became cold, without rain; (As, TA;) and so the latter: (L:) or the latter, the trees broke forth with leaves after the close of the Sayof [or summer ]: (S, TA:) and AlguSonu ↓ trw~H The branch put forth leaves after other leaves had fallen from it. (R, TA.) [See another meaning of rAH Al$jr near the beginning of this art.] ― -b7- rAH , (S, K,) aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. raAHapN , (S,) said of a horse, [perhaps from the same verb as signifying “ he was, or became, brisk, lively, ” &c.,] He became a stallion, or fit to cover. (S, K.) -A2- raAHatohu Alr~iyHu , aor. taraAHu , The wind smote it; namely, a thing; (L, K;) as, for instance, a tree, and said of a tempestuous wind. (L.) And riyHa , said of a pool of water left by a torrent, It was smitten [or blown upon ] by the wind. (S, A, K.) In like manner also it is said of other things. (TA.) One says, riyHati Al$~ajarapu The tree was blown upon by the wind: or was blown about, or shaken, by the wind, so that its leaves were made to fall: or had the dust scattered upon it by the wind. (L.) And riyHuwA They (a people, or party,) were smitten and destroyed by the wind: (K, TA:) or they entered upon [ a time of ] wind; (K;) as also, in this latter sense, ↓ A^araAHuwA , (S, K,) or ↓ A^arowaHuwA . (A.) ― -b2- rAH Al$~aYo'a , (A 'Obeyd, S, K,) first pers. riHotu , (A 'Obeyd, S,) aor. yaraAHu (A 'Obeyd, S, K,) and yariyHu , (AA, S, K,) [inf. n., app., of the former rawoHN and of the latter riyHN as in the phrase of similar meaning following;] and ↓ A^araAHahu , (Ks, S, K,) and ↓ A^arowaHahu ; (AZ, K;) He smelt the thing; perceived its smell, or odour; (S, K, &c.;) as also ↓ AstrAHhu and ↓ AisotarowaHahu : (Ham p. 228:) and rAH Alr~iyHa , aor. yaraAHu , inf. n. rawoHN ; and aor. yariyHu , inf. n. riyHN ; and ↓ A^araAHahaA ; He smelt the odour. (Msb.) You say of an object of the chase, ↓ A^araAHaniY , (S,) and ↓ A^arowaHaniY , (AZ, S, A,) inf. n. of the latter A_irowaAHN , (AZ, TA,) He smelt me; perceived my smell, or odour: (AZ, S, A, TA:) and of the same, ↓ ArAH , (K,) and ↓ A^arowaHa , (T, S, K,) and ↓ AisotarowaHa , and ↓ AstrAH , (T, S,) He smelt a human being; perceived his smell, or odour: (T, S, K:) and the second of these four, (K, TA,) and the third and fourth, (TA,) he smelt gently, that he might perceive the odour of a thing: (K, TA:) or the third and fourth of the same, he smelt, or perceived, odour: (A:) and these two, said of a stallion, he perceived the smell of the female: and of a beast of prey you say, Alr~iyHa ↓ A^arowaHa , and ↓ A^araAHahaA , and ↓ AstrAHhA , and ↓ AisotarowaHahaA , meaning he smelt, or perceived, the odour; and accord. to Lh, some say, raAHahaA ; but this is seldom used. (TA) [It is asserted (in Har p. 324) that ↓ AstrAH is only from Alr~aAHapu ; but this assertion is of no weight against the authorities cited above.] It is said in a trad., mano qatala nafosFA muEaAhidapF lamo yaraHN raAy^iHapa Aljan~api , (A 'Obeyd, S, Mgh, * Msb, *) or lm yariHo , (AA, S, Msb,) or ↓ lm yuriHo , (Ks, S, Mgh, Msb,) i. e. [ He who slays a person with whom he is on terms of peace, (or, as in' the TA, muw^ominFA , i. e. a believer, )] he will not perceive the odour of Paradise: (S, Mgh, Msb:) As says, I know not whether it be from riHotu or from A^araHotu . (S.) You say also, minohu TiybFA ↓ A^arowaHotu I perceived from him (a man, S) a sweet odour. (S, A.) ― -b3- [And hence, app.,] rAH minoka maEoruwfFA , and ↓ ArAHhu , (assumed tropical:) He obtained from thee a favour, or benefit. (K.) -A3- rawiHa , aor. yarowaHu , inf. n. rawaHN , He (a man) had the quality termed rawaHN , [explained below, i. e. width in the space between the thighs or legs; &c.; or] a spreading in the fore part of each foot. (Lth, TA.) And rawiHato qadamuhu His foot had the quality so termed. (TA.)

definition: ― -b2- AlmuraAwaHapu fiY AlEamalayoni , (S,) or bayona AlEamalayoni , (Mgh, K,) signifies The doing the two deeds, or works, alternately;
sourceDefinition: : see 1, in the latter half of the paragraph. ― -b2- AlmuraAwaHapu fiY AlEamalayoni , (S,) or bayona AlEamalayoni , (Mgh, K,) signifies The doing the two deeds, or works, alternately; this one time, and that one time: (S, Mgh, K:) as, for instance, reading, or reciting, at one time, and writing at another time: (Mgh:) and AlmrAwHp byn Alr~ijolayoni the standing upon the two legs alternately; upon each in turn: and AlmrAwHp byn Aljanobayoni the turning over [ upon the two sides alternately, or] from side to side. (K.) You say, rAwH bayona Eamalayoni [ He did two deeds, or works, alternately; he alternated them ]. (A.) And rAwH bayona rijolayohi He stood upon one of his legs one time and upon the other another time: (S, Mgh:) it is said also of one walking [as meaning he moved his legs alternately ]. (A.) And it is said in a trad., kaAna yuraAwiHu bayona qadamayohi mino Tuwli AlqiyaAmi He used to rest upon one of his feet one time and upon the other another time to give relief to each of them [ in consequence of long standing ]. (TA.) One says also, rAwHhu He did a thing with him by turns, each of them taking his turn [ and so relieving the other: for AlmuraAwaHapu signifies the giving mutual relief, or rest ]. (TA in art. Eqb .) [See also 6.] -A2- raAyaHa , inf. n. muraAyaHapN : see 1, in the former part of the paragraph.
