sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, O, K, &c.,) inf. n. DarobN , (S, O, &c.,) [ He beat, struck, smote, or hit, him, or it; ] and ↓ Dr~bhu [signifies the same in an intensive sense, i. e. he beat, &c., him, or it, much, or violently; or in a frequentative sense, i. e. several, or many, times: or rather Dr~b is used in relation to several, or many, objects, as will be shown in what follows]: (K:) accord. to Er-Rághib, AlD~arobu signifies the making a thing to fall upon another thing; and, as some say, the making it to fall with violence, or vehemence. (TA.) You say, Darabahu bihi [ He struck him, or it, with it ], i. e. with a sword, (A, Mgh, Msb), &c. (A, Msb.) And taDoribu fiY HadiydK baAridK [ Thou beatest upon cold iron ]: a prov. [expl. in art. Hd ]. (Har p. 633.) And Darabotu zayodFA sawoTFA , meaning bisawoTK [i. e. I struck Zeyd with a whip ], or Darobapa sawoTK [ a stroke of a whip ]: (M in art. swT , q. v.:) and Darabahu miAy^apa sawoTK [ He struck him a hundred strokes of the whip ]. (S and K in art. sHl , &c.) And Darabotu Eunuqahu [ I smote his neck, meaning I beheaded him ]; and AlA^aEonaAqa ↓ Dar~abotu [ I smote the necks, meaning I struck off the heads ]; the teshdeed denoting muchness [of the action] or multiplicity [of the objects]: AZ says that, when the object is one, the Arabs use only the former verb, without teshdeed; but when there is a plurality of objects, either of the verbs; (Msb;) [so that] one says, DarabuwA A^aEonaAqahumo [ They smote their necks, or beheaded them ], and A^amara Alr~iqaAbi ↓ bitaDoriybi [ He gave the order to smite the necks, or to strike off the heads ]: (A:) faDaroba Alr~iqaAbi in the Kur xlvii. 4 is originally faA@DoribuwA Alr~iqaAba DarobFA [meaning Then do ye smite the necks, i. e. strike off the heads ]; (Bd;) the inf. n. being here put for its verb. (Jel.) [Respecting the phrase huwa A@loyaDoribuka , see 1 in art. jdE .] ― -b2- [Hence a variety of meanings and phrases here following.] ― -b3- Daraba kalobahu EalaY AlS~ayodi (assumed tropical:) [ He beat, or disciplined, or trained, his dog for the purpose of the chase ]: whence the phrases Daraba Ealayohi jirowatahu and Daraba jirowapa nafosihi and Darabotu jirowatiY Eanohu [expl. voce jirowapN ]. (Z, and TA in art. jrw .) ― -b4- laA tuDorabu A^akobaAdu AlA_ibili A_il~aA valaAvapi masaAjida (assumed tropical:) Camels shall not be ridden, save to three mosques: [namely, that of Mekkeh, that of El-Medeeneh, and that of El-Aksà at Jerusalem:] a trad. (TA. [See also 4 in art. Eml .]) ― -b5- [ Daraba bihi AlA^aroDa , lit. He smote with him, or it, the ground; meaning (assumed tropical:) he cast, threw, or flung, him, or it, upon the ground. And Daraba bisaloHihi AlA^aroDa (assumed tropical:) He cast forth his excrement, or ordure, upon the ground. ] And [hence] Daraba AlA^aroDa and AlgaAy^iTa (tropical:) He voided excrement, or ordure; (A, TA;) and so AlxalaA='a . (TA.) [ Daraba binafosihi AlA^aroDa see expl. in the latter half of this paragraph.] ― -b6- Darabotu Alqawosa biAlmiDorabi I struck the string of the bow with the wooden implement [or mallet ] used in separating cotton. (Msb.) ― -b7- Daraba AlEuwda [ He struck the chords of the lute; meaning he played upon the lute; and so Daraba biAlEuwdi ]. (S.) ― -b8- Daraba Alwatida , aor. and inf. n. as above, He beat [or knocked or struck ] the tent-peg, or stake, so that it became firm in the ground. (Lh, TA.) And [hence] Daraba Alxayomapa (tropical:) He pitched the tent, by knocking in its pegs with a mallet: (Kull p. 231:) or he set up the tent. (Msb.) ― -b9- Daraba Ald~irohama , aor. and inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He struck, coined, or minted, the dirhem, or piece of money. (TA.) And Daraba EalaY A@smihi (assumed tropical:) [ He struck, coined, or minted, money in his name ]. (ISd, TA in art. jwz .) ― -b10- Daraba EalaY Almakotuwbi (tropical:) He sealed, or stamped, the writing. (A, * TA.) [And Daraba Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He erased it; namely, anything written.] ― -b11- Daraba AlT~iyna EalaY AljidaAri (assumed tropical:) [ He stuck, or applied, the mud upon the wall, as a plaster]. (TA.) ― -b12- Hence, accord. to some, the phrase Duribato Ealayohimu A@l*~il~apu , in the Kur ii. 58, considered as meaning (assumed tropical:) Vileness was made to cleave to them: or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) encompassed them, like as the tent encompasses him over whom it is pitched. (Ksh, Bd.) And [in like manner] one says, Duribato Ealayohimu DariybapN (tropical:) An impost, of the tax called jizoyap , &c., was imposed upon them. (A, * Mgh, Msb. *) And Daraba EalaY AlEabodi AlA^itaAwapa (tropical:) He imposed upon the slave the tax according to a fixed time. (TA. [See DirybapN .]) And Durba Ealayohimu AlbaEovu (assumed tropical:) The being sent to the war was appointed them and imposed upon them as an obligation. (Mgh in art. bEv .) ― -b13- Daraba Al$~abakapa EalaY AlT~aAy^iri (assumed tropical:) He cast the net over the bird: (Mgh:) and Duriba Alfax~u EalaY AlT~aAy^iri (tropical:) [ The snare was cast over the bird ]. (A, TA.) ― -b14- Daraba All~ayolu biA^aruwaAqihi (assumed tropical:) [ The night cast its folds of darkness; ] meaning the night came. (TA.) [And (assumed tropical:) The night became dark, or was dark; as appears from the following verse.] Homeyd says, saraY mivola naboDi AlEiroqi waAll~ayolu DaAribN biA^rowaAqihi waAlS~uboHu qado kaAda yasoTaEu (assumed tropical:) [ He went on in his night-journey, like the pulsing of the vein, while the night was casting its folds of darkness over the earth, and the dawn had almost risen ]. (TA. [See also DaAribN .]) You say also, Daraba Ealayohi HijaAbFA (assumed tropical:) [ He put, or let down, a veil, or curtain, or covering, over him, or it ]. (TA.) And Duriba bayonahumaA sad~N (assumed tropical:) [ A barrier was set between them two ]. (A in art. sd .) DarabonaA EalaY A=*aAnihimo [in the Kur xviii. 10] means (tropical:) We prevented their sleeping; (K, TA;) as though by putting a covering over their ears; a metonymical [and elliptical] mode of saying we made them to sleep by preventing any sound from penetrating into their ears, in consequence of which they would have awoke: (Zj, L, TA:) or Daraba EalaY A=*aAnihimo means (assumed tropical:) he poured upon them sleep so that they slept and did not awake: and one says also, Darabotu Aln~awoma EalaY A^u*unihi [meaning (assumed tropical:) I poured sleep upon him by closing his ear ]. (Msb.) ― -b15- Darabati , AlEaqorabu , (A, K, * TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The scorpion stung. (A, K, * TA.) ― -b16- [ Darabatohu Alr~iyHu (assumed tropical:) The wind beat it, or blew upon it; namely, herbage, and water, &c.] And Darabahu Albarodu (IKtt, K, TA) (assumed tropical:) The cold smote it so as to injure it; namely, herbage; and in like manner one says of the wind: (IKtt, TA:) and ↓ ADrbhu Albarodu (A, TA) (tropical:) The cold smote it by its vehemence, so that it dried up; and in like manner one says of the wind: (TA:) and AlD~ariybu AlA^aroDa ↓ ADrb (assumed tropical:) The hoar-frost, or rime, fell upon the land, so that its herbage became nipped, or blasted. (AZ, TA. [See also Dariba .]) And Duriba bibaliy~apK (assumed tropical:) He was smitten with a trial, or an affliction. (L, TA.) ― -b17- Tariyqu mak~apa maA DarabahaA AlEaAma qaTorapN (tropical:) [ The road to Mekkeh, not a drop of rain has fallen upon it this year ]. (A, TA.) ― -b18- Daraba AlfaHolu Aln~aAqapa , (S, A, * Msb, K, * TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. DiraAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and DarobN also, accord. to Fr, but this latter, though agreeable with analogy, is disallowed by Sb and Akh, (TA,) (tropical:) The stallion leaped the she-camel; (Msb, TA;) i. e. (TA,) compressed (A, K, TA) her. (TA.) DiraAbu Aljamali is used elliptically for vamanu DiraAbi Aljamali (tropical:) The hire of the camel's leaping the female: the taking of which, as also the taking of the hire of any stallion for covering, is forbidden in a trad. (TA.) ― -b19- Daraba Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i (tropical:) He mixed the [one] thing with the [other] thing; (A, K;) as also ↓ Dr~bhu , (K,) inf. n. taDoriybN : (TA:) accord. to some, said peculiarly in relation to milk; (MF, TA;) but [SM says,] this I have not found in any lexicon. (TA.) Daraba All~abana fiY Als~iqaA='i means (tropical:) Haqanahu [i. e. He collected the milk in the skin, and poured fresh milk upon that which was curdled, or thick, or upon that which was churned; or he poured the milk into the skin, and kept it therein that its butter might come forth ]. (A.) In the L and other lexicons it is said that Darabotu bayonahumo fiY Al$~ar~i means I caused them to become confused [or I involved them ] in evil or mischief. (TA. [And Dr~bt bayonahumo has a similar meaning: see 2.]) And Durbati Al$~aApu bilawoni ka*aA means The sheep, or goat, was intermixed with such a colour. (L, TA.) ― -b20- Daraba Al$~ajaru biEuruwqihi fiY AlA^aroDi [ The trees struck their roots into the earth ]. (A and TA in art. Erq .) ― -b21- [Hence, the saying,] Darabato fiyhi fulaAnapu biEiroqK *iY A^a$abK i. e. AilotibaAs ; (S and TA in the present art., and in like manner, in both, in art. A$b , with the addition of *iY before AilotibaAsK ;) (tropical:) [app. meaning Such a woman implanted, or engendered, in him a strain, i. e. a radical, or hereditary, quality, of a dubious kind: or the pronoun in fyh relates to a family, or people; for it is said that] the meaning is, such a woman corrupted their race by her bringing forth among them: or, as some say, Erqt fiyhimo Eiroqa sawo'K [i. e. Ear~aqato , or, accord. to more common usage, A^aEoraqato , i. e., implanted, or engendered, among them, or in them, an evil strain, or radical or hereditary disposition ]. (TA. [This saying is also mentioned in the A, as tropical, but is not expl. therein.]) ― -b22- Daraba biAlqidaAHi , (S, Mgh, K,) and Daraba AlqidaAHa , (A, TA,) (tropical:) He turned about, or shuffled, ( A^ajaAla ,) the arrows, [ in the ribaAbap (q. v.), in the game called Almuyosir ,] EalaY Aljazwri [ for the slaughtered camel ]. (Mgh. [See HuroDapN .]) [And (assumed tropical:) He played with the gamingarrows; practised sortilege with arrows, or with the arrows. ] You say, Darabotu maEa Alqawomi bisahomK (assumed tropical:) I practised sortilege with the people, or party, with an arrow; syn. saAhamotuhumo . (Msb.) And Daraba biAlqidoHayoni (assumed tropical:) He practised sortilege with the two arrows; one of which was inscribed with the sentence “ My Lord hath commanded me, ” and the other with “ My Lord hath forbidden me: ” a person between hope and despair is likened to one practising this mode of sortilege, which was used by the people of the Time of Ignorance when they doubted whether they should undertake an affair or abstain from it. (Har pp. 465 and 553.) One says also, Daraba fiY AljazuwribisahomK meaning (assumed tropical:) He obtained a share, or portion, of the slaughtered camel. (Mgh.) And hence the saying of El-Hareeree, waDarabotu fiY maroEaAhaA binaSiybK (assumed tropical:) [ And I obtained a share of its pasture ]. (Mgh.) And the lawyers say, yaDoribu fiyhi biAlv~uluvi i. e. (assumed tropical:) He shall take thereof somewhat, according to what is due to him, of the third part. (Mgh.) They say also, Daraba fiY maAlihi sahomFA i. e. (assumed tropical:) He assigned [ a share, or portion, of his property ]: and thus is expl. the saying of Aboo-Haneefeh, laA yaDoribu lilomuwSaY lahu fiymaA zaAda EalaY Alv~uluvi (assumed tropical:) He shall not assign, or give, to the legatee, aught of more than the third part; the true objective complement being suppressed. (Mgh.) ― -b23- Daraba biyadayohi [lit. He beat with his arms; meaning (assumed tropical:) he moved his arms about, or to and fro; brandished, tossed, or swung them ]: you say, Daraba biyadayohi waHar~akahumaA fiY mi$oyatihi (assumed tropical:) [ He swung his arms, and moved them about, in his manner of walking ]. (TA in art. jdf . [See jadafa .]) And Daraba fiY AlmaA='i [ biyadayohi being understood after the verb] (assumed tropical:) He swam. (K.) ― -b24- Daraba biyadihi A_ilaY $aYo'K (assumed tropical:) He made a sign, or pointed, with his hand, towards a thing. (TA.) And Daraba [alone] (assumed tropical:) He made a sign, or pointed. (K.) And Daraba biyadihi A_ilaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He put forth his hand towards such a thing, to take it, or to point, or make a sign. (TA.) And Daraba yadahu A_ilaY Eamali ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ He applied his hand to the doing of such a thing ]. (Lth, TA.) [And Daraba yadayohi fiY AlmaAli a phrase expl. to me by IbrD as meaning (assumed tropical:) He busied his hands with the property, in the giving, or dispensing of it.] ― -b25- Daraba EalaY yadihi (assumed tropical:) [ He struck his (i. e. another man's) hand; meaning] he struck, or made, the bargain with him; or ratified the sale with him: for it is a custom, when two persons are bargaining together, for one of them to put his hand upon the other's in ratifying the bargain. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b26- And (tropical:) He prohibited, or prevented, or hindered, him, from doing a thing, or from doing a thing that he had begun: (TA:) and [in like manner] Daraba EalaY yadayohi (tropical:) he withheld, or restrained, him, or it. (K, TA.) And (i. e. the former phrase) (tropical:) He (the judge, A, Mgh, TA) prohibited, or interdicted, him from the using, or disposing of, his property according to his own free will. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, TA.) ― -b27- Also (tropical:) He corrupted, vitiated, marred, or disordered, his affair, or case, or state. (A, Msb, TA.) ― -b28- Daraba Eanohu (assumed tropical:) He turned away a person or thing from him [or it ]; as also ↓ ADrb : (TA:) [or] Enh ↓ ADrb signifies, (S, Msb,) or signifies also, (TA,) and (Msb, TA) so does Daraba Enh , (Msb, K, TA,) [the latter app. for Daraba nafosahu Eanohu ,] (assumed tropical:) He turned away from, avoided, shunned, or left, him, or it; (S * Msb, K * TA; *) namely, a person, (TA,) or a thing. (Msb.) A^afanaDoribu Eanokumu A@l*~ikora SafoHFA , in the Kur [xliii. 4], is said to mean (assumed tropical:) Shall we then neglect you, and not teach you what is incumbent on you? the phrase being taken from a rider's striking his beast with his stick when he desires to turn him from the course that he is pursuing: or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) shall we then turn away the Kur-án from you, and not invite you thereby to the faith, turning away ourselves from you? (TA.) One says also, Darabotu Eanohu SafoHFA meaning (assumed tropical:) I turned away from him and left him. (S and TA in art. SfH : see 1 in that art.) See also the saying Daraba A^axomaAsahu fiY A^asodaAsihi voce xumusN . ― -b29- And fulaAnN yaDoribu A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK : see voce ximosN . ― -b30- Daraba binafosihi AlA^aroDa , (K,) inf. n. DarobN , (TA,) [lit. He smote with himself the ground; and hence, (assumed tropical:) he cast, threw, or flung, himself upon the ground; app. often used in this sense; (a phrase similar to Daraba bihi AlA^aroDa expl. before;) and hence,] (assumed tropical:) he remained, stayed, or abode; (K;) and so ↓ ADrb (AZ, ISk, S, K, TA) as used in the phrase ADrb Alr~ajulu fiY Albayoti (tropical:) The man remained, stayed, or abode, in the tent, or house, (AZ, ISk, S, A, TA,) not quitting it: (ISk, A, TA:) and [in like manner] Daraba b*anabihi , [ AlA^aroDa being understood,] (assumed tropical:) He stayed, or abode, and remained fixed. (K in art. *nb . [See also other explanations of this last phrase in a later part of this paragraph.]) And Daraba Alwatida bimaHal~i ka*aA (tropical:) He remained, stayed, or abode, [lit., struck the tent-peg, ] in such a place of alighting. (A.) And Darabati AlA_ibilu biEaTanK , [ AlA^aroDa being understood after AlAbl ,] (assumed tropical:) The camels lay down [ in a place by the water ]: (S in art. ETn :) or satisfied themselves with drinking and then lay down around the water or by the watering-troughs, to be brought again to drink another time: (IAth, TA in that art.:) and [hence,] Daraba Aln~aAsu biEaTanK , occurring in a trad., (assumed tropical:) The people's camels satisfied themselves with drinking until they lay down and remained in their place [ at the water ]: (TA in the present art.:) or the people satisfied their thirst and then abode at the water. (K in art. ETn .) ― -b31- Daraba bi*aqanihi AlA^aroDa (tropical:) He was cowardly; and feared; (A, O,* K, TA;) and clave to the ground: (O, TA:) or he was, or became, affected with shame, shyness, or bashfulness. (A, TA.) ― -b32- yaDoribu lahu AlA^aroDa kul~ahaA [lit. He beats for it the whole land, i. e. in journeying,] means (assumed tropical:) he seeks it through the whole land: so says AZ in explanation of the phrase here following. (O, TA.) yaDoribu Almajoda (assumed tropical:) He seeks to gain, or obtain, glory: (O, K:) or he applies himself with art and diligence to gain glory, ( yakotasibuhu ,) and seeks it through the whole land. (AZ, TA. [See also 8.]) ― -b34- Daraba All~abina , (A,) or All~ibona , (tropical:) He made [or moulded ] bricks. (MA.) And Daraba AlxaAtama (tropical:) He made, fashioned, or moulded, the signet-ring. (TA.) [Hence one says,] AiDoribohu EalaY TaboEi h`*aA i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Make thou it, fashion it, or mould it, ] according to the model, make, fashion, or mould, of this. (IAar, O and K in art. TbE .) And h`*ihi Dariybatuhu Al~atiY Duriba EalayohaA , and DuribahaA , and Duriba alone, [for Duriba EalayohaA ,] meaning TubiEa [i. e. (assumed tropical:) This is his nature, with an adaptation, or a disposition, to which he was moulded, or created; or to which he was adapted, or disposed, by creation ]. (Lh, TA.) And Duriba fulaAnN EalaY Alkarami (tropical:) [ Such a one was moulded, or created, with an adaptation or a disposition, to generosity; or was adapted, or disposed, by creation, or nature, to generosity ]. (A.) ― -b35- Daraba mavalFA (S, A, O, &c.) (tropical:) He rehearsed, propounded, or declared, a parable, a similitude, an example, or a proverb; said of God [and of a man]: (S, * O, * Msb, TA:) or he mentioned, or set forth, a parable, &c.: or he framed a parable: thus expl., the verb has but one objective complement: or the phrase signifies he made [such a thing] an example, or the subject of a parable or similitude &c.; and so has two objective complements: in the saying in the Kur [xxxvi. 12] waA@Doribo lahumo mavalFA A^aSoHaAba A@loqaroyapi (assumed tropical:) [ And propound thou to them a parable, the people of the town ] i. e., the story of the people of the town, [or make thou to them a parable, or similitude, or an example, the people of the town; ] mvlA may be in the accus. case as an objective complement, ADHAb Alqryp being a substitute for mvlA ; or ASHAb Alqryp may be regarded as a second objective complement [i. e. second in the order of the words, but first in the order of the sense]: the phrase is differently expl. on account of the different meanings of the verb Daraba ; which signifies he described, or rehearsed; and he declared, propounded, or explained; and he made, caused to be, or constituted; &c.; accord. to some, it is taken from the phrase Daraba Aldirohama [q. v.]; because of the impression which a parable or the like makes upon the mind: accord. to some, from DariybN signifying “ a like; ” because the first thing is made like the second: accord. to some, from Daraba AlT~iyna EalaY AljidaAri [q. v.; because the mud, applied as a plaster, conforms to the shape of the wall]: and accord. to some, from Daraba AlxaAtama [q. v.]; because of the correspondence between a parable or the like and the object to which it is applied, and the correspondence between the signet and its impression. (TA, from the M and L &c.) yaDoribu A@ll~`hu A@loHaq~a waA@lobATila , in the Kur [xiii. 18], means (assumed tropical:) God likeneth, or compareth, truth and falsity. (TA.) One says also, Daraba bihi mavalFA (assumed tropical:) [ He made him, or it, a subject of a parable, a similitude, an example, or a proverb; he propounded, or framed, a parable, &c., respecting him, or it ]. (TA.) And yuDorabu Almavalu lika*aA [ The proverb, &c., is applied to, in relation to, or to the case of, such a thing ]. (Meyd &c., passim.) ― -b36- Daraba lahu A^ajalFA (assumed tropical:) He specified, or notified, to, or for, him, or it, a term, or period. (Mgh, Msb. *) ― -b37- Daraba lahumo TariyqFA (assumed tropical:) He assigned to them, or made for them, a way; syn. jaEala . (MA. [App. from a phrase in the Kur xx. 79, q. v.]) ― -b38- AlD~arobu as a conventional term of the accountants, or arithmeticians, means The multiplying a number by another number; (Mgh, Msb;) as when you say, [ Daraba xamospF fiY sit~apK He multiplied five by six; and] xamosapN fiY sit~apK bivalaAviyna [ Five multiplied by six is thirty ]. (Msb.) ― -b39- Daraba [is often intrans., and thus] signifies also taHar~aka [i. e. (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, in a state of commotion, &c.]: (K:) [see also 8, which is more commonly used in this sense:] or, so with strength, or force. (TA.) [And hence several phrases here following.] ― -b40- Daraba AlEiroqu (A, TA,) inf. n. DarobN and DarabaAnN , (TA,) (tropical:) The vein pulsed, or beat, (A, TA,) and throbbed: (TA:) and Daraba , inf. n. DarabaAnN , (tropical:) it (the vein) pained, and was, or became, in a state of strong commotion. (TA.) And Daraba AljuroHu , inf. n. DarabaAnN , (S, A, Msb,) (tropical:) The wound [ throbbed; or] pained violently: (A, Msb:) and so AlDirosu (tropical:) [ the tooth ]. (A, TA.) ― -b41- Darabati Aln~aAqapu , (A, K,) or, as in some lexicons, AlmaxaADu , (TA,) (tropical:) The she-camel, (A, K,) or the pregnant camel, (TA,) raised her tail, and smote her vulva with it, (A, K, TA,) and then went along. (K, TA.) ― -b42- Daraba fiY jahaAzihi (tropical:) He (a camel) took fright, and ran away at random, (S, A, L, TA,) and ceased not to gallop and leap until he had thrown off all his furniture, or load. (L, TA.) ― -b43- jaA='a yaDoribu bi$ar~K (tropical:) He came hastening [ with mischief, or] in an evil affair. (A.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, When such and such things shall happen, (mentioning faction, or sedition, or the like,) Daraba yaEosuwbu Ald~iyni bi*anabihi , meaning, accord. to AM, (assumed tropical:) The leader of the religion shall hasten to go away through the land, fleeing from the faction, or sedition: or, as some say, shall go away hastily through the land, with his followers. (O, TA. [But see yaEosuwbN : and see also *anabN .]) And you say also, Darabotu fiYAls~ayori , (Msb,) inf. n. DarobN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) I hastened in journeying. (S, * Msb.) And Daraba fiY AlA^aroDi , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. DarobN (S, K, TA) and maDorabN (S, TA) and DarabaAnN , (K, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He journeyed in the land (S, Mgh, Msb) seeking sustenance, (S,) and for the purpose of traffic: (Mgh:) [and Daraba AlA^aroDa , as shown above, has a similar meaning:] or (tropical:) he went forth in the land as a merchant; (A, K;) or warring and plundering, (K,) or so Daraba fiY sabiyli A@ll~`hi [meaning in the cause of God ]: (A:) or he hastened through the land: (A, K:) or he arose, and hastened in his journey through the land: (TA:) or he went, or went away, in the land: (A, K:) or he traversed, or journeyed through, the land. (TA.) The verb is [similarly] used in relation to almost all employments: you say, Daraba fiY Alt~ijaArapi (assumed tropical:) [ He travelled for the purpose of traffic ]: (TA:) and A_in~a liYfiY A^alofi dirohamK lamaDorabFA i. e. DarobFA [ Verily I have to make a journey for the sake of, or on account of, a thousand dirhems ]. (S, TA: but in my copies of the S, lY is omitted.) And Darabati AlT~ayoru , aor. as above, (tropical:) The birds went, or went away, [or migrated, ] seeking sustenance. (K, TA.) ― -b44- Daraba said of time, (assumed tropical:) It went, passed, or passed away. (K.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru mino DarabaAnihi , or, accord. to one reading, mino Darobihi , occurring in a trad., (tropical:) The time in part passed; [ the time pursued a part of its course; ] or a part of the time passed. (TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru DarabaAnahu (assumed tropical:) Fortune, or time, produced, or brought to pass, its events: (IKtt, TA:) a phrase like quDiYa mina AlqaDaA='i . (S, L, TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru mino DarabaAnihi A^ano kaAna ka*aA waka*aA (tropical:) [ Fortune, or time, brought to pass, among its events, that such and such things happened ]. (A, L, TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru bayonanaA (tropical:) Fortune, or time, separated us: (AO, A, TA:) or made a wide separation between us; syn. baE~ada . (K.) ― -b45- Also (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, long: (K, TA:) so in the saying, Daraba All~ayolu Ealayohimo (assumed tropical:) [ The night was, or became, long to them ]. (TA.) ― -b46- And Daraba A_ilayohi (assumed tropical:) It inclined to it. (TA.) [One says, yaDoribu A_ilaY Als~awaAdi (assumed tropical:) It inclines to blackness, and A_ilaY AlHumorapi to redness, &c.: often occurring in the lexicons.] -A2- DaArabahu faDarabahu , aor. of the latter : see 3. -A3- Darubato yaduhu i. q. jaAda DarobuhaA [meaning Excellent, or how excellent, is his hand, or arm, in beating, striking, smiting, or hitting! a phrase similar to ramuwto yaduhu ]. (K.) -A4- Dariba , (IKtt, A, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. DarabN , said of herbage, (tropical:) It was marred, or spoilt, by the cold: (A:) or it was smitten by the cold, (IKtt, K, TA,) and injured thereby, and by the wind. (IKtt, TA.) And Daribati AlA^aroDu , inf. n. DarabN , (assumed tropical:) The land was smitten by hoar-frost, or rime, and its herbage was nipped, or blasted, thereby: (AZ, TA:) and Duribat [in like manner] (tropical:) it (i. e. land) was smitten by hoar-frost, or rime; or had hoar-frost, or rime, fallen upon it. (S, A, TA.)

[Hence a variety of meanings and phrases here following.]

Daraba kalobahu EalaY AlS~ayodi (assumed tropical:) [ He beat, or disciplined, or trained, his dog for the purpose of the chase ]: whence the phrases Daraba Ealayohi jirowatahu and Daraba jirowapa nafosihi and Darabotu jirowatiY Eanohu [expl. voce jirowapN ]. (Z, and TA in art. jrw .)

laA tuDorabu A^akobaAdu AlA_ibili A_il~aA valaAvapi masaAjida (assumed tropical:) Camels shall not be ridden, save to three mosques: [namely, that of Mekkeh, that of El-Medeeneh, and that of El-Aksà at Jerusalem:] a trad. (TA. [See also 4 in art. Eml .])

[ Daraba bihi AlA^aroDa , lit. He smote with him, or it, the ground; meaning (assumed tropical:) he cast, threw, or flung, him, or it, upon the ground. And Daraba bisaloHihi AlA^aroDa (assumed tropical:) He cast forth his excrement, or ordure, upon the ground. ] And [hence] Daraba AlA^aroDa and AlgaAy^iTa (tropical:) He voided excrement, or ordure; (A, TA;) and so AlxalaA='a . (TA.) [ Daraba binafosihi AlA^aroDa see expl. in the latter half of this paragraph.]

(TA.) You say, Darabahu bihi [ He struck him, or it, with it ], i. e. with a sword, (A, Mgh, Msb), &c. (A, Msb.) And taDoribu fiY HadiydK baAridK [ Thou beatest upon cold iron ]: a prov. [expl. in art. Hd ]. (Har p. 633.) And Darabotu zayodFA sawoTFA , meaning bisawoTK [i. e. I struck Zeyd with a whip ], or Darobapa sawoTK [ a stroke of a whip ]: (M in art. swT , q. v.:) and Darabahu miAy^apa sawoTK [ He struck him a hundred strokes of the whip ]. (S and K in art. sHl , &c.) And Darabotu Eunuqahu [ I smote his neck, meaning I beheaded him ]; and AlA^aEonaAqa ↓ Dar~abotu [ I smote the necks, meaning I struck off the heads ]; the teshdeed denoting muchness [of the action] or multiplicity [of the objects]: AZ says that, when the object is one, the Arabs use only the former verb, without teshdeed; but when there is a plurality of objects, either of the verbs; (Msb;) [so that] one says, DarabuwA A^aEonaAqahumo [ They smote their necks, or beheaded them ], and A^amara Alr~iqaAbi ↓ bitaDoriybi [ He gave the order to smite the necks, or to strike off the heads ]: (A:) faDaroba Alr~iqaAbi in the Kur xlvii. 4 is originally faA@DoribuwA Alr~iqaAba DarobFA [meaning Then do ye smite the necks, i. e. strike off the heads ]; (Bd;) the inf. n. being here put for its verb. (Jel.) [Respecting the phrase huwa A@loyaDoribuka , see 1 in art. jdE .] ― -b2- [Hence a variety of meanings and phrases here following.] ― -b3- Daraba kalobahu EalaY AlS~ayodi (assumed tropical:) [ He beat, or disciplined, or trained, his dog for the purpose of the chase ]: whence the phrases Daraba Ealayohi jirowatahu and Daraba jirowapa nafosihi and Darabotu jirowatiY Eanohu [expl. voce jirowapN ]. (Z, and TA in art. jrw .) ― -b4- laA tuDorabu A^akobaAdu AlA_ibili A_il~aA valaAvapi masaAjida (assumed tropical:) Camels shall not be ridden, save to three mosques: [namely, that of Mekkeh, that of El-Medeeneh, and that of El-Aksà at Jerusalem:] a trad. (TA. [See also 4 in art. Eml .]) ― -b5- [ Daraba bihi AlA^aroDa , lit. He smote with him, or it, the ground; meaning (assumed tropical:) he cast, threw, or flung, him, or it, upon the ground. And Daraba bisaloHihi AlA^aroDa (assumed tropical:) He cast forth his excrement, or ordure, upon the ground. ] And [hence] Daraba AlA^aroDa and AlgaAy^iTa (tropical:) He voided excrement, or ordure; (A, TA;) and so AlxalaA='a . (TA.) [ Daraba binafosihi AlA^aroDa see expl. in the latter half of this paragraph.] ― -b6- Darabotu Alqawosa biAlmiDorabi I struck the string of the bow with the wooden implement [or mallet ] used in separating cotton. (Msb.) ― -b7- Daraba AlEuwda [ He struck the chords of the lute; meaning he played upon the lute; and so Daraba biAlEuwdi ]. (S.) ― -b8- Daraba Alwatida , aor. and inf. n. as above, He beat [or knocked or struck ] the tent-peg, or stake, so that it became firm in the ground. (Lh, TA.) And [hence] Daraba Alxayomapa (tropical:) He pitched the tent, by knocking in its pegs with a mallet: (Kull p. 231:) or he set up the tent. (Msb.) ― -b9- Daraba Ald~irohama , aor. and inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He struck, coined, or minted, the dirhem, or piece of money. (TA.) And Daraba EalaY A@smihi (assumed tropical:) [ He struck, coined, or minted, money in his name ]. (ISd, TA in art. jwz .) ― -b10- Daraba EalaY Almakotuwbi (tropical:) He sealed, or stamped, the writing. (A, * TA.) [And Daraba Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He erased it; namely, anything written.] ― -b11- Daraba AlT~iyna EalaY AljidaAri (assumed tropical:) [ He stuck, or applied, the mud upon the wall, as a plaster]. (TA.) ― -b12- Hence, accord. to some, the phrase Duribato Ealayohimu A@l*~il~apu , in the Kur ii. 58, considered as meaning (assumed tropical:) Vileness was made to cleave to them: or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) encompassed them, like as the tent encompasses him over whom it is pitched. (Ksh, Bd.) And [in like manner] one says, Duribato Ealayohimu DariybapN (tropical:) An impost, of the tax called jizoyap , &c., was imposed upon them. (A, * Mgh, Msb. *) And Daraba EalaY AlEabodi AlA^itaAwapa (tropical:) He imposed upon the slave the tax according to a fixed time. (TA. [See DirybapN .]) And Durba Ealayohimu AlbaEovu (assumed tropical:) The being sent to the war was appointed them and imposed upon them as an obligation. (Mgh in art. bEv .) ― -b13- Daraba Al$~abakapa EalaY AlT~aAy^iri (assumed tropical:) He cast the net over the bird: (Mgh:) and Duriba Alfax~u EalaY AlT~aAy^iri (tropical:) [ The snare was cast over the bird ]. (A, TA.) ― -b14- Daraba All~ayolu biA^aruwaAqihi (assumed tropical:) [ The night cast its folds of darkness; ] meaning the night came. (TA.) [And (assumed tropical:) The night became dark, or was dark; as appears from the following verse.] Homeyd says, saraY mivola naboDi AlEiroqi waAll~ayolu DaAribN biA^rowaAqihi waAlS~uboHu qado kaAda yasoTaEu (assumed tropical:) [ He went on in his night-journey, like the pulsing of the vein, while the night was casting its folds of darkness over the earth, and the dawn had almost risen ]. (TA. [See also DaAribN .]) You say also, Daraba Ealayohi HijaAbFA (assumed tropical:) [ He put, or let down, a veil, or curtain, or covering, over him, or it ]. (TA.) And Duriba bayonahumaA sad~N (assumed tropical:) [ A barrier was set between them two ]. (A in art. sd .) DarabonaA EalaY A=*aAnihimo [in the Kur xviii. 10] means (tropical:) We prevented their sleeping; (K, TA;) as though by putting a covering over their ears; a metonymical [and elliptical] mode of saying we made them to sleep by preventing any sound from penetrating into their ears, in consequence of which they would have awoke: (Zj, L, TA:) or Daraba EalaY A=*aAnihimo means (assumed tropical:) he poured upon them sleep so that they slept and did not awake: and one says also, Darabotu Aln~awoma EalaY A^u*unihi [meaning (assumed tropical:) I poured sleep upon him by closing his ear ]. (Msb.) ― -b15- Darabati , AlEaqorabu , (A, K, * TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The scorpion stung. (A, K, * TA.) ― -b16- [ Darabatohu Alr~iyHu (assumed tropical:) The wind beat it, or blew upon it; namely, herbage, and water, &c.] And Darabahu Albarodu (IKtt, K, TA) (assumed tropical:) The cold smote it so as to injure it; namely, herbage; and in like manner one says of the wind: (IKtt, TA:) and ↓ ADrbhu Albarodu (A, TA) (tropical:) The cold smote it by its vehemence, so that it dried up; and in like manner one says of the wind: (TA:) and AlD~ariybu AlA^aroDa ↓ ADrb (assumed tropical:) The hoar-frost, or rime, fell upon the land, so that its herbage became nipped, or blasted. (AZ, TA. [See also Dariba .]) And Duriba bibaliy~apK (assumed tropical:) He was smitten with a trial, or an affliction. (L, TA.) ― -b17- Tariyqu mak~apa maA DarabahaA AlEaAma qaTorapN (tropical:) [ The road to Mekkeh, not a drop of rain has fallen upon it this year ]. (A, TA.) ― -b18- Daraba AlfaHolu Aln~aAqapa , (S, A, * Msb, K, * TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. DiraAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and DarobN also, accord. to Fr, but this latter, though agreeable with analogy, is disallowed by Sb and Akh, (TA,) (tropical:) The stallion leaped the she-camel; (Msb, TA;) i. e. (TA,) compressed (A, K, TA) her. (TA.) DiraAbu Aljamali is used elliptically for vamanu DiraAbi Aljamali (tropical:) The hire of the camel's leaping the female: the taking of which, as also the taking of the hire of any stallion for covering, is forbidden in a trad. (TA.) ― -b19- Daraba Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i (tropical:) He mixed the [one] thing with the [other] thing; (A, K;) as also ↓ Dr~bhu , (K,) inf. n. taDoriybN : (TA:) accord. to some, said peculiarly in relation to milk; (MF, TA;) but [SM says,] this I have not found in any lexicon. (TA.) Daraba All~abana fiY Als~iqaA='i means (tropical:) Haqanahu [i. e. He collected the milk in the skin, and poured fresh milk upon that which was curdled, or thick, or upon that which was churned; or he poured the milk into the skin, and kept it therein that its butter might come forth ]. (A.) In the L and other lexicons it is said that Darabotu bayonahumo fiY Al$~ar~i means I caused them to become confused [or I involved them ] in evil or mischief. (TA. [And Dr~bt bayonahumo has a similar meaning: see 2.]) And Durbati Al$~aApu bilawoni ka*aA means The sheep, or goat, was intermixed with such a colour. (L, TA.) ― -b20- Daraba Al$~ajaru biEuruwqihi fiY AlA^aroDi [ The trees struck their roots into the earth ]. (A and TA in art. Erq .) ― -b21- [Hence, the saying,] Darabato fiyhi fulaAnapu biEiroqK *iY A^a$abK i. e. AilotibaAs ; (S and TA in the present art., and in like manner, in both, in art. A$b , with the addition of *iY before AilotibaAsK ;) (tropical:) [app. meaning Such a woman implanted, or engendered, in him a strain, i. e. a radical, or hereditary, quality, of a dubious kind: or the pronoun in fyh relates to a family, or people; for it is said that] the meaning is, such a woman corrupted their race by her bringing forth among them: or, as some say, Erqt fiyhimo Eiroqa sawo'K [i. e. Ear~aqato , or, accord. to more common usage, A^aEoraqato , i. e., implanted, or engendered, among them, or in them, an evil strain, or radical or hereditary disposition ]. (TA. [This saying is also mentioned in the A, as tropical, but is not expl. therein.]) ― -b22- Daraba biAlqidaAHi , (S, Mgh, K,) and Daraba AlqidaAHa , (A, TA,) (tropical:) He turned about, or shuffled, ( A^ajaAla ,) the arrows, [ in the ribaAbap (q. v.), in the game called Almuyosir ,] EalaY Aljazwri [ for the slaughtered camel ]. (Mgh. [See HuroDapN .]) [And (assumed tropical:) He played with the gamingarrows; practised sortilege with arrows, or with the arrows. ] You say, Darabotu maEa Alqawomi bisahomK (assumed tropical:) I practised sortilege with the people, or party, with an arrow; syn. saAhamotuhumo . (Msb.) And Daraba biAlqidoHayoni (assumed tropical:) He practised sortilege with the two arrows; one of which was inscribed with the sentence “ My Lord hath commanded me, ” and the other with “ My Lord hath forbidden me: ” a person between hope and despair is likened to one practising this mode of sortilege, which was used by the people of the Time of Ignorance when they doubted whether they should undertake an affair or abstain from it. (Har pp. 465 and 553.) One says also, Daraba fiY AljazuwribisahomK meaning (assumed tropical:) He obtained a share, or portion, of the slaughtered camel. (Mgh.) And hence the saying of El-Hareeree, waDarabotu fiY maroEaAhaA binaSiybK (assumed tropical:) [ And I obtained a share of its pasture ]. (Mgh.) And the lawyers say, yaDoribu fiyhi biAlv~uluvi i. e. (assumed tropical:) He shall take thereof somewhat, according to what is due to him, of the third part. (Mgh.) They say also, Daraba fiY maAlihi sahomFA i. e. (assumed tropical:) He assigned [ a share, or portion, of his property ]: and thus is expl. the saying of Aboo-Haneefeh, laA yaDoribu lilomuwSaY lahu fiymaA zaAda EalaY Alv~uluvi (assumed tropical:) He shall not assign, or give, to the legatee, aught of more than the third part; the true objective complement being suppressed. (Mgh.) ― -b23- Daraba biyadayohi [lit. He beat with his arms; meaning (assumed tropical:) he moved his arms about, or to and fro; brandished, tossed, or swung them ]: you say, Daraba biyadayohi waHar~akahumaA fiY mi$oyatihi (assumed tropical:) [ He swung his arms, and moved them about, in his manner of walking ]. (TA in art. jdf . [See jadafa .]) And Daraba fiY AlmaA='i [ biyadayohi being understood after the verb] (assumed tropical:) He swam. (K.) ― -b24- Daraba biyadihi A_ilaY $aYo'K (assumed tropical:) He made a sign, or pointed, with his hand, towards a thing. (TA.) And Daraba [alone] (assumed tropical:) He made a sign, or pointed. (K.) And Daraba biyadihi A_ilaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He put forth his hand towards such a thing, to take it, or to point, or make a sign. (TA.) And Daraba yadahu A_ilaY Eamali ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ He applied his hand to the doing of such a thing ]. (Lth, TA.) [And Daraba yadayohi fiY AlmaAli a phrase expl. to me by IbrD as meaning (assumed tropical:) He busied his hands with the property, in the giving, or dispensing of it.] ― -b25- Daraba EalaY yadihi (assumed tropical:) [ He struck his (i. e. another man's) hand; meaning] he struck, or made, the bargain with him; or ratified the sale with him: for it is a custom, when two persons are bargaining together, for one of them to put his hand upon the other's in ratifying the bargain. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b26- And (tropical:) He prohibited, or prevented, or hindered, him, from doing a thing, or from doing a thing that he had begun: (TA:) and [in like manner] Daraba EalaY yadayohi (tropical:) he withheld, or restrained, him, or it. (K, TA.) And (i. e. the former phrase) (tropical:) He (the judge, A, Mgh, TA) prohibited, or interdicted, him from the using, or disposing of, his property according to his own free will. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, TA.) ― -b27- Also (tropical:) He corrupted, vitiated, marred, or disordered, his affair, or case, or state. (A, Msb, TA.) ― -b28- Daraba Eanohu (assumed tropical:) He turned away a person or thing from him [or it ]; as also ↓ ADrb : (TA:) [or] Enh ↓ ADrb signifies, (S, Msb,) or signifies also, (TA,) and (Msb, TA) so does Daraba Enh , (Msb, K, TA,) [the latter app. for Daraba nafosahu Eanohu ,] (assumed tropical:) He turned away from, avoided, shunned, or left, him, or it; (S * Msb, K * TA; *) namely, a person, (TA,) or a thing. (Msb.) A^afanaDoribu Eanokumu A@l*~ikora SafoHFA , in the Kur [xliii. 4], is said to mean (assumed tropical:) Shall we then neglect you, and not teach you what is incumbent on you? the phrase being taken from a rider's striking his beast with his stick when he desires to turn him from the course that he is pursuing: or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) shall we then turn away the Kur-án from you, and not invite you thereby to the faith, turning away ourselves from you? (TA.) One says also, Darabotu Eanohu SafoHFA meaning (assumed tropical:) I turned away from him and left him. (S and TA in art. SfH : see 1 in that art.) See also the saying Daraba A^axomaAsahu fiY A^asodaAsihi voce xumusN . ― -b29- And fulaAnN yaDoribu A^axomaAsFA liA^asodaAsK : see voce ximosN . ― -b30- Daraba binafosihi AlA^aroDa , (K,) inf. n. DarobN , (TA,) [lit. He smote with himself the ground; and hence, (assumed tropical:) he cast, threw, or flung, himself upon the ground; app. often used in this sense; (a phrase similar to Daraba bihi AlA^aroDa expl. before;) and hence,] (assumed tropical:) he remained, stayed, or abode; (K;) and so ↓ ADrb (AZ, ISk, S, K, TA) as used in the phrase ADrb Alr~ajulu fiY Albayoti (tropical:) The man remained, stayed, or abode, in the tent, or house, (AZ, ISk, S, A, TA,) not quitting it: (ISk, A, TA:) and [in like manner] Daraba b*anabihi , [ AlA^aroDa being understood,] (assumed tropical:) He stayed, or abode, and remained fixed. (K in art. *nb . [See also other explanations of this last phrase in a later part of this paragraph.]) And Daraba Alwatida bimaHal~i ka*aA (tropical:) He remained, stayed, or abode, [lit., struck the tent-peg, ] in such a place of alighting. (A.) And Darabati AlA_ibilu biEaTanK , [ AlA^aroDa being understood after AlAbl ,] (assumed tropical:) The camels lay down [ in a place by the water ]: (S in art. ETn :) or satisfied themselves with drinking and then lay down around the water or by the watering-troughs, to be brought again to drink another time: (IAth, TA in that art.:) and [hence,] Daraba Aln~aAsu biEaTanK , occurring in a trad., (assumed tropical:) The people's camels satisfied themselves with drinking until they lay down and remained in their place [ at the water ]: (TA in the present art.:) or the people satisfied their thirst and then abode at the water. (K in art. ETn .) ― -b31- Daraba bi*aqanihi AlA^aroDa (tropical:) He was cowardly; and feared; (A, O,* K, TA;) and clave to the ground: (O, TA:) or he was, or became, affected with shame, shyness, or bashfulness. (A, TA.) ― -b32- yaDoribu lahu AlA^aroDa kul~ahaA [lit. He beats for it the whole land, i. e. in journeying,] means (assumed tropical:) he seeks it through the whole land: so says AZ in explanation of the phrase here following. (O, TA.) yaDoribu Almajoda (assumed tropical:) He seeks to gain, or obtain, glory: (O, K:) or he applies himself with art and diligence to gain glory, ( yakotasibuhu ,) and seeks it through the whole land. (AZ, TA. [See also 8.]) ― -b34- Daraba All~abina , (A,) or All~ibona , (tropical:) He made [or moulded ] bricks. (MA.) And Daraba AlxaAtama (tropical:) He made, fashioned, or moulded, the signet-ring. (TA.) [Hence one says,] AiDoribohu EalaY TaboEi h`*aA i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Make thou it, fashion it, or mould it, ] according to the model, make, fashion, or mould, of this. (IAar, O and K in art. TbE .) And h`*ihi Dariybatuhu Al~atiY Duriba EalayohaA , and DuribahaA , and Duriba alone, [for Duriba EalayohaA ,] meaning TubiEa [i. e. (assumed tropical:) This is his nature, with an adaptation, or a disposition, to which he was moulded, or created; or to which he was adapted, or disposed, by creation ]. (Lh, TA.) And Duriba fulaAnN EalaY Alkarami (tropical:) [ Such a one was moulded, or created, with an adaptation or a disposition, to generosity; or was adapted, or disposed, by creation, or nature, to generosity ]. (A.) ― -b35- Daraba mavalFA (S, A, O, &c.) (tropical:) He rehearsed, propounded, or declared, a parable, a similitude, an example, or a proverb; said of God [and of a man]: (S, * O, * Msb, TA:) or he mentioned, or set forth, a parable, &c.: or he framed a parable: thus expl., the verb has but one objective complement: or the phrase signifies he made [such a thing] an example, or the subject of a parable or similitude &c.; and so has two objective complements: in the saying in the Kur [xxxvi. 12] waA@Doribo lahumo mavalFA A^aSoHaAba A@loqaroyapi (assumed tropical:) [ And propound thou to them a parable, the people of the town ] i. e., the story of the people of the town, [or make thou to them a parable, or similitude, or an example, the people of the town; ] mvlA may be in the accus. case as an objective complement, ADHAb Alqryp being a substitute for mvlA ; or ASHAb Alqryp may be regarded as a second objective complement [i. e. second in the order of the words, but first in the order of the sense]: the phrase is differently expl. on account of the different meanings of the verb Daraba ; which signifies he described, or rehearsed; and he declared, propounded, or explained; and he made, caused to be, or constituted; &c.; accord. to some, it is taken from the phrase Daraba Aldirohama [q. v.]; because of the impression which a parable or the like makes upon the mind: accord. to some, from DariybN signifying “ a like; ” because the first thing is made like the second: accord. to some, from Daraba AlT~iyna EalaY AljidaAri [q. v.; because the mud, applied as a plaster, conforms to the shape of the wall]: and accord. to some, from Daraba AlxaAtama [q. v.]; because of the correspondence between a parable or the like and the object to which it is applied, and the correspondence between the signet and its impression. (TA, from the M and L &c.) yaDoribu A@ll~`hu A@loHaq~a waA@lobATila , in the Kur [xiii. 18], means (assumed tropical:) God likeneth, or compareth, truth and falsity. (TA.) One says also, Daraba bihi mavalFA (assumed tropical:) [ He made him, or it, a subject of a parable, a similitude, an example, or a proverb; he propounded, or framed, a parable, &c., respecting him, or it ]. (TA.) And yuDorabu Almavalu lika*aA [ The proverb, &c., is applied to, in relation to, or to the case of, such a thing ]. (Meyd &c., passim.) ― -b36- Daraba lahu A^ajalFA (assumed tropical:) He specified, or notified, to, or for, him, or it, a term, or period. (Mgh, Msb. *) ― -b37- Daraba lahumo TariyqFA (assumed tropical:) He assigned to them, or made for them, a way; syn. jaEala . (MA. [App. from a phrase in the Kur xx. 79, q. v.]) ― -b38- AlD~arobu as a conventional term of the accountants, or arithmeticians, means The multiplying a number by another number; (Mgh, Msb;) as when you say, [ Daraba xamospF fiY sit~apK He multiplied five by six; and] xamosapN fiY sit~apK bivalaAviyna [ Five multiplied by six is thirty ]. (Msb.) ― -b39- Daraba [is often intrans., and thus] signifies also taHar~aka [i. e. (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, in a state of commotion, &c.]: (K:) [see also 8, which is more commonly used in this sense:] or, so with strength, or force. (TA.) [And hence several phrases here following.] ― -b40- Daraba AlEiroqu (A, TA,) inf. n. DarobN and DarabaAnN , (TA,) (tropical:) The vein pulsed, or beat, (A, TA,) and throbbed: (TA:) and Daraba , inf. n. DarabaAnN , (tropical:) it (the vein) pained, and was, or became, in a state of strong commotion. (TA.) And Daraba AljuroHu , inf. n. DarabaAnN , (S, A, Msb,) (tropical:) The wound [ throbbed; or] pained violently: (A, Msb:) and so AlDirosu (tropical:) [ the tooth ]. (A, TA.) ― -b41- Darabati Aln~aAqapu , (A, K,) or, as in some lexicons, AlmaxaADu , (TA,) (tropical:) The she-camel, (A, K,) or the pregnant camel, (TA,) raised her tail, and smote her vulva with it, (A, K, TA,) and then went along. (K, TA.) ― -b42- Daraba fiY jahaAzihi (tropical:) He (a camel) took fright, and ran away at random, (S, A, L, TA,) and ceased not to gallop and leap until he had thrown off all his furniture, or load. (L, TA.) ― -b43- jaA='a yaDoribu bi$ar~K (tropical:) He came hastening [ with mischief, or] in an evil affair. (A.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, When such and such things shall happen, (mentioning faction, or sedition, or the like,) Daraba yaEosuwbu Ald~iyni bi*anabihi , meaning, accord. to AM, (assumed tropical:) The leader of the religion shall hasten to go away through the land, fleeing from the faction, or sedition: or, as some say, shall go away hastily through the land, with his followers. (O, TA. [But see yaEosuwbN : and see also *anabN .]) And you say also, Darabotu fiYAls~ayori , (Msb,) inf. n. DarobN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) I hastened in journeying. (S, * Msb.) And Daraba fiY AlA^aroDi , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. DarobN (S, K, TA) and maDorabN (S, TA) and DarabaAnN , (K, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He journeyed in the land (S, Mgh, Msb) seeking sustenance, (S,) and for the purpose of traffic: (Mgh:) [and Daraba AlA^aroDa , as shown above, has a similar meaning:] or (tropical:) he went forth in the land as a merchant; (A, K;) or warring and plundering, (K,) or so Daraba fiY sabiyli A@ll~`hi [meaning in the cause of God ]: (A:) or he hastened through the land: (A, K:) or he arose, and hastened in his journey through the land: (TA:) or he went, or went away, in the land: (A, K:) or he traversed, or journeyed through, the land. (TA.) The verb is [similarly] used in relation to almost all employments: you say, Daraba fiY Alt~ijaArapi (assumed tropical:) [ He travelled for the purpose of traffic ]: (TA:) and A_in~a liYfiY A^alofi dirohamK lamaDorabFA i. e. DarobFA [ Verily I have to make a journey for the sake of, or on account of, a thousand dirhems ]. (S, TA: but in my copies of the S, lY is omitted.) And Darabati AlT~ayoru , aor. as above, (tropical:) The birds went, or went away, [or migrated, ] seeking sustenance. (K, TA.) ― -b44- Daraba said of time, (assumed tropical:) It went, passed, or passed away. (K.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru mino DarabaAnihi , or, accord. to one reading, mino Darobihi , occurring in a trad., (tropical:) The time in part passed; [ the time pursued a part of its course; ] or a part of the time passed. (TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru DarabaAnahu (assumed tropical:) Fortune, or time, produced, or brought to pass, its events: (IKtt, TA:) a phrase like quDiYa mina AlqaDaA='i . (S, L, TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru mino DarabaAnihi A^ano kaAna ka*aA waka*aA (tropical:) [ Fortune, or time, brought to pass, among its events, that such and such things happened ]. (A, L, TA.) And Daraba Ald~ahoru bayonanaA (tropical:) Fortune, or time, separated us: (AO, A, TA:) or made a wide separation between us; syn. baE~ada . (K.) ― -b45- Also (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, long: (K, TA:) so in the saying, Daraba All~ayolu Ealayohimo (assumed tropical:) [ The night was, or became, long to them ]. (TA.) ― -b46- And Daraba A_ilayohi (assumed tropical:) It inclined to it. (TA.) [One says, yaDoribu A_ilaY Als~awaAdi (assumed tropical:) It inclines to blackness, and A_ilaY AlHumorapi to redness, &c.: often occurring in the lexicons.] -A2- DaArabahu faDarabahu , aor. of the latter : see 3. -A3- Darubato yaduhu i. q. jaAda DarobuhaA [meaning Excellent, or how excellent, is his hand, or arm, in beating, striking, smiting, or hitting! a phrase similar to ramuwto yaduhu ]. (K.) -A4- Dariba , (IKtt, A, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. DarabN , said of herbage, (tropical:) It was marred, or spoilt, by the cold: (A:) or it was smitten by the cold, (IKtt, K, TA,) and injured thereby, and by the wind. (IKtt, TA.) And Daribati AlA^aroDu , inf. n. DarabN , (assumed tropical:) The land was smitten by hoar-frost, or rime, and its herbage was nipped, or blasted, thereby: (AZ, TA:) and Duribat [in like manner] (tropical:) it (i. e. land) was smitten by hoar-frost, or rime; or had hoar-frost, or rime, fallen upon it. (S, A, TA.)

(S, TA.) One says, ↓ DArbhu faDarabahu , aor. of the latter verb , (K, TA,) agreeably with the general rule respecting verbs signifying the surpassing, or overcoming, in a contest, (MF, TA,) He contended with him in beating, &c., and he surpassed him, or overcame him, therein. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ maDoruwbN [ Beaten, struck, &c.]. (K, TA.) ― -b2- A tent-peg, or stake, struck so as to be firm in the ground; as also ↓ maDoruwbN . (Lh, TA.) ― -b3- See also DarobN , in three places. ― -b4- Also, (As, ISd, K, TA,) or Dariybu Al$~awoli , accord. to Aboo-Nasr, (assumed tropical:) Milk of which some is milked upon other: or, accord. to some of the Arabs of the desert, milk from a number of camels, some of it being thin, and some of it thick: (S:) or milk of which some is poured upon other: (As, TA:) or such as is milked from a number of camels (ISd, K, TA) into one vessel, and mixed together, not consisting of less than the milk of three camels: (ISd, TA:) or milk upon which other has been milked at night, and other on the morrow, and which has been mixed together. (TA.) [See also SariybN .] ― -b5- And What is bad, of the kind of plants called HamoD : or what is broken in pieces, thereof. (K.) -A2- See also miDorabN . ― -b2- [Hence,] (tropical:) The person who is intrusted, as deputy, with [ the disposal of ] the gaming-arrows [ in the game called Almayosir ]: or the person who shuffles those arrows, or who plays with them; ( Aal~a*iY yaDoribu biAlqidaAHi ;) as also ↓ DaAribN : (K:) or both of these epithets signify the person who shuffles those arrows ( Aal~a*iY yaDoribu biAlqidaAHi ); and he is the person who is intrusted, as deputy, with [ the disposal of ] them: (S:) the former is of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure faAEilN : (Sb, TA:) and the pl. is DurabaA='u . (S, A.) You say, huwaDariybiY , meaning (tropical:) He is my playfellow with the gamingarrows ( mino yaDoribu AlqidaAHa maEiY ). (A, TA.) ― -b3- And AlD~ariybu is a name of (assumed tropical:) The third arrow of those used in the game called Almayosir : (K, * TA:) that arrow is thus called by some: by others Alr~aqiybu [q. v.]: it has three notches; and three portions are assigned to it if successful, and three fines if unsuccessful. (Lh, L, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence, app.,] DariybN signifies also (assumed tropical:) A share, or portion. (K.) ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) Hoar-frost, or rime; (S, K;) like jaliydN and saqiyTN : (S in art. jld :) and (assumed tropical:) snow. (K.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The head: (K:) so called because often in a state of agitation. (TA.) -A3- And i. q. $ahodN [i. e. honey, or honey in its comb, or honey not expressed from its comb ]: and EasalN DariybN honey becoming, or become, white and thick. (TA. [See also DarabN .]) -A4- Also Big-bellied, ( baTiynN , [in some copies of the K baTon ,]) [as an epithet] of men, (K, TA,) and of others. (TA.)

definition: A man, (K,) or anything, (T, S, * TA,) living or dead, (T, TA,) struck, or smitten, with the sword: (T, S, K, TA:) the p is affixed, though the word has the meaning of a pass.
sourceDefinition: A man, (K,) or anything, (T, S, * TA,) living or dead, (T, TA,) struck, or smitten, with the sword: (T, S, K, TA:) the p is affixed, though the word has the meaning of a pass. part. n., because it becomes numbered with substs., like naTiyHapN and A^akiylapN . (S.) ― -b2- [And also] The place [or part ] upon which the blow, or stroke, falls, of the body that is beaten, or struck. (Ham p. 129.) ― -b3- And Wool, or [ goats' ] hair, separated, or plucked asunder, with the fingers, and then folded together, and bound with a thread, and spun: (S: [more fully expl. voce saliylapN :]) and wool that is beaten with a mallet: (TA:) or a portion of wool: (K:) or a portion of cotton, and of wool: (TA:) pl. DaraAy^ibu . (S.) ― -b4- Also (tropical:) An impost that is levied, of the poll-tax or land-tax and the like, (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) and of [ the tolls, or similar exactions, termed ] A^aroSaAd : (S, O, TA:) pl. as above. (S, A, Mgh, &c.) And (hence, TA) (tropical:) The gal~ap [as meaning the income, or revenue, arising from the service ] of a slave; (S, K, TA;) i. e. Dariybapu AlEabodi means what the slave pays to his master, of the impost that is laid upon him: DariybapN being of the measure faEiylapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN . (TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) A nature; or a natural, a native, or an innate, disposition or temper or the like: [as though signifying a particular cast of constitution, moulded by the Creator: ] syn. TabiyEapN , (S, A, K,) and sajiy~apN : (S:) pl. as above. (A, TA.) You say, fulaAnN kariymu AlD~ariybapi [(tropical:) Such a one is generous in respect of nature ]; and lay^iymu AlD~ariybapi [(tropical:) mean &c.]; (S;) and A_in~ahu lakariymu AlD~araAy^ibi [(tropical:) Verily he is generous in respect of natural dispositions ]: and xuliqa Aln~aAsu EalaY DaraAy^iba $at~aY [ Men are created of diverse natures &c.]. (TA.) ― -b6- See also maDoribN .

definition: [ Beating, striking, smiting, or hitting: &c.
sourceDefinition: [ Beating, striking, smiting, or hitting: &c.:] act. part. n. of Daraba [in all its senses]. (K, TA.) ― -b2- A she-camel that strikes her milker: (S, K:). or one which, having been submissive, or tractable, before conceiving, afterwards strikes her milker away from before her: or [the pl.] DawaAribu signifies she-camels that resist after conceiving, and become repugnant, so that one cannot milk them. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, and DaAribapN , (K, TA,) the former a possessive epithet [i. e. denoting the possession of a quality], and the latter a verbal epithet [i. e. an act. part. n.], (TA,) (tropical:) A she-camel that raises her tail, and smites with it her vulva, (K, A, in which latter only the pl. is mentioned,) and then goes: (K:) pl. DawaAribu . (A, TA.) And the former is like tDrAb , [i. e. ↓ tiDoraAbN , as appears from what follows,] expl. by Lh as meaning (assumed tropical:) A she-camel that has been covered by the stallion, [ and app. that raises her tail in consequence thereof, ] but respecting which one knows not whether she be pregnant or not: (TA:) or ↓ tiDoraAbN signifies a she-camel recently covered by the stallion [ and therefore often raising her tail ]. (Mz, 40th nwE .) ― -b4- The former ( DaAribN ) signifies also (assumed tropical:) Swimming, (S, TA,) in water. (TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, layaAliYa All~ahowi yaTobiyniY faA^atobaEuhu kaA^an~aniY DaAribN fiY gamorapK laEibu [ In the nights of diversion he calls me and I follow him as though I were swimming in a deep water, sporting therein]. (S, TA.) ― -b5- TayorN DawaAribu (tropical:) Birds seeking sustenance: (S, A, TA:) or birds traversing the land, [or migrating, ] in search of sustenance. (L, TA.) ― -b6- See also DariybN . ― -b7- DaAribN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A dark night: (K:) or a night of which the darkness extends to the right and left, and fills the world. (S, O. [So in my copies of the S and in the O and TA: but accord. to Golius, as from the S, “ yet not filling the air. ”]) See the verse of Homeyd cited in the first paragraph. [J cites as an ex. of the last of the meanings expl. above, and so does Sgh in the O, the verse in the sentence here next following.] ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) Anything long: applied in this sense to a night: thus in the following verse: waraAbaEatoniY taHota layolK DaAribi bisaAEidK faEomK wakaf~K xaADibi (assumed tropical:) [ And that she helped me in lifting and putting on the loads, beneath the darkness of a long night, with a plump fore arm and a hand dyed with hinnà ]. (TA.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) A place, (S,) or a depressed place, (K, TA,) and a valley, (TA,) in which are trees. (S, K, TA.) (KL.) ― -b3- maDoribu AlZ~aribaAni means (assumed tropical:) The line, or long mark, upon the face of the animal called ZrbAn [as though it were a place upon which it had been struck]. (TA in art. Zrb , q. v.) ― -b4- And maDoribN , (assumed tropical:) A place where a tent is pitched, or set up. (Msb.) ― -b5- See also miDorabN . ― -b6- Also, (thus in the TA in art. swf , as from the A,) or ↓ maDorabN , (thus in a copy of the A in the present art.,) (tropical:) i. q. masaAfapN [meaning A space, or tract, or an extent, over which one journeys; as being a place of beating the ground]: so in the saying, baEiydN ↓ bayonahumo maDorabN [or maDoribN , i. e. (tropical:) Between them is a far-extending space to be traversed ]. (A.) ― -b7- [ maDoribu EasalapK is a euphemism for (assumed tropical:) The place of injection of sperma: and hence it means (assumed tropical:) the source from which one springs; origin, ancestry, or parentage; &c.] One says, maA A^aEorifu lahu maDoriba EasalapK (S, A) meaning A^aEoraAqahu [i. e. (tropical:) I know not the sources (or the source ) from which he has sprung; or his ancestry, or parentage ]: (S:) or maA yuEorafu lahu maDoribu EasalapK (tropical:) No source or origin [or parentage ], nor people, nor ancestor or father, nor nobility, pertaining to him, is know. (M, K, TA.) And maA lifulaAnK maDoribu EasalapK (S, A, in the latter lizayodK ,) i. e. (tropical:) [ Such a one has no source ] of kindred ( nasab ), nor of cattle or property ( maAl ). (S.) [See also DariybapN .] ― -b8- One says also, A^atati Aln~aAqapu EalaY maDoribihaA , meaning (assumed tropical:) The she-camel arrived at the time [ of year ] of her being leaped by the stallion; making the time to be like the place. (S.) ― -b9- maDoribN , (S, A, O, and so in the M in art. rm ,) or ↓ maDorabN , (K, * TA,) with fet-h to the m , (K, TA,) and to the r also, (TA,) [but this is app. a mistake, as the weight of authority is in favour of the former,] (assumed tropical:) A bone in which is marrow: (S, O, K:) or a bone that is broken and from which marrow is extracted [or sought to be extracted ]. (M in art. rm .) (Ham ubi suprà.) ― -b11- [ maDoribu mavalK means (assumed tropical:) The secondary idea, or thing, signified by a parable or proverb, and compared to the primary idea, or thing; the thing, or case, to which a parable or proverb is applied: correlative of maworidu mavalK : pl. maDaAribu .] ― -b12- And [the pl.] maDaAribu signifies (assumed tropical:) Stratagems in war. sourceDefinition: signifies The beating [a thing], or striking [it, in any manner, and with anything]; (K, TA;) this being the primary meaning: (TA:) or with the miToraqap , (K, TA,) which is the implement of the blacksmith and of the artificer [with which he beats the iron], and the rod, or stick, with which one beats wool [or hair] to loosen or separate it: (TA:) and the slapping (K, TA) with the hand. (TA.) You say, Taraqa AlbaAba , aor. , inf. n. TaroqN , He knocked [or (as we say) knocked at ] the door. (Msb.) Taraqa AlS~uwfa , (S, O, TA, *) or Al$~aEara , (TA,) aor. as above, (S, O,) and so the inf. n., (S, O, K,) He beat the wool, (S, O, K, TA,) or the hair, (TA,) with the rod, or stick, called miToraqap , (S, O,) to loosen it, or separate it: (S, * O, * TA:) or he plucked it [ so as to loosen it, or separate it ]. (K, TA.) AuToruqiY wamiy$iY , a prov., and occurring in a verse of Ru-beh, [originally addressed to a woman,] and [lit.] meaning Beat thou the wool with the stick, and mix the hair with the wool, is said to him who confuses or confounds, in his speech, and practises various modes, or manners, therein. (Az, TA. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 28.]) And you say also, Taraqa AlHadiydapa He beat the piece of iron [ with the miToraqap ]: (Mgh, * Msb:) and ↓ Tr~qhA he beat it much, or vehemently. (Msb.) And Taraqahu bikaf~ihi , inf. n. as above, He slapped him with his hand. (TA.) And Taraqotu AlT~ariyqa I travelled [or beat ] the road. (Msb.) [And hence, app.,] TaroqN signifies also The being quick of pace; [probably as an inf. n.;] or quickness of going along. (Sh, TA.) And Turiqati AlA^aroDu The ground was beaten so as to be rendered even, or easy to be travelled; and trodden with the feet. (TA.) And Taraqa Ald~awaAb~u AlmaA='a biAlr~ijoli Hat~aY tukad~irahu [ The beasts beat the water with the foot so as to render it turbid, or muddy ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or Taraqati AlA_ibilu AlmaA='a , (S, O, TA,) aor. as above, (O,) (tropical:) the camels staled and dunged in the water. (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) The coming by night; (K, TA;) because he who comes by night [generally] needs to knock at the door; as some say; (TA;) and so TuruwqN [which is the more common in this sense]. (K, TA.) You say, Taraqa , aor. , inf. n. TuruwqN , He came by night. (S.) A^ataAnaA fulaAnN TuruwqFA (assumed tropical:) Such a one came to us by night. (S.) And Taraqa Alqawoma , aor. , inf. n. TaroqN and TuruwqN , (assumed tropical:) He came to the people, or party, by night. (TA.) And Taraqa A^aholahu , (TA,) or Taraqa A^aholahu layolFA , (S, O,) inf. n. TuruwqN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He came to his Ahl [meaning wife ] by night: (S, * O, TA:) the doing of which by him who has been long absent is forbidden by the Prophet. (O, TA. *) And Taraqa Aln~ajomu , aor. , inf. n. TuruwqN , (assumed tropical:) The star, or asterism, rose: and of anything that has come by night, one says Taraqa . (Msb.) One says also, Turiqa fulaAnN (assumed tropical:) Such a one was made an object of [or was visited by or was smitten by ] nocturnal accidents or calamities. (TA.) And Taraqahu Alz~amaAnu binawaAy^ibihi (assumed tropical:) [ Time, or fortune, visited him, or smote him, with its accidents, or calamities; or did so suddenly, like one knocking at the door in the night ]. (TA.) And TaraqaniY xayaAlN (assumed tropical:) [ An apparition, or a phantom, visited me in the night ]. (TA.) And TaraqaniY ham~N (assumed tropical:) [ Anxiety came upon me; or did so suddenly, like one coming in the night ]. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] Taraqa samoEiY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ Such a thing struck my ear ]: and Turiqato masaAmiEiY bixayorK (assumed tropical:) [ My ears were struck by good tidings ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The stallion's covering the she-camel; (Msb, K; *) and so TuruwqN ; (K, TA;) and TiraAqN likewise [app. another inf. n. of Taraqa , as its syn. DiraAbN is of Daraba ]: (TA:) or his leaping her, (S, O, TA,) and covering her. (TA.) You say, Taraqa AlqaHolu Aln~aAqapa , (S, O, Msb, TA,) aor. , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. TaroqN , (Msb,) or TuruwqN , (S) or both, (O, TA,) The stallion covered the she-camel: (Msb:) or leaped the she-camel, (S, O, TA,) and covered her. (TA.) ― -b4- And [The practising of pessomancy; ] i. q. DarobN biAlHaSaY , (S, IAth, O, K,) which is performed by women, (IAth, TA,) or by a diviner; (K;) a certain mode of divination: (S:) or [the practising of geomancy; i. e.] a man's making lines, or marks, upon the ground, with two fingers, and then with one finger, and saying, AibonaYo EiyaAno A^asoriEaA AlbayaAno : (AZ, O, TA: [see this saying explained, with another description of the process, in the first paragraph of art. xT :]) or it is the making lines, or marks, upon the sand: (TA:) you say, Taraqa , aor. , inf. n. TaroqN , He made lines, or marks, with a finger, (&c.,) in divining. (JK.) [See the last sentence in art. jbt .] Also The diviner's mixing cotton with wool when divining. (Lth, K.) ― -b5- And TaraqonaA Aln~aEojapa , aor. , inf. n. TaroqN , We branded the ewe with the mark called TiraAq . (ISh, O.) -A2- Turiqa , (K, TA,) like EuniYa , (TA,) [inf. n., app., TaroqN , q. v.,] (tropical:) He was, or became, weak in intellect, (K, TA,) and soft. (TA.) -A3- Tariqa , aor. , (K,) inf. n. TaraqN , (Fr, S, O, K,) He (a camel) had a weakness in his knees: (Fr, S, O, K: [see HalalN :]) or, said of a human being and of a camel, he had a weakness in the knee and in the arm or the fore leg: (TA:) or, said of a camel, he had a crookedness in the saAq (Lth, * O, * K) of the kind leg, [app. meaning in the thigh, ] without the [ kind of straddling termed ] faHaj , and with an inclining in the heel. (Lth, O.) ― -b2- [See also TaraqN below.] -A4- Tariqa signifies also He drank turbid, or muddy, water, (O, K, TA,) such as is termed [ TaroqN and ] maToruwqN . (TA. [In the K it is said to be, in this sense, like samiEa ; which seems to indicate that the inf. n. is TaroqN , not TaraqN .])

definition: ― -b2- Tr~q TariyqFA He made a road plane, or even, so that people travelled it [or beat it with their feet ] in their passing along.
sourceDefinition: : see 1, former half. ― -b2- Tr~q TariyqFA He made a road plane, or even, so that people travelled it [or beat it with their feet ] in their passing along. (TA.) The saying laA tuTar~iquwA AlmasaAjida means Make not ye the mosques to be roads [or places of passage ]. (TA.) Tar~aqotu lahu is from AlT~ariyqu : (S, O:) you say, Tr~q lahaA [app. referring to camels ] He made for them a road, or way: (K:) or Tr~q lahu he gave a way to, or admitted, him, or it. (MA.) ― -b3- Tar~aqato said of the [bird called] qaTaAp , peculiarly, (inf. n. taToriyqN , O, K,) She arrived at the time of her egg's coming forth: (As, A'Obeyd, S, O, K:) or she (a qTAp ) hollowed out in the ground a place wherein to lay her eggs: as though she made a way for them: so says A Heyth: but the verb may be similarly used of other than the qTAp , metaphorically; whence the saying, qado Tar~aqato bibikorihaA A^um~u Tabaqo i. e. (tropical:) Calamity [ has prepared to bring forth her first-born ]. (Az, TA.) [Hence, app.,] one says also, Darabahu Hat~aY Tar~aqa bijaEorihi [ He beat him until he gave passage, or was about to give passage, to his ordure ]. (As, S, O.) And Tr~q liY , inf. n. taToriyqN , signifies A^axoraja [app. meaning He gave forth, or produced, to me something]. (TA.) ― -b4- Tar~aqato biwaladihaA , said of a camel, means She brought forth with difficulty, her young one sticking fast, and not coming forth easily; and in like manner it is said of a woman: (As, S, O, K:) so in a verse of Ows Ibn-Hajar, cited voce nifaAsN : (O:) or Tr~qt said of a woman and of any pregnant female, means the half of her young one came forth, and then it stuck fast. (Lth, TA.) [Hence,] Tr~q fulaAnN biHaq~iY (tropical:) Such a one acknowledged my right, or due, after disacknowledging it. (As, S, O, K, TA.) ― -b5- Accord. to AZ, (TA,) Tr~q AlA_ibila means He withheld the camels from pasture, (S, O, K, TA,) or from some other thing: (S, O, TA:) Sh, however, says that he knew not this; but that IAar explained Tar~afotu , with f , as meaning “ I repelled. ” (TA.) ― -b6- A^axa*a fulaAnN fiY Alt~aToriyqi means (assumed tropical:) Such a one practised artifice and divination. (TA.) -A2- Tar~aqotu Alt~urosa I sewed the shield upon another skin: and Tar~aqotu Aln~aEola , inf. n. taToriyqN , I made the sole of two pieces of skin, sewing one of them upon the other. (Msb. [See also the next paragraph.])

definition: [meaning I sewed another sole upon the sole ] is an instance of a verb of the measure faAEala relating to the act of a single agent.
sourceDefinition: [meaning I sewed another sole upon the sole ] is an instance of a verb of the measure faAEala relating to the act of a single agent. (AAF, TA in art. xdE .) [See also 2, last sentence.] You say also, TArq Alr~ajulu naEolayohi , [inf. n. muTaAraqapN ,] The man put one of his two soles upon the other and sewed them together. (As, TA.) TaAbaqa , (K,) or ZaAhara , i. e. He put on himself one of the two garments, or one of two garments, [and one of the two coats of mail, ] over the other. (S, O.) definition: He lent him his stallion [ camel ] to cover his she-camels.
sourceDefinition: He lent him his stallion [ camel ] to cover his she-camels. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- laA A^aToraqa A@ll~`hu Ealayoka , (O,) or Ealayohi , (K, TA,) means (tropical:) May God not cause thee, or him, to have one whom thou mayest, or whom he may, take to wife, or compress. (O, K, TA.) ― -b3- See also 3, latter part. ― -b4- ATrq raA^osahu He inclined his head [ downwards ]. (TA.) And A^aToriqo baSaraka Lower thine eyes towards thy breast, and be silent: occurring in a trad. respecting the looking unexpectedly [at one at whom one should not look]. (TA.) And A^aToraqa , alone, He bent down his head: (MA:) or he lowered his eyes, looking towards the ground; (S, O, K;) and sometimes the doing so is natural: (TA: [and the same is indicated in the S:]) and it may mean he had a laxness in the eyelids: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or he contracted his eyelids, as though his eye struck the ground: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and he was, or became, silent, (ISk, S, O, K,) accord. to some, by reason of fright, (TA,) not speaking. (ISk, S, O, K.) It is said in a prov., A^aToriqN karaA A^aToriqN karaA A_in~a Aln~aEaAma fiY AlquraY [ Lower thine eyes karà: lower thine eyes karà: ( krA meaning the male of the karawaAn , a name now given to the stone-curlew, or charadrius ædicnemus: ) verily the ostriches are in the towns, or villages ]: applied to the self-conceited; (S, O;) and to him who is insufficient, or unprofitable; who speaks and it is said to him, “ Be silent, and beware of the spreading abroad of that which thou utterest, for dislike of what may be its result: ” and by the saying An~ AlnEAm fY AlqrY is meant, they will come to thee and trample thee with their feet: (O:) it is like the saying faguD~i AlT~arofa . (S. [See also karawaAnN : and see also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 30-31.]) It is asserted that when they desire to capture the krA , and see it from afar, they encompass it, and one of them says, A^aToriqo karaA A_in~aka laA turaY [or lano turaY (Meyd in explanation of the preceding prov.) i. e. Lower thine eyes, or be silent, karà: thou wilt not be seen: ] until he becomes within reach of it; when he throws a garment over it, and takes it. ('Eyn, TA.) And A^aToriqo karaA yuHolabo laka [ Lower thine eyes, or be silent, karà: milk shall be drawn for thee: ] is [a prov., mentioned by Meyd,] said to a stupid person whom one incites to hope for that which is vain, or false, and who believes [what is said to him]. (O.) ― -b5- One says also, ATrq A_ilaY All~ahowi (tropical:) He inclined to diversion, sport, or play. (IAar, K, TA.) ― -b6- ATrq All~ayolu Ealayohi : see 8: ― -b7- and ATrqt AlA_ibilu : see 6. -A2- ATrq AlS~ayoda He set a snare for the beasts, or birds, of the chase. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, ATrq fulaAnN lifulaAnK (assumed tropical:) Such a one plotted against such a one by calumny, or slander, in order to throw him into destruction, or into that from which escape would be difficult. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [originally an inf. n., and as such app. signifying An act of striking the lute &c.: and hence,] a species ( DarobN ) of the A^aSowaAt [meaning sounds, or airs, or tunes, ] of the lute: (TA:) or any Sawot [i. e. air, or tune ], (Lth, O, K, TA,) or any nagomap [i. e. melody ], (K, TA,) of the lute and the like, by itself: (Lth, O, K, TA:) you say, taDoribu h`*ihi AljaAriyapu ka*aA waka*aA TaroqFA [ This girl, or young woman, or female slave, plays such and such airs or tunes, or such and such melodies, of the lute or the like ]. (Lth, O, K. *) ― -b2- [Hence, probably,] Einodahu TuruwqN mina AlkalaAmi , sing. TaroqN , a phrase mentioned by Kr; thought by ISd to mean He has [ various ] sorts, or species, of speech. (TA.) ― -b3- See also TaroqapN , in four places. -A2- Also (tropical:) A stallion [ camel ] covering: (O, K, TA:) pl. TuruwqN and Tur~aAqN : (TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst. [or an epithet]: (O, K, TA:) for *uw TaroqK . (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The sperma of the stallion [camel]: (S, K:) a man says to another, A^aEironiY Taroqa faHolika AlEaAma i. e. [or coll. gen. n.] is ↓ TaraqN , (S, K,) signifies [the same, or] the snare ( HibaAlap ) of the sportsman, (S, O, K,) having [ what are termed ] kifaf [pl. of kif~apN , q. v.]. (S, O) -A5- And A palm-tree: of the dial. of Teiyi. (AHn, K.) -A6- And (tropical:) Weakness of intellect, (K, TA,) and softness. (TA [See Turiqa .])

[or an epithet]: (O, K, TA:) for *uw TaroqK . (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The sperma of the stallion [camel]: (S, K:) a man says to another, A^aEironiY Taroqa faHolika AlEaAma i. e. [or coll. gen. n.] is ↓ TaraqN , (S, K,) signifies [the same, or] the snare ( HibaAlap ) of the sportsman, (S, O, K,) having [ what are termed ] kifaf [pl. of kif~apN , q. v.].
