(TA.) -A2- Also A brand made upon the middle of the ear of a ewe, (En-Nadr, O, K,) externally; being a white line, made with fire, resembling a track of a road: (En-Nadr, O:) there are two such brands, called TiraAqaAni . (TA.) -A3- See also Tir~iyqapN .

definition: A road, way, or path;
sourceDefinition: A road, way, or path; syn. sabiylN ; (S;) [i. e. a beaten track, being of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; and applied to any place of passage; ] and ↓ TuroqapN signifies the same: (K:) [see also musotaToraqN :] it is masc. (S, O, Msb, K *) in the dial. of Nejd, and so in the Kur xx. 79; (Msb;) and fem. (S, O, Msb, K) in the dial. of El-Hijáz: (Msb:) the latter accord. to general usage: (MF:) [see zuqaAqN :] the pl. [of pauc.] is A^aToriqapN (S, Msb, K) with those who make the sing. masc. (Msb) and A^aToruqN (O, K) with those who make the sing. fem. (TA) and [of mult.] TuruqN (S, O, Msb, K) and TuroqN [of which see an ex. voce dilaAlapN ] (K) and A^aToriqaA='u , (O, K,) and TuruqaAtN is a pl. pl. (Msb, K) i. e. pl. of TuruqN . (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- In the saying banuw fulaAnK yaTaw^uhumu AlT~ariyqu , accord. to Sb, AlT~ariyqu is for A^aholu AlT~alriyqi : [the meaning therefore is, (assumed tropical:) The sons of such a one sojourn, or encamp, where the people of the road tread upon them, i. e., become their guests: (see more in art. wTA^ :)] or, as some say, AlTryq here means the wayfarers without any suppression. (TA.) ― -b3- Haq~u AlT~ariyqi [ The duty relating to the road ] is the lowering of the eyes; the putting away, or aside, what is hurtful, or annoying; the returning of salutations; the enjoining of that which is good; and the forbidding of that which is evil. (El-Jámi' es- Sagheer. See jalasa .) ― -b4- qaTaEa AlT~ariyqa [ He intercepted the road ] means he made the road to be feared, relying upon his strength, robbing, and slaying men [or passengers ]. (Msb in art. qTE .) [And A^aSaAba AlT~ariyqa means the same; or, as expl. by Freytag, on the authority of Meyd, He was, or became, a robber. ] ― -b5- [Hence,] Aibonu AlT~ariyqi means (assumed tropical:) The robber [ on the highway ]. (T in art. bnY .) ― -b6- [But A^aholu Tariyqi A@ll~`hi means (assumed tropical:) The devotees. ] ― -b7- A^um~u TariyqK , thus correctly in the 'Eyn, [and shown to be so by a verse there cited, q. v. voce EasobN ,] (assumed tropical:) The hyena: erroneously written by Sgh, ↓ Am~ Tur~ayoqK ; and the author of the K has copied him in this instance accord. to his usual custom. (TA.) ― -b8- See also A^um~u AlT~ariyqi and A^um~apu AlT~ariyqi in art. Am . ― -b9- banaAtu AlT~ariyqi means (assumed tropical:) The branches of the road, that vary, and lead in any, or every, direction. (TA.) ― -b10- TariyqN signifies also The space between two rows of palm-trees; as being likened to the Tariyq [commonly so called] in extension. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b11- A^axa*a fulaAnN fiY AlT~ariyqi means the same as A^axa*a fiY Alt~aToriyqi [expl. before: see 2, near the end]. (TA.) ― -b12- TariyqN as syn. with TariyqapN : see the latter word, first sentence. ― -b13- [ biAlT~ariyqi AlA^awolaY is a phrase of frequent occurrence, app. post-classical; lit. By the fitter way; meaning with the stronger reason; à fortiori: see an ex. in Beyd xlii. 3, and De Sacy's Anthol. Gr. Ar. p. 467.] -A2- Also A sort of palm-tree. (TA.) ― -b2- See also TariyqapN (of which it is said to be a pl.), last sentence.

definition: A she-camel covered by the stallion;
sourceDefinition: A she-camel covered by the stallion; of the measure faEuwlapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN . (Msb.) Taruwqapu AlfaHoli means The female of the stallion [ camel ]. (S, O.) And (S, O) A she-camel that has attained to the fit age for her being covered by the stallion: (S, O, Msb, K:) it is not a condition of the application of the term that he has already covered her: (Msb:) or a young, or youthful, she-camel that has attained to that age and kept to the stallion and been chosen by him. (TA.) And one says to a husband, kayofa Taruwqatuka , meaning (assumed tropical:) How is thy wife? (TA:) every wife is termed Taruwqapu zawojihaA , (O,) or Trwqp baEolihaA , (Msb,) or Trwqp faHolihaA ; (K, * TA;) which is thought by ISd to be metaphorical. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also, naw~axa A@ll~`hu AlA^aroDa TaruwqapF lilomaA='i i. e. (assumed tropical:) God made, or may God make, the land capable of receiving the water [of the rains so as to be impregnated, or fertilized, or soaked, thereby ]; expl. by jaEalahaA mim~aA tuTiyquhu . (S in art. nwx .) [See also a verse cited in art. sfd , conj. 4.]

definition: A way, course, rule, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or the like, (syn.
sourceDefinition: A way, course, rule, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or the like, (syn. ma*ohabN , S, TA, and siyrapN , and masolakN , TA,) of a man, (S, TA,) whether it be approved or disapproved; (TA;) as also ↓ TariyqN , which is metaphorically used in this sense: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [like ma*ohabN , often relating to the doctrines and practices of religion: and often used in post-classical times as meaning the rule of a religious order or sect:] and meaning also a manner of being; a state, or condition; (syn. HaAlapN , S, or HaAlN , O, K;) as in the saying, maA zaAla fulaAnN EalaY TariyqapK waAHidapK [ Such a one ceased not to be in one state, or condition ]; (S;) and it is applied to such as is good and to such as is evil. (O.) One says also, huwa EalaY Tariyqatihi [ He is following his own way, or course ]. (TA voce jadiy~apN .) lawi A@sotaqaAmuwA EalaY AlT~ariyqapi , in the Kur [lxxii. 16], means, accord. to Fr, [ If they had gone on undeviating in the way ] of polytheism: but accord. to others, of the right direction. (O.) [The pl. is TaraAy^iqu .] ― -b2- [It is also used for A^aholu TariyqapK : and in like manner the pl., for A^aholu TaraAy^iqa . Thus,] kun~aA TaraAy^iqa qidadFA , in the Kur [lxxii. 11], means (assumed tropical:) We were sects differing in our desires. (Fr, S, O. [See also qid~apN .]) And Tariyqapu Alqawomi means (tropical:) The most excel-lent, (S, O, K, TA,) and the best, (S, O,) and the eminent, or noble, persons, (K, TA,) of the people: (S, O, K, TA:) and you say, h`*aA rajulN Tariyqapu qawomihi (tropical:) [ This is a man the most excellent, &c., of his people ]: and h`w^ulaA='i Tariyqapu qawomihimo and TaraAy^iqu qawomihimo (tropical:) These are [ the most excellent, &c., or] the eminent, or noble, persons of their people: (S, O, K, * TA:) so says Yaakoob, on the authority of Fr. (S, O, TA.) waya*ohabaA biTariyqatikumu AlmuvolaY , in the Kur [xx. 66], means [ And that they may take away ] your most excellent body of people: (O:) or your eminent, or noble, body of people who should be made examples to be followed: and Zj thinks that bTryqtkm is for biA^aholi Tariyqatikum : (TA:) or, accord. to Akh, the meaning is, your established rule or usage, and your religion, or system of religious ordinances. (O, TA.) ― -b3- [Also (assumed tropical:) The way, or course, of an event: and hence,] TaraAy^iqu Ald~ahori means (assumed tropical:) The vicissitudes of time or fortune. (TA.) ― -b4- [And (assumed tropical:) The air of a song &c.: but this is probably post-classical.] ― -b5- Also A line, streak, or stripe, in a thing: (K, TA:) [and a crease, or wrinkle; often used in this sense:] and [its pl.] TaraAy^iqu signifies the lines, or streaks, that are called Hubuk , of a helmet. (TA.) The Tariyqap [or line ] that is in the upper part of the back: and the line, or streak, that extends upon [i. e. along ] the back of the ass. (TA.) [ A vein, or seam, in a rock or the like. A track in stony or rugged land &c. A narrow strip of ground or land, and of herbage.] An extended piece or portion [i. e. a strip ] of sand; and likewise of fat; and [likewise of flesh; or] an oblong piece of flesh. (TA.) ― -b6- [Hence, app.,] vawobN TaraAy^iqu A garment old and worn out [as though reduced to strips or shreds ]. (Lh, K.) ― -b7- *aAtu TaraAy^iqa and fiyhaA TaraAy^iqu are phrases used, the latter by Dhu-r-Rummeh, in describing a spear-shaft ( qanaAp ) shrunk by dryness [app. meaning Having lines, or what resemble wrinkles, caused by shrinking ]. (TA.) ― -b8- And TaraAy^iqu signifies also The last remains of the soft and best portions of pasturage. (TA.) ― -b9- And The stages of Heaven; so called because they lie one above another: (TA:) [for] Als~am`waAtu saboEu TaraAy^iqa baEoDuhaA fawoqa baEoDK [ The Heavens are seven stages, one above another ]; (Lth, O, TA:) and they have mentioned [likewise] the stages of the earth [as seven in number: and of hell also: see darakN ]. (TA.) See also TaraqapN . ― -b10- Accord. to Lth, (O, TA,) TariyqapN signifies also Any A^uHoduwrap , (so in the O and in copies of the K and accord. to the TA, and thus also in the JK,) or A^uxoduwdap , (thus accord. to the CK,) [neither of which words have I found in any but this passage, nor do I know any words nearly resembling them except A^uHoduwr and A^uxoduwd , of which they may be mistranscriptions, or perhaps dial. vars., the former signifying a declivity, slope, or place of descent, and the latter a furrow, trench, or channel, ] of the earth or ground: (O, K, TA:) or [ any ] border, or side, ( Sanifap ,) of a garment, or piece of cloth; or of a thing of which one part is stuck upon another, or of which the several portions are stuck one upon another; and in like manner of colours [ similarly disposed ]. (O, TA.) ― -b11- And A web, or thing woven, of wool, or of [ goats' ] hair, a cubit in breadth, (S, O, K, TA,) or less, (S, O, TA,) and in length four cubits, or eight cubits, (TA,) [or] proportioned to the size of the tent (S, O, K, TA) in its length, (S, O,) which is sewed in the place where the $iqaAq [or oblong pieces of cloth that compose the main covering of the tent ] meet, from the kisor [q. v.] to the kisor ; (S, O, K, TA;) [ it is app. sewed beneath the middle of the tent-covering, half of its breadth being sewed to one $uq~ap and the other half thereof to the other middle $uq~ap ; (see Burckhardt's “ Bedouins and Wahábys, ” p. 38 of the 8vo ed.;) and sometimes, it seems, there are three TaraAy^iq , one in the middle and one towards each side; for it is added,] and in them are the heads of the tentpoles, [ these generally consisting of three rows, three in each row, ] between which and the TrAy^q are pieces of felt, in which are the nozzles ( A^unuwf ) of the tent-poles, in order that these may not rend the TrAy^q . (TA.) ― -b12- Also A tent pole; any one of the poles of a tent: a xibaA=' has one Tryqp : a bayot has two and three and four [and more]: and the part between two poles is called matonN : (AZ, TA in art. zbE :) or the pole of a [ large tent such as is called ] miZal~ap , (K, TA,) and of a xibaA=' . (TA.) ― -b13- And A tall palm-tree: (K:) or the tallest of palm-trees: so called in the dial. of ElYemámeh: (AA, ISk, S, O:) or a smooth palmtree: or a palm-tree [ the head of ] which may be reached by the hand: (TA:) pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ TariyqN . (AA, ISk, S, O.)

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of Taraqa ; and, as such, generally meaning] Coming, or a comer, (S,) [i. e.] anything coming, (O, Msb,) by night: (S, O, Msb:) one who comes by night being thus called because of his [generally] needing to knock at the door: in the Mufradát [of Er-Rághib] said to signify a wayfarer ( saAlikN lilT~ariyqi ): but in the common conventional language particularly applied to the comer by night: its pl. is A^aToraAqN , like A^anoSaArN pl. of naASirN , [and app., as in a sense hereafter mentioned, Tur~aAqN also, agreeably with analogy,] and the pl. of [its fem.] TaAriqapN is TawaAriqu . (TA.) [ TaAriqu AlmanaAyaA , like daAEiY AlmanaAyaA , means The summoner of death, lit., of deaths; because death makes known its arrival or approach suddenly, like a person knocking at the door in the night.] ― -b2- Hence AlT~aAriqu , mentioned in the Kur [lxxxvi. 1 and 2], The star that appears in the night: (Er-Rághib, O:) or the morning-star; (S, O, K;) because it comes [or appears] in [the end of] the night. (O.) ― -b3- Hence the saying of Hind (S, O) the daughter of 'Otbeh the son of Rabee'ah, on the day [of the battle] of Ohud, quoting proverbially what was said by Ez-Zarkà El-Iyádeeyeh when Kisrà warred with Iyád, (O,) laA nanovaniY liwaAmiqi naHonu banaAtu TaAriqi namo$iY EalaY Aln~amaAriqi (assumed tropical:) [ We are the daughters of one like a star, or a morning-star: we bend not to a lover: we walk upon the pillows ]: (S, * O, * TA:) meaning we are the daughters of a chief; likening him to the star in elevation; (O, TA;) i. e. our father is, in respect of elevation, like the shining star: (S:) or banaAtu TaAriqK means (assumed tropical:) The daughters of the kings. (T and TA in art. bnY .) ― -b4- And TaAriqN signifies also [ A diviner: and particularly, by means of pebbles; a practiser of pessomancy: or] one who is nearly a kaAhin ; possessing more knowledge than such as is termed HaAzK : (ISh, TA in art. HzY :) Tur~aAqN [is its p., and] signifies practisers of divination: and TawaAriqu [is pl. of TaAriqapN , and thus] signifies female practisers of divination: Lebeed says, laEamoruka maA tadoriY AlT~awaAriqu biAlHaSaY walaA zaAjiraAtu AlT~ayori maA A@ll~`hu SaAniEu [ By thy life, or by thy religion, the diviners with pebbles know not, nor the diviners by the flight of birds, what God is doing ]. (S, O.)

definition: An apparition, a phantom, a spectre, or an imaginary form, ( xayaAlN ,) coming in sleep;
sourceDefinition: An apparition, a phantom, a spectre, or an imaginary form, ( xayaAlN ,) coming in sleep; (IDrd, O, K;) one says Tayofu xayaAlK and ↓ TaAy^ifu xayaAlK [meaning thus]: (IDrd, O:) or anything that obscures the sight, [ arising ] from a vain suggestion of the Devil: (Lth, TA:) or a jinnee, and a human being, and a xayaAl , that comes to, or visits, a man [generally in sleep ]; as also ↓ TaAy^ifN ; so says IF in art. Twf : (Msb:) both of these words signify alike; i. e. a thing like the xayaAl ; and a thing that comes to one, or visits one: (Fr, TA:) and ↓ TiyfN , with kesr, signifies a xayaAl itself: (Kr, TA:) or [ TayofN is properly, or originally, an inf. n.; and] Tayofu AlxayaAli signifies the coming of the xyAl in sleep: (S, O, K: *) accord. to El-Mufaddal, (O,) one says TayofN as meaning TaAy^ifu xayaAlK because it is originally [ TayowifN , and then] Tay~ifN ; like may~itN and mayotN from maAta , aor. yamuwtu . (O, K.) Tayofu Al$~ayoTaAni and ↓ TaAy^ifuhu signify The Devil's visitation, by touch, or madness or insanity, ( biA@lomas~i ,) or by vain prompting or suggestion: (Msb:) or TayofN mina Al$~ayoTaAni signifies A touch, or slight degree, or somewhat [ of a taint or an infection ], of insanity or possession, from the Devil; syn. lamamN ; occurring in the Kur vii. 200, accord. to one reading; another reading being mina Al$~ayoTaAni ↓ TaAy^ifN , which signifies the same. (S, O. [See also TawofN .]) One says also Tayofu junuwnK [ A touch, or slight degree, of insanity, or diabolical possession ]. (S, O.) And TayofN [alone] signifies Insanity, or diabolical possession: (O, K:) so says A 'Obeyd, on the authority of ElAhmar: (TA:) and this is said by Az to be the meaning of the word in the language of the Arabs. (O, TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Anger: (I'Ab, Mujáhid, O, K:) because the intellect of the angry departs [for a time] so that he assumes the the likeness of the insane, or possessed: (O, TA:) said by I'Ab to mean thus in the Kur vii. 200. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , has for its inf. n. ZalomN , (M, Msb, K, and so in some copies of the S,) or ↓ ZulomN , (so in other copies of the S,) or both, (T,) or the latter is a simple subst., (T, M, Msb, TA,) which is put in the place of the inf. n., (TA, [and the same is indicated in the T and K by the saying that the proper inf. n. is with fet-h,]) and ↓ maZolimapN , (S, TA,) or this is likewise a simple subst., (Msb,) and ↓ maZolamapN , [or this also is a simple subst.,] and ↓ ZilaAmN also is said to be an inf. n. like ZulomN , these two being like libaAsN and lubosN , [or it is a simple subst. like as ZulomN is said to be, or it is an inf. n. of 3, as such occurring in the middle of this paragraph,] or, accord. to Kr, it is pl. of ZulomN [like as rimaAHN is pl. of rumoHN ]: (TA:) [ Zalama when intrans. generally means He did wrong; or acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: and when trans., he wronged; or treated, or used, wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically; or he misused: ] accord. to most of the lexicologists, (Er-Rághib, TA,) primarily, (As, T, S, Msb,) ↓ AlZ~ulomu signifies the putting a thing in a place not its own; putting it in a wrong place; misplacing it: (As, T, S, M, Er-Rághib, Msb, K:) and it is by exceeding or by falling short, or by deviating from the proper time and place: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or the acting in whatsoever way one pleases in the disposal of the property of another: and the transgressing the proper limit: (El-Munáwee, TA:) [i. e.] the transgressing the proper limit much or little: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or, accord. to some, it primarily signifies Aln~aqoS [as meaning the making to suffer loss, or detriment ]: (MF, TA:) and it is said to be of three kinds, between man and God, and between man and man, and between a man and himself; every one of which three is really liln~afosi [i. e. a wrongdoing to oneself ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [when it is used as a simple subst.,] the pl. of ZulomN , accord. to Kr. is ZilaAmN , as mentioned above, and ↓ ZulaAmN , with damm, is said to be syn. with ZulomN , or a pl. thereof, [of an extr. form, commonly regarded as that of a quasi-pl. n.,] like ruxaAlN . (TA.) One says, mani A@sotaroEaY Al*~iy^oba faqado Zalama [ He who asks, or desires, the wolf to keep guard surely does wrong, or puts a thing in a wrong place ]: a prov. (S, Msb.) And mano A^a$obaha A^abaAhu famaA Zalama , (As, T, S,) a prov., meaning [ Whoso resembles his father in a quality, or an attribute,] he has not put the likeness in a wrong place. (As, T. [See art. $bh .]) walamo taZolimo minohu $ayoy^FA , in the Kur [xviii. 31], means walamo tanoquSo [i. e. And made not aught thereof to suffer loss, or detriment ]: (M, K:) and in like manner Fr explains the saying in the Kur [ii. 54 and vii. 160], wamaA ZalamuwnaA wal`kino kaAnuwA A^anofusahumo yaZolimuwna And they made not us to suffer loss, or detriment, by that which they did, but themselves they made to suffer loss, or detriment: (T, TA:) in which sense it seems to be indicated in the A that the verb is tropical. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also trans. by means of bi ; as in the phrase in the Kur [vii. 101 and xvii. 61] faZalamuwA bihaA , because the meaning is kafaruwA [i. e. And they disbelieved in them ], referring to the A=yaAt [or signs ]; (M, TA; *) the verb having this meaning tropically or by implication; or being thus made trans. because implying the meaning of Alt~ako*iyb : or [the meaning is, and they wronged themselves, or the people, because of them; for], as some say, the b is causative, and the objective complement, i. e. A^anofusahumo , or Aln~aAsa , is suppressed. (TA.) ― -b3- And it is doubly trans. by itself: (TA:) one says, Zalamahu Haq~ahu [ He made him to suffer loss, or detriment, of his right, or due; or defrauded, or despoiled, or deprived, him of it ]; and Haq~ahu ↓ tZl~mhu : (M, K:) [and] you say, fulaAnN ↓ taZal~amaniY , [as well as tZl~mnY maAliY , occurring in a verse cited in the M,] meaning ZalamaniY maAliY [i. e. Such a one caused me to suffer loss, &c., of my property ]. (S.) It is said in the Kur [iv. 44], A_in~a A@ll~`ha laA yaZolimu mivoqaAla *ar~apK , for laA yaZolimuhumo mivoqaAla *ar~api , and the verb is made doubly trans. because the meaning is laA yasolubuhumo [i. e. Verily God will not despoil them, or deprive them, of the weight of one of the smallest of ants, or a grub of an ant, &c.]: or mivoqaAla *ar~apK , may be put in the place of the inf. n., for ZalomFA HaqiyrFA kamivoqaAli *ar~apK [i. e. with a paltry spoliation or deprivation, such as the weight of one of the smallest of ants, &c.]. (M.) ― -b4- One says also, A^araAda ZilaAmahu and muZaAlamatahu , [these two nouns being inf. ns. of ↓ ZaAlamahu , or the former, as mentioned above, is, accord. to some, an inf. n. of Zalama ,] meaning Zulomahu or Zalomahu [i. e. He desired the wronging, &c., of him ]. (M, K.) ― -b5- Zalamahu , inf. n. ZulomN [or ZalomN ?], also means He imposed upon him a thing that was above his power, or ability. (TA.) And yuZolamu He is asked for a thing that is above his power, or ability. (S.) ― -b6- And one says, Zalama AlbaEiyra (tropical:) He slaughtered the camel without disease. (S, K, TA.) And Zulimati Aln~aAqapu (assumed tropical:) The she-camel was slaughtered without disease: or was covered without her desiring the stallion. (M.) And Zalama AlHimaAru AlA^ataAna (tropical:) The he-ass leaped the she-ass (K, TA) before her time: (TA:) or when she was pregnant: (K, TA:) so in the A. (TA.) ― -b7- And Zalama AlwaToba , (S, K,) inf. n. ZulomN [or ZalomN ?], (S,) (tropical:) He gave to drink of the milk of his skin before its becoming thick (S, K, TA) and its butter's coming forth. (TA. [And the like is said in the T and M.]) And Zalama Alqawoma (assumed tropical:) He gave to drink to the people, or party, (T, M, K,) milk before it had attained to maturity, (T, K,) as related on the authority of A 'Obeyd, (T,) or [ milk such as is termed ] Zaliymap : (M:) but this is a mistake: it is related on the authority of Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà [i. e. Th] and AHeyth that one says, Zalamotu Als~iqaA='a , and All~abana , meaning I drank, or gave to drink, what was in the skin, and the milk, before its attaining to maturity and the extracting of its butter: accord. to ISk, one says, Zalamotu waTobiYa Alqawoma , [but I think that it is correctly Zalamotu waTobiY liloqawmi , agreeably with a verse cited in the T and M,] meaning I gave to drink [ to the people, or party, ] the contents of my milk-skin before the thickening thereof. (T.) And Zalamotuhu is said of anything as meaning (assumed tropical:) I did it hastily, or hurriedly, before its proper time, or season. (M, TA.) ― -b8- Zalamotu AlHawoDa means (assumed tropical:) I made the watering-trough in a place in which watering-troughs should not be made. (ISk, T.) And Zalama AlA^aroDa means (tropical:) He dug the ground in what was not the place of digging: (M, K, TA:) or when it had not been dug before. (M.) And, said of a torrent, (assumed tropical:) It furrowed the earth in a place that was not furrowed. (T.) And Zalama AlbiTaAHa , said of a torrent, (tropical:) It reached the bTAH [or wide water-courses containing fine, or broken, pebbles, &c.], not having reached them before. (A, TA.) And Zalama AlwaAdiY (tropical:) The water of the valley reached a place that it had not reached before. (Fr, T, S, K, TA.) ― -b9- When men have added upon the grave other than its own earth, laA taZolimuwA (tropical:) [ Transgress not ye the proper limit ] is said to them. (TA.) ― -b10- And one says, laA taZolimo waDaHa AlT~ariyqi (assumed tropical:) Turn not thou from the main part, or the beaten track, of the road. (M.) And laA taZolimo Eanohu $ayoy^aA (assumed tropical:) Turn not thou from it at all. (T.) And lazima AlT~ariyqa falamo yaZolimohu (assumed tropical:) [ He kept to the road, and ] did not turn from it to the right and left. (TA.) ― -b11- And maA Zalamaka A^ano tafoEala (T, K, TA) (tropical:) What has prevented thy doing (K, TA) such a thing? (TA.) A man complained to Abu-l-Jarráh of his suffering indigestion from food that he had eaten, and he said to him, maA Zalamaka A^ano taqiYo'a (assumed tropical:) [ What has prevented thy vomiting? ]. (Fr, T.) And one says, maA Zalamaka Eano ka*aA (assumed tropical:) What has prevented thee from such a thing? (T.) Respecting the saying qaAla balaY yaA maY~a waAlyawomu Zalamo [addressed by a man to a woman who had invited him to visit her], Fr says, they say that the meaning is Haq~FA [ Truly, or in truth; i. e. He said, Yes, O Meiya, truly, or in truth, I will visit thee]; and it is a prov.; (T;) or Alyawomu Zalama , or balaY waAlyawomu Zalama , is a prov.; (Meyd;) and thus it was expl. by IAar, as used in the manner of an oath: but Fr says, in my opinion the meaning is, and a day in which is a cause of prevention shall not prevent me: [so that the words of the hemistich above may be rendered, he said, Yes, O Meiya, though the day present an obstacle, for I will overcome every obstacle]: (T:) accord. to Kr, qadima fulaAnN waAlyawomu Zalama means Such a one came truly, or in truth: [or it may be rendered such a one came though the day presented an obstacle: ] but in the saying A_in~a AlfiraAqa Alyawoma waAlyawomu Zalamo the meaning is said by some to be waAlyawomu ZalamanaA [i. e. Verily separation is to-day, and the day has wronged (us)]: or, as some say, Zlm here means, has put the thing in a wrong place: (M:) accord. to ISk, the phrase waAlyawomu Zalam means [ And, or but, or though, ] the day has put the affair in a wrong place. (T.) [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 911.] -A2- Zalima , said of the night: see 4.

sourceDefinition: , said of the night, (Fr, T, S, M, Msb, K,) and ↓ Zalima , (Fr, T, S, K,) the latter with kesr, (S,) like samiEa , (K,) [erroneously written in the TT as from the M Zalama ,] It became dark; (S, K;) or it became black; (M;) or it came with its darkness. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 19], waA_i*aA A^aZolama Ealayohimo qaAmuwA [ And when it becomes dark to them they stand still ]; the verb being intrans.: or, accord. to the Ksh, and Bd follows it, it may be trans. [so that the meaning is, and when He makes their place dark &c.]; as is shown by another reading, which is A^uZolimuwA : accord. to AHei, it is known by transmission as only intrans.; but Z makes it to be trans. by itself; Ibn-Es-Saláh affirms it to be trans. and intrans.: and Az [so in the TA, but correctly ISd, in the M,] mentions the saying, takal~ama faA^aZolama EalayonaA AlbayEta (assumed tropical:) [ He spoke, and made dark to us the house, or chamber, or tent ], meaning he made us to hear what we disliked, or hated, the verb being trans. (TA.) ― -b2- And A^aZolamuwA They entered upon the ZalaAm [or darkness, or beginning of night ]: (S, M, Msb, K:) or, as in the Mufradát [of Er-Rághib], they became in darkness. (TA.) ― -b3- And they said, maA A^aZolamahu and mA A^aDowaA^ahu [ How dark is it! and How light, or bright, is it! ]; which is anomalous. (S, TA.) -A2- And AZlm Alv~agoru The front teeth glistened. (T, K.) Hence the saying [of a poet], A_i*aA maA A@jotalaY Alr~aAy^iY A_ilayohaA biTarofihi guruwba vanaAyaAhaA A^aDaA='a waA^aZolamaA [as though meaning, When the beholder of her with his eye looks at the fineness, or sharpness, (but guruwb is variously explained,) of her central teeth, it shines brightly, and glistens: but Az plainly indicates another meaning; i. e., he sees (lit. lights on, or finds, ) brightness and lustre; for he immediately adds, without the intervention of wa or A^awo , evidently in relation to this verse,] A^aDaA='a A^aYo A^aSaAba Dawo'FA waA^aZolama A^aSaAba ZalomFA : (T:) [and ISd cites the verse above with the substitution of biEaynihi for biTarofihi and of A^anaAra for A^aDaA='a immediately after saying that] A^aZolama signifies he looked at the teeth and saw lustre ( AlZ~aloma ). (M.) [In the K, next after the explanation of AZlm Alv~agoru given above, it is added that AZlm said of a man signifies A^aSaAba ZalomFA : thus, with fet-h, to the Z , accord. to the TA: in my MS. copy of the K and in the CK, ZulomFA , which is doubtless a mistranscription.]

definition: tZl~m minohu (T, S, M, K, [but in some copies of the S, mnh is omitted,]) He complained of his Zulom [or wrongdoing, &c.
sourceDefinition: tZl~m minohu (T, S, M, K, [but in some copies of the S, mnh is omitted,]) He complained of his Zulom [or wrongdoing, &c.], (S, M, K,) A_ilaY AlHaAkimi [ to the judge ]: (T:) in some copies of the S, tuZul~ima . (TA.) ― -b2- And tZl~m signifies also He transferred the responsibility for the Zulom [or wrongdoing, &c.,] upon himself, (M, K,) accord. to IAar, who has cited as an ex., kaAnato A_i*aA gaDibato EalaY~a taZal~amato [as though meaning She used, when she was angry with me, to transfer the responsibility for the wrongdoing upon herself; which may mean that she finally confessed the wrongdoing to be hers]; but [ISd says] I know not how that is: the taZal~um in this case is only the complaining of AlZ~ulom ; for when she was angry with him, it was not allowable [to say] that she attributed the Zulom to herself. (M.) ― -b3- See also 1, former half, in two places.

definition: (S, M, Msb) The people, or company of men, treated, or used, one another wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically ( Zalama baEoDuhumo baEoDFA ).
sourceDefinition: (S, M, Msb) The people, or company of men, treated, or used, one another wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically ( Zalama baEoDuhumo baEoDFA ). definition: The lustre, and brightness, of gold.
sourceDefinition: The lustre, and brightness, of gold. (Z, TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (Z, TA,) The lustre (lit. running water ) upon the teeth; (Lth, T, Z, TA;) the lustre ( maA=' , S, M, K, and bariyq , S, K) of the teeth, (Lth, T, S, M, Z, K, TA,) from the clearness of the colour, not from the saliva, (Lth, * T, * M,) like blackness within the bone thereof, by reason of the intense whiteness, (S, K,) resembling the firinod [q. v.] of the sword, (S, K,) or appearing like the firinod [ of the sword ], so that one imagines that there is in it a blackness, by reason of the intense lustre and clearness: (M:) or, accord. to Sh, whiteness of the teeth, as though there were upon it [ somewhat of ] a blackness: or, as Abu-l-'Abbás ElAhwal says, in the Expos. of the “ Kaabeeyeh, ” lustre (lit. running water ) of the teeth, such that one sees upon it, by reason of its intense clearness [app. meaning transparency ], what resembles dustcolour and blackness: or, accord. to another explanation, fineness, or thinness, and intense whiteness, of the teeth: (TA:) pl. ZuluwmN . (Lth, T.)

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ ZulumapN (S, M, K) [accord. to the CK ZulomN and ZulumN , both of which are wrong,] and ↓ ZalomaA='u (S, M, Msb, K) Darkness; contr. of nuwrN : (S, Msb:) or nonexistence of nuwr [or light ]: or an accidental state that precludes the coëxistence therewith of nuwr : (Er-Rághib, TA:) or the departure of light; as also ↓ ZalaAmN ; (M, K;) which last has no pl.; (T, TA;) or this last signifies the beginning, or first part, of night, (S, M, Msb,) even though it be one in which the moon shines; and is said by Sb to be used only adverbially; one says, A^atayotuhu ZalaAmFA , meaning I came to him at night, and maEa AlZ~alaAmi i. e. at the time of the night: (M, TA:) the pl. of ZulomapN is ZulamN and ZulumaAtN and ZulamaAtN (T, S, Msb) and ZulomaAtN , (S, Msb,) or, accord. to IB, the first of these pls. is of ZulomapN and the second is of ZulumapN . (TA.) One says, ↓ huwa yaxobiTu AlZ~alaAma [or fiY AlZ~alaAmi , expl. in art. xbT ], and AlZ~ulomapa [which means the same] and ↓ AlZ~alomaA='a [which is also expl. in art. xbT ]. (TA.) ― -b2- ZulomapN is also [tropically] used as a term for (assumed tropical:) Ignorance: and (assumed tropical:) belief in a plurality of gods: and (assumed tropical:) transgression, or unrighteousness: like as nuwrN is used as a term for their contraries: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and it is said in the A that AlZ~ulomu is ZulomapN , like as AlEadolu is nuwrN . (TA.) ZulumaAtu AlbaHori means (assumed tropical:) The troubles, afflictions, calamities, or hardships, of the sea. (M.) -A2- And one says layolapN ZulomapN , [using the latter word as an epithet, (in the CK, erroneously, ZalimapN ,)] and ↓ layolapN ZalomaA='u , both meaning A night intensely dark; (M, K;) or the latter means muZolimapN [i. e. dark, or black ]: (S:) and ↓ layolN ZalomaA='u also, (M, K,) which is anomalous, (K,) mentioned by IAar, but [ISd says] this is strange, and in my opinion he has put layolN in the place of layolapN , as in his mentioning layolN qamoraA='u [q. v.]. (M.) ― -b2- See also ZulamN : ― -b3- and see the paragraph next preceding it.

sourceDefinition: [as syn. with maZoluwmN in the primary sense of the latter I have not found: but as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates it signifies] (tropical:) Milk that is drunk before its becoming thick and its butter's coming forth or being extracted; (S, * M;) as also ↓ ZaliymapN , (T, S, M,) and ↓ maZoluwmN . (T, S.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A place that is ↓ maZoluwm [i. e. dug where it should not be dug ]: (M, TA:) used in this sense by a poet describing a person slain in a desert, for whom a grave was dug in a place not proper for digging [it]. (M.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) The earth of land that is ↓ maZoluwmap (S, K, TA) i. e. dug, (TA,) or dug for the first time. (S.) And (assumed tropical:) The earth of the laHod [or lateral hollow ] of a grave; which is put back, over it, after the burial of the dead therein. (T, TA.) -A2- Also The male ostrich: (T, S, M, K:) said (by IDrd, TA) to be so called because he makes a place for the laying and hatching of the eggs ( yudaH~iY , inf. n. tadoHiyapN ,) where the doing so is not proper: (M, TA:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib and others, because he is believed to be deaf: (TA:) pl. ZilomaAnN (T, M, K) and ZulomaAnN (M, K) and A^aZolimapN , (T, M,) which last is a pl. of pauc. (T.) ― -b2- And AlZ~aliymaAni is an appellation of Two stars; (M, K, * TA;) the two stars of Alqawos [or Sagittarius ] that are on the northern curved end of the bow [i. e. λ and μ , above the nine stars called Aln~aEaAy^im , or “ the ostriches ”]. (Kzw in his descr. of Sagittarius.) And AlZ~aliymu is the name of The bright star [ α ] at the end of Aln~ahor [i. e. Eridanus ]: and A star upon the mouth of AlHuwt [i. e. Piscis Australis ] (Kzw in his descr. of Eridanus.) [It seems to be implied in the K that AlZ~aliymu is the name of two stars; or it may be there meant that each of two stars is thus called. Freytag represents the sing. as “ a name of stars, ” and the dual also as “ a name of stars; ” referring, in relation to the former, to Ideler's “ Untersuch, ” pp. 201, 228, and 233; and in relation to the latter, to the same work, pp. 106 and 184.]

definition: [ More, and most, wrongful, unjust, injurious, or tyrannical, in conduct ].
sourceDefinition: [ More, and most, wrongful, unjust, injurious, or tyrannical, in conduct ]. El-Muärrij says, I heard an Arab of the desert say to his companion, A^aZolamiY waA^aZolamuka fafaEala A@ll~`hu bihi , meaning The more wrongful in conduct of me and of thee [ may God do to him what He will do; i. e. may God punish him]. (T.) [And] one says, laEana A@ll~`hu A^aZolamiY waA^aZolamaka i. e. [ May God curse ] the more wrongful in conduct of us. (K. [But in the TA, a doubt is intimated as to the correctness of this latter saying.]) One says also, lahuwa A^aZolamu mino Hay~apK [i. e. Verily he is more wrongful in conduct than a serpent ]: because it comes to a burrow which it has not excavated, and makes its abode in it: (Fr, T:) for it comes to the burrow of the [lizard called] Dab~ , and eats its young one, and takes up its abode in its burrow. (TA voce Hay~apN .) ― -b2- And AlA^aZolamu is an appellation of The Dab~ ; because it eats its young ones. (TA.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) A house, or chamber, decorated with pictures;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A house, or chamber, decorated with pictures; (M, TA;) as though the pictures were put therein where they should not be: it is related in a trad. that the Prophet, having been invited to a repast, saw the house, or chamber, to be muZal~am , and turned away, not entering: (M:) or adorned with gilding and silvering; an explanation disapproved by Az, but pronounced by Z to be correct, from AlZ~alomu signifying “ the lustre, and brightness, of gold. ” (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Herbage spreading ( munobav~N [in the CK munobat ]) upon the ground, not rained upon. (K, TA.) ― -b3- Also, of birds, (assumed tropical:) The raxam [or vultur percnopterus ], and crows, or ravens. (IAar, M, K. *)

definition: A thing, (S, O,) or anything, (TA,) hard: (S, O:) or strong, hard, and erect: (Lth, O, K:) or thick;
sourceDefinition: A thing, (S, O,) or anything, (TA,) hard: (S, O:) or strong, hard, and erect: (Lth, O, K:) or thick; (As, AHn, O;) as also ↓ EaAridN and EurudN [correctly ↓ Eurud~N ] and EurayodN [evidently a mistranscription for ↓ EurunodN ] and ↓ EaridN : (AHn, O:) and ↓ EaranodadN , (S, O, K,) quasi-coordinate to safarojalN , (S, O,) and ↓ EurunodN , (K, TA,) with two dammehs, (TA, in the CK Euranod ,) the n being a substitute for d , (TA,) and ↓ EaridN (O, K) and ↓ Eurud~N , (K,) signify hard, (S, O, K,) or hard and strong, applied to anything: (TA:) and ↓ Eurud~N , applied to a spear, and a bow-string, signifies strong: (Fr, TA:) and ↓ EurunodN , in measure like turunojN , applied to a bow-string, (Sb, S, O,) thick; (Sb, S;) or strong and thick; as also ↓ Eurud~N ; and thus both signify applied to a rope, or well-rope, and any other thing. (O.) One says, A_in~ahu laEarodu magurizi AlEunuqi [ Verily he is hard, or strong, or thick, in respect of the base of the neck ]. (Lth, O, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] The penis: or a hard and strong penis: (TA:) or a penis distended and erect (O, K, TA) and hard: pl. A^aEoraAdN . (TA.) ― -b3- And The ass: (O, K:) so called because of the thickness of his neck. (TA.) ― -b4- And [it is said to signify] The base of the neck. (K. [But this I think doubtful: see a saying mentioned above (in this paragraph), from a mistranscription of which it may have originated.])

definition: [The lycium, or box-thorn;
sourceDefinition: [The lycium, or box-thorn; of several species; but now particularly applied to the lycium Europæum of Linn.: accord. to Sprengel (Hist. rei herb. p. 252, as stated by Freytag), applied to the zizyphus spina Christi, which is the rhamnus spina Christi of Linn.; but this is the sidor :] a species of thorn: (S, O, K: *) certain trees of the thorn-kind, (L,) having a round red fruit [or berry ] like the carnelian-bead, (O, L,) which is sweet, and is eaten: (O:) or a species of thorntrees having a bitter red fruit in which is acidity, called muSoEN : (Msb:) or certain trees having many thorns, and of several species, whereof is one that produces a red fruit, called muSoEN , in which is acidity: (T:) when it grows large, it is called garoqadN : (O, Msb:) and because of the softness of its wood, the women of the Arabs of the desert make of it spindles for spinning wool: (O:) the n. un. is with p : (S, O, Msb: [in the K, EawosajN is termed the pl. of EawosajapN :]) and it is said that the pl. of the n. un. is EawaAsiju : (TA:) ISd says, the genuine Eawosaj is short between the knots, hard in the wood, small in the leaves, and does not grow large, and this is the best sort: thus says AHn: (L:) some say that it is the Elyq [i. e. Eul~ayoq , q. v.]: Dioscorides says, it is a tree that grows in tracts that exude water and produce salt, having erect thorny branches, and leaves somewhat long, overspread with a moist viscous substance: and there is another species, whiter than this: and another species, of which the leaves are blacker than those of the former, and wider, inclining a little to redness, and its branches are long, their length being about five cubits, and having more numerous thorns, and weaker, and less sharp, and its fruit is wide and thin, as though it were in sheaths: and the Ewsj has a fruit like the twv [or mulberry ], which is eaten: it grows mostly in cold, or cool, countries. (Avicenna [Ibn-Seenà], book ii. p. 232. [In this extract from Dioscorides, in the original, are some unimportant words which I have passed over, including two imperfectly printed, and unintelligible: and what is said in it respecting the fruit I think doubtful, as being inapplicable to the fruit of the box-thorn.])

definition: A period of eight days between [ camels' ] twice coming to water;
sourceDefinition: A period of eight days between [ camels' ] twice coming to water; for they come to water on the tenth day [counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first]; and in like manner, the term for every one of the periods between two waterings is with kesr: [see vilovN :] (S, O:) or camels' coming to water on the tenth day [ after the next preceding period of abstinence, i. e., counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]: or on the ninth day [ not counting the day of the next preceding watering; for it is evident that these two explanations are virtually one and the the same]; (K;) as in the Shems el-'Uloom, on the authority of Kh, where it is added that they keep them from the water nine nights and eight days, and then bring them to water on the ninth day, which is the tenth from [by which is meant including] the former [day of] watering: (TA:) after the Ei$or , there is no name for a period between the two waterings until the twentieth [day]; (S, O;) but you say, hiYa taridu Ei$orFA wagib~FA , and Ei$orFA wariboEFA , [and so on,] to the twentieth [day counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first]; (As;) and then you say, that their period between two waterings is Ei$oraAni , (As, S, O,) i. e., eighteen days; (S, O;) and when they exceed this, they are termed jawaAziy^u [meaning “ that satisfy themselves with green pasture so as not to need water ”]. (As, S, O.) ― -b2- Also The eighth young one, or offspring. (A in art. vlv .) -A2- And A piece that is broken off from a cooking-pot, (K, TA,) or from a drinking-cup or bowl, (TA,) and from anything; (K, TA;) as though it were one of ten pieces; (TA;) as also ↓ Eu$aArapN , (K, TA,) which signifies a piece of anything: (O, TA:) pl. of the former, A^aEo$aArN [and pl. pl. A^aEaA$iyru ]; (TA;) and of ↓ the latter, Eu$aAraAtN . (O, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] buromapN A^aEo$aArN A cookingpot, or one of stone, broken in pieces: thus [we find the latter word] occurring in the pl. form [and used as an epithet]. (S, O.) And qidorN A^aEo$aArN A cooking-pot broken into ten pieces: (K:) or a large cooking-pot, of ten pieces joined together by reason of its largeness: (A:) or a cooking-pot so large that it is carried by ten men, (K,) or by ten women: (TA:) or [simply] a cooking-pot broken in pieces; not derived from anything: (TA:) pl. quduwrN A^aEo$aArN , (A,) and A^aEaA$iyru . (A, K.) And jafonN A^aEo$aArN [ A scabbard of a sword, or a sword-case, ] broken in pieces. (O.) And qalobN A^aEo$aArN [(assumed tropical:) A broken heart. ] (S, K.) And A^aEo$aAru jazuwrK The portions of a slaughtered camel [for which players at the game called Almayosir contend, and which are ten in number; not seven, as is said in one place in the TA. In Har p. 579, AE$Ar in this case is said to be pl. of Eu$orN ; but I think that we have better reason for regarding it as a pl. of Ei$orN ]. (Az, S, O, K.) Imra-el-Keys says, wamaA *arafato EayonaAki A_il~aA litaDoribiY bisahomayoki fiY A^aEo$aAri qalobK muqat~ali [ And thine eyes did not shed tears but that thou mightest play with thy two arrows for the portions of a heart subdued and killed by the passion of love ]: he means, by the two arrows, the two called AlmuEal~aY and Alr~aqiyb ; to the former of which are assigned seven portions, and to the latter, three; so that both together gain all the portions; for the slaughtered camel is divided into ten portions: therefore he means that she has played for his heart with her two arrows, [alluding to the glances shot from her eyes,] and gained possession of it altogether: (Az, S, * O: * [see also a verse cited voce raqiybN :]) or accord. to some, he means that his heart had been broken, and then repaired like as cooking-pots are repaired: but Az says that the former explanation, which is mentioned by Th, pleases him more. (TA.) Hence the saying, Daraba fiY A^aEo$aArihi walamo yaroDa bimiEo$aArihi [ He played for all the portions of it, and was not content with the fifth of it ]; meaning he took the whole of it. (A.) ― -b3- And A^aEo$aArN alone means Cooking-pots that boil the ten portions [ of a jazuwr ]. (Har. p. 579.) -A3- A^aEo$aArN also signifies The primary feathers of the wing of a bird; (S, O, TA;) and so ↓ EawaA$iru . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ Ten; ] the first of the Euquwd ; (A, K;) with p , (Msb,) and with fet-h to the $ , (TA,) for the masc.; (Msb, TA;) and Ea$orN , without p , (Msb, TA,) and with one fet-hah, (TA,) for the fem. (Msb, TA.) You say, Ea$arapu rijaAlK [ Ten men ]: and Ea$oru nisowapK [ ten women ]. (S, O, Msb, TA.) [In De Sacy's Arabic Grammar, for the former is inadvertently put Ea$orapN ; and for the latter, Ea$arN ; and in Freytag's lexicon we find Ea$arN instead of Ea$orN .] Ea$araAtN [is the pl. of Ea$arapN : and also] signifies Decimal numbers. (M in art. st .) The vulgar make Ea$orN masc., as meaning a number of days, saying AlEa$oru AlA^aw~alu , and AlEa$oru AlA^axiyru ; but this is wrong [unless thereby they mean to speak of nights with their days, as will be shown by what follows]: the month consists of three Ea$araAt ; namely, AlEa$oru AlA^uwalu [ The first ten nights. with their days], pl. of A^uwlaY ; and AlEa$oru AlwusaTu [ The middle ten nights, with their days], pl. of wusoTaY ; and AlEa$oru AlA^axaru [ The last, lit. the other, ten nights, with their days], pl. of A^uxoraY ; or AlEa$oru AlA^awaAxiru [ The last ten nights, with their days], pl. of A=xrapN . (Msb.) [ AlEa$oru AlA^awaAxiru is also especially applied to The last ten nights of Ramadán, with their days: and Ea$oru *iY AlHij~api to The first ten nights of Dhu-l-Hijjeh, with their days: and AlEa$oru , alone, to The first ten nights of El-Moharram, with their days.] The Arabs also said, sironaA Ea$orFA , meaning We journeyed ten nights, with their days; making the fem. [ layaAlK ] to predominate over the masc. [ A^ay~aAm ]; as is the case in the Kur ii. 234. (Msb.) And A^ay~aAmu AlEa$ori is used for A^ay~aAmu All~ayaAliY AlEa$ori [ The days of the ten nights ]. (Mgh.) [See some other observations applying to the syntax of Ea$arapN and Ea$orN , voce xamosapN . And respecting a peculiar pronunciation of the people of El-Hijáz, and a case in which Ea$arap is imperfectly decl., see valaAvapN .] ― -b2- [ Ea$orN is also applied to A portion, or paragraph, of the Kur-án properly consisting of ten verses; but it is often applied to somewhat more, or less, than what is considered by some, or by all, as ten verses, either because there is much disagreement as to the divisions of the verses or for the sake of beginning and ending with a break in the tenour of the text: (see EaA$irapN :) pl. A^aEo$aArN . These divisions have no mark to distinguish them in some MSS.: in others, each is marked by a round ornament at the end; or by the word E$r , or the letter E , over, or over against, the commencement.] ― -b3- When you have passed the number ten, you make the masc. fem., and the fem. masc. [to nineteen inclusively]: in the masc., you reject the p in Ea$arap ; and from thirteen to nineteen [inclusively], you add p to the former of the two nouns; and [in every case] you pronounce the $ with fet-h; and you make the two nouns one noun, [and, as such,] indecl., with fet-h for the termination: (TA:) you say, A^aHada Ea$ara [ Eleven ], (S, O, Msb,) [and AivonaA Ea$ara Twelve, ] and valaAvapa Ea$ara [ Thirteen ], and so on; (Msb, TA;) with fet-h to the $ ; and in one dial. with sukoon [ A^aHada Ea$ora , &c.]; (Msb;) or the former only: (S, O:) and, as ISk says, some of the Arabs make the E quiescent, [as many do in the present day,] saying A^aHada Eo$ara , and so on to tisoEapa Eo$ara [inclusively] except in the instance of AivonaA Ea$ara and AivonaYo Ea$ara , because of the quiescence of the A and Y ; and Akh says that they make the E quiescent because the noun is long and its vowels are many: (S, O) in the fem., you add p to the latter of the two nouns, and reject the p in the former of them, and make the $ in E$rp quiescent: you say A_iHodaY Ea$orapa (TA,) [and AivonataA Ea$orapa ,] and so on to tisoEa Ea$orapa [inclusively]: and if you choose, you say A_iHodaY Ea$irapa , [&c.,] with kesr to the $ : the former is of the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, [and is the more common,] and the latter is of the dial. of the people of Nejd: (S, O, TA:) but fet-h to the $ in this case is unknown to the grammarians and lexicologists, as Az says, though an instance has been adduced in an unusual reading of the Kur ii. 57, and another in vii. 160. (TA.) Every noun of number, from eleven to nineteen [inclusively], is mansoob, [or more properly speaking, each of the two nouns of which it is composed is indecl., with fet-h,] in the cases of refa and nasb and khafd, except that of twelve; for AivonaA and AivonataA are decl. [i. e. you say, in a case of nasb or khafd, AivonaYo Ea$ara and AivonataYo Ea$orapa ]. (TA.) ― -b4- [In the same manner also Ea$ara and Ea$orapa are used in the ordinal compounds,]

sourceDefinition: A she-camel that has been ten months pregnant, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) from the day of her having been covered by the stallion: she then ceases to be [of those] called maxaADF , and she is called E$rA until she brings forth, and also after she has brought forth, (S, O,) or when she has brought forth, at the completion of a year: or when she has brought forth she is termed EaAti*N : (TA:) or that has been eight months pregnant: or, applied to a she-camel, i. q. nufasaA='u applied to a woman: (K:) it is applied also to any female that is pregnant, but mostly to the female of the horse and camel: (IAth:) it is the only sing. word of this measure, which is a pl. measure, except nufasaA='u : (MF:) the dual is Eu$araAwaAni : (S, O, TA; in one copy of the S Eu$oraAwaAni :) and pl. Eu$araAwaAtN ; (S, O, K, TA; in one copy of the S, and in the CK Eu$orAwAt ;) but some disallow this; (MF;) and Ei$aArN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) like as nifaAsN is pl. of nufasaA='u ; (Msb;) and Eu$aArN : (K in art. nfs :) or Ei$aArN is applied to she-camels until some of them have brought forth and others are expected to bring forth. (K.) Some say that Ei$aAr have no milk; though El-Farezdak applies this term to camels that are milked, because of their having recently brought forth; and it is said that camels are most precious to their owners when they are E$Ar . (TA.) Ea$aAy^iru , as pl. of Ei$aArN , which is pl. of Eu$araA='u , signifies Gazelles that have recently brought forth. (O.)

(K.) Some say that Ei$aAr have no milk; though El-Farezdak applies this term to camels that are milked, because of their having recently brought forth; and it is said that camels are most precious to their owners when they are E$Ar . (TA.) Ea$aAy^iru , as pl. of Ei$aArN , which is pl. of Eu$araA='u , signifies Gazelles that have recently brought forth. (O.)

sourceDefinition: Twenty; twice ten: (K:) applied alike to a masc. and a fem.: (Msb:) you say Ei$oruwna rajulFA [ Twenty men ], and Ei$oruwna A@moraA^apF [ Twenty women: the noun following it being in the accus. case as a specificative]: (TA:) it is decl. with w and Y [like a pl. formed by the addition of w and n ]; (Msb;) and when you prefix it to another noun, making it to govern the latter in the gen. case, you drop the n , (S, Msb,) and say, Ei$oruw zayodK [ The twenty of Zeyd ], (Msb,) and Ei$oruwka [ Thy twenty ], (S, O, Msb,) and Ei$uriY~ [ My twenty ], changing the w into Y [in this last case], because of the letter following it, and these incorporating: (S, O:) so says Ks; but most disallow this mode of prefixing in the case of a decimal number [of this kind], (Msb.) [It signifies also Twentieth. ] It is not a pl. of Ea$arapN , (so in a copy of the S and in the O and in the TA.) or Ea$orN , (so in another copy of the S,) [or perhaps the right reading is Ei$orN , as may be inferred from what will be presently added: but first it should be observed that if it were pl. of Ea$arapN , or of Ea$orN , it would signify at least three times ten: some hold it to be a pl. of Ei$orN , saying, (TA.) as Ei$orN signifies camels' coming to water on the ninth day, they do not say Ei$oraAni [for twenty], but they say Ei$oruwna , (in the K, lamo yuqalo Ei$orayoni waqaAluwA Ei$oriyna : but the correct reading seems to be lamo yaquwluwA : TA: [in the CK it is more incorrect, lm yql Ei$oriyna wqAlwA Ei$orayoni :]) making eighteen days to be Ei$oraAni , and the nineteenth and twentieth a portion of the third Ei$or ; and so, [regarding the portion as a whole,] forming the pl. Ei$oruwna ; (K, * TA;) agreeably with a well-known license, which allows the calling two and a part of the third a pl: (TA:) this is the opinion of Kh and IDrd and some others: but J and most of the lexicologists hold that Ei$oruwna is not a pl. of Ea$arapN nor of Ei$orN nor of any other word, and their opinion I hold to be correct, applying as it does to the other similar nouns of number. (MF.)

definition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ EaA$irN (O, Msb, K) and ↓ muEa$~irN (TA) One who takes, or receives, the Eu$or [q.
sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ EaA$irN (O, Msb, K) and ↓ muEa$~irN (TA) One who takes, or receives, the Eu$or [q. v.] of property. (S, Msb, K.) Where the punishment of the Ea$~aAr , or EaA$ir , is mentioned in traditions, as where it is said that the EaA$ir is to be put to death, the meaning is, he who takes the tenth as the people in the Time of Ignorance used to do: such is to be put to death because of his unbelief; or because, being a Muslim, he holds this practice to be lawful: but such as performed the like office for the Prophet and for the Khaleefehs after him may be thus called because of the relation of what he takes to the tenth, as the quarter of the tenth, and the half of the tenth, and as he takes the tenth wholly of the produce that is watered [only] by the rain, and the tenth of the property in merchandise [of foreigners, and half the tenth of that] of non-Muslim subjects. (TA.) [There is either a mistake or an omission in the last part of the statement above, in the TA, which I have rectified by inserting “ of foreigners ” &c.]

definition: A company, or collective body, (Az, S, O, Msb, K,) of people, (S,) consisting of men, exclusive of women;
sourceDefinition: A company, or collective body, (Az, S, O, Msb, K,) of people, (S,) consisting of men, exclusive of women; like nafarN and qawomN and rahoTN ; (Az, Msb;) having no proper sing.: (Az:) or any company, or collective body, whose state of circumstances is one; a community; as the mE$r of the Muslims and that of the Polytheists: (Lth:) or a great company, or collective body; so called [from Ea$arapN ,] because they are many; for E$rp is that large and perfect number after which there is no number but what is composed of the units comprised in it: (MF:) or the family of a man: or jinn (i. e. genii ) and mankind: (K: [or the author of the K may mean, or jinn: and also mankind: ]) in the Kur [vi. 130, and lv. 33], we find the expression yaA maEo$ara A@lojin~i waA@loA_inosi ; but this means O mE$r consisting of the jinn and of mankind: and [vi. 128], yaA maEo$ara Aljin~i , without the mention of AlAns : (MF:) pl. maEaA$iru . (S, Msb.) [See also Ea$iyrapN .] -A2- maEo$ara : see Eu$aAra , in four places.

EaqobN and EuquwbN , (Msb, TA,) He came after him; [as though at his heel; and hence, properly, close after him; but often meaning near after him; ] (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) followed him; succeeded him; (S, Mgh, K, TA;) came in, or took, his place; as also ↓ AEqbhu : (S, K, TA:) and in like manner both are said of anything, (TA,) as also ↓ Eq~bhu , (Msb, K, TA,) inf. n. taEoqiybN ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ EAqbhu ; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ AEtqbhu ; (TA;) meaning it came after; (S, * Msb, K, * TA;) &c., as above: (TA:) and ↓ tEq~bhu is used in this sense, but not rightly. (Mgh.) [All primarily denote proximate sequence.] You say, EaqabuwnaA and EaqabuwA mino xalofinaA They came after us. (TA.) And EaqabuwnaA mino xalofinaA and ↓ Eaq~abuwnaA They succeeded us, in alighting, or taking up their abode, after our departure. (TA.) And AlEid~apu taEoqubu AlT~alaAqa The Eid~ap [q. v.] follows divorce. (Mgh, Msb.) And A@bonuhu ↓ *ahaba fulaAnN faA^aEoqabahu , as also Eaqabahu , Such a one went away, and his son succeeded him, or took his place. (S, O.) And h`*aA h`*aA ↓ AEqb [ This succeeded this ] is said when the latter is gone, and there remains nothing of it, and the former has taken its place. (TA.) And one says, Eaqaba fulaAnN makaAna A^abiyhi , (S, O, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaqobN , (TA,) and quasi-inf. n. ↓ EaAqibapN , this being a subst. used in the sense of an inf. n., like as kaA*ibapN is [said to be] in the Kur lvi. 2, (S, O,) or it is an inf. n. syn. with EaqobN , (Msb in art. Efw ,) Such a one succeeded, or took the place of, his father; (S, O, TA;) as also ↓ Eq~b . (TA.) [Hence also several phrases here following.] ― -b3- It is said in a trad., kul~u gaAziyapK gazato yaEoqubu baEoDuhaA baEoDFA i. e. [ Every party that goes forth on a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition ] shall take its turn, one after another: ] when one company has gone forth and returned, it shall not be constrained to go forth again until another has taken its turn after it. (TA.) ― -b4- Eaqabotu Alr~ajula fiY A^aholihi means bagayotuhu bi$ar~K waxalafotuhu [i. e. I sought to do evil to the man, and took his place (see art. xlf ), with respect to his wife; i. e. I committed adultery with his wife ]: (S, O:) or Eaqabahu signifies [simply] bigaAhu bi$ar~K [ he sought to do evil to him ]: (K: [in which waxalafahu seems to have been inadvertently omitted: but SM immediately adds what here follows:]) and one says also, Eaqaba fiY A_ivori Alr~ajuli bimaA yukorahu , aor. , inf. n. EaqobN , meaning He accused the man [app. behind his back ] of a thing disliked, or hated; he [ so ] defamed him, or charged him with a vice or fault or the like. (TA.) ― -b5- Eaqaba fulaAnN EalaY fulaAnapa [like xalafa EalayohaA ] Such a man married such a woman after her first husband. (TA.) ― -b6- Eaqaba Al$~ayobu , aor. and , inf. n. EuquwbN , Whiteness of the hair, or hoariness, came after [or took the place of ] blackness: as also ↓ Eq~b . (TA.) ― -b7- Eaqaba said of a horse, aor. [or ?], inf. n. EaqobN , [which see below,] He performed a run after another run. (L, TA.) ― -b8- Eaqabati AlA_ibilu mino makaAnK A_ilaY makaAnK , aor. , inf. n. EaqobN ; and ↓ AEtqbt ; The camels removed from place to place, pasturing. (IAar, TA.) ― -b9- maA Eaqaba fiyhaA faEalayoka mino maAlika , (TA,) or ↓ maA Eaq~aba , (so in the O, [in which fiY mAlk is put in the place of mn mAlk ,]) Whatever evil consequence happen to me, with respect to it, (referring to merchandise,) the responsibility for it will be on thee [and compensation shall be made from thy property ]: and [ taEoqibapN (thus in the O) appears, from what follows, to be an inf. n. of the latter verb in this sense; or it may perhaps be from the former verb, like taholikapN from halaka ; for] one says, baAEaniY siloEapF waEalayohi taEoqibapN A_ino kaAnat fiyhaA [ He sold me an article of merchandise, and was responsible for an evil consequence, (or for damage afterwards found in it,) should there be any in it ]. (ISh, O, TA. *) ― -b10- Eaqabahu and ↓ Eq~bhu and ↓ AEqbhu signify also He took, or received, from him something in exchange, an exchange, a substitute, or an equivalent, for another thing: it is said in a trad., A_ino lamo yaqoruwhu falahu A^ano yaEoqubahumo bimivoli qiraAhu If they entertain him not. he shall have a right to take from them as a substitute the like of his entertainment which they denied him: and one says also minohu xayorFA ↓ AstEqb , or $ar~FA , He took, or received, from him in exchange good, or evil: (TA:) and Eaqaba Alr~ajula , aor. , He took from the man's property the like of what he (the latter) had taken from him. (O, * TA.) After the words in the Kur lx. 11, waA_ino faAtakumo $aYo'N mino A^azowaAjikumo A_ilaY A@lokuf~aAri , there are three different readings, ↓ faEaAqabotumo , and ↓ faEaq~abotumo , and faEaqabotumo : (TA:) the first means and ye take, or carry off, spoil: (Masrook Ibn-El-Ajda', S, TA:) or the second has this meaning; and the first means and ye punish them so that ye take, or carry off, spoil: and the third means and ye have a requital: the second is the best; and the third is also good; but the second has a more intensive meaning: (Aboo-Is-hák the Grammarian, L, TA:) accord. to Fr, the first and second signify the same: (L, TA:) and As says that EaqobN [inf. n. of Eaqaba ] is syn. with EiqaAbN [inf. n. of EaAqaba ; but whether with reference to this case, I do not find]. (TA.) ― -b11- And Eaqaba , aor. , inf. n. EaqobN , also signifies He sought, or sought after, wealth, or some other thing. (TA.) -A2- Eaqaba , (S, O, K,) aor. and , (TA,) inf. n. EaqobN , (S, O,) He bound a thing with [ the kind of sinew, or tendon, called ] Eaqab ; as also ↓ Eq~b [inf. n. taEoqiybN , of which see an ex. in a verse cited voce maSonaEN ]: he bound therewith a xawoq . i. e. the ring of an ear-drop, fearing lest it should incline on one side: or he bound an earring with a thread called EuqaAb : (TA:) and he wound round a bow, (S, O, K,) and an arrow, (S, O,) with [ the kind of sinew, or tendon, called ] Eaqab , (O,) or with somewhat thereof: (S, K:) or Eaqabahu biAlEaqabi he bound it, namely, the [arrow termed] qidoH , with the Eaqab , in consequence of its having broken. (IB, L, TA.) -A3- EaqabonaA Alr~akiy~apa [thus I find it written without teshdeed, but perhaps it should be ↓ Eaq~abonaA , from A^aEoqaAbu AlT~aY~ , (see EaqibN ,)] We lined the well with stones behind [ the other ] stones. (TA. [See also 4.]) -A4- [The inf. n.] AlEaqobu also signifies Alr~ajoEu , [which generally means The making, or causing, to return, or go back; but this may perhaps be a mistake for Alr~ujuwEu , for it is immediately added,] Dhu-rRummeh says, kaA^an~a SiyaAHa Alkudori yanoZurona EaqobanaA taraATunu A^anobasATK Ealayohi TagaAmi meaning [ As though the crying of the dusky she-camels] looking, or waiting, for our returning from watering that they might go to the water after us [ were the barbarous talk of low, or ignoble, Nabathæans, over it, i. e. over the water]. (TA.) -A5- Eaqiba Aln~abotu , [aor. ,] inf. n. EaqabN , The branches of the plant, or herbage, became slender, and the leaves thereof turned yellow. (IAar, TA. [See also 2.])

sourceDefinition: see 1, first three quarters, in seven places. ― -b2- The inf. n., taEoqiybN , signifies also The doing a thing and then returning to doing it: (IAth, TA:) the performing an act of prayer, or another act, and then returning to doing it in the same day: (Sh, TA:) and [particularly] the making a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition, and then another in the same year. (S, O, K.) [See also muEaq~ibN .] You say, Eq~b biSalaApK baEoda SalaApK , and bigazaApK baEoda gazaApK , He followed up one prayer with another, and one warring, or warring and plundering, expedition with another. And Euq~iba AlgaAziyapu biA^amovaAlihaA , and ↓ A^uEoqiba , The warring, or warring and plundering, party was made to be followed by another, consisting of the likes of it, sent in its place. (TA.) sourceDefinition: : see 1, second sentence. ― -b2- Also EAqb Alr~ajula , (Mgh, * TA,) inf. n. muEaAqabapN and EiqaAbN , (Mgh,) He did a thing with the man alternately, each taking his turn; (Mgh, TA;) and so ↓ AEqbhu . (TA.) And [particularly], (TA,) inf. n. muEaAqabapN , (S, O,) He rode in his turn after the man, each riding in his turn; (S, O, TA;) as also ↓ AEqbhu , (S, O, K,) and ↓ AEtqbhu . (TA.) And EaAqabotu Alr~ajula fiY Alr~aAHilapi I rode in my turn after the man, upon the camel, he riding in his turn after me. (S, O.) And in like manner you say, ↓ AiEotaqabuwhu , and ↓ taEaAqabuwhu They rode by turns with him, taking their turns after him. (TA.) ― -b3- And EAqb bayona Al$~ayoy^ayoni [ He made an interchange, or alternation between the two things; he made the two things interchangeable, or commutable; ] he brought, or did, the two things interchangeably, or alternately, i. e. one of them one time and the other of them another time. (TA.) [Thus, for instance,] AlEarabu tuEaAqibu bayona AlfaA='i wAlv~aA='i [ The Arabs make an interchange between f and v ; make f and v interchangeable, or commutable; i. e. put f in the place of v , and v in the place of f ]; as in jadafN and jadavN ; and ↓ tuEoqibu signifies the same. (S, O.) ― -b4- And EAqb signifies also He stood upon one of his legs one time and upon the other another time; or moved his legs alternately. (TA.) ― -b5- [ EAqbhu as denoting consequence, and retaliation, or retribution, also signifies He punished him. ] You say, EAqbhu bi*anobihi , (S, Msb, * TA,) inf. n. EiqaAbN (S, Msb, TA) and muEaAqabapN , (Msb, TA,) He punished him for his crime, sin, fault, or offence: (S, * Msb, * TA:) and [in like manner] ↓ tEq~bhu He punished him (i. e. a man, S, O) for a crime, a sin, a fault, or an offence, that he had committed. (S, O, K.) In the saying in the Kur [xvi. last verse but one], waA_ino EaAqabotumo faEaAqibuwA bimivoli maA EuwqibotumN bihi [ And if ye punish, then punish ye with the like of that with which ye have been afflicted, lit. punished ], the verb first denotes punishment, and is afterwards used for the purpose of assimilation: and similar to this is the saying in the same [xxii. 59], wamano EaAqaba bimivoli maA Euwqiba bihi [ And whoso punisheth with the like of that with which he hath been afflicted, lit. punished ]. (O.) For another ex., from the Kur lx. 11, [where it implies retaliation or retribution,] see 1, latter half. [In like manner,] it is said in a trad., A^aboTala Aln~afoHa A_il~aA A^ano yuDoraba fayuEaAqiba [ He made the kicking of a beast with the hind leg to be of no account unless it were beaten by its master, or rider, and retaliated by kicking another person]; meaning, he made nothing to be incumbent on the master of the beast unless the latter made the kicking to be a consequence of that [i. e. unless the beast kicked in consequence of its being beaten by the master, or rider]. (TA.) [See also 4, which has a similar meaning, that of requital.] ― -b6- Euwqibato said of a mare means She was required to perform run after run. (Ham p. 277.)

(TA.) ― -b4- [And It made a thing to follow as a consequence to him: the verb in this sense being doubly trans.] One says, AEqbhu nadamFA It occasioned him as its consequence repentance, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and ham~FA anxiety. (TA.) And A^akala A^akolapF A^aEoqabatohu saqamFA He ate a repast that occasioned him as its consequence a sickness. (S, O.) And [hence] A^uEoqiba Eiz~uhu *ul~FA His might was exchanged for, or changed into, [lit. made to be followed by, ] abasement. (TA.) See also 2, first quarter, for another ex. See also 1, latter half, where the verb is expl. in the contr. sense, that of taking, or receiving, in exchange. ― -b5- AEqbhu AlT~aAy^ifu The diabolical visitation, or insanity, returned to him at times. (S, O.) ― -b6- AEqb TaY~a Albiy^ori biHijaArapK mino waraAy^ihaA [is app. from A^aEoqaAbu AlT~aY~i (see EaqibN ), and] means He laid stones compactly together at the back [ behind the regular casing ] of the well. (TA. [See also 1, near the end.]) -A2- AEqb as intrans., He (a man) died, and left offspring. (S, O, K.) One says, A^aEoqaba minohumo rajulaAni wadaraja waAHidN [ Two men of them died and left offspring, and one died and left no offspring ]: and Tufeyl El-Ghanawee says, kariymapu Hur~i Alwajohi lamo tadoEu haAlikFA ↓ mina Alqawomi hulokFA fiY gadK gayora muEoqibi [ A female noble of countenance, (or whose nobility was manifest in what appeared of her countenance,) she did not invoke one of the people dead, on a morrow after an engagement, as having perished without leaving a successor, or one to fill his place: ] i. e. when a chief of her people died, another chief came; so that she did not bewail a chief who had not his equal. (TA.) ― -b2- He (a borrower of a cooking-pot) returned a cooking-pot with the remains termed Euqobap in it. (S, O, K.) ― -b3- He (a man) returned from evil to good. (TA.) ― -b4- AEqb Ealayohi yaDoribuhu He set upon him beating him. (O.) ― -b5- A^aEoqabato raAHilatuka Thy riding-camel became, or has become, jaded, or fatigued. (O.)

definition: He looked to the consequence, end, issue, or result: and he considered a second time.
sourceDefinition: He looked to the consequence, end, issue, or result: and he considered a second time. (TA. [See also 2, last quarter.]) ― -b2- tEq~b mino A^amorihi He repented of his affair. (TA.) ― -b3- tEq~b Eani Alxabari He doubted of the information, or questioned it, and asked again respecting it. (S, O, K, TA. [In my copies of the S, and in the O, Alxayori : but see what follows; in which mutaEaq~ab is used as a noun of place of the verb in this sense.]) Tufeyl says, ↓ walamo yaku Eam~aA xab~aruwA mutaEaq~abu [ And there was no place of, or ground for, doubting, and asking again, respecting what they told ]. (S, O, TA.) And one says, lamo A^ajido Eano qawolika ↓ mutaEaq~abFA , (A, TA,) i. e. [ I found not ] any place of, or ground for, inquiring into, or investigating, thy saying; syn. mutafaH~aSFA ; (A, TA;) [or questioning it; or returning to examine it; ] meaning, thy saying was right and true, so that it did not require Alt~aEaq~ub ; (A;) or I did not allow myself to doubt, and ask again, respecting it, that I might see whether I should do what thou saidst or abstain from it. (TA.) ― -b4- [And the verb is used transitively in a similar sense.] You say, tEq~b Alxabara He searched after the information repeatedly, or time after time; (Mgh, * TA;) syn. tatab~aEa : (Mgh, TA:) and ↓ AEtqb has a like meaning. (Ham p. 287.) And He asked respecting the information another person than the one whom he asked the first time. (A, TA.) ― -b5- And taEaq~abotu Alr~ajula I sought to discover in the man that which he would be ashamed to expose; or the slip, or fault, that he had committed: and ↓ AisotaEoqabotuhu signifies the same. (O, K. *) [In critical observations and the like, tEq~bhu is often used as meaning He found fault with him; animadverted upon him; or impugned his judgment or assertion; biqawolihi ka*aA waka*aA by his saying so and so. And tEq~b Ealayohi seems to be similarly used as meaning He animadverted upon his saying: (compare AiEotaraDa Ealayohi :) but more commonly as meaning he animadverted upon it, i. e. a saying, and the like.] ― -b6- See also 3, near the middle of the para- graph. ― -b7- tEq~b AlA^amora He thought repeatedly upon the affair, or case. (TA in art. rwA^ .) ― -b8- tEq~b raA^oyahu He found his opinion to have a good issue, or result. (S, O. [See a somewhat similar signification of 8 and 10, under the former.]) ― -b9- See also 1, second sentence. ― -b10- [The saying of Aboo-Thumámeh, waA_ino manoTiqN zal~a Eano SaAHibiY ↓ taEaq~abotu A=xara *aA muEotaqabo may be rendered, nearly in accordance with an explanation by Et-Tebreezee, And if a speech slip by mistake from my companion, 1 substitute another having superiority: or tEq~bt may here mean I search out: but see the Ham p. 287; where are some remarks, on this verse, that appear to me to be fanciful and far-fetched.]

definition: (T, S, O, Msb, TA) They follow each other [ by turns ];
sourceDefinition: (T, S, O, Msb, TA) They follow each other [ by turns ]; or alternate; (T, Msb, TA;) one coming and the other going; (TA;) said of the night and the day; (T, Msb;) or as the night and the day; (S, O, TA;) as also ↓ yaEotaqibaAni . (TA.) You say, taEaAqaba AlmusaAfiraAni EalaY Ald~aAb~api The two travellers rode upon the beast, each of them in his turn. (TA: and the like is said in the Msb.) And tEAqbA EamalFA They two did a work, or deed, by turns, or alternately: syn. AirotawaHaAhu , (K and TA in art. rwH ,) and taraAwaHaAhu (TA in that art.) And tEAqbA They helped each other by turns. (TA.) And biAlD~arobi ↓ yaEotaqbaAnihi They two ply him by turns with beating (A.) See also 3, near the beginning. Alt~aEaAqubu also signifies The coming to water [ by turns, or] time after time. (TA.)

definition: The EaSab [meaning sinews, or tendons, ] of which A^awotaAr [i.
sourceDefinition: The EaSab [meaning sinews, or tendons, ] of which A^awotaAr [i. e. strings for bows or the like ] are made: (S, O, K: [see also 1, last quarter:]) n. un. with 3: (S, O:) or such as are white of the A^aTonaAb of the joints; (Mgh, Msb; [see EaSabN ;]) the EaSab being such as are yellow: (Mgh and Msb in art. ESb :) accord. to IAth, the EaSab [or sinews, or tendons, ] of the two portions of flesh next the back-bone on either side, and of the saAqaAni and waZiyfaAni [meaning the hind and fore shanks ], that are intermingled with the flesh, of any animal; the half of one whereof, divided lengthwise from the other half, is extended, or drown out, and trimmed, and cleansed of the flesh, and the watar [or string for the bow or the like ] is made thereof; and they are sometimes in the two sides of the camel; but [ properly speaking ] there is a difference between the EaSab and the Eqab ; the former being such as incline to yellow, whereas the latter incline to white, and are the harder, and firmer, or stronger, of the two: AHn says, on the authority of Aboo-Ziyád, that the Eaqab are [the sinews, or tendons, ] of the two portions of flesh next the back-bone on either side, of the sheep or goat, and of the camel, and of the ox or cow, (TA.) [See also EilobaA='N .]

definition: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ EaqobN , (Msb, TA,) the latter being a contraction of the former, (Msb,) [The heel of a human being;] the hinder part of the foot of a human being: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) of the fem. gender: (S, O, Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoqubN (TA) and [of mult. as well as of pauc.] A^aEoqaAbN : (Msb, TA:) and ↓ EaqiybN is said to signify the same; but MF cites an assertion that this is a word of a bad dialect. (TA.) wayolN liloA^aEoqaAbi mina Aln~aAri [ Wo to the heels from the fire of Hell], (O, Msb, TA,) and wyl liloEaqibi mn Aln~Ar [ Who to the heel &c.], (TA,) occurring in a trad., means wo to him who neglects the washing of the heels in the ablution preparatory to prayer. (O, * Msb, TA. *) Eaqibu Al$~ayoTaAni , (O, Msb, TA,) or, as some say, ↓ Euqobapu Al$yTAn , (Msb, TA,) with damm, (TA,) which is forbidden in prayer, is expl. as meaning The placing the buttocks upon the heels between the two prostrations; which is what some term AlA_iqoEaA='u : (Mgh, * O, Msb, TA:) so says A'Obeyd: (Msb:) or, accord. to some, this means the leaving the heels unwashed in the ablution preparatory to prayer. (O.) waTiy^a Aln~aAsu Eaqiba fulaAnK [lit. The people trod upon the heel of such a one ] means the people walked after, or near after, such a one: and in like manner, huwa muwaT~aA^u AlEaqibi [lit. He is one whose heel is trodden upon ]: (O, TA; *) because of his having command over people, and their being submissive to him: (O:) the latter phrase means he is one who has many followers: (A, TA: [see also art. wTA^ :]) jaA='a zayodN yaTaA^u Eaqiba EamorKw primarily signifies Zeyd came putting his foot in the place of the foot [or heel ] of 'Amr every time that the latter raised his foot. (Msb.) And one says, mino A^ayona Eaqibuka , (A, O,) or mino A^ayona kaAna Eaqibuka , (TA,) meaning Whence camest thou? or Whence hast thou come? (A, O, TA.) And rajaEa fulaAnN EalaY Eaqibihi Such a one returned by the way of his heel; i. e., by the way that was behind him, and whence he had come; quickly. (Msb.) And wal~aY EalaY Eaqibihi , and EalaY Eaqibayohi , He turned back, or receded, from a thing to which he had betaken himself. (TA.) laA tarud~ahumo EalaY A^aEoqaAbihimo , occurring in a trad., means Turn not thou them back to their former condition of not emigrating [for the sake of religion]: and maA zaAluwA murotad~iyna EalaY A^aEoqaAbihimo , in another trad., means They ceased not to return to infidelity: as though they went back wards. (TA.) ― -b2- The Eaqib of the naEol [or sandal] is The part [or wide strap ] that embraces the heel. (AO, in an anom. sourceDefinition: : see EaqibN , in three places. ― -b2- Also The last that remains: so in the saying, fulaAnN Euqobapu baniY fulaAnK [ Such a one is the last that remains of the sons of such a one ]. (L.) ― -b3- And A turn; or time at which, or during which, anything is, or is to be, done, or had, in succession: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) pl. EuqabN . (Msb.) One says, tam~ato Euqobatuka Thy turn is completed. (S, O.) And daArato Euqobapu fulaAnK The turn of such a one came round. (TA.) And rakiba EuqobapF He rode one turn: and rakiba Euqobatahu He rode his turn, or in his turn. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., mano ma$aY Eano daAb~atipi EuqobapF falahu ka*aA Whoso walks a turn to a certain point, instead of his beast, to him shall be given such a thing. (TA.) Euqobapu AlA^jiyri means The hired-man's turn to ride; when the hirer dismounts, for example in the morning, and he ( the former ) rides. (Mgh.) And [the pl.] EuqabN means [particularly] The turns of camels, when they are being watered: the watering of a number of camels together after another number is termed their Euqobap . (TA.) definition: (Lh, S, O, K) and ↓ EuqobapN , (Lh, O, K,) but the former is the more approved, (Lh, TA,) and Eqb , (so in the TA, [app.
sourceDefinition: (Lh, S, O, K) and ↓ EuqobapN , (Lh, O, K,) but the former is the more approved, (Lh, TA,) and Eqb , (so in the TA, [app., if not a mistranscription, ↓ EaqibN ,]) A mark, sign, trace, impress, characteristic, or outward indication. (Lh, S, O, K.) One says, Ealayohi Eiqobapu Als~arowi , (S, O,) and ↓ Euqobatuhu , (O,) and AljamaAli , (S, O,) i. e. Upon him is the mark &c. [ of generosity and manliness, and of beauty ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- Eiqobapu Alqamari and ↓ Eaqobapu Alqmr mean The return of the moon, when it has set, or disappeared, and then risen: (L:) [or the return of the moon after the change; for] one says, maA yafoEalu *`lika A_il~aA Eiqobapa Alqamari , (S,) or ↓ Euqobapa Alqmr , (so in the O,) meaning He does not that save once in each month: (S, O:) but, accord. to IAar, Alqamari ↓ Euqobapu , with damm, is a certain star, or asterism, which is in conjunction with the moon once in the year; and Euqobapa Alqamari means once in the year: so in the following verse, of one of the Benoo-'Ámir: laA yuToEimu Almisoka waAlkaAfuwra lim~atahu walaA Al*~ariyrapa A_il~aA Euqobapa Alqamari [ He will not apply to his hair that descends below the ear musk and camphor, nor the perfume called *ryrp , save once in the year ]: or, as Lh relates it, Eiqobapa Alqmr : thus in the L; in which it is added that this saying of IAar requires consideration, because the moon cuts [a meridian of] the celestial sphere once in every month: but MF replies that it may be in conjunction with the said star only once in the year, as the moon's path varies in each successive month. (TA. [See also EaqomapN .]) -A2- See also EaqobapN .
