definition: [ A mountain-road;
sourceDefinition: [ A mountain-road; ] a road in [or upon ] a mountain: (Bd in xc. 11:) or a road in the upper part of a mountain: (Ham p. 287:) or a difficult place of ascent of the mountains: (K:) or it is in a mountain and the like thereof: (Msb:) or [it sometimes signifies] a long mountain that lies across the way, and over which the way therefore leads; long, or high, and very difficult; so called, too, when it is further impassable after it is ascended; rising high towards the sky, ascending and descending; most difficult of ascent; but sometimes its height is one [or uniform ]; and its acclivity is in appearance like a wall: (TA:) [generally it means a road over, or up, or down, or over some part of, a mountain: ] pl. EiqaAbN . (S, O, Msb, K.) AiqotaHama AlEaqabapa [properly signifying He attempted the mountain-road ] is metaphorically used as meaning He entered upon a hard, or difficult, affair. (Bd in xc. 11.) See also EuqobapN , near the end. ― -b2- It is also n. un. of EaqabN [q. v.]. (S, O.)

definition: [The eagle; ] a certain bird, (S, O, K,) of those that prey, (Msb,) well known: (K:) of the fem. gender: (S, O, Msb:) [though] applied to the male and the female; but with this distinction, that you...
sourceDefinition: [The eagle; ] a certain bird, (S, O, K,) of those that prey, (Msb,) well known: (K:) of the fem. gender: (S, O, Msb:) [though] applied to the male and the female; but with this distinction, that you say of the male, h`*aA EuqaAbN *akarN [ This is a male eagle ]: or it is only female; and a bird of another kind couples with it; whence Ibn-'Oneyn says, satirizing a person named Ibn-Seyyideh, Say thou to Ibn-Seyyideh, maA A^anota A_il~aA kaA@loEuqaAbi faA^um~uhu maEoruwfapN walahu A^abN majohuwlu [“ Thou art not other than the like of the eagle; ” for his mother is known, but he has a father unknown ]: (MF, TA:) the pl. (of pauc., S, O) is A^aEoqubN , (S, O, K,) because it is of the fem. gender and the measure A^afoEulN specially belongs to pls. of fem. nouns [though not to such exclusively], (S, O,) and A^aEoqibapN , (Kr, TA,) and (of mult., S, O) EiqobaAnN (S, O, K) and EaqaAy^ibu accord. to AHei, but Ed-Demámeenee thinks this to be strange; and pl. pl. EaqaAbiynu . (TA.) EiqobaAnu Aljiro*aAni [ The eagles that prey upon the large field-rats ] are not black, but of the colour termed kuhobap ; and no use is made of their feathers, except that boys feather with them round-topped pointless arrows. (AHn, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlEuqaAbu is the name of (assumed tropical:) One of the northern constellations, [i. e. Aquila, ] the stars of which are nine within the figure, and six without, of the former of which are three well known, called Aln~asoru AlT~aAy^iru [q. v.]. (Kzw.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) The EuqaAb of the banner, or standard; (S, O;) [app. meaning the flag attached to a lance; ] what is bound [ to a lance ] for a prefect, or governor; likened to the bird so called; and of the fem. gender. (L, TA.) It is also the name of (assumed tropical:) The banner, or standard, of the Prophet. (O, K.) And EuqaAbN also means (assumed tropical:) A large banner or standard. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) i. q. gaAyapN : so in the saying of Aboo-Dhu-eyb, describing wine, lahaA gaAyapN tahodiY AlkiraAma EuqaAbuhaA [meaning It has a banner, which guides the generous; like as the military banner guides and attracts warriors: for gaAyapN sometimes signifies a sign which the vintner used to set up to attract customers]: the repetition is approvable because of the difference of the two words in themselves: pl. EiqobaAnN . (TA.) ― -b4- EuqaAbN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A black she-camel; as being likened to the bird. [so called], (AA, O.) ― -b5- And A stone (or piece of rock, L) protruding in the inside of a well, which lacerates the [ leathern ] bucket; (S, O, K, TA;) sometimes it is before [i. e. above ] the casing [ of stones or bricks ]: it is when a mass of stone becomes displaced; and sometimes the water-drawer stands upon it: it is of the fem. gender: pl. as above. (TA.) And The stone upon which the waterer stands, (O, K,) [accord. to SM,] projecting beyond the casing in a well, the same that is meant in the next preceding sentence, (TA,) [but this I think doubtful, for Sgh adds,] between two stones which support it. (O.) Accord. to IAar, the qabiylap is a mass of stone, or rock, at the mouth of a well; and the EuqaAbaAni are [ two masses of stone ] at the two sides of the qbylp , supporting it. (TA.) And A rock, or mass of stone, projecting in the side of a mountain, like a stair, or series of steps: (S, O, K:) or an ascent, like stairs, in the side of a mountain. (TA.) ― -b6- Also A hill; syn. raAbiyapN . (O, K.) And Anything elevated, that is not very long or tall. (O, K. *) ― -b7- A channel by which water flows to a trough, or tank. (O, K.) ― -b8- A thing resembling an almond, that comes forth in one of the legs of a beast. (O, K.) ― -b9- A small thread that enters into [or passes through ] the two bores of the ring of the quroT [or ear-drop ], (O, K, *) with which the latter is bound, or fastened: (O:) or, accord. to Az, the thread that binds the two extremities of the ring of the quroT . (TA.) ― -b10- Accord. to Th, it signifies also Garments of the kind called A^aboraAd [pl. of burodN , q. v.]. (TA voce xudaAriy~apN .) ― -b11- And accord. to Kr, [in the Munjid,] i. q. HarovN [app. meaning A ploughshare ]. (TA.) ― -b12- See also A^aEoqaAbN . ― -b13- And AlEuqaAbaAni signifies Two pieces of wood between which a man is extended to be flogged: (L, TA:) or two pieces of wood which are set up, stuck in the ground, between which he who is beaten, or he who is [ to be ] crucified, is extended. (Mgh.)

definition: Anything that is a sequent, of, or to, another thing;
sourceDefinition: Anything that is a sequent, of, or to, another thing; [ in an absolute sense, ] (S, Msb, TA,) as when you say, Als~alaAmu EaqiybN lilt~a$ah~udi [ The salutation is a sequent to the t$h~d (q. v.)], and AlEid~apu EaqiybN lilT~alaAqi [ The Eid~ap (q. v.) is a sequent to divorcement ], i. e., one follows the other; (Msb;) and [ by alternation, ] as when one says of the night and the day, kul~u waAHidK minohumaA Eaqiybu SaAHibihi [ Each of them is the alternating sequent of its correlative ]: (Az, Msb, TA:) you say of the night and the day, humaA EaqiybaAni [ They are two alternating sequents ]; and Eaqiybuka signifies He who does a deed, or work, with thee by turn, he doing it one time and thou another: (A, * TA:) and ↓ muEaAqibN signifies the same, (S, Msb,) as also [↓ muEoqibN and ↓ muEotaqibN and] ↓ muEaq~ibN . (Msb.) As for the saying of the lawyers, yafoEalu *`lika Eaqiyba AlS~alaApi [meaning He does that after the prayer ], and the like thereof, there is no reason to be given but a suppression; the meaning being, fiY waqotK Eaqiyb waqoti AlS~alaApi [ in a time following that of prayer ], Eqyb being an epithet qualifying wqt : (Msb:) and Er-Rázee says, in the Mukhtár es- Siháh, that he had found no authority in the T nor in the S for the phrase jaA='a Eaqiybahu meaning He came after him. (TA.) See also EaqibN , first sentence. [And compare EaAqibN .]

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of Eaqaba ;] Coming after [&c.]. (Msb.) EaAqibu $aYo'K means Any person [or thing ] that comes after, or succeeds, or comes in the place of, a thing. (S, O, TA.) AlEaAqibu is an appellation applied to the Prophet (S, O, Msb) by himself (S, O) because he came after other prophets, (Msb,) meaning The last of the prophets, (S, O.) And EaAqibN liA@moraA^apK means One who is the last of the husbands of a woman. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] EaAqibapN mino TayorK Birds succeeding one another, this alighting and flying, and then another alighting in the place where the former alighted. (TA.) And A_ibilN EaAqibapN Camels that betake themselves to plentiful pasture where they feed freely, after eating of the [ kind of plants called ] HamoD : [or] they are not so called unless they be camels that, in a severe year, eat of trees, and then of the HmD ; not when they pasture upon fresh, juicy, or tender, herbage. (IAar, TA.) And A_ibilN EawaAqibu Camels that drink water, and then return to the place where they lie down by the water, and then go to the water again. (IAar, S, O, K.) ― -b3- And EaAqibN signifies also A successor of another in goodness, or beneficence; and so ↓ EaquwbN . (O, K.) ― -b4- And A chief, or lord: or one who is below the chief or lord: (TA:) or the successor of the chief or lord. (S, K.) ― -b5- See also EaqibN , in two places.

definition: Coming after, or near after, another thing.
sourceDefinition: Coming after, or near after, another thing. (O.) See EaqiybN . ― -b2- It is said that it is applied as an epithet to an angel; that one says malaka muEaq~ibN [meaning An angel that follows another ]; and malaAy^ikapN muEaq~ibapN ; and that muEaq~ibaAtN is a pl. pl. (O.) AlmuEaq~ibaAtu means The angels of the night and the day; (S, O, K;) because they succeed one another by turns; and the fem. form is used because of the frequency of their doing so, in like manner as it is in the words nas~aAbapN and Eal~aAmapN : (S, O:) the angles called AlHafaZapu [pl. of HaAfiZN , q. v.]: so in the Kur xiii. 12: in which some of the Arabs of the desert read maEaAqiybu : (TA:) this [may be an anomalous pl. of EaqiybN , like as mahaAjiynu is of hajiynN , or it] is pl. of muEaq~ibN or of muEaq~ibapN , the Y being to compensate for the suppression of one of the two q . (Bd.) ― -b3- AlmuEaq~ibaAtu also signifies The she-camels that stand behind those that are pressing towards the wateringtrough, or tank; so that when one she-camel goes away, another comes in her place. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And The ejaculations of suboHaAna A@ll~`hi , which follow one another, (O, K,) repeated at the end of the ordinary prayer, thirty-three in number, and which are followed by AaloHamodu lil~`hi thirty-three times, and Aall~`hu A^akobaro thirty-four times. (O.) ― -b5- And muEaq~ibN signifies also One who makes repeatedly warring, or warring and plundering, expeditions; and who journeys repeatedly, and does not stay with his family after his return. (TA.) ― -b6- And One who seeks after a thing repeatedly, striving, or exerting himself: (S, O:) one who follows after a thing that is his due, demanding restitution of it: or one who follows close after a man, for something that is his due: one who seeks to recover his right, or due: and one who, being despoiled of all his property in a hostile attack, makes a hostile attack upon him from whom he has thus suffered, and endeavours to recover his property. (TA.) Lebeed says, describing a [wild] he-ass and his female, Hat~aY tahaj~ara biAlr~awaAHi wahaAjahaA Talaba AlmuEaq~ibi Haq~ahu AlmuZoluwmu (S, O, but in the latter fiY Alr~awaAHi ,) i. e. [ Until he went along in the midday heat, ( bAlrwAH or fY AlrwAH being redundant,)] and drove her on [by a pursuit] like the seeking of him who is making repeated efforts, having been wronged, to obtain his due: (O:) AlmZlwm is an epithet qualifying AlmEq~b , and is in the nom. case agreeable with the meaning, (S, O,) because it is put after its proper place; (O;) and AlmEq~b is literally in the gen. case, but as to the meaning is an agent: (S, O: *) or, accord. to some, AlmEq~b [here] signifies the debtor who puts off the payment of his debt; so that AlmZlwm is an agent and AlmEq~b is an objective complement: (S:) or, as some say, AlmEq~b signifies he who demands the payment of a debt and repeats his demand thereof. (TA.) ― -b7- Also Any one returning [app. to the doing of a thing]. (O.) ― -b8- See also maEaAqibN . ― -b9- laA muEaq~iba liHukomihi , in the Kur [xiii. 41], means There is no repeller of his decree. (TA.) -A2- Also A man who descends into a well to raise a stone of the kind called EuqaAb . (TA.) [See also the verb.]

definition: , perfectly decl.
sourceDefinition: , perfectly decl., because it is an Arabic word, not altered, and, although having an augmentative letter at the beginning, not of the measure of a verb; whereas yEqwb as a proper name of foreign origin is imperfectly decl.; (S, O;) The Hajal [or partridge ]: (K:) or the male of the Hajal ; (S, O, Msb;) or of the qaboj ; (Lh, Mgh;) but ISd says, I know not whether Lh mean by this the Hajal or the qaTaA or the karawaAn , nor do I know that the qaboH is the same as the Hajal : (TA:) and the male of the qaTaA [or sand-grouse ]: (TA:) pl. yaEaAqiybu . (S, Mgh, O, Msb.) kaA^an~akumo yaEaAqiybu AlHajali , occurring in a trad., means [ As though ye were the males of partridges ] in your haste, and your flying into destruction: for they are such that, when they see the female in the possession of the fowler, they throw themselves upon him, so as to fall into his hand. (Z, TA in art. rkb .) ― -b2- And accord. to some, (TA,) the pl. also signifies Horses: they being thus termed as being likened to the yEAqyb of the Hajal , (O, TA,) because of their swiftness: (TA:) so in the phrase rakoDa AlyaEaAqiybi [ As the running of the horses, or of the swift horses ]; in a verse of Selámeh Ibn-Jendel: (O, TA:) but others say that the meaning [here] is, the males of the Hajal . (TA.) It is said in the L that farasN yaEoquwbN means A horse that has a run after another run [or the power of repeating his running ] ( *uw EaqobK [or EaqibK ]). (TA.) ― -b3- J has cited [in the S] the words of a poet, EaAlK yuqaS~iru duwnahu AlyaEoquwbu [ High, so that the yEqwb falls short of reaching it ] as an ex. of the last word meaning the male of the Hajal : but IB says that it appears to mean in this case the male of the EuqaAb [or eagle ]; like as Alyaroxuwmu means the male of the raxam ; and AlyaHobuwru , the male of the HubaAraY ; for the Hajal is not known to have so high a flight: and ElFarezdak describes yaEaAqiyb as congregating with vultures over the slain. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A woman who has become of middle age remaining a virgin, (Lth, A, Mgh,) not having married; (Lth, Mgh;) or a woman who has not married, but waits, or expects, to be married; (Fr, TA;) or who has stayed long in the abode of her family after having attained to puberty, until she has ceased to be reckoned among virgins, and has not married; (S, O, Msb, K;) beyond the age of her who is termed muEoSirN ; (Ks, S, O;) and ↓ muEan~asapN signifies the same: (Fr, Mgh, TA:) pl. EawaAnisu and EunosN and Eun~asN (S, O, K) and EunuwsN : (O, K:) and the pl. of ↓ muEan~asapN is maEaAnisu and muEan~asaAtN . (TA.) And EaAnisN is applied in like manner to a man, (S, O, K,) signifying One who is far advanced in age and has not married: (Msb, TA:) and its pl. is EaAnisuwna . (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A camel fat, and complete, or perfect, in make: fem. with p : (O, K, TA:) or [the pl.] Eun~asN applied to camels means such as are above the bikaArap [pl. of bakorN ]; i. e. the young in a middling degree. (TA.)

definition: , aor. yaEoniyhi and yaEonuwhu , inf. n. EinaAypN and EanaAyapN (K, TA) and EuniY~N , (TA, as from the K, but not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K,) The affair, or event, or case, disquieted...
sourceDefinition: , aor. yaEoniyhi and yaEonuwhu , inf. n. EinaAypN and EanaAyapN (K, TA) and EuniY~N , (TA, as from the K, but not in the CK nor in my MS. copy of the K,) The affair, or event, or case, disquieted him; syn. A^aham~ahu [more fully expl. by what here follows]: (K, TA:) [ EanaAhu may be generally rendered it concerned him; agreeing with this in meaning it made him uneasy in mind, anxious, or careful; and in meaning it affected his interest, or was of importance to him; like A^aham~ahu : and also it concerned him meaning it related, or belonged, to him; or was of his business; as will be shown by what follows: and] EanaAniY ka*aA , aor. yaEoniyniY , means such a thing occurred, or happened, to me, and occupied me [or my mind ]. (Msb.) The saying [in the Kur lxxx. 37], likul~i A@moriy^K minohumo yawomay^i*K $aA^onN yaEoniyhi , thus accord. to one reading, means yuhim~uhu [i. e. To every man of them shall belong, on that day, a business that will disquiet him, &c.]: (Ksh, Bd;) or a business in conjunction with which no other will disquiet him: and like this is the other reading, which is with g ; (TA;) i. e. yugoniyhi , meaning which will suffice him in respect of his being disquieted thereby; (Ksh, Bd;) or the meaning of the latter reading is, [ a business such that ] he will not be able, in conjunction with his being disquieted thereby, to be disquieted by any other; (TA;) or a state that will occupy him so as to divert him from the state of any other. (Jel.) And it is said in a trad. respecting charming, bisomi A@ll~`hi A^aroqiyka mino kul~i daA='K yaEoniyka i. e. [ By the name of God I charm thee from, or against, any disease ] that may disquiet thee, &c., ( yuhim~uka ,) and occupy thee [or thy mind ]. (TA.) And in another trad. it is said, mino Husoni A_isolaAmi Almoro'i tarokuhu maA laA yaEoniyhi , meaning maA laA yuhim~uhu [i. e. A condition of the goodness of the man's submitting himself to the requirements of God is his leaving, or relinquishing, that which does not disquiet him, &c.]; (S, TA;) the exceptions therefrom being such things as necessary food and clothing. (So in a marginal note in a copy of the Jámi' es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee.) See also the prov. muEotariDN liEananK lamo yaEonihi expl. voce EinaAnN . [It is like the common saying, yatakal~amu fiymaA laA yaEoniyhi He talks of that which does not concern him; meaning that which does not relate, or belong, to him; or that which is not of his business. ] ― -b2- EuniYa in the phrase EuniYa biAlA^amori is [said to be] one of a class of verbs used in the pass. form though having the sense of the act. form, like zuhiYa : (S in art. zhw :) [but is expl. as though pass. of EanaAhu meaning as above, or quasipass.:] you say, EuniYa biAlA^amori , with damm, (K, TA,) i. e. in the pass. form, (TA,) inf. n. EinaAyapN , (K, TA,) with kesr; (TA;) and EaniYa bihi , of the class of raDiYa , (K, TA,) mentioned by IDrst and others of the expositors of the Fs, and by Hr and Mtr, (MF, TA,) and by IKtt on the authority of Et- Toosee, (TA,) but this is seldom used, (K, TA,) the former being that which is commonly known, and this alone being mentioned by Th in his Fs, and by J and others; (TA;) i. q. Aihotam~a bihi [i. e. He became disquieted by the affair, or case; or rendered uneasy in mind, anxious, or careful, by it; and consequently, he became occupied by it, or with it; or set about it, and managed it ]; as also bihi ↓ AiEotanaY : (K, TA:) or biA^amorihi ↓ AiEotanayotu means I became disquieted by his affair, or case; or rendered uneasy in mind, anxious, or careful, by it; ( Aihotamamotu bihi ;) and minded it; or managed it well; ( AiHotafalotu bihi ;) and Eanayotu bihi , of the class of ramaY , inf. n. EinaAyapN , signifies the same: and Euniyotu biA^amori fulaAnK , in the pass. form, inf. n. EinaAyapN and EuniY~N , signifies I became occupied [either actually or (as is shown by what follows) in mind ] by, or with, the affair, or case, of such a one; and sometimes one said Eanayotu biA^amorihi [in this sense as well as the similar sense expl. above], using the act. form: (Msb:) one says [also], Euniytu biHaAjatika , with damm to the first letter, [which may be rendered I became occupied by, or with, thy want, ] aor. A^uEonaY , inf. n. EinaAyapN : (S:) and lituEona biHaAjatiY , (S, Msb,) which is the imperative form, (S,) meaning [ Be thou occupied by, or with, my want; or] let my want occupy, or busy, thy mind: (Msb:) and in interrogating, you say, kayofa mano tuEonaY biA^amorihi [ How is he by, or with, whose affair, or case, thou art occupied, or disquieted, &c.?]: you do not say, in this case, taEan~aY [for tataEan~aY ]. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- EanaY A@ll~`hu bihi , [inf. n. EinaAyapN , as is implied in the TA,] means God preserved him: (Msb, TA:) and it is said that it may be from EanaY biHaAjatihi [as syn. with EuniYa bihaA ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And EaniYa , (S, Msb,) thus in the Tahdheeb of IKtt, (TA,) with kesr, (S, TA,) of the class of taEiba , (Msb,) aor. yaEonaY ; (S, Msb;) or EanaY , (K, TA,) with fet-h, thus in the copies of the K, and likewise in the M; (TA;) inf. n. EanaA^'N , (S, K, TA,) or this is a simple subst., from Ean~aAhu , (Mgh, Msb,) and EanoyapN is syn. therewith; (ISd, K, TA;) He suffered difficulty, distress, or trouble; (S, Msb, K, TA;) or fatigue, or weariness: and ↓ tEn~Y , also, has the former or the latter meaning. (S, K, TA.) You say, Eaniytu fiY AlA^amori , meaning ↓ taEan~ayotu [i. e. I suffered difficulty, &c., in the affair, or case ]: mentioned by Az. (TA.) ― -b5- And EaniYa signifies [also] He stuck fast in captivity; (K in this art., and Msb in art. Enw ;) as also EanaA , inf. n. Eunuw~N : (Msb in art. Enw :) or both signify he became a captive. (K in art. Enw .) -A2- EanaY [as intrans.] said of an event, (K, TA,) inf. n. EanoYN , (TA,) It befell, or betided; (K, TA;) as also ↓ AEtnY : (TA:) and it occurred, or happened: (K:) EanaY lahu AlA^amoru is said to mean The event occurred, or happened, to him. (TA.) -A3- EanaY fiyhi AlA^akolu , (K, TA,) inf. n. EanoYN and EuniY~N and EanFY , (TA,) signifies The eating had an agreeable, a wholesome, or a beneficial, effect upon him, (syn. najaEa ,) and [it is said that] the aor. is yaEoniaY , like yaromiY and yaroDaY , (K, TA,) the latter mentioned by ISd, as being anomalous, but MF says that the latter has not been heard unless as having its pret. like raDiYa , [i. e. EaniYa , of which EanFY is the inf. n. accord. to analogy,] and [SM adds that] thus it is accord. to IKtt, who mentions the verb as said also, in the same sense, of the drinking of milk; (TA in this art.;) and he states that EanaA , aor. yaEonuw , inf. n. Eunuw~N , is a dial. var. thereof. (TA in this art. and in art. Enw .) -A4- EanaY bAlqawoli ka*aA , (S, K, TA,) aor. yaEoniY , (TA,) He meant, or intended, by the saying, such a thing; syn. A^raAda , (S, K, TA,) and qaSada . (TA.) Eanayotuhu , aor. A^aEoniyhi , inf. n. EanoYN , signifies qaSadotuhu [as meaning I intended it: and app. in other senses expl. in art. qSd ]. (Msb.) And you say, EanaAniY A^amoruka , meaning qaSadaniY [i. e., app., Thy command, or thy affair, had me for its object ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Eanayotu Al$~aYo'a : and Eanati AlA^aroDu biAln~abaAti : see 1 in art. Enw . -A5- Eanayotu AlkitaAba : see Q. Q. 1 in art. Enw .

To every man of them shall belong, on that day, a business that will disquiet him, &c.]: (Ksh, Bd;) or a business in conjunction with which no other will disquiet him: and like this is the other reading, which is with g ; (TA;) i. e. yugoniyhi , meaning which will suffice him in respect of his being disquieted thereby; (Ksh, Bd;) or the meaning of the latter reading is, [ a business such that ] he will not be able, in conjunction with his being disquieted thereby, to be disquieted by any other; (TA;) or a state that will occupy him so as to divert him from the state of any other. (Jel.) And it is said in a trad. respecting charming, bisomi A@ll~`hi A^aroqiyka mino kul~i daA='K yaEoniyka i. e. [ By the name of God I charm thee from, or against, any disease ] that may disquiet thee, &c., ( yuhim~uka ,) and occupy thee [or thy mind ]. (TA.) And in another trad. it is said, mino Husoni A_isolaAmi Almoro'i tarokuhu maA laA yaEoniyhi , meaning maA laA yuhim~uhu [i. e. A condition of the goodness of the man's submitting himself to the requirements of God is his leaving, or relinquishing, that which does not disquiet him, &c.]; (S, TA;) the exceptions therefrom being such things as necessary food and clothing. (So in a marginal note in a copy of the Jámi' es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee.) See also the prov. muEotariDN liEananK lamo yaEonihi expl. voce EinaAnN . [It is like the common saying, yatakal~amu fiymaA laA yaEoniyhi He talks of that which does not concern him; meaning that which does not relate, or belong, to him; or that which is not of his business. ] ― -b2- EuniYa in the phrase EuniYa biAlA^amori is [said to be] one of a class of verbs used in the pass. form though having the sense of the act. form, like zuhiYa : (S in art. zhw :) [but is expl. as though pass. of EanaAhu meaning as above, or quasipass.:] you say, EuniYa biAlA^amori , with damm, (K, TA,) i. e. in the pass. form, (TA,) inf. n. EinaAyapN , (K, TA,) with kesr; (TA;) and EaniYa bihi , of the class of raDiYa , (K, TA,) mentioned by IDrst and others of the expositors of the Fs, and by Hr and Mtr, (MF, TA,) and by IKtt on the authority of Et- Toosee, (TA,) but this is seldom used, (K, TA,) the former being that which is commonly known, and this alone being mentioned by Th in his Fs, and by J and others; (TA;) i. q. Aihotam~a bihi [i. e. He became disquieted by the affair, or case; or rendered uneasy in mind, anxious, or careful, by it; and consequently, he became occupied by it, or with it; or set about it, and managed it ]; as also bihi ↓ AiEotanaY : (K, TA:) or biA^amorihi ↓ AiEotanayotu means I became disquieted by his affair, or case; or rendered uneasy in mind, anxious, or careful, by it; ( Aihotamamotu bihi ;) and minded it; or managed it well; ( AiHotafalotu bihi ;) and Eanayotu bihi , of the class of ramaY , inf. n. EinaAyapN , signifies the same: and Euniyotu biA^amori fulaAnK , in the pass. form, inf. n. EinaAyapN and EuniY~N , signifies I became occupied [either actually or (as is shown by what follows) in mind ] by, or with, the affair, or case, of such a one; and sometimes one said Eanayotu biA^amorihi [in this sense as well as the similar sense expl. above], using the act. form: (Msb:) one says [also], Euniytu biHaAjatika , with damm to the first letter, [which may be rendered I became occupied by, or with, thy want, ] aor. A^uEonaY , inf. n. EinaAyapN : (S:) and lituEona biHaAjatiY , (S, Msb,) which is the imperative form, (S,) meaning [ Be thou occupied by, or with, my want; or] let my want occupy, or busy, thy mind: (Msb:) and in interrogating, you say, kayofa mano tuEonaY biA^amorihi [ How is he by, or with, whose affair, or case, thou art occupied, or disquieted, &c.?]: you do not say, in this case, taEan~aY [for tataEan~aY ]. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- EanaY A@ll~`hu bihi , [inf. n. EinaAyapN , as is implied in the TA,] means God preserved him: (Msb, TA:) and it is said that it may be from EanaY biHaAjatihi [as syn. with EuniYa bihaA ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And EaniYa , (S, Msb,) thus in the Tahdheeb of IKtt, (TA,) with kesr, (S, TA,) of the class of taEiba , (Msb,) aor. yaEonaY ; (S, Msb;) or EanaY , (K, TA,) with fet-h, thus in the copies of the K, and likewise in the M; (TA;) inf. n. EanaA^'N , (S, K, TA,) or this is a simple subst., from Ean~aAhu , (Mgh, Msb,) and EanoyapN is syn. therewith; (ISd, K, TA;) He suffered difficulty, distress, or trouble; (S, Msb, K, TA;) or fatigue, or weariness: and ↓ tEn~Y , also, has the former or the latter meaning. (S, K, TA.) You say, Eaniytu fiY AlA^amori , meaning ↓ taEan~ayotu [i. e. I suffered difficulty, &c., in the affair, or case ]: mentioned by Az. (TA.) ― -b5- And EaniYa signifies [also] He stuck fast in captivity; (K in this art., and Msb in art. Enw ;) as also EanaA , inf. n. Eunuw~N : (Msb in art. Enw :) or both signify he became a captive. (K in art. Enw .) -A2- EanaY [as intrans.] said of an event, (K, TA,) inf. n. EanoYN , (TA,) It befell, or betided; (K, TA;) as also ↓ AEtnY : (TA:) and it occurred, or happened: (K:) EanaY lahu AlA^amoru is said to mean The event occurred, or happened, to him. (TA.) -A3- EanaY fiyhi AlA^akolu , (K, TA,) inf. n. EanoYN and EuniY~N and EanFY , (TA,) signifies The eating had an agreeable, a wholesome, or a beneficial, effect upon him, (syn. najaEa ,) and [it is said that] the aor. is yaEoniaY , like yaromiY and yaroDaY , (K, TA,) the latter mentioned by ISd, as being anomalous, but MF says that the latter has not been heard unless as having its pret. like raDiYa , [i. e. EaniYa , of which EanFY is the inf. n. accord. to analogy,] and [SM adds that] thus it is accord. to IKtt, who mentions the verb as said also, in the same sense, of the drinking of milk; (TA in this art.;) and he states that EanaA , aor. yaEonuw , inf. n. Eunuw~N , is a dial. var. thereof. (TA in this art. and in art. Enw .) -A4- EanaY bAlqawoli ka*aA , (S, K, TA,) aor. yaEoniY , (TA,) He meant, or intended, by the saying, such a thing; syn. A^raAda , (S, K, TA,) and qaSada . (TA.) Eanayotuhu , aor. A^aEoniyhi , inf. n. EanoYN , signifies qaSadotuhu [as meaning I intended it: and app. in other senses expl. in art. qSd ]. (Msb.) And you say, EanaAniY A^amoruka , meaning qaSadaniY [i. e., app., Thy command, or thy affair, had me for its object ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Eanayotu Al$~aYo'a : and Eanati AlA^aroDu biAln~abaAti : see 1 in art. Enw . -A5- Eanayotu AlkitaAba : see Q. Q. 1 in art. Enw .

sourceDefinition: [signifying The meaning, or intended sense, of a word or saying,] is from EanaY biAlqawoli ka*aA [q. v.]; so says Z: (TA:) it is an inf. n. [of this verb] used in the sense of the pass. part. n.; or a contraction of the latter; i. e. of maEoniY~N : (Dict. of the Technical Terms used in the Sciences of the Musalmans:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, it signifies the import of a word or an expression, from the phrase Eanati AlA^aroDu biAln~abaAti meaning “ the land made apparent, or showed, its plants, or herbage: ” accord. to El-Munáwee, as he says in the Towkeef, [and the like is said in the KT,] an idea, i. e. a mental image, considered as having a word, or an expression, applied to denote it, and as being intended by that word or expression: [the idea, or mental image,] considered as accruing, from the word or expression, in the mind, is termed mafohuwmN : considered as what is said in reply to maA huwa [“ What is it? ”], it is termed maAhiy~apN : considered as existing objectively, [as that by which a thing is what it is,] it is termed HaqiyqapN : and considered as distinguished from others, it is termed huwiy~apN : (TA:) signifying [as expl. above, i. e.] the opposite to lafoZN , it may be either a substance, or thing that subsists by itself, i. e. EayonN , or an accident, or attribute, i. e. EaraDN : but it also signifies the opposite to EayonN , i. e. the opposite to a thing that subsists by itself: (Kull p. 238:) [hence Aisomu maEonFY , opposed to Aisomu EayonK ; both of which are expl. voce AisomN , in art. smw :] maEonaY AlkalaAmi and ↓ maEonaAtuhu and ↓ maEoniy~uhu (S, K, TA) and ↓ maEoniy~atuhu , (K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, maEoniyatuhu , without the sign of teshdeed,]) the last mentioned by ISd, (TA,) are one [in signification], (S, K, TA,) as syn. with faHowaAhu (TA, and so in some copies of the S,) and maqoSaduhu [both of which are generally understood as signifying the meaning, or intended sense, of the saying ]: (TA:) AHát says, the vulgar say, liA^aY~i maEonFY faEalota [ For what intent didst thou such a thing?]; but the Arabs know not AlmaEonaY , and never say it: this is the case: but some of the Arabs say, maA h`*aA ↓ maEoniY~u [i. e. What is the meaning, or intent, (lit. the meant or intended object,) of this? ], with kesr to the n and with the Y musheddedeh: and AZ says, *aAka ↓ h`*aA fiY maEonaApi and fiY maEonaAhu sawaA='N , i. e. This is [used] in a manner the like of that in respect of indication and import and acceptation: El-Fárábee, also, says, maEonaY Al$~aYo'i and ↓ maEonaAtuhu are one [in signification]; and maEonaAhu and faHowaAhu and muqotaDaAhu and maDomuwnuhu all signify that which the word, or expression, [termed before the thing, ] indicates: and it is said in the T, on the authority of Th, that AlmaEonaY and Alt~afosiyru and Alt~aA^owiylu , are one [in signification, as meaning explanation, or interpretation, or the like ]: and people have used their phrase h`*aA maEonaY kalaAmihi , and the like, meaning this is the import, and the indication of the meaning, of his saying; which is agreeable with what is said by AZ and El-Fárábee: the grammarians and lexicologists, moreover, have agreed respecting a mode of expression of which they have made frequent use, their saying h`*aA bimaEonaY h`*aA [ this is used with the meaning of this ], and h`*aA wah`*aA fiY AlmaEonaY waAHidN [ this and this are in meaning one ] and fiY AlmaEonaY sawaA='N [ in meaning alike ], and h`*aA fiY maEonaY h`*aA [ this is used in the sense of this ] i. e. this is like this [ in meaning ]: (Msb, TA:) the pl. of maEonFY is maEaAnK . (TA.) ― -b2- Eilomu AlmaEaAniY is expl. by El-Munáwee in the “ Towkeef ” as The science whereby one knows how to express clearly one meaning in various ways: (TA:) [but this definition is applied in the “ Talkhees ” (Talkhees el-Miftáh), and Hájjee Khaleefeh uses the same words with only one unimportant variation, in explaining Eilomu AlbayaAni ; and a similar explanation of the latter is given in the Kull: in a marginal note in a copy of the Ksh, cited by De Sacy in his Anthol. Gr. Ar. p. 305, Elm AlmEAnY is expl. as the science whereby is known the manner of adapting language to the requirements of the case; (and it is similarly expl. in the “ Talkhees ” and other works;) and Elm AlbyAn , as the science that concerns comparisons and tropes and metonymies.] ― -b3- [ SuwrapN bilaA maEonFY means A form without any intrinsic quality. ] ― -b4- And AlmaEaAniY signifies also The qualities that are commended, or approved; [ the charms, or graces; ] such as knowledge, or science, and piety, and generosity, and goodliness of make, &c. (Har p. 644.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaEiyvu , inf. n. EayovN (S, O, K) and EuyuwvN and EayavaAnN , (TA,) He acted corruptly; or made, or did, mischief; syn. A^afosada : (S, O, K:) or, accord. to Az, he hastened, or was hasty or quick, in so acting: (TA:) accord. to Er-Rághib, EayovN and EuviY~N , or EiviY~N , and Euvuw~N are nearly alike; but EayovN is mostly used in relation to that which is perceived by sense; and EvY~ and Evw~ , in relation to that which is perceived by the [mind or] judgment: some say that Evw~ is the “ acting corruptly in the utmost degree: ” and some, that it is the “ acting wrongfully, injuriously, or unjustly; ” and sometimes does not involve the acting corruptly: (MF, TA:) Lh says that EaviYa is of the dial. of El-Hijáz, and is the [more] approved form; and EAv is of the dial. of the BenooTemeem, who say, laA taEiyvuwA fiY AlA^aroDi [ Act not ye corruptly, or do not ye mischief, in the earth ]. (TA.) Hence one says, EAv Al*~iy^obu fiY Alganami The wolf made, or did, mischief among the sheep or goats; syn. A^afosada . (S, A, O.) And EiyviY jaEaAri [ Do mischief, O she-hyena ]: a prov. used in declaring a thing to be vain, or false. (K in art. jEr .) And EAv fiY maAlihi He dissipated his property; or squandered, and wasted, or ruined, it: and he expended it quickly. (TA.) ― -b2- EAv , aor. and inf. ns. as above, also signifies He took without gentleness. (L.) ― -b3- And EAv , inf. n. EayovN , He ventured upon an affair not caring what he fell upon. (AA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S,) and [the fem.] gavoraA='u , (K,) Dustcoloured: (K, TA:) or of a dingy, or dusky, colour: (TA:) or of a dingy, or dusky, colour: (TA:) or [ of the colour termed guvorap , which is] nearly the same as dust-coloured. 'Omárah says, Hat~aY A@kotasayotu mina Alma$iybi EimaAmapF gavoraA='a A^agofiru lawonahaA bixiDaAbi [ Until I attired myself with a dusky turban of hoariness, the colour of which I concealed with hair-dye ]. (TA.) ― -b2- A^agovaru is applied as an epithet to a ram That is not red [or brown ] nor black ner white; (IAar, TA;) meaning of a dusky, or dingy, colour. (TA.) And it is so applied to a wolf. (IAar, TA.) And AlA^agovaru signifies The wolf; (TA;) as also AlA^agobaru . (TA in art. gbr .) ― -b3- And [in like manner] AlgavoraA='u signifies The hyena, or female hyena; (K, TA;) because of its colour: (TA;) as also ↓ gavaAri , (O, K, TA,) like qaTaAmi , (O, TA,) determinate; (K, TA;) [accord. to the CK guvaArN , which is wrong;] and accord. to IAar ↓ gavaAru , imperfectly declinable. (TA.) ― -b4- And AlA^agovaru signifies also The lion; and so ↓ Algavawovaru : (K:) or the latter, as also ↓ Algawovaru , the lion that is in a confused, or perplexed, case. (S, TA.) ― -b9- Also (assumed tropical:) The ignorant man: and the stupid man: likened to the hyena, or female hyena, which is one of the most stupid of beasts, and of which one of the appellations is AlgavoraA='u . (IDrd, TA.) ― -b10- And AlgavoraA='u and Alguvoru , (S, K, TA,) which latter is the pl. of AlA^agovaru , (S, TA,) (assumed tropical:) The low, base, vile, ignoble, mean, or sordid, or the refuse, or rabble, of mankind; as also ↓ Algavorapu , (S, K, TA,) said to be originally ↓ Algayovarapu , (S, TA,) which signifies the same: (S, K, TA:) and gavoraA='u is also expl. as meaning a mixed assemblage of people (K, TA) of the low, base, vile, ignoble, mean, or sordid, or of the refuse, or rabble, of mankind; (TA;) and so ↓ gayovarapN : (AZ, TA:) or a mixed assemblage of people of various tribes: or the unknown common people: or the commonalty, or generality, of men. (TA.)

(MF.)

definition: A young gazelle, waladu ZaboyapK : (Msb:) or a $aAdin [or young gazelle ], (T, S, O, Msb, K, TA,) or, as some say, the female, (TA, [but see what follows,]) when it becomes active, or in motion, (T, S, O, Msb, K, TA.
sourceDefinition: A young gazelle, waladu ZaboyapK : (Msb:) or a $aAdin [or young gazelle ], (T, S, O, Msb, K, TA,) or, as some say, the female, (TA, [but see what follows,]) when it becomes active, or in motion, (T, S, O, Msb, K, TA.) and walks; (T, Msb, K, TA;) to which the girl, or young woman, is likened in [the commencing of an ode by what is termed] Alt~a$obiyb , wherefore the epithet and the verb [therein] are made mase.; (TA;) after the becoming a vaniY~ [q. v.]: (T, Msb:) or in the stage after that in which he is termed TalFA [q. v.]: (AHát, Msb, TA:) or from the time of his birth until he attains to the most vehement running; (K, TA;) which is when he puts his legs together, [app. meaning his fore legs together and so his hind legs, ] and puts them down together and raises them together: (TA:) or i. q. ZaboYN [i. e. a gazelle, of any age ]: (M in art. ZbY : for AlZ~aboYu is there expl. as meaning AlgazaAlu : [but this seems to be a loose rendering:]) the female is called ↓ gazaAlapN ; (Msb, MF, TA;) though it seems from what is said in the K [&c.] that AlgazaAlu is applied peculiarly to the male, and that the female is called only ZaboyapN , as several of the lexicologists have decisively asserted: (MF, TA:) the pl. [of pane.] is gizolapN and [of mult.] gizolAnN . (S, O, Msb, K.) -A2- gazaAlu $aEobaAna A certain insect ( duwayob~apN ), (K, TA,) a species of the [ locusts, or locust-like insects, called ] janaAdib [pl. of junodabN ]. [See also damu AlgazaAli and damu AlgizolaAni and dumoyapu AlgizolaAni voce dmN in art. dmw or dmY ; and see likewise EanodamN .]

sourceDefinition: fem. of gazaAlN , q. v. -A2- AlgazaAlapu , also, signifies The sun; (S, O, K;) because it extends [what resemble] cords, [meaning its rays,] as though it were spinning: (K:) or the sun when rising; (Msb, K;) [therefore] one says TalaEati AlgazaAlapu , but not garabati AlgazaAlapu : (TA:) or the sun when high: (M, * K, TA:) or the Eayon [meaning the disk, or, as it sometimes means, the rays, or beams, ] of the sun. (K.) ― -b2- And gazaAlapu AlD~uHaY means, (S, O, K,) as also gazaAlaAtuhu , (K,) [or gazaAlaAtuhaA ,] The beginning of the DuHaY [or early part of the forenoon, after sunrise ]; (S, O, K;) [whence] one says, jaA='a fiY gazaAlapi AlD~uHaY [ He came in the beginning of the DuHaY ]; and Dhu-r-Rummeh uses AlgazaAlapa , in the accus. case, as an adv. n., (S, O,) meaning in the time [or in the beginning ] of the DuHaY ; (O;) or, accord. to IKh, this is for TuluwEa AlgazaAlapi , meaning at the rising of the sun: (TA:) or the meaning of the phrases first mentioned in this sentence is after, or a little after, (accord. to different copies of the K,) the spreading of the son, [i. e. of the sunshine, ] and its entrance upon the DuHaY : or the first part of the DuHaY , until the passing away of a fifth (or about a fifth, TA) of the day. (K.) -A3- Also (i. e. AlgazaAlapu ) A certain herb, (Aboo-Nasr. O, K,) of the [ kind called ] suT~aAH , spreading upon the ground, with green leaves, having no thorns nor broaches; from the middle whereof comes forth a tall qaDiyb [or shoot ], which is peeled and eaten, (Aboo-Nasr, O,) and it is sweet, (Aboo-Nasr, O, K,) and has yellow blossoms from its bottom to its top: and it is a pasture: (Aboo-Nasr, O:) every thing [i. e. animal ] eats it: (Aboo-Nasr, O, K;) and the places of its growth are the plain, or soft, tracts. (Aboo-Nasr, O)

[meaning More practised, or skilled, in weaving than a spider ]: and so mino surofapK [ than a surofap , q. v.]. (Meyd.) ― -b2- And one says also, A^agozalu mini A@moriy^i Alqayosi , (S, Meyd, O,) likewise a prov., meaning [ More practised, or skilled, ] in the celebrating of the person and qualities of the beloved in verse [ than Imra-el-Keys ]. (Meyd.) ― -b3- And [hence,] A^agozalu mina AlHum~aY (assumed tropical:) [ More frequent in visiting, or more habitual, and more recurrent, than the fever ]; a saying of the Arabs, by which they mean that it [the fever] is a frequent visiter of the sick person, recurrent to him; as though passionately loving him: thus, correctly, as in the L: in the K it is said that AlA^agozalu applied to the fever ( AlHum~aY [though this is fem.]) means such as is a frequent visiter of the sick person; recurrent. (TA.) ― -b4- And A^agozalu mino furoEulK [ More confounded and perplexed than a young one of the hyena ]; from Algazalu as signifying “ the being confounded and perplexed ” like as is the dog (Meyd, O, K) when pursuing the young gazelle; for it may be that the frEl becomes in the like state in pursuing the object of its chase: (Meyd:) or frEl was a man of ancient times, and this saying (which is a prov., Meyd) is like A^agozalu mini A@moriy^i Alqayosi . (Meyd, O, TA.)

definition: and ↓ mugozalN (Fr, Th, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ magozalN , (Th, O, K,) the first as pronounced by [the tribe of] Temeem, the second as pronounced by [that of] Keys, and the last the most rare, (TA,) or the second as pronounced by Temeem, (Msb,) A spindle;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ mugozalN (Fr, Th, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ magozalN , (Th, O, K,) the first as pronounced by [the tribe of] Temeem, the second as pronounced by [that of] Keys, and the last the most rare, (TA,) or the second as pronounced by Temeem, (Msb,) A spindle; i. e. the thing with which one spins: (S, MA, O, Msb, K. KL:) Fr says that ↓ mugozalN is the original form, from A^ugozila “ it was made to turn round ” or “ revolve ” [or “ was twirled ”]; (S, TA;) but the dammeh was deemed by the Arabs difficult of pronunciation, and therefore they said migozalN , and in like manner miSoHafN and mixodaEN and mijosadN and miTorafN : accord. to IAth, migozalN signifies the instrument [ with which one spins ]; and ↓ magozalN , the place of the gazol [which means the act of spinning and the span thread or yard ]; and ↓ mugozalN , the place in which ( fiyhi [or this may here mean upon which ]) the gazol [i. e. spun thread or yarn ] is put: (TA:) pl. magaAzilu . (MA.) A^aEorY mino migozalK is a prov. [meaning More naked than a spindle ]. (Meyd.) And one says, SaAHibu Algazali A^aDal~u mino saAqi migozalK [ The practiser of the talk and actions &c. usual between the lover and the object of love is more erring than the shank (i. e. pin ) of a spindle ), of which the error is its [aiding in] clothing mankind while it is [itself] naked. (A, TA.) ― -b2- It is said in a book of certain of the Jews, Ealayokumo ka*aA waka*aA waruboEu Almigozali , meaning [ I pon you lie as due from you such and such things and ) the fourth part of what your women have spun. (TA.) ― -b3- And [the pl.] magaAzilu signifies The Eamad (O) or Eumud (K) [app. meaning the upright wooden supports of the seat ] of the [ machine called ] naworaj [q. v.] with which the reaped grain heaped together is thrashed. (O, K.)

definition: [ The epiglottis: and also, app.
sourceDefinition: [ The epiglottis: and also, app. by extension of the primary signification, the larynx, or upper part of the windpipe: ] the thing that rises up in the uppermost part of the throat, and is said to throw the meat and drink into the œsophagus, or gullet: (Zj, in his “ Khalk-el-Insán: ”) the piece of flesh [or cartilage ] that is between the head and the neck: or the Eujorap [or projecting thing ] that is upon the place where the uvula and gullet meet: (K:) or [by an extended application] the head of the Huloquwm [or windpipe ], (S, Msb, K,) with its [ ducts called ] $awaArib [q. v. voce $aAribN ] and its Haroqadap [app. meaning pomum Adami ]; (K;) i. e. the projecting place [or part ] in the Haloq [here app. meaning, as it does in many cases, throat ]: (S, Msb:) or the root, or base, of the tongue: (K:) or the place where the Huloquwm [or windpipe, i. e. the head thereof, ] becomes in conjunction with the Haloq [or fauces ] when the eater swallows a mouthful and it descends from [ over ] the Huloquwm : (TA:) pl. galaASimu . (Msb.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) The chiefs, lords, nobles, or men of distinction: and the congregated or collective body [of a people], or the mass [thereof]; syn. AljamaAEapu : (K:) pl. as above. (TA.) And [hence] one says, huwa fiY galoSamapK mino qawomihi i. e. fiY $arafK waEadadK [meaning (assumed tropical:) He is among ( such as are distinguished by ) nobility and number, of his people ], (ISk, K, TA,) [or] meaning, accord. to As, he is among the chief portion of his people, and the nobility thereof: (TA:) [and in the same sense ↓ galoSam is used, without p , but perhaps only by poetic license:] Abu-n-Nejm says, A^abiY lujayomN waA@somuhu milo'u Alfami fiY galoSami AlhaAmi wahaAmi galoSami [(assumed tropical:) My father is, or was, Lujeym, and his fame (a tropical rendering) is what fills the mouth; one among the chief portion and the nobility of the headmen, and among headmen of a chief portion and of nobility ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. gam~N , (Msb, TA,) He covered it, (S, Msb, K, TA,) veiled it, or concealed it; (TA;) namely, a thing: (Msb, K, TA:) this is the primary meaning. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, gum~a AlhilaAlu (S, Msb, K, TA) EalaY Aln~aAsi , (S, TA,) inf. n. gam~N , (TA,) The new moon was veiled, or concealed, (S, Msb,) to the people, (S,) by clouds, or otherwise, (S, Msb,) or was intercepted by thin clouds, (K, TA,) or otherwise, (TA,) so that it was not seen. (S, Msb, TA.) It is said in a trad., faA_ino gum~a Ealayokumo faA^akomiluwA AlEid~apa , (Mgh, * Msb, TA,) i. e. And if it [the new moon] be veiled, &c., to you, then complete ye the reckoning of Shaabán, thirty [days], in order that the entering upon the fast of Ramadán may be with [inferential] knowledge. (Msb.) Az says that gum~a and A^ugomiYa and gumiYa all signify the same: (TA:) and all three occur in the trad. above mentioned accord. to different relations thereof. (Mgh.) [See also 1 in art. gmY .] ― -b2- And [hence] gam~a Alqamaru Aln~ujuwma The moon concealed the stars: or almost concealed the light of the stars. (TA.) ― -b3- And gum~a Ealayohi Alxabaru The information, or narration, was dubious, confused, or vague, to him; such as to be difficult to be understood; or such as not to be understood; (S, K;) like A^ugomiYa : (S:) or was obscure, or unapparent, to him. (Msb.) ― -b4- And gam~ahu , (S, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. gam~N , (TA,) It (i. e. ham~ [here meaning “ grief, ” see gam~N below,]) covered [or was as though it covered ] his heart: (Har p. 637:) or [accord. to common acceptation] it, or he, grieved him; or caused him to mourn or lament, or to be sorrowful or sad or unhappy; syn. A^aHozanahu . (K, and Har p. 422. [See also 4.]) ― -b5- gam~ahu , in which the pronoun relates to an ass, &c., (S, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. gam~N , (TA,) means He put [ as a covering ] to his mouth and his nostrils the ↓ gimaAmap , (S, K, TA,) which is a thing like the kiEaAm [or muzzle ], (so in the S and CK,) or a thing like the fidaAm [which seems to be here similar in meaning to kEAm ]: (so in other copies of the K:) or he put [ as a covering ] to his mouth a nose-bag, or the like, to prevent his feeding; and this is termed a ↓ gimaAmap : (TA:) [the verb that I have rendered “ put to ” in these explanations is A^aloqama , of which I do not find in its proper place any signification that would be exactly apposite in this case:] or ↓ gimaAmapN signifies a sort of bag for the mouth of a camel and the like, (K, TA,) his mouth being put into it: (TA:) pl. gamaAy^imu : (S, TA:) and one says, gam~ahu biAlgimaAmapi [ he covered his mouth with the gmAmp ], aor. and inf. n. as above. (TA.) ― -b6- gam~a Al$~aYo'a , aor. , also signifies EalaAhu [app. as meaning It rose upon, or above, the thing, as though forming a covering over it]: mentioned on the authority of IAar, who cites [as an ex.] the saying of En-Nemir Ibn-Towlab, [app. describing a rawoDap , or meadow,] A^unufN yagum~u AlD~aAlu nabota biHaArihaA [ Not depastured, the trees called DAl rising upon, or above, the herbage of its fertile tracts, or its tracts near to water ]. (TA.) See also 8. -A2- [ gam~a is also intrans.: one says,] gam~a yawomunaA , (S, K, TA,) inf. n. gam~N and gumuwmN ; (TA;) and ↓ A^agam~a ; Our day was, or became, [ sultry, or] intensely hot, (S, K, TA,) so that it took away, (S,) or almost took away, (TA,) the breath: (S, TA:) or both verbs, said of a day, and of the sky, mean it brought gam~ [or distress that affected the breath or respiration ], arising from closeness of heat, or clouds. (Msb.) -A3- gam~a Al$~axoSu , of the class of taEiba , [the first pers. being gamimotu ,] inf. n. gamamN , The person's hair of his head flowed down so that his forehead and the back of his neck were narrowed. (Msb.) [See also gamamN below.]

definition: [an inf. n. used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates,] Grief, mourning, lamentation, sorrow, sadness, or unhappiness; syn. HuzonN ; (Msb, K;) so called because it covers...
sourceDefinition: [an inf. n. used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates,] Grief, mourning, lamentation, sorrow, sadness, or unhappiness; syn. HuzonN ; (Msb, K;) so called because it covers happiness and forbearance; (Msb;) or gam~ in the heart is thus called because it veils, or precludes, happiness: (Ham p. 21:) [it may therefore be rendered gloominess of mind: ] or i. q. karobN , (K,) which signifies Huzon , (K in art. krb ,) or gam~ , (S, in that art.,) [ that affects the breath or respiration, lit.] that takes away the breath; (S and K in that art.;) as also ↓ gam~aA='u (K) and ↓ gum~apN , (S, K,) the last [expl. in the S as syn. with kurobapN , which is syn. with karobN , and] mentioned by Lh: (TA:) [see also SaqaEN :] it is karob [or grief, &c.,] that befalls the heart because of what has happened; differing from ham~N , which is krb that befalls because of annoyance, or harm, that is expected to happen: or, as some say, both are one [in meaning]: the differing is asserted by 'Iyád and [many] others: (TA:) [see also gaSabN :] the pl. of gam~N is gumuwmN . (S, K.) ― -b2- It is also an inf. n. used as an epithet in the phrase yawomN gam~N (S, TA) i. e. A day that is [ sultry, or] intensely hot, so that it [ almost ] takes away the breath; and layolapN gam~N [ such a night ], i. e. ↓ gaAm~apN : (S:) or one says yawomN gam~N and ↓ gaAm~N and ↓ migam~N , (K, TA,) the last with kesr to the m , (TA,) [in the CK ↓ mugim~N ,] meaning a day of heat, (K,) or of intense heat: (TA:) or a day of gam~ [i. e. grief, &c.]: and [in a similar sense, as is implied by the context immediately preceding,] layolapN gam~N and gam~apN and ↓ gam~aY : (K:) [but] A'Obeyd mentions, on the authority of AZ, ↓ layolapN gam~aY and ↓ layolapN gam~apN as meaning a night in which there is over the sky [ a covering of clouds, or] what is termed gamoYN [a word belonging to art. gmY , being in measure] like ramoYN ; (S;) and [in the like sense] yawomN gam~N . (So in one of my copies of the S.) ― -b3- And one says, kaAna EalaY Als~amaA='i gm [app. gam~N , but this, I think, requires confirmation, for which I have searched in vain,] and gmY [app. ↓ gam~aY , or perhaps gamoYN , a word mentioned above,] meaning There was over the sky a collection [or an expanse ] of thin clouds, or a DabaAbap [i. e. mist, or the like ], faHaAla duwna AlhilaAli [ and it intercepted the new moon ]: and h`*ihi layolapu ↓ gam~aY , and some say ↓ gum~aY , This is a night [ of a covering of clouds, or] of a DabaAbap [or mist, or the like ], intervening between the new moon and men; so that the new moon is not seen: (Msb:) and [hence] ↓ SumonaA lilogam~aY , and ↓ lilogum~aY , (S, Msb, K,) both mentioned by ISk on the authority of Fr, (S,) and ↓ lilogam~aA='i , (S, K,) and ↓ lilogum~iy~api , (K, TA, but omitted in the CK,) and ↓ lilogum~api , (TA,) [i. e. We fasted after, or from the time of, the covering of clouds, or the mist, or the like, that concealed the new moon; (the prep. li being here used in the sense of baEoda , or mino waqoti , as in the Kur xvii. 80;) virtually] meaning [ we fasted ] without a sight [ of the new moon ]: (Msb, TA:) a rájiz says, TaAmisK hilaAluhaA ↓ layolapa gum~aY A^awogalotuhaA wamukorapN A_iyogaAluhaA [ In a night of a covering of clouds, or of a mist, or the like, having its new moon effaced: I journeyed quickly and far in it, ( A^awogalotuhaA ) being used, app. by poetic license, for A^awogalotu fiyhaA ,) and disliked was the journeying so therein ]: (S, TA:) and it is said that layolapu gm~Y [i. e. ↓ gam~aY and ↓ gum~aY ] signifies also the last night of the [ lunar ] month; being so called because the case thereof is veiled to people so that it is not known whether it be of the coming [month] or of the past. (TA.)

And A^aroDN gum~apN means (assumed tropical:) A strait, or narrow, land. (TA.) ― -b4- Also The bottom of the interior of a skin for clarified butter (S, K) &c. (S.) [See also the first sentence in art. gml .]

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ mifotaHN (Msb, K) A key; an instrument with which a lock is opened; (Msb;) [ a key ] of a door; and of anything that is closed, or locked; (S;) an instrument for opening, (K, TA,) i. e. anything with which a thing is opened: (TA:) pl. of the former mafaAtiyHu and mfaAtiHu , said by Akh to be similar to A^amaAniY~u and A^amaAnK ; (S;) or mfAtyH is pl. mifotaAHN , and mfAtH is pl. of ↓ mifotaHN [as well as of mafotaHN ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And A^uwitiytu mafaAtiyHa Alkalimi , or mafaAtiHa Alkalimi , accord. to different relaters, occurring in a trad., i. e. I have been given the keys of words, means [I have been given] an easy faculty, granted by God, for the acquirement of eloquence and chasteness of speech, and the attaining to the understanding of obscure meanings, and novel and admirable kinds of knowledge, and the beauties of expressions and phrases, which are closed against others, and difficult to be learnt by them. (L.) ― -b4- And AlmifotaAHu signifies also (assumed tropical:) A certain brand upon the thigh and neck (K, TA) of a camel, in the form of what is [ properly ] thus called. (TA.)

definition: He took, or seized, the opportunity;
sourceDefinition: He took, or seized, the opportunity; or he arose and hastened to be before another, or others, in taking, or seizing, the opportunity; syn. You say also, AftrS AlA^umuwra [ He took, or seized, opportunities to do things ]. (A.) And fulaAnN laA yufotaraSu A_aHosaAnuhu wabir~uhu [ Such a one's beneficence and kindness are not caught at ]; because there is no fear that his beneficence and kindness will become beyond one's reach. (A, TA. (IAth, L, TA. *) -A2- AftrSt Alwaraqapu [from AlfariySapu , “ the quivering muscle ” so called,] The leaf was caused to quiver. (M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: A turn; a time at which, or during which, a thing is, or is to be, done, or had, in succession: (S, A, K:) or a turn, or time, for persons' coming to water in succession, (Yaakoob, S, * M, A, * Msb, K, *) in the cases of the periodical drinkings of their camels, such as the ximos and the riboE and the sidos &c., (Yaakoob, M,) when the water is little; (Msb;) as also ↓ firoSapN (M) and ↓ fariySapN : (Yaakoob, M:) a dial. var. of the same is with s ; (IAar, M;) and rufoSapN is another: (TA:) pl. furaSN . (M, Msb.) You say, jaA='ato furoSatuka mina Albiy^ori Thy turn, or time, for watering from the well has come. (As, S, * Msb. *) ― -b2- A portion, or share, of what falls to one's lot, of water; syn. $irobN . (S, K.) ― -b3- An opportunity; a time at which, or during which, a thing may be done, or had; syn. nuhozapN ; (S, M, TA;) and furosapN is a dial. var. of the same. (M.) You say, Ainotahaza AlfuroSapa , i. e. AigotanamahaA [expl. above: see 8]. (S.) And A^ay~aAmuka furaSN [ Thy days are opportunities ]. (A, TA.) -A2- See also firoSapN . -A3- Also The temper ( sajiy~ap ), and outstripping, and strength, of a horse. (M.)

sourceDefinition: One who shares in water with another, each taking of it in turn. (S, K.) (TA.) -A2- fariySN is also, like faraAy^iSu , pl. of fariySapN ; (S;) [or, rather, fariySN is a coll. gen. n., whereof the n. un. is ↓ fariySapN ;] which signifies The portion of flesh [or muscle ] between the side and the shoulder-blade which incessantly trembles, or quakes, (As, S, K,) in a beast: (As, S:) or the portion of flesh which is in the part extending from the marojiE [or lower part, next the armpit, ] of the shoulder-blade to the arm, on either side, and which trembles, or quakes, when the man, or beast, is frightened: (Zj, in his “ Khalk el-Insán: ”) or the portion of flesh which is by the nagoD of the katif , [which may app. be here rendered with sufficient exactness the cartilage of the shoulder-blade; or the part of it where it moves to and fro; ] in the middle of the side, by the place where the heart beats: there are two such portions, each of them thus called, which tremble, or quake, on an occasion of fright: and the piece of flesh that is between the breast ( vadoY ) and the marojiE [expl. above] of the shoulder-blade, of a man and of a beast: or, as some say, the lower part ( A^aSol ) of the marojiEu Almirofaqayoni [or place to which either elbow returns, in a beast, when, having been removed from the usual place, it is brought back thereto ]: (M:) or a small piece of flesh which is in the heart, and which trembles, or quakes, by reason of a calamity, when one is frightened: (A 'Obeyd:) or a piece of flesh [or muscle ] in the side, which trembles, or quakes, when one is frightened. (A.) [Hence the saying,] ↓ huwa Daxomu AlfariySapi (tropical:) He is bold and strong. (A, TA.) ― -b2- fariySu AlEunuqi The external jugular veins ( A^awodaAj ) of the neck: n. un. with p : (A 'Obeyd, S, K:) or the tendons, or sinews, ( EaSab ,) and veins, of the neck: so, app., says A 'Obeyd, in the following words of a trad.: A_in~iY laA^akorahu A^ano A^araY Alr~ajulu vaAy^irFA fariySu raqabatihi qaAy^imFA EalaY murayoy^atihi yaDoribuhaA [ Verily I hate to see the man having the tendons, or sinews, and veins, of his neck swelling with anger, rising against his little wife, beating her ]: for these are what swell out in anger: (S:) or, accord. to IAar, the meaning is, the hair of the fryS , which term is metaphorically used in relation to the neck, though it [really] has no faraAy^iS , because anger causes its veins to swell out [like as fright causes the fariyS properly so called to tremble or quake]: (Az, TA:) fariysN is a dial. var. of the same. (TA.) [See faraSahu , last signification.]

definition: Filled; applied in this sense to a skin for water or milk; as also mufoA^amN : but as to ↓ mafoEuwmN , IAar asserts that he had not heard it except in a verse of Kutheiyir: Az, however, mentions it...
sourceDefinition: Filled; applied in this sense to a skin for water or milk; as also mufoA^amN : but as to ↓ mafoEuwmN , IAar asserts that he had not heard it except in a verse of Kutheiyir: Az, however, mentions it as signifying full [like faEomN ], applied to a river, or rivulet: and Aboo-Sahl cites an ex. of it from the verses of the Fs as signifying full of flesh. (TA.) ― -b2- The phrase sayolN mufoEamN may be of the same category as ham~N naASibN [for ham~N *uw naSabK ], the meaning being A torrent having the quality of filling; though the possessive epithet in most instances has the form of the act. part. n., such as TaAliqN [for *aAta TalaAqK ] and muroDiEN [for *aAtu raDiyEK ]: or it may be that mafoEamN in this case is expressive of muchness, or abundance, like the latter word in the phrase $iEorN $aAEirN and in mawotN maAy^itN . (Ham p. 106.)

definition: A tremour, (S, O, K,) from cold or from fear: (S:) hence, in a trad.
sourceDefinition: A tremour, (S, O, K,) from cold or from fear: (S:) hence, in a trad., A^axa*aniY A^afokalu [ A tremour seized me ]: (S, * O:) and in another, fabaAta walahu A^afokalu [ And he passed the night having a tremour, or shivering ]: (O:) thus used, as indeterminate, it is perfectly decl.; but if used as a [proper] name of a man, it is imperfectly decl. because determinate and also of the measure of a verb: (S, O:) some say, (IF, O,) no verb is formed from it; (IF, S, O;) but such is not the case, for they said rajulN mafokuwlN [which shows that it had a verb though none is known to have been in use]. (IF, O.) [ A^axa*ato biY naAqatiY A^afokalFA mina Als~ayori is a saying mentioned in the O and K, (in the former as from Ibn-'Abbád,) but the meaning is not expl., nor indicated by the context, in either of them; and the strangeness of its phraseology convinces me that it presents a mistranscription: I believe that the first word is mistranscribed for A^aHodavato , and, consequently, that the meaning is, My she-camel produced in me a tremour arising from the rate of journeying: some copies of the K, as is stated in the TA, for mina Als~ayori , have mn Als~aboqi , from the outstripping. ] ― -b2- Also The [ bird commonly called ] $iqir~aAq [generally meaning the green wood-pecker ]; (O, K;) because they regard it as of evil omen; so that when it presents itself to them, they are frightened at it, and tremble. (O.) -A2- And A company, or collective body, of men: one says, jaAw^uwA biA^afokalihimo They came with their company [i. e. all together ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) A^afaAkiylu [is app. a pl. thereof, and, as such,] signifies A^afowaAjN [pl. of fawojN , q. v.]: thus in the phrase A^afaAkiylu mino ka*aA [app. meaning Multitudes of such a kind of thing ]: (K:) [or] thus in the saying, mentioned by Ibn-'Abbád, Einodahu A^afaAkiylu mino kalaAmK [app. meaning He has multitudes of sayings, or words; for kalaAmN (q. v.) is used in a pl. sense as well as in a sing. sense]. (O. [The difference of these two exs. in respect of the last word suggests that there may be in one of them a mistranscription.])

definition: A man who succeeds, or overcomes, in his argument, plea, allegation, or the like;
sourceDefinition: A man who succeeds, or overcomes, in his argument, plea, allegation, or the like; as also ↓ falojN . (TA.) And Als~ahomu AlfaAliju The arrow that is successful: (S, O, K:) the winning arrow in the game called Almayosir : or it may mean the arrow that is successful in a contest at archery. (TA.) -A2- See also filojN , in four places. ― -b2- faAlijN (S, O, L, K) and ↓ falojN (L) also signify A large, or bulky, camel, with two humps, that is brought from Es-Sind for the purpose of covering: (S, O, * K:) or a camel with two humps, between the Bukhtee ( AlbuxotiY~ ) and the Arabian: so called because his hump is divided in halves, or because his two humps have different inclinations: (L:) pl. of the former fawaAliju . (S, M, K; all in art. Sr .) ― -b3- And AlfaAliju signifies [ Palsy, or paralysis, whether partial or general; hemiplegia or paraplegia: ] a disease arising from a flaccidity in one of the lateral halves of the body; (A;) or a flaccidity in one of the lateral halves of the body, (K, TA,) arising suddenly, (TA,) occasioned by an efflux of a phlegmatic humour, and causing the passages of the spirit to become obstructed; (K, TA;) this being its first effect; it deprives the patient of his senses and his motion; and is sometimes in one member: (TA:) or a flatus ( riyHN S, O, L, TA) which attacks a man, and deprives him [ of the use ] of one lateral half of the body; (thus in the L, and the like is said in the 'Eyn; TA;) whence it is thus called: (IDrd, S, O:) or a disease that arises in one of the lateral halves of the body, occasioning the loss of the senses and of motion, and sometimes in both lateral halves, and sudden in its attack; on the seventh [ day ] it is dangerous; but when it has passed the seventh, its acuteness ceases; and when it has passed the fourteenth, it becomes a chronic disease: (Msb:) it is called in a trad. of Aboo-Hureyreh daA='u AlA^anobiyaA='i [ the disease of the prophets ]: and is said by Et-Tedmuree, in the Expos. of the Fs, to be a disease that attacks a man when the venters ( buTuwn ) of the brain become filled with certain moistures, or humours, occasioning the loss of sensation and of the motions of the members, and rendering the patient like a dead person, understanding nothing. (TA.) -A3- A^anaA mino h`*aA AlA^amori faAliju bonu xalaAwapa , or kafaAliji boni xalaAwapa , is a saying expl. in art. xlw .

sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n., The tragacanth-tree; ] a species of thorny tree; this is the larger sort; (S;) a species of thorny and hard tree, which bears a pod, and of which the fruit is like that of the samur [or gum-acacia-tree ], growing in Nejd and Tihámeh; n. un. with p ; (L;) it is a species of hard tree having thorns like needles; (K;) a species of tree having thorns like needles, and a small dust-coloured leaf, and a fruit growing therewith of the same colour, resembling the date-stone; (AHn, O, * L;) the large qtAd [ thus described ] produces large wood, and its thorns are curved and short, and it is of the [ class termed ] EiDaAh ; (Aboo-Ziyád, L;) or it is not reckoned among the EiDaAh : (AHn, L: [but this assertion may perhaps be meant to apply to the smaller sort: respecting the larger, see also 1 and 2:]) the smaller sort is a species of tree of which the fruit is a bladder ( nuf~aAxap ) like that of the Eu$ar [q. v.]; (S, O, L;) accord. to the ancient Arabs of the desert, it is not tall, being of the size of a man sitting; (L;) and this sort grows upwards, no part of it spreading, consisting of twigs, or shoots, in a collected state, every one of which is full of thorns from its top to its bottom. (Aboo-Ziyád, L.) It is said in a prov., mino duwnihi xaroTu AlqataAdi [expl. in art. xrT , first paragraph]. (S, L.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A,) [aor. ,] inf. n. qadoHN , (Lth, S, Mgh,) The worm, or worms, effected a cankering, or corrosion, (Lth, S, A, Mgh,) fiY Al$~ajari , [ in the trees ], (Lth, S, Mgh,) or fiY AlEuwdi [ in the wood ], (A,) and fiY AlA^asonaAni [ in the teeth ]. (Lth, S, A, Mgh.) And qudiHa and qudiHa fiyhi , inf. n. as above, It (the tree, and the tooth,) became cankered, or corroded. (L.) ― -b2- [Hence,] qadaHa fiyhi , (Msb, K,) or fiY EiroDihi , and fiY saAqihi , (A,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (Msb,) from the incidency of the qawaAdiH [or canker-worms] in the saAq [or stem] of the tree, (A,) (tropical:) He impaired, injured, detracted from, impugned, or attacked, his honour, or reputation; blamed, censured, or reproached, him; found fault with him; or spoke against him. (A, Msb, K.) And qadaHa fiY nasabihi (tropical:) He found fault with, or spoke against, his parentage, genealogy, or pedigree. (S, A, Msb.) And qadaHa fiY EadaAlatihi (assumed tropical:) He impugned his rectitude as a witness, mentioning something that should have the effect of causing his testimony to be rejected. (Msb.) And qadaHa fiY saAqi A^axiyhi (tropical:) He acted dishonestly, or insincerely, towards his brother, and did that which was displeasing to him, or that which he hated. (L, TA.) And fulaAnN yafut~u fiY EaDudi fulaAnK wayaqodaHu fiY saAqihi (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one seeks to injure such a one by diminishing, or impairing, ( in number or power ) the people of his house, or his aiders, or assistants; and blames, censures, or reproaches, him ]: by EaDudihi being meant A^aholi bayotihi ; and by nafosihi saAqihi . (IAar, T. [See EaDudN .]) ― -b3- qadaHa fiY AlqidoHi , (A, K, TA,) aor. as above, (TA,) He (a maker of arrows, A) made a hole in [ the end of ] the [ arrow in the state in which it is termed ] qidoH with the tang of the iron head [ for the insertion of the said tang ]: (A, K, TA:) which hole is termed ↓ maqodaHN . (S, A. [See naqaba AlEayona .]) ― -b6- qadaHa Aln~aAra , (S, L,) aor. and inf. n. as above, He struck, or produced, fire with a flint &c.: (L:) or qadaHa Aln~aAra mina Alz~anodi [or Alz~anodapi i. e. definition: An arrow, (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: An arrow, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) [i. e.] the pared wood, or rod, of an arrow, (Mgh,) before it has been furnished with feathers and a head: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.:) or an arrow when straightened, and fit to be feathered and headed: (T, voce bariY~N , q. v.:) or a rod that has attained the desired state of growth, and been pruned, and cut according to the required length for an arrow: (AHn:) and [particularly] such as is used in the game called Almayosir : (S, L:) pl. qidaAHN , (S, A, Mgh, L, K,) a pl. of mult., (TA,) and [of pauc., and accord. to the L of qidoHN in the last of the senses expl. above,] A^aqoduHu (S, L, K) and A^aqodaAHN (L, TA) and A^aqaAdiyHu , (S, L, K,) which last is a pl. pl. [i. e. pl. of A^aqodaAHN ]. (L.) [One says, in speaking of the arrows used in the game called Daraba biAlqidaAHi Almayosir , and Daraba AlqidaAHa : and in speaking of the two arrows used in practising sortilege, Daraba biAlqidoHayoni : see art. Drb , p. 1778, col. iii.] SadaqaniY wasoma qidoHihi (tropical:) He told me truly what was the brand of his gaming- arrow ] is a prov.; meaning he told me the truth: (A, * TA:) so says AZ: (TA:) or it means he told me what was in his mind: the wsm of the qdH is the mark that denotes its share [of the slaughtered camel]; and the sign is sometimes made by means of fire. (Meyd.) And they say, A^aboSiro wasoma qidoHika (tropical:) [ See, or look at, the brand of thy gaming- arrow ]; (TA;) which is [also] a prov.; (A;) meaning know thyself. (A, TA.) And qidoHu A@boni muqobilK (assumed tropical:) [ The gaming- arrow of Ibn-Mukbil, which seems to have been one remarkable for frequent good luck,] is a proverbial expression relating to goodness of effect. (TA.)

definition: [ A drinking-cup or bowl;
sourceDefinition: [ A drinking-cup or bowl; ] a certain vessel (Msb, K) for drinking, (S, Mgh,) well known, (Msb,) large enough to satisfy the thirst of two men: (A 'Obeyd, K:) or a small one and a large one: (K:) [in the K voce EulobapN , it is applied to a vessel used for milking, sometimes made of camel's skin and sometimes of wood: it was used for drinking and for milking: ] pl. A^aqodaAHN . (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., laA tajoEaluwniY kaqadaHi Alr~akibi [ Make not ye me to be like the drinkingcup of the rider on a camel ]; meaning, make not ye me to be last in being mentioned; because the rider on a camel suspends his qdH on the hinder part of his saddle when he is finishing the puttingon of his apparatus, (Mgh, TA,) placing it behind him. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A certain measure of capacity, in Egypt, containing two hundred and thirty-two daraAhim . (Es-Suyootee in his “ Husn el-Mohádarah. ” See A_irodab~N , in art. rdb .)

definition: Of a colour inclining to xuDorap : or of a dull or dingy or dusky white: (K:) and white: (S, Msb, K:) or intensely white: (IKtt:) fem.
sourceDefinition: Of a colour inclining to xuDorap : or of a dull or dingy or dusky white: (K:) and white: (S, Msb, K:) or intensely white: (IKtt:) fem. qamoraA='u : (S, K:) pl. qumorN . (S, Msb.) You say HimaArN A^aqomaru (S, A, Msb, K) An ass of the colour termed qumorap : (K:) or a white ass: (S, A, Msb:) and A^ataAnN qamoraA='u a she-ass of the colour termed qumorap : (K:) or a white she-ass. (S.) The Arabs say, that when the sky appears of the hue of the belly of a she-ass of this colour, it is most abundant in rain. (TA.) Also farasN A^aqomaru A moon-coloured horse. (Mgh.) And saHaAbN A^aqomaru A cloud, or clouds, of a white colour: (S:) or intensely bright, by reason of the abundance of water therein: and [hence] full [ of water ]. (TA.) ― -b2- layolapN qamoraA='u , (S, A, K,) and muqomirapN , (A, Msb, K,) and ↓ muqomirN , (K) and ↓ qamirapN , (IAar, K,) which last is held by ISd, to be a kind of rel. n., or possessive epithet, (TA,) A moon-lit night; a night in which the moon shines: (A, K:) or a light, or bright, night: (S:) or a white night. (Msb.) IAar, mentions layolN qamoraA='u ; but ISd, says this is strange, and I think, he adds, that by lyl he means lylp , or that he makes lyl fem. as a pl. (TA.) You also say layolapu AlqamoraA='i , meaning The night of moonlight: (Lth, A, Mgh:) for AlqamoraA='u also signifies the moonlight. (Lth, A, Mgh, K.) And qaEadNnaA fiY AlqamoraA='i We sat in the moonlight. (A.) And A^atoyotuhu fiY AlqamoraA='i [ I came to him in the moonlight ]. (S.) ― -b3- wajohN A^aqamaru A face likened to the moon (K, * TA) in respect of whiteness. (TA.)

It has the last of these significations in a trad. of Mujáhid, in which it is said, yagoduw Al$~ayoTaAnu biqayorawaAnihi A_ilaY Als~uwqi falaA yazaAlu yahotaz~u AlEaro$u mim~aA yaEolamu A@ll~`hu maA laA yaEolamu [ The devil goeth in the morning with his companions and assistants to the market-place, and the empyrean ceaseth not to shake in consequence of the assertions that God knoweth what He knoweth not ]: meaning, that the devil incites men to say “ God knoweth such a thing, ” of things whereof God knoweth the contrary: [as for instance, “ God knoweth that such a commodity cost me (the seller) such a sum of money: ”] yaEolamu A@ll~`hu being a form of asseveration. (IAth.) [ qyrwAn is written qayoruwaAnN in some copies of the S and K. It is mentioned in this art., and in art. qrw , in the K: in the S, only in the latter art., and part of the above trad. is there cited.]

(TA.) It is used metaphorically in relation to every kind of disagreeable, hateful, or evil, things. Thus you say, saqaAhu kaA^osFA mina Al*~ul~i (tropical:) [ He gave him to drink a cup of abasement ]: and mina Alfuroqapi (tropical:) [ of separation ]: and mina Almawoti (tropical:) [ of death ]: and mina AlHub~i (tropical:) [ of love ]. (TA.) You say also, saqaAhu AlkaA^osa AlA^amar~a (tropical:) [ He gave him to drink the most bitter cup ]; meaning death: (A, TA:) and kuw^uwsa AlmanaAyaA (tropical:) [ The cups of death; lit., deaths ]. (A.) Az. thinks that it may be derived from kaASa fulaAnN mina AlT~aEaAmi waAl$~araAbi , meaning, “ Such a one ate and drank much ”; because S and s are interchangeable in many words on account of the nearness of their places of utterance. (TA.)

definition: , aor. , (inf. n. kabotN , TA,) He threw him down prostrate; (K;) as also kabatahu liwajohihi : (S:) he threw him, or it, down upon his, or its face; like kab~ahu : this is the primary signification....
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (inf. n. kabotN , TA,) He threw him down prostrate; (K;) as also kabatahu liwajohihi : (S:) he threw him, or it, down upon his, or its face; like kab~ahu : this is the primary signification. (TA.) ― -b2- kabatahu All~`hu liwajohihi May God prostrate him, so that he may not succeed in his enterprise, or may not gain the victory! (TA.) ― -b3- kabata AlkaAfira He (God) prostrated the unbeliever, and denied him what he desired, or disappointed him, or caused him to fail of attaining his desire. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- kabatahu He repelled him (i. e. an enemy) in his rage, or wrath. (K.) ― -b5- I. q. kasarahu [here app. signifying He routed him; or put him to flight. ] (K.) ― -b6- kabatahu , (inf. n. kabotN , S,) He turned away, or averted, him: (S, K:) and abased him; debased him; rendered him vile, despicable, or ignominious. (S, K.) Syn. A^a*al~ahu and A^axozaAhu (K) Ex. kabata All~`hu AlEaduw~a God averted and abased the enemy. (S.) ― -b7- kubituwA kamaA kubita Al~a*iyna mino qabolihimo , in the Kur, [lviii, 6,] signifies, They [who oppose God and his Apostle] have been abased, and punished, by their being overcome, like as those who were before them, of such as opposed God, were abased, &c.: (Zj:) or they have been enraged, and grieved, on the occasion of the war of the Moat, like as those who were before them, who fought with the prophets, were enraged and grieved: (Fr:) in favour of which latter interpretation it has been argued, that Alkbt is formed from Alkbd , the liver, by the substitution of t for d , and that the liver is the source of rage and malevolence. (Az.) -A2- kabatahu i. q. kabadahu , He smote, or hurt, his liver. (TA.) ― -b2- kabata gayoZahu fiY jawofihi (tropical:) He restrained his rage in his inside [or bosom ]. You say, mano kabata gayoZahu fiY jawofihi kabata All~`hu Eaduw~ahu mino xawofihi [ Whoso restraineth his rage in his bosom, God will avert and abase his enemy, through fear of him ]. (A.)

definition: A portion, or quantity, of corn or other food, (or of dates, TA,) or dust, or earth, &c.
